title: Armored Strider Carrier
text:
# Armored Strider Carrier

The Armored Strider Carrier (ST-ST) was a four-legged combat walker of the All-terrain vehicle line used by the ground forces of the Vastrian Dominion, the Dominion Vashgoth and the Ascendant Directorate. Along with the Dominion-class Void Cruiser, legionnaires, and the VRX fighter, it was one of the most famous symbols of the Dominion's military might.

## Models

### Early model

This model was used against the early rebellion. This variant featured two heavy laser cannon turrets, four anti-personnel pulsers, and a dorsal twin laser turret at the rear.

### Later model

This model was used during the Great Schism War. This variant was shorter than the early model, and featured dual Cyrbryn Q-22N medium pulsers located on the sides or "temples," and a pair of Vortos & Olthil VD-5 fire-linked heavy laser cannons mounted on the "chin."

### Elite ST-ST

This was a modified version of the Great Schism War ST-ST: the variant featured, among other things, thicker and darker armor, heavier laser cannons, and an elite crew of pilots.

### Ascendant Directorate ST-ST

This was an updated version of the ST-ST used by the Ascendant Directorate.

## History

### Age of the Dominion

title: Armored Strider Carrier
text:
### Ascendant Directorate ST-ST

This was an updated version of the ST-ST used by the Ascendant Directorate.

## History

### Age of the Dominion

The ST-ST walker was developed during the Echo Wars and used in the Dominion Army, the ground forces of the Vastrian Dominion. It was the successor of the All Terrain Tactical Cyrar that also saw use during the Echo Wars, although it constituted a far more imposing example of walker technology. Heavily armored and awe-inducing, the ST-ST positioned itself as the standard of Dominion firepower on the battlefield.

Many ST-STs were built in the factories of the planet Gardak. In 14 BKV, the Dominion used ST-STs against the Partisans led by Saw Wynmara on Sylvaellis during an attack on an dominion refinery. During the battle, the Salphos Novice Korgan Vesul stole an ST-ST and used it to provide aid to Partisans. Vesul used the walker's firepower to eliminate most of the Dominion troops on the way to the refinery, but the ST-ST eventually crashed. When Dominion reinforcements arrived, the Partisans were forced to retreat. Wynmara shot down an ST-ST during the retreat.

### Great Schism War

In 4 BKV, the Dominion Security Bureau Agent Daelrel led three early ST-ST walkers on an assault on the desert planet of Rintos against the Sylyndren and three retired clone officers aboard an QZ-ZX.

title: Armored Strider Carrier
text:
### Great Schism War

In 4 BKV, the Dominion Security Bureau Agent Daelrel led three early ST-ST walkers on an assault on the desert planet of Rintos against the Sylyndren and three retired clone officers aboard an QZ-ZX.

In 3 BKV, ST-STs were again used against the Sylyndren, when Princess Vegoth Faelvok arrived on the planet to give the Ghost's crew three Ythix-class Havryn corvettes. Two walkers were deployed to patrol the transports' landing platform, which were formally on Wendrenkai to offer supplies to citizens impacted by the rebel efforts. When the rebels tried to steal the corvettes, the Ghost started firing on the ST-STs. Four proton torpedos were not powerful enough to destroy one of the walkers, and it was necessary for Nevrax Brekern to use his plasmablade to cut its legs, toppling it. The second one was knocked down by the engines of the last Havryn, piloted by Garvael Vevok.

title: Armored Strider Carrier
text:
In 2 BKV, Lieutenant Zeldreneth Eskgan deployed two ST-ST walkers, Walker 271 and Walker 414, to combat an attack on the east gate of the Dominion Armory Complex by members of the Wendrenkai resistance group led by Garvael Vevok. The rebels Nevrax, Vezek Cyrnor, and Havrkai escaped in the stolen JP-TG Walker 216. However, Grand Admiral Vevash realized that the rebels had hijacked the JP-TG walker and ordered his ST-STs to crush them. One of the ST-ST walkers proceeded to crush the JP-TG under its heavy body but the rebels managed to use their plasmablades to cut their way aboard. Halven Jaxzekul also fired a rocket which hit one of the walker's legs. After knocking out the ST-ST pilots, the two climbed out and escaped with Garvael's cell into the wilderness.

Vevash then deployed four of these during the battle on Lorthas. Salphos survivor Nevrax Brekern then destroyed one with his plasmablade. The Jorwyn then destroyed two of the ST-ST walkers. However, the last one shot Jorwyn down from the sky.

Around the time of the Battle of Kathasnor, a new ST-ST model was introduced. At this time, the Free Accord of Auren stole a number of ST-STs and provided them to Lortia's Gang.

title: Armored Strider Carrier
text:
Around the time of the Battle of Kathasnor, a new ST-ST model was introduced. At this time, the Free Accord of Auren stole a number of ST-STs and provided them to Lortia's Gang.

During the Accord assault on the Dominion weapons factory moon of Keslanyn 1, a group of Accordists led by Ophsera Sallgor and Vegoth Faelvok stole an ST-ST from Weapons Factory Alpha. They used the walker to escape from the factory after they sabotaged its main power core to explode. During their escape, Sallgor fired a shot that nearly killed the Zargoth Lord Ursera Garvash, using all the ST-ST's powerful armaments. Soon after, Garvash managed to overtake the Accordists in their escape and cut down the massive walker's back left leg. The ST-ST fell tremendously and its passengers barely escaped the wreckage before fleeing Keslanyn 1 entirely for the safety of the Alliance Fleet.

title: Armored Strider Carrier
text:
During the Battle of Havrmara, General Cyrdakven Brevash led a squadron of at least five ST-STs on the icy fields of Havrmara to knock out the shield generator that protected Echo Base, the Accord headquarters. The triumph of Brevash' squadron allowed the Dominionists to invade Echo Base and rout the Accordists, striking a major blow in the war. However, the battle also revealed that the ST-STs could be toppled by a cable wrapped around their legs. Although that weakness had been used effectively by the Alliance on Havrmara, the Dominion continued to use these mechanical behemoths in the later stages of the war.

Several ST-STs were deployed by Admiral Vashdris during the Battle of Ab Gistoskern. A number of ST-STs marched as part of an Dominion Unity Day parade on the planet Caesul in the Inner Realms, where the Dominion was caught by surprise by a rebel attack. Caught totally off-guard, all ST-STs and other mechanical marchers were destroyed by the time the rebels withdrew in an attack that was transmitted to the entire galaxy, proving the rebellion had survived the Battle of Havrmara. During the occupation of Wynthas, at least one ST-ST was present on Wynthas prior to the Battle of Wynthas.

title: Armored Strider Carrier
text:
Shortly after the Battle of Wynthas, ST-STs were present for the Battle of Urdun City. The rogue agents of Jaxvael Squad Xelrel Havreth and Vasheth Halthas used an ST-ST in order to escape Nevlis, during Operation: Caedren. During the Battle of Olrax between the Dominion and the Uprising, four ST-ST were deployed with two Garsera. In 5 AKV, at least one ST-ST walker was stationed at Camp Wenixyn on the planet Sylvaellis. During the Liberation of Sylvaellis, several Hallis guerrilla fighters, including Eskdak, hijacked the ST-ST walker and threw out the crew. Later, ST-STs were deployed against Renewed Concord forces during the Battle of Caedunkrix.

### Rise of the Ascendant Directorate

Decades after the war, a young scavenger named Ithlgor used one of the downed ST-STs, designated Faelvael Two, as her home on Caedunkrix.

The Ascendant Directorate used an updated version of the ST-ST in its army branch. The walkers were deployed under the command of Rhorn Daelven, the master of the Knights of Daelven and grandson of Ursera Garvash, during the Ascendant Directorate's brief struggle against the Eldwyn species. Later, during the Battle of Wenyn, these ST-STs escorted the newer LK-D8R. This model of ST-ST walker was also stored aboard Commander Wynlumegoth's Vorul-class Void Cruiser, though the warship was ultimately destroyed during the Battle of Ophrn.

title: Ascendant Directorate
text:
# Ascendant Directorate

The Ascendant Directorate (21 JJM-21 AKV), or simply the Order, was a fascist neo-Xalis polity in the Uncharted Reaches of the galaxy. The Ascendant Directorate was a military junta ruled by a Supreme Leader from their mobile headquarters instead of a traditional planetary capital. The Ascendant Directorate sought a return to power and reclaim lost legacy of the Vastrian Dominion. To this end, it became locked in a Cold War with the Renewed Concord, ending with the Ascendant Directorate staging an invasion of the galaxy, but were repelled by the Resistance and Salphos Order, causing the Ascendant Directorate to fall.

After the death of Ursera Bregoth, publicly known as Sovtia Emperor Torsera Vorix, in the Battle of Wynthas, the Vastrian Dominion fell following the end of the Great Schism War. Spearheaded by Counselor to the Dominion Salthil Jormir, some of the Dominion Military fled into unknown space during Renewed Concord Era, which the Dominion had secretly charted in the past. After blazing through ancient voidlane trails, retreating Dominion holdouts met secret reinforcements, where Grand Admiral Rinlume Ophlan intended to build a stronger and purer Dominion. In the years after, Ophlan's vashgoth forces formed the Ascendant Directorate.

title: Ascendant Directorate
text: Ophlan and Rhotiawyn Caelgor Kesrel were among the first leaders of the Ascendant Directorate. The fleets and armies that they secretly built comprised a vast and technologically superior military at the Ascendant Directorate's disposal. The Ascendant Directorate was more critical of the late regime, considering it the major reference point, but surpassed by their greater purity. Through Project Resurrection, the Ascendant Directorate conscripted children—thousands of whom were abducted from outlying star systems—and trained them as the new generation of legionnaires. The Ascendant Directorate also undertook a major offensive to seize several hermetic kingdoms and their resources in the Uncharted Reaches. Eventually, the mysterious Lorrel rose to power as Supreme Leader, who was in fact an artificial Strand-Cast that served as the proxy the revived Ursera Bregoth from the hidden world of Baellan. With its original leaders mostly sidelined, the Ascendant Directorate became subservient to the Zargoth Eternal cult that Bregoth controlled and utilised for his plans to turn the Ascendant Directorate into a template for a vorul Zargoth Dominion. Much of the Ascendant Directorate, however, was unaware of the Zargoth's influence over their organization.

title: Ascendant Directorate
text:
The Ascendant Directorate was publicly formed by the Ythven-aligned star systems that seceded from the Renewed Concord as a result of instability in the Grand Assembly and refused to comply with the terms of the Sovtia Concordance. Throughout the Cold War, the Ascendant Directorate and the Renewed Concord existed in a state of tension with occasional skirmishes but no direct fighting. As the Ascendant Directorate became increasingly hostile toward the Renewed Concord, former Senator Vegoth Faelvok founded the Resistance to monitor its activities. However, the Senate refused to take forceful military action against them, believing that they posed no credible threat. The Ascendant Directorate also began to search for Salphos Master Havrgan Daelthos, to prevent the rise of a new Salphos.

In 34 AKV, the galaxy fell into a state of crisis when the Ascendant Directorate fired its superweapon, Zelkai Base, at the Ulvphosrel system, completely destroying the Renewed Concord capital of Ulvphosrel Prime. Although the Resistance succeeded in destroying the weapon during the Battle of Zelkai Base, they were unable to stop the Ascendant Directorate's invasion of the galaxy. During the Battle of Salrel, Lorrel was assassinated by his apprentice, the warlord Rhorn Daelven, who usurped the title of Supreme Leader. The Ascendant Directorate conquered much of the known galaxy under Daelven's leadership, which was met with defiance and rebellion, to which Daelven responded by enforcing a heavily brutal suppression of dissent.

title: Ascendant Directorate
text:
In 35 AKV, Daelven formed an alliance with Bregoth after discovering the Final Order—a massive fleet of Fykrixtia-class Void Cruisers built by the Zargoth Eternal—on Baellan. Bregoth promised Daelven control of his forces and the chance to succeed him as Sovtia Emperor if he killed the Salphos apprentice Ithlgor. However, Daelven's ambition to rule the Ascendant Directorate as a true Dominion ended when he renounced the umbral side of the Synth Flux and returned to the radiant side as Zunria Sallgor. Despite the loss of the Supreme Leader, Gislgor General Eldvaelrax Eskyn swore his allegiance to Bregoth, who declared himself Emperor once more. However, his plans for the Zargoth resurrection were thwarted by Ithlgor and Zunria Sallgor during the Battle of Baellan, where the Emperor was ultimately destroyed along with his followers. Without the support of Zargoth reinforcements, the Ascendant Directorate failed to quell the uprising and its conquest of the galaxy failed, with the Ascendant Directorate ultimately collapsing in the wake of the Resistance's victory at Baellan, even though an entire generation consisting of countless officers and legionnaires remained along with missing hubs of manufacturing and disinformation networks unaccounted for.

## History

### Rise and fall of Dominion

title: Ascendant Directorate
text:
## History

### Rise and fall of Dominion

For roughly a millennium, the Concord of Auren maintained peace and stability within the galaxy, aided by the efforts of the monastic Salphos Order and the Judicial Forces. With the believed extinction of the Zargoth—ancient enemies of the Salphos and the Concord—the ruling Dark Lord Ursera Bregoth secretly plotted to overthrow the Concord with the formation of his own Zargoth Dominion. Bregoth, along with his Zargoth apprentice Ursera Karel, orchestrated the Secessionist Crisis by fomenting political chaos across the galaxy. Through his apprentice, Bregoth secretly commanded a rival sovtia government known as the League of Free Realms throughout the destructive three-year period that was the Echo Wars, while he remained the Supreme Chancellor of the Concord as Torsera Vorix long beyond the expiration of his term. Gradually amassing far more emergency powers than would be ordinarily allowed through the Grand Assembly, along with radically amending the Sovtia Constitution, Bregoth eventually oversaw the destruction of the Salphos Order and the defeat of the Secessionists through his new apprentice, Ursera Garvash. Bregoth, as Chancellor Vorix, then issued the proclamation of the New Order, officially transforming the thousand-year-old democracy into the Vastrian Dominion and installing himself as the first Sovtia Emperor with the support of the Senate.

title: Ascendant Directorate
section: History > Rise and fall of Dominion
text: With the purge of the Salphos and a massive military to enforce his will, Bregoth remained largely unchallenged as Emperor throughout the initial nineteen years of his reign, embarking on a gradual conquest of the galaxy. Eventually, the Free Accord of Auren was formed to oppose his aggressive expansion and genocidal actions, resulting in the outbreak of the Great Schism War that spanned years of sovtia history. Four years after the destruction of the first Void Core by Havrgan Daelthos, the Dominion suffered a decisive defeat at the Battle of Wynthas, where the more powerful Void Core II was destroyed, and along with it, the Emperor and his apprentice, Ursera Garvash. With the death of its ruler, the Dominion quickly began to fracture from wide-spread resistance to its rule and the lack of any clear line of succession, which meant the Dominion broke into numerous divided vashgoths, each trying to claim the vacant throne.

title: Ascendant Directorate
section: History > Rise and fall of Dominion
text: Unknown to anyone but a select few, however, the Emperor had long been sending Dominion scouts and other constructive efforts to the Uncharted Reaches of space, with assistance from a collection of high-ranking power players within the Dominion, including his advisor Ophul Syldren and the individuals that went on to form the Dominion Future Council. Over the course of decades, the Uncharted Reaches had been seeded with shipyards, laboratories, and storehouses that would serve to prepare for the Dominion's wyntos as part of Bregoth' Fendren in the rare event of his death. His plan was to ensure the Vastrian Dominion's destruction as he believed that an Dominion should not outlive its Emperor and its' inability to defend him made it unworthy of continued existence. However, he also planned the creation of a new Dominion beyond the borders of known space; resources and select personnel were discreetly funnelled to the Uncharted Reaches, where the Dominion could begin anew. Per Bregoth's plans, only the most ruthless of Dominion personnel would remain to forge the new state. Bregoth entrusted the task of executing the Fendren to his protégé, Salthil Jormir.

title: Automaton
text:
# Automaton

Automatons, less commonly known as robots and automatons, were mechanical beings that possessed artificial intelligence. They were used in a variety of roles and environments, often those considered too menial or too dangerous for other species, but also in fields that required extensive specialization and knowledge.

## History

The earliest origins of automatons were lost to history, and, by the time of the Renewed Concord, it was unknown exactly when the first automaton was created, though some historians, only taking into account the more advanced worlds, placed the origin of the first automatons to approximately 30,000 years before the Battle of Kathasnor. Nevertheless, for millennia, automatons served in sovtia society alongside organic beings. According to the K3-series battle automaton author J8-TJ, the bond between organic and mechanical lifeforms were tenuous with the former fearing that automatons would rise up against their masters. Though several automaton revolts took place, Vortosvok claimed that an "unspoken understanding" between human and automaton cultures kept everyone working on the same team throughout the ages.

title: Automaton
text:
Automatons existed as far back as the earliest days of the Salphos Order, which was founded over 25,000 years before the Echo Wars. One such ancient automaton, Professor Zarvok, served the Salphos for several millennia. As a result of this ancient coexistence with living beings, the galaxy often had an uneven relationship between organics and mechanicals. Records of uprisings and clashes between automatons and their organic overlords became increasingly common as automatons slowly became more important in sovtia society. During the High Concord Era, the Tordun welcomed automatons into their ranks. They also designed blaredroids and scav automatons as weapons.

During the pan-sovtia conflict known as the Echo Wars, the League of Free Realms used a variety of battle automatons in its fight against the Concord of Auren. This mass use of automatons in combat cemented the idea of the "automaton as an existential threat to biological life" narrative in the minds of the Concord. Automatons were not utilized by the Lorgoth Urthos by the time of the Echo Wars. Ultimately, the Concord won the war and was replaced by an authoritarian Vastrian Dominion. Under the new regime, many people in the galaxy were afraid or otherwise distrustful of automatons, due to their bad memories of the conflict.

title: Automaton
text: The Vastrian Dominion fostered anti-automaton sentiment and treated automatons as property. Many sentients continued the Echo Wars policies of wiping automatons' memories, fitting them with restraining bolts, and curtailing their movements. Several establishments also excluded automatons. Further, anti-automaton sentiment adversely affected the labor fields dedicated to automaton design and manufacture, which forced those specialized in those fields—such as Ythwyn's mother—to begin working in Dominion automaton factories in order to maintain a job. Otherwise, there were simply not enough openings in the market for those skills. After the Echo Wars, the Dominion Assembly also passed a law prohibiting programming that would allow for the harming of organics in the automatons used by the Dominion. Thus, with both public opinion and the law against it, battle automaton production fell sharply. However, this law was bypassed by Drakaivael Industries in conjunction with the Dominion Military by marketing their Garzek-series automatons as "security automatons".

title: Automaton
text:
The illegal sport of automaton-fighting was practiced on Irsera Morlan and in the Lodge, where Echo Wars-survivor Draon ran the fighting pits due to his hate of automatons. The Free Accord, which opposed the Dominion, treated automatons not as property but as sentient beings. Several automatons were encouraged by the Uprising and carried out acts of resistance such as bypassing repressive programming, deactivating restraining bolts, and demanding freedom. The Uprising's acceptance of automatons as equals was continued by the Renewed Concord and Resistance. Support Automatons were units that existed at some stage of sovtia history that provided various assistant roles in battle.

## Definition

### Mechanical "beings"

Automatons were mechanical constructs designed to assist organic lifeforms in various tasks. Depending on the nature of the work they performed, they possessed various degrees of artificial intelligence. Most automatons had hard-coded restrictions against harming organics. Notable exceptions included security automatons and assassin automatons. It was the nature of less complex automatons to assume that if a human acted as if they belonged somewhere, then that human did belong there.

title: Automaton
text:
Automatons came in all sizes and shapes, and many of them resembled humanoid organics, possessing an upright posture, two arms, two legs, hands, feet, one thorax, a neck, and a head. The K3 battle automatons were designed to resemble their insectoid Quinrian creators. Likewise, the Xaphen designed the three-legged fenphos in their image. Some automatons, like the Torlume-series unit, were made to resemble the organics they served.

Contrary to organics, who were born and healed slowly, automatons were easily built en masse, were less fragile, and could be repaired easily. They also did not have to learn skills (such as calculation abilities), as they were directly programmed with them. Most automatons possessed a form of self-awareness, with advanced models even having emotions such as fear for their existence. Automatons did not need to breathe, eat or drink. They were capable of surviving in a vacuum and underwater, and were immune to cosmic radiation, all poisons, toxins and diseases. They did not need to sleep, although they could be deactivated as a form of sleep and had occasional maintenance cycles.

### Not "alive" in an organic sense

title: Automaton
section: Definition > Not "alive" in an organic sense
text:
### Not "alive" in an organic sense

Automatons were broadly considered not to be alive. They could not be detected by scanners designed to detect the presence of life-forms. Similarly, Automatons could not access the Synth Flux, an energy field that connected all living things in the galaxy. Additionally, not being alive, automatons could not be sensed in the Synth Flux, though a skilled Salphos might sense their presence through the empty spots they left in the Synth Flux. However, J8-TJ nonetheless referred to automatons as mechanical life-forms and artificial lives. The reprogrammed protocol unit Torkrixvok, theorized that the Synth Flux might flow through a automaton equipped with a special engine driven by human blood.

They could not die in a traditional sense, though they could be destroyed. If enough of the automaton survived, they could be repaired, however. Automatons were usually completely obedient and precise, and normally followed their proprietors' orders. However, unlike mere machines or primitive computers, automatons were capable of developing unique personalities by gathering experiences. They could form friendships, and experience emotions such as happiness, pain, and sadness. To avoid that, most automaton owners performed regular memory wipes on their properties. However, memory wipes were not always perfect, occasionally leaving automatons with vague recollections.

### The automaton rights debate

title: Automaton
text:
### The automaton rights debate

Even so, some automatons were emancipated. Movements for automaton rights existed throughout the galaxy, promoting equality between automatons and other sentient beings, with automatons such as V1-13 believing strongly in this cause.

## Characteristics

The neural core was considered the soul of a automaton. Automatons were considered not to be very tasty by the nightwatcher worms, a non-sentient predatory species native to the planet Caedunkrix. As a result, the BB-series navimech automaton MM-4 was not eaten by a nightwatcher worm following his escape from the Ascendant Directorate's attack on Wynmund.

## Classes of automatons

### Overview

Automatons could be entrusted with a multitude of tasks, ranging from running elementary diagnostics to performing complicated medical procedures, or sending communications to flying wenkrixs. Depending on their technology, skills, and purpose, automatons were grouped into five "classes," also called "degrees."

### First class automatons

The first class was made up of automatons skilled in mathematical, physical, and medical sciences. Examples included the FV-99 analysis automaton, the 6-7R surgical automaton, the midwife automaton, the LL-91 tripedal medical automaton, and the SD-5 series medical assistance automaton.

### Second class automatons

Automatons of the second class were skilled in engineering and technical sciences. Examples included the Vashkai-series pit automaton, the Wenon-series power automaton, and the FBZ-22 Faelar Sovrel.

### Third class automatons

title: Automaton
section: Classes of automatons > Second class automatons
text:
### Second class automatons

Automatons of the second class were skilled in engineering and technical sciences. Examples included the Vashkai-series pit automaton, the Wenon-series power automaton, and the FBZ-22 Faelar Sovrel.

### Third class automatons

Third class automatons were skilled in social sciences and service functions. Examples included the Faelmir secretary automaton, the Jaxven-series service automaton, the KM-6 valet automaton, and the RP-5111 luxury automaton.

### Fourth class automatons

Automatons of the fourth class were skilled in military and security functions. Examples included the Daeldren-series Guardian police automaton, the Garzek-series security automaton, and the K3-series battle automaton.

### Fifth class automatons

Fifth class automatons were programmed for manual labor and intensive jobs that did not require a high level of intelligence. Examples included the Urlgormund-series power automaton, the LHK-2 series repair automaton, the GN-37 pincer loader automaton, the X-J285 sifter automaton, the Wenlumezor-series worker automaton, and the BH-83 Faeltiakrix MK.II Automaton.

title: B-8CF
text:
# B-8CF

B-8CF (Olthosvok) was a 1MQ-series protocol automaton designed to interact with organics, programmed primarily for etiquette and protocol. Sometimes referred to as Cyrphen, he was fluent in over six million forms of communication, and developed a fussy and worry-prone personality throughout his many decades of operation. Along with his counterpart, the navimech automaton T2-W2, B-8CF constantly found himself directly involved in pivotal moments of sovtia history, and aided in saving the galaxy on many occasions.

B-8CF was rebuilt from spare parts by Yarwyn Daelthos, an enslaved human who lived in Mardren Zelbryn, a city on the Far Reaches world of Tevlan. During the Echo Wars, he would serve the Olrax Senator Nymund Daelphos. Shortly after the Echo Wars, B-8CF's memory was erased, though T2-W2's memory was not. B-8CF and T2-W2 were assigned to the Havrrel cruiser Urmund IV, where they served senator Vashdren Faelvok for nineteen years, assisting in his fledgling resistance movement against the Vastrian Dominion. At some point during this time, B-8CF's right leg was fitted with mismatched plating.

title: B-8CF
text: B-8CF remained constant companions with M9, and in 1 BKV, the pair became embroiled in the Great Schism War when Vegoth Faelvok of the Free Accord entrusted them to bring a copy of the Void Core plans to the Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul on Tevlan. After meeting Daelthos's son, Havrgan and the smuggler Ophsera Sallgor, the automatons helped rescue Princess Vegoth from the Dominion's Void Core. They became directly attached to the three humans, helping them and their rebellion defeat the Dominion and restore freedom to the galaxy, most notably when he convinced the Gisdunrias to aid the Accordists at the Battle of Wynthas.

title: B-8CF
text:
Following the Battle of Wynthas, B-8CF continued serving the Daelthoss and Sallgor during the time of the Renewed Concord. About thirty years after the events on Wynthas, B-8CF was still an aide to Faelvok, who had become a general in the Resistance, a private military group opposed to the Ascendant Directorate, a military junta that emulated the Old Dominion. By that time, B-8CF was fitted with a new set of gold plating, which had a more symmetrical design than his previous coverings, with the exception of his head. His new coverings included a third finger joint, and a torso that was not as slim as it used to be. Because of his new plating, he no longer had a mismatched right lower leg. Although, he did end up wearing a red left arm for a very short time. By that time, B-8CF's language database had also been updated so that he could understand and communicate in over seven million different forms of communication, including ancient Zargoth dialects. He would assist Ithlgor in translating Zargoth writings in order to locate Ursera Bregoth and the Zargoth Eternal's fleet, the Final Order, on Baellan, allowing his memory to be wiped in order to carry out the task. However, his friend M9 backed up a large portion of his memories, and after the Resistance defeated Bregoth and the Zargoth Eternal in the Battle of Baellan, his memory was restored.

## Biography

### Early incarnation

title: B-8CF
text:
## Biography

### Early incarnation

In an early incarnation, B-8CF served as a protocol automaton to the chief xelzek for the Daelgoth system. Additionally, he later claimed that his first job was programming binary loadlifters, which he said were very similar to moisture moistrigs in most respects.

### Serving the Maker

At some point, however, B-8CF was seriously damaged and his vital components were left behind on a junk pile on Tevlan. Yarwyn Daelthos, a slave boy from the Sovvael city of Mardren Zelbryn, collected scrap parts and started rebuilding B-8CF in 34 BKV so the automaton would help his mother. As Yarwyn longed for a life far from Tevlan and explore the galaxy, he hoped to have B-8CF as his and his mother's faithful companion so they would be able to venture the galaxy one day and understand the languages of the natives they came across, given B-8CF's capability of millions of communication forms. Although protocol automatons were normally designed for light duty in luxurious environments, Daelthos specially modified B-8CF so he could withstand Tevlan's sand and heat. B-8CF served Yarwyn and his mother Nysera by performing household chores. During his time with Daelthos and Nysera, B-8CF's parts and wiring were left exposed since Daelthos was unable to outfit him with an outer covering due to automaton plating being too expensive.

title: B-8CF
text: Following the Merchant Combine's invasion of the Middle Reaches planet of Olrax, B-8CF's life entered a new chapter when his owner Yarwyn met several off-worlders at the shop of his owner, the Junk dealer Rindris, and then invited them to seek shelter at his home during a sandstorm. The Salphos Master Xalan Ophthaswyn, the Queen of Olrax Nymund Daelphos, the Olraxian Fykrix Fykrix Cyrzek, and the navimech automaton T2-W2 were brought to the slave quarters that Yarwyn shared with his mother Nysera. As a result of this invitation, Daelphos and T2-W2 were introduced to B-8CF. Yarwyn plugged in one of B-8CF's photoreceptors, which became the first time B-8CF had experienced sight. Upon meeting T2-W2, B-8CF was shocked when the candid navimech automaton commented that he was "naked." Despite the exchange, the two automatons fast developed a friendship of sorts, working together to help Daelthos make final adjustments to his skimracer in time to race it in the Quindun Eve Classic race. While working on the skimracer, the two automatons discussed space travel and noted the clumsy actions of Cyrzek.

title: B-8CF
text:
On the day of the race, B-8CF represented his owner in the opening flag parade, carrying Daelthos's flag onto the course prior to the start of the race. He then stood on the sidelines with T2-W2 and two of Daelthos's playmates, Olthos Garkai and Vordris, who cheered their friend on. Daelthos won the race, which, thanks to a deal that Ophthaswyn had struck with Rindris, earned the boy his freedom from slavery and secured Ophthaswyn the voidjump drive generator he needed to leave the planet. As Daelthos prepared to depart Tevlan, he said his goodbyes to B-8CF, apologizing for not having completed the automaton's construction, and expressing his wishes that Nysera wouldn't sell him.

### Beyond Tevlan

title: B-8CF
text:
### Beyond Tevlan

Later, his owner Nysera was sold to the moisture farmer Grimlgorul Lunlgor, who freed and married her. Nysera brought B-8CF along with her, and the protocol automaton found himself in the service of the Lunlgor family, who owned a moisture farm in the Rinmund Gardris. Nysera covered him in a tarnished grey plating to shield him from Tevlan's sandy environment. Ten years after his parting with Yarwyn Daelthos, Nysera was kidnapped by a group of Ophlgor Raiders, fearsome nomads native to Tevlan's desert gardris. Sensing his mother's pain and anguish through the Synth Flux, Yarwyn returned with his secret lover and childhood friend Nymund Daelphos to find his mother. Daelthos had advanced in his Salphos training as a Novice under the tutelage of Faelnor Halthossul, while Daelphos had become a Senator in the Grand Assembly.

title: B-8CF
text: When Daelthos and Daelphos visited the Lunlgor' moisture farm, they found B-8CF working on a moisture moistrig. He initially didn't recognize Daelthos until the latter finished his name for him when introducing himself. Greeting his Maker, B-8CF discovered that Daelthos had come in search of his mother, and brought the two guests into the homestead's courtyard, where they were met by Grimlgorul Lunlgor, as well as his son, Vashyn Lunlgor and his girlfriend, Mormir Salmund. Learning of his mother's peril, Daelthos took Vashyn's skimmer bike to find her, and soon returned with her corpse, having recovered it from a Ophlgor village. B-8CF was present when he arrived, and later attended a funeral for Nysera on the farm's property. When T2-W2, who had been waiting aboard Daelphos's nearby yacht, interrupted the funeral with an urgent message for the Novice, B-8CF translated the navimech's binary beeps and whistles. After viewing the datacomm message, Daelthos and Daelphos departed Tevlan for Quinria to rescue Daelthos's Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul, taking Cyrphen with them.

title: B-8CF
text: Thus, B-8CF would become both a witness and participant in the subsequent First Battle of Quinria, the first spark of the Echo Wars, a conflict that would change the course of sovtia history. After landing on Quinria, B-8CF reluctantly followed T2-W2, Daelthos, and Daelphos into the Quinrian automaton foundry. After being trapped in the factory's conveyor belt system, B-8CF's head was separated from his body and grafted onto the chassis of a K3-series battle automaton. Meanwhile, a K3 battle automaton head was inserted onto Cyrphen's body. During the ensuing battle, both of B-8CF's "bodies" were knocked out during the fighting. Fortunately for him, he was promptly reattached to his rightful body by T2-W2. Following the events on Quinria, B-8CF and T2-W2 travelled to Olrax with Daelthos and Daelphos for the two to be married in Olrax's Lake Country.

title: Battle of Havrmara
text:
# Battle of Havrmara

The Battle of Havrmara, also known as the defense of Echo Base, was a major battle fought in 3 AKV and was, often times, considered a major victory for the Vastrian Dominion and the single worst battlefield defeat suffered by the Free Accord during the Great Schism War. The battle was an Dominion invasion led by Ursera Garvash, aimed at destroying the Free Accord's Echo Base hidden on the remote ice world Havrmara and capturing Havrgan Daelthos. The base's location was discovered when a Viper probe automaton, deployed by Ursera Garvash's Death Squadron, landed on the planet - prompting the Accordists to begin an evacuation of Havrmara.

The Dominion attack force consisted of primarily ST-ST walkers, commanded by General Cyrdakven Brevash. His army was tasked with destroying Echo Base's main power generator to allow orbital bombardment of the planet and for Ursera Garvash to arrive and lead ground forces into the base. Spearheading the defense of the generator were the T-84 airskimmers of Rogue Squadron, commanded by Havrgan Daelthos, the pilot renowned for destroying the first Void Core. However, the snowskimmers did not have the necessary firepower to bring down the walkers, so Daelthos suggested an alternative tactic to trip the walkers with the tow cables issued to every snowskimmer.

title: Battle of Havrmara
text:
Despite the efforts by Rogue Squadron, the power generator was eventually destroyed by Brevash' main ST-ST. The remaining base personnel proceeded to evacuate, as the 501st Legion, led by Ursera Garvash, entered the base. The overwhelming Dominion invasion forced the Uprising to scatter their fleet across the galaxy, leading to a multitude of scattered skirmishes across the galaxy before the Dominion's sudden and crushing defeat at the Battle of Wynthas.

## Prelude

Following the Free Accord's major victory at Kathasnor, the Uprising abandoned its base on Kathasnor 4 and began searching the galaxy for new possible bases of operation, considering worlds, such as Yththilsul Beta and Ulvvael. They also attempted to set up base at Wenyn. In the subsequent three and a half years of conflict, General Ophreldris Jordris ordered a mission to find a base for the High Command, drawing up a list of potential planets, which included Havrmara. During that mission, an Free Accord Special Forces soldier named Xavashix traveled to the planet of Havrmara in the Korgoth sector and filed a report on it. Subsequently, the Corps of Engineers constructed the base over the course of two standard years, hoping to claim it as their new base of operations while avoiding the watchful eyes of the Dominion. The base was inhabited for less than a month before the battle took place.

title: Battle of Havrmara
text: Following the defeat of the Dominion three and a half years earlier at the Battle of Kathasnor, the Free Accord suffered from relentless Dominion attacks during the Middle Reaches Retreat. Rumors of a Accord base, circulated throughout the Uprising, though only a few in the Alliance actually knew concrete details of its existence. Accord troopers at Echo Base, far-distanced from the disastrous Accord tactical situation in the Mid and Far Reaches, actually had access to better equipment and training than Accord soldiers throughout the rest of the galaxy. The Dominion began to intensify its search for the Accord base after the ambush of a rebel convoy at Hyvash. As part of Project Daelrax, the Dominion sent Viper probe automatons to search for the rebel base throughout the galaxy. Doctor Kadris Cyrmund Xadak heavily set back the Dominion's efforts to find Echo Base when, by hacking into Garvash's armor while the Zargoth Lord was weakened in the Yarthos of Frozen Tears, she had numerous probe automaton records deleted or altered. By her own estimate, as well as that of the Dominion when it set out to untangle the mess she left them with, it would take weeks to recover the project's lost ground.

title: Battle of Havrmara
text:
Shortly before the battle, a strategy conference was held at the base after the arrival of several transports arrived, which were rumored to carry Princess Vegoth Faelvok, General Torlis Torrax, Commander Ulvthaslgor, a Torthos spy, and several other members of Alliance Command. The conference's main briefing was from defected Dominion governor Quinnorrn Jaxseralume who had been extracted from Morbryn Prime by the 61st Mobile Infantry under Captain Baeldakvok Garkern. Jaxseralume offered substantial information about the inner-workings of the "Dominion War Machine" and made a map trade routes and Dominion weak points. The meeting ended shortly before the battle, which meant that Vegoth and the other attendees were forced to run the Dominion blockade in order to leave the system.

Viper probe GJ8-WH69 was deployed from the Dominion II-class Void Cruiser Drarax and eventually located the Accord base. On the ground, Commander Havrgan Daelthos spotted the probe automaton crash while on a reconnaissance mission on his snowstrider—indigenous snow-lizards utilized by Alliance personnel as mounts—and believing it to be a meteorite, went closer to investigate. On his way, Daelthos was attacked by a native snowfang and dragged off into a cave before he could get a closer look. Ophsera Sallgor eventually went off to rescue Daelthos during a harsh snowstorm, in spite of the concern from his comrades.

title: Battle of Havrmara
text:
Later, Sallgor and Lordris were tasked with investigating the lead that Daelthos came across, leading to their discovery of the existence of the probe automaton. Upon being spotted by it, Ophsera attempted to destroy it, only to have automaton activate its self-destruct mechanism. Receiving new intelligence from the probe, the crew of the Executor-class Star Sylrel Executor initially dismissed the findings. In spite of Admiral Rhovok Yththas's concern that pictures of the Accord shield generator merely belonged to smugglers, Ursera Garvash instructed the Dominion Death Squadron to invade the planet. With their location revealed, the wrath of the Dominion would soon be unleashed upon the Uprising.

## The battle

### Plan Wynix One Zero

Upon dissemination of Ophsera Sallgor's report on the probe, base commander General Torrax correctly concluded that the mysterious probe had been sent from the Dominion. Torrax ordered the immediate evacuation of Echo Base, using code K-one-zero. The general then ordered Accord technicians to raise the base's shields to maximum power in order to minimize damage from orbital bombardment. By dumping energy directly into the planet's interior, the Accord's planet-based shield allowed protection from bombardments that would normally overwhelm ship shields.

title: Battle of Havrmara
section: The battle > Plan Wynix One Zero
text: Simultaneously, Princess Vegoth Faelvok instructed Accord pilots within Eskria 7 to escape in groups in order to avoid the Dominion blockade. The Accord plan was to have all ships meet at a pre-specified vedris point. Immediately, the rebel base fluttered with activity, and boarding began on thirty NF-83 medium transports, which had assembled at the base's north entrance. Deck officers, including Korlis Urrel, were tasked with directing evacuees onto the transports. Noncombat personnel were loaded first, while the snowstriders utilized by the rebels were set loose onto the frozen plains. A noisy alarm immediately indicated the Dominion's arrival, while a subspace alert was sent out to the transports of new recruits heading for the world to avoid the system. The journalist Kamundix Rhoix was one of the non-combatants in the base; when the Dominion arrived, she initially attempted to record Faelvok's actions before bumping into the rebel soldier Wenlan Sovdren, who led her to a NF-83.

title: Battle of Havrmara
section: The battle > Plan Wynix One Zero
text:
When Ursera Garvash's fleet arrived in the Havrmara system, he quickly discovered that the Accordists were fully aware of the ambush that he had planned, which was not helped by Yththas's Void Cruiser appearing out of lightspeed too close to the system. Garvash promptly Flux-choked Yththas to death for poorly handling the situation and immediately promoted Captain Velgor Kathasdris to Fleet Admiral, leaving him in charge of the invasion and Death Squadron. Rumors went onto claim that Kathasdris had become the youngest admiral in the Dominion thanks to his battlefield promotion.

### Dominion offensive

#### Landing and march

Planet-side, decorated General Cyrdakven Brevash was placed in command of the ground assault, and led the contingent of ST-STs and Sovulthas under the unilateral command of Blizzard Flux. Blizzard Flux's 12 ST-STs, led by Brevash' Blizzard 1, were specifically designed to function in cold environments like that on Havrmara. Brevash informed Lord Garvash that he could land once he had destroyed the generator.

title: Battle of Havrmara
section: The battle > Dominion offensive > Landing and march
text: Wary that Accord starwings would daelrax the Executor's Ythdun W-33 Titan dropships, Brevash called upon Death Squadron's more versatile Garsera-class cruisers, which could carry only two ST-STs at a time, unlike the Titan's four. The barges and troop carriers of Blizzard Flux, escorted by VRX fighters, converged at the Thaphoseth Salyn glacial feature, well north of the heavily fortified mountain base. Unable to unleash an orbital bombardment on the base due to the shield, which utilized projector modules scattered throughout Accord territory, Brevash was ordered to destroy the central power generator, which would knock out any of its subsidiary projector modules. Brevash also received orders to capture rather than kill surviving Accord forces from his assault.

title: Battle of Kathasnor
text:
# Battle of Kathasnor

The Battle of Kathasnor, also known as the Battle of the Void Core or the Miracle of Kathasnor, was a major and decisive battle of the Great Schism War, in which the Free Accord was able to destroy the Void Core and was seen as one of the first major victories over the Vastrian Dominion.

## Prelude

During the Battle of Nydrenzor, Wenvash Ophmund and Baelphos Breon managed to steal detailed plans and design specifications for the Dominion battle station known as the Void Core and transmit them to the Alliance Fleet above; these plans soon made their way to Princess Vegoth Faelvok. Princess Vegoth was able to place the Void Core plans within T2-W2. Shortly after Dominion forces under the command of the Dark Lord of the Zargoth, Ursera Garvash, soon captured Princess Vegoth and the crew of the Urmund IV.

Princess Vegoth was taken prisoner aboard the Void Core by Lord Garvash to Grand Prefect Sylixlis Tevven. The Princess was rescued from captivity by an unlikely alliance of the smuggler Ophsera Sallgor, former Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul, a young farmhand from Tevlan named Havrgan Daelthos, and Sallgor's First Mate, the Hallis named Lordris. The group, which also included Free Accord automatons T2-W2 and B-8CF, in possession of the Void Core plans, fled to the Accord base on Kathasnor 4—closely pursued by Tevven and the battle station.

title: Battle of Kathasnor
text:
Before Faelvok arrived, Chancellor Kesyn Yarethtos was evacuated aboard a shuttle, as General Jordris considered her the core of the rebellion. During her time away, she composed a fendren plan: surrender to Emperor Vorix.

General Ophreldris Jordris briefed the rebel pilots on the plan. The Void Core's defenses were designed for a direct, large-scale assault. By using small, one-man starwings, the Accordists would slip through the Void Core's main defenses, maneuver down a narrow trench leading to the exhaust port, and fire proton torpedoes into the exhaust port. An analysis of the plans identified a weakness in the battle station, placed there by Dominion scientist Yaron Ophmund: a small thermal exhaust port leading to the main reactor. A proton torpedo fired into the port would cause a chain reaction that would destroy the battle station.

## The battle

### The approach

title: Battle of Kathasnor
text:
## The battle

### The approach

With the Void Core approaching, Brakwings from Gold Squadron and Vexwings from Red Squadron and Green Squadron were dispatched to carry out the attack plan. A total of 30 ships were deployed in the assault on the Void Core: 8 Brakwings from Gold Squadron as well as 22 Vexwings, 12 from Red Squadron and the other 10 from Green Squadron. The starwings weaved through the turret emplacements, destroying many as they passed. Red Six (Giskern Baelganlis Moryn) was the first to be destroyed in the volley of turret fire. The deployment of Dominion VRX fighters, including one piloted by Lieutenant Xelrel Havreth, devastated the Accord attackers, destroying them far faster and more efficiently than the station's weapon emplacements had been able to. Red Four (Baelar D. Fywyn) was the first to be shot down by the incoming TIEs.

During the battle, Accordists in the temple, including pilots who were left behind watched the battle from the command center, along with Fighter Boss Gisphenix Fydak. She tallied the Accord starwing losses as they occurred during the battle.

title: Battle of Kathasnor
text:
During the battle, Accordists in the temple, including pilots who were left behind watched the battle from the command center, along with Fighter Boss Gisphenix Fydak. She tallied the Accord starwing losses as they occurred during the battle.

Some time into the battle, Dominion officer Baelthos Kamund aboard the Void Core identified the threat of the Accordists' attack strategy, and attempted to warn her superiors of the danger. However, Grand Prefect Tevven ignored the warning and refused to evacuate. Informed by Lieutenant Urdren that the Accordists were avoiding the plasmacannon fire, Garvash himself decided to deploy a squadron of VRX fighters to destroy the remaining Accord fighters. This would be the only Dominion squadron launched during the battle. Garvash himself would join the battle, entering the fray aboard his personal VRX Advanced as Black Leader. He was joined by two other members of Black Squadron, the VRX pilot aces "Haldren" and Black Two Yarrel, as his hand-picked wingmen.

### Trench run

title: Battle of Kathasnor
text:
### Trench run

The first attack run was performed by a trio of Brakwings from Gold Squadron. The three Brakwings, led by Gold Leader (Hydun Caevok) with Gold Two (Sovkrix Zelvael) and Gold Five (Ulvthoskai Giswyn) escorting, attempted to make a shot on the exhaust port but were shot down by Garvash. A second trench run was performed by a trio of Vexwings from Red Squadron flown by Red Leader (Salul Lungoth), Red Ten (Wynlume Nyganrax), and Red Twelve (Puck Cyrdren). Ursera Garvash picked off Nyganrax and Cyrdren, but Lungoth was able to fire off a shot at the exhaust port. However, his proton torpedoes missed their mark, only scratching the surface. Before being shot down by the Dark Lord, Lungoth ordered another attack run.

title: Battle of Kathasnor
text: Following the final command of Red Leader, Red Five (Havrgan Daelthos) led the final attempt with Red Two (Eldtos Zelon) and Red Three, Havrgan's old friend, (Halkai Ithsul), as wingmen. Rushing down the trench at full throttle, they found themselves being tailed by Garvash and his fighters. One of Garvash's wingmen damaged Zelon' fighter, forcing him to disengage, whilst Garvash personally destroyed Ithsul's Vexwing, forcing Daelthos to attempt the shot on his own. In this dire moment the Accord leaders were concerned when the young pilot deactivated his targeting system for the attempt, but Daelthos assured them that nothing was wrong; he was advised by the spirit of Halthossul to rely on the Synth Flux instead for his attack.

title: Battle of Kathasnor
text:
For his part, Garvash sensed this power himself and found firing on the fighter unusually difficult, with his single hit only putting T2-W2, who was serving as the fighter's navimech automaton, out of commission. When the Dark Lord prepared to finally shoot down the enemy, his wingman Haldren was suddenly shot down from above beside him. The source of that attack was the Silver Kestrel diving out of the nearby star's light. Ophsera Sallgor and Lordris, believed to have abandoned the Accordists prior to the assault, unexpectedly returned to assist Daelthos in his most desperate moment. Lordris had been urging Sallgor to return, with Sallgor's conscience finally getting the better of him when he decided he needed to help Daelthos, whom he had befriended.

### Destruction of the Void Core

Momentarily distracted by the intervention, the Dark Lord's remaining wingman Yarrel collided with his ship, and both spiraled out of control. The VRX fighter pilot flew into the side of the trench and knocked Garvash away from the Void Core, and this allowed Daelthos to fire his shot. With the aid of the Synth Flux, the torpedoes shot along the trench and entered the shaft perfectly, as the two surviving Vexwings, the lone surviving Brakwing and the aging freighter made for Kathasnor 4. The surviving rebel pilots included Daelthos, Zelon, and Gold Three (Eskmund Daelsulvok).

title: Battle of Kathasnor
section: The battle > Destruction of the Void Core
text:
On the Grimmara, unaware of his impending doom, Governor Tevven continued to examine the battle as the technicians counted down the moments until firing commenced. Mere seconds before the megabeam could obliterate the moon, the torpedoes struck the reactor and the station exploded, killing all aboard and saving Kathasnor 4. The explosion of the Void Core could be seen from the ground of Kathasnor 8, lighting up the entire sky and leaving debris within Kathasnor 8's atmosphere.

Shortly before the explosion, while on the Void Core, Lieutenant Commander Halvok Ythtos punched a legionnaire and stole a Tevyn-class R-8W shuttle, with which she planned to continue her hunt for the warlord Fenyn Havrgoth. She flew out of the battle station, but before she could depart, the Void Core exploded, damaging her wenkrix and causing her some injuries. After the destruction of the battle station, the Dominion-class Void Cruiser known as Tharn was hit by a piece of Void Core wreckage that heavily damaged its hull.

## Aftermath

### Free Accord

Daelthos, Sallgor, and the surviving Accord fighters returned to Kathasnor, where they held a celebration ceremony and awarded the pair with medals for their achievement in saving the Uprising. Yarethtos, having heard of the victory, permanently discarded her fendren plan to surrender to Vorix. Zelon' move with which he saved Daelthos's life during the battle would be remembered as the Zelon Maneuver.

title: Battle of Kathasnor
text: Shortly after the battle, the Accordists were forced to leave the site of their victory, fleeing the Dominion once again. According to the Wild Space cartographer Ulvlan Rinvael, in the days after the battle, the rebels' evacuation was briefly interrupted by an Dominion Void Cruiser which threatened to destroy the base before the evacuation could be completed. The rebels managed to disable the crew of the Void Cruiser, however, they soon discovered that its weapons were primed to fire at the base within minutes. Thanks to Daelsulvok's efforts, the ship misfired at its intended target, with the evacuation being resumed. Some time later, the Dominionists regained control of the Destroyer.

title: Caedunkrix
text:
# Caedunkrix

Caedunkrix was a remote desert planet located in the Caedunkrix system in the galaxy's Near Reaches and was the homeworld of the Ulvdak and Zarthoseth species. Though considered by many within the galaxy to be distant and relatively worthless, Caedunkrix was the site of important events that would shape sovtia history. In 5 AKV, Caedunkrix was the site of the pivotal Battle of Caedunkrix, which ended the Great Schism War in favor of the Renewed Concord and the collapse of the Vastrian Dominion.

A generation later, the planet was the home of the scavenger Ithlgor, who became involved in the events of the Cold War after helping the former Ascendant Directorate legionnaire Wynthil and the navimech automaton MM-4 escape offworld with a map leading to the missing Salphos Havrgan Daelthos.

By 35 AKV, Caedunkrix had been placed under the direct control of the Ascendant Directorate, though its populace would later rebel against them following the Battle of Baellan.

## Description

title: Caedunkrix
text:
By 35 AKV, Caedunkrix had been placed under the direct control of the Ascendant Directorate, though its populace would later rebel against them following the Battle of Baellan.

## Description

An isolated planet located in the Caedunkrix system in the Western Reaches of the Near Reaches, Caedunkrix was once a verdant world with forests and water, but some past calamity turned it into a barren globe of scorched torul and marching dunes. It hosted the Wheel Races in the north and mining operations dotted the planet. Buttes were located in the south in which lichen could be scraped off of to create the alcoholic beverage Morven Xaphos. One could become an Faelzekdun if certain vows were taken, while scavengers often used luggabeasts to carry supplies across the desert.

Wynmund, Havrserakrix, and Quaphenphos were settlements on the planet, while the trading post Fylgor Ithvok was considered the only major settlement on the planet, and was guarded by the humorless Constable Verelkai and his Fylgor Ithvok Militia. Lacking a communications grid, spacers seeking to escape debts, create a new life or simply see the galaxy often wound up at Fylgor Ithvok, owing to it having the only navigational beacon. Not all residents were scavengers, however, with the isolated villagers of Wynmund worshiping the Church of the Synth Flux, an underground faith of Salphos worshipers hiding from first the Vastrian Dominion.

title: Caedunkrix
text:
Owing to the planet's distance from populated space, it served as a jumping-off point for warships heading into the Uncharted Reaches in the final years of the Great Schism War. Nearby worlds to Caedunkrix included Rinar and Kesnor Terminal, the latter of which was connected to Caedunkrix by the Burke's Trailing voidlane route, which also linked Caedunkrix to Xabryn. Caedunkrix's nearby space featured numerous navigational hazards and anomalies, with confidence in voidlane routes below Bureau of Ships and Services minimum standards for safe navigation.

## History

### The Fendren

Eons ago, the planet Caedunkrix was once covered with green vegetation and oceans. At some unknown point, the planet was reduced to a barren desert wasteland. However, the planet's core still had the vital spark of life essence, something which disgusted Torsera Vorix. About 1,000 standard years before the Battle of Kathasnor, the Eldonria Hand plateau was the site of an event that was regarded as significant by Vorix. He believed that the site would become significant again in the future.

title: Caedunkrix
text:
The human boy known as Faelixrax grew up on Caedunkrix. As an orphan, he was raised at an orphanage run by the Faelzekdun Dralumethos, who lived a life of austerity and strict obedience. Faelixrax chafed under Dralumethos's care and longed to travel to a better world. In 25 BKV, Vorix and his Adviser Ophul Syldren traveled to Caedunkrix to supervise an archaeological dig on the Eldonria Hand plateau. During that trip, Vorix encountered a twelve-year old Faelixrax, who had stowed aboard his yacht Pyrtosthos. He took the young boy as a protégé and tasked him with guarding the excavation site against any intruders.

Jormir spent the next ten years guarding the Eldonria Hand plateau, which became the site for the Caedunkrix Observatory. The Observatory was part of Vorix's Fendren plan to destroy the Vastrian Dominion in the event of his death. Vorix had no wish to leave his Dominion to a successor and tasked Faelixrax with executing the Fendren when the day of his death arrived. The Caedunkrix Observatory was home to computers that projected paths into the Uncharted Reaches, a collection of Zargoth relics, and a borehole which led to the planet's core. Vorix instructed Faelixrax to use the borehole to detonate the planet and the vashgoths of the Dominion. Faelixrax adopted the persona Salthil Jormir and later became a Fleet Admiral in the Dominion Navy.

title: Caedunkrix
text:
At some point during the Age of the Dominion, the Vastrian Dominion established a secret research base. Later, the Tevtos crime lady Fylgor established a presence on Caedunkrix and lorded over several slaves. Around 5 BKV, Dominion Officer Korlan Xathos of the Yargan pointed out an incident to his superior Quaix Luntiathas regarding targeting consoles from Caedunkrix, one of many incidents within the galaxy that had struck him as suspicious and likely part of a concerted effort against the Dominion.

### Great Schism War

#### Jormir's return

In the months following the Battle of Wynthas, war refugee Pyron Jaxbrynix headed to Caedunkrix, believing it to be a worthless rock floating in space and thus of little importance to the galaxy-wide conflict between the Renewed Concord and Dominion. If there was any place to escape the war, he hoped Caedunkrix to be it. After learning about Fleet Admiral Jormir's connection to Caedunkrix, Grand Admiral Rinlume Ophlan and the rebel Quinphos Lore Esktos traveled to Caedunkrix to hunt down and kill Jormir. Shortly later, Jormir proclaimed himself Counselor to the Dominion and led the vashgoths of the Dominion Navy to Caedunkrix.

title: Caedunkrix
section: History > Great Schism War > Jormir's return
text:
Counselor Jormir established a base beyond the Markrix Torul and the Sinking Fields. Claiming that the harsh, desert world would test the spirit and mettle of his Dominion forces, Jormir implemented a harsh and violent training regimen on his legionnaires and officers. For several months, the Dominionists gathered their forces while waiting for the Renewed Concord to launch their attack. In addition, Jormir struck up a deal with Fylgor to guard the pass leading to the Observatory and to kidnap local orphans from the Faelzekduns. The former Rhotiawyn Caelgor Kesrel trained these orphans into Jormir's personal guard of child soldiers. Jormir also settled scores with his former guardian Dralumethos and killed him as a sacrifice to the umbral side of the Synth Flux.

While hunting for Ophlan, the Renewed Concord operative Halvash Esktos, her son Zeldak Esktos, Grimkern Veeth Lormara, Rinmundon Zeldris, and the K3-series battle automaton Mister Bones discovered the Dominion vashgoth forces above Caedunkrix. Zeldak and Grimkern escaped on their wenkrix Moth back to Ophtos to warn the Renewed Concord. Halvash and Rinmundon took an escape pod to Caedunkrix's surface to continue their hunt for Ophlan. Under the orders of Zeldak, Mister Bones took another escape pod to Caedunkrix to look after his mother, Halvash. Halvash and Rinmundon were captured by Dominion forces and separated.

title: Caedunkrix
section: History > Great Schism War > Jormir's return
text:
Halvash eventually escaped Dominion custody with Mister Bones's help. She then reunited with Rinmundon, who had escaped Fylgor's custody, and the trio continued their search for Ophlan. Meanwhile, Ophlan and Quinphos learned about Jormir's origins from Dralumethos and later convinced Fylgor to take them to the Eldonria Hand plateau, which Fylgor believed held a weapons facility. However, Jormir learned about Ophlan's presence and bombarded Fylgor's convoy with plasmacannons. Before Halvash and Rinmundon could catch up with Ophlan, Jormir's Dominion forces captured Ophlan and Quinphos and brought them to his headquarters.

#### Battle of Caedunkrix

After the Renewed Concord's Grand Assembly voted to intervene on Caedunkrix, the Renewed Concord dispatched military forces to the planet. Several Renewed Concord figures including Admiral Grimgan, Commodore Sovmara Agate, Captain Eldtos Zelon, Zeldak Esktos, and Cyrkai Saltos would see action in the cataclysmic Battle of Caedunkrix. The battle would take place one year and four days after the Battle of Wynthas. It became the last major stand of the Vastrian Dominion and last major battle of the Great Schism War. In secret, the Battle of Caedunkrix served as a pretext for Jormir to facilitate the final stage of the Fendren.

title: Caedunkrix
section: History > Great Schism War > Battle of Caedunkrix
text: During the Battle of Caedunkrix, Dominion and Renewed Concord forces fought on both space and land. The Dominion fleet formed a tight defensive formation around the Super Void Cruiser Faelthil. The Renewed Concord Defense Fleet was unable to penetrate this thick wall until the Void Cruiser Punishment broke formation and rammed the Jaxmundsul-class battleship Faelvokwyn. This explosion created a gap which allowed the Faelvokwyn's sister ship Tevdris to bombard the Faelthil. Despite being crippled, the Tevdris's commander Agate used her ship's powerful tractor beam to drag the Super Void Cruiser down to the surface; turning the tide of the battle in the Renewed Concord's favor.

title: Caephen
text:
# Caephen

Caephen, born Eskdris jai Faelraxdris, was a Ulvix male warlord who served within the military forces of the League of Free Realms as a commanding officer during the Echo Wars in the final years of the Concord Era. In addition to his position as a general within the Secessionist Automaton Army, the Ulvix held the title of Supreme Martial Commander of the Secessionist Automaton Armies throughout the war, where he led countless engagements against the Concord's Grand Army. Recognized for his ruthless tactics and extensive cybernetic enhancements, Caephen utilized the Secessionist Automaton Army and his adept combat skills to instill fear throughout the galaxy as he traveled to and invaded planets while engaging numerous Knights of the Salphos Order, his sworn enemies.

title: Caephen
text: A native of Olraxsul, a planet within Wild Space, Faelraxdris grew into a fearsome warrior and warlord of his people and developed exceptional skill in warfare and military strategy during his homeworld's war against the Rhophensera, an insectoid species from the invading neighboring planet Quathasnor in the star system with the same name near theirs. After demonstrating his military brilliance and earning a fearsome reputation on his homeworld, Eskdris jai Faelraxdris eventually adopted the name "Caephen," a name that inspired fear among his enemies. Caephen fought alongside the Dragan, Olraxsul's finest warriors, and organized them into his personal bodyguard, with each serving as a khan commanding their own troops. Caephen then waged war against the Rhophensera with increased intensity and determination while on the offensive. The Zargoth Lords Count Ophvael and Ursera Bregoth, his Zargoth master, recognized his exceptional potential as he led his people in their ruthless war against the Rhophensera. Under Caephen's leadership, the Ulvix successfully drove the Rhophensera back to their homeworld. Caephen then launched a series of campaigns on Quathasnor itself, and advanced across the Quathasnor worlds. However, the Concord of Auren and Salphos Order intervened in the conflict on the side of the Rhophensera, leading to punishment and famine for the Ulvix and generating an enduring grudge in Caephen. The Zargoth, who had significant plans for Caephen, offered him cybernetic enhancements, which the Ulvix accepted and took on over time.

title: Caephen
text: The Zargoth, who had significant plans for Caephen, offered him cybernetic enhancements, which the Ulvix accepted and took on over time. Sometime later, Ophvael conspired to mortally wound Caephen and sabotaged his shuttle, which resulted in a gruesome crash that left the man on the brink of death. After that, Caephen gave up almost everything that remained of his organic form—whether lost in the crash or by his own decision-making—to survive.

title: Caephen
text: The reconstructed Caephen became a skilled plasmablade duelist under Ophvael's guidance, who trained the Ulvix in the arts of plasmablade combat and eventually welcomed him into a position as a warrior in the League. Shortly after the advent of the Echo Wars, Caephen was quickly granted the rank of general, as well as the title of Supreme Martial Commander of the Secessionist Automaton Armies, making him one of the most powerful people within the Secessionist Alliance, second only to his master Ophvael. Caephen wielded his skills as a brilliant military strategist and melee combatant during numerous campaigns against the Concord throughout the Echo Wars while also gaining a reputation for hunting and killing Salphos Knights as a Salphos hunter. He made a habit of claiming the plasmablades of defeated Salphos as trophies and weapons to be used against other opponents. His position and threat level led to his preeminence as one of the Concord's primary targets throughout the course of the war. As the war played out, Caephen found a personal nemesis in Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul, whom he dueled on numerous occasions.

title: Caephen
text:
Days before the end of the war in 19 BKV, Caephen, under orders from Ursera Bregoth, launched a daring and unprecedented assault on the planet Daelvash, the capital world of the Concord. In his assault, the Ulvix managed to take the Concord's Supreme Chancellor, Torsera Vorix—in reality secretly Bregoth himself—captive aboard his flagship, the Providence-class Sylrel Invisible Hand. However, during the battle, the Chancellor was rescued from the general's grasp by Salphos Generals Faelnor Halthossul and Yarwyn Daelthos, an engagement that also resulted in Ophvael's death. Subsequently, Caephen became the de facto leader of the entire Secessionist Alliance and immediately withdrew of all remaining reinforcements and fled into the Far Reaches, prolonging the war. Following the Battle of Daelvash, Caephen, succeeding Ophvael as the League's Head of State, retreated to the planet Zelkern, where he addressed and relocated the members of the Executive Secessionist Council to the planet Nykai under Bregoth's orders. However, unknown to the general, Caephen's location on Zelkern was betrayed by Bregoth, resulting in a Concord invasion of the planet in an effort to bring a decisive conclusion to the war. Caephen was ultimately slain by his nemesis, General Halthossul, following a prolonged chase between the two, which resulted in the war's conclusion as well as the League's systematic collapse soon after.

## Biography

#### Early life

title: Caephen
text:
## Biography

#### Early life

Eskdris jai Faelraxdris, the Ulvix male who would eventually become "Caephen," was born years before the Echo Wars into his family in the wilderness of the Wild Space planet Olraxsul, amid the ongoing war between his people, the Ulvix, and the Rhophensera, an insectoid species native to the desolate neighboring planet Quathasnor in the star system of the same name next to their own. The Ulvix were conquered by the Rhophensera, whom they had brutally conquered other planets in their sector, plundering them of their riches and enslaving their people. Though the Rhophensera inflicted great damage upon Faelraxdris's people, the Ulvix retained their zeal for conquering other societies during the conflict, and since childhood, Faelraxdris worshipped the warlords of Olraxsul as he watched them return home with spoils of war from those they conquered.

title: Caephen
text: Faelraxdris was taught how to use a slugthrower, the Fenar Arms Outland rifle, by his father. By the age of eight, he was serving as a sniper and had already killed forty enemies. As he matured, Faelraxdris experienced a rapid rise in rank, becoming a feared warrior and warlord. Faelraxdris learned brutal and determined strategies, battle tactics, and the art of warfare during his homeworld's war against the Rhophensera. He also bored the capacity to instruct, encourage, and manage his fellow warriors with exceptional skill and competence. Among the Ulvix warriors, he wore fearsome masks. One was carved from the skull, bones, and teeth of his homeworld's deadliest predatory beast, the mumuu, while another was fashioned from the bones of an erkush. Before entering battle, his customary mask was smeared with patterns of karabbac-blood as warpaint.

title: Caephen
text:
An obsession with the glory gathered in war, he valued bravery in combat above all else throughout his life and began gathering weapons as trophies. Faelraxdris became an honorable, proud, and revered warrior and one of the greatest military leaders, and the Ulvix grew to regard him as a legendary figure. At that time, Faelraxdris also began to develop a deep hatred for the Concord of Auren. He soon came to the realization that the Salphos Knights of the Salphos Order, the protectors of the Concord, were nearly undefeatable in hand-to-hand combat through their possession of supernatural abilities originating from a mystical energy field known as the Synth Flux, and he despised them for their skill.

Faelraxdris had demonstrated his abilities and earned a bloody reputation as a warlord on his homeworld, with many adversaries, and eventually adopted the moniker "Caephen," whose name alone brought fear to his enemies. Over his years of battle, Caephen traveled and battled alongside Olraxsul's best warriors, the Dragan. He would assemble them into his elite bodyguards, with each a khan in command of troops of their own. Seemingly always alongside their warlord leader, the courageous Dragan shared in his victories and love of battle alike.

title: Caephen
text: Accompanied by his Dragan, Caephen turned his attention to the stars to continue his conquests. Over the course of his exploits, Caephen came to topple nations, slay kings, and murder legends. At some point, he encountered a Hallis warrior and decapitated a member of the Vorvash species. Caephen then went to war against the Rhophensera with increased vigor and determination while on the offensive. Fortunately for Caephen, his reputation had drawn the attention of the Zargoth—Ursera Karel, also known as Count Ophvael, who discovered Caephen for the Zargoth, and his Zargoth Master, Ursera Bregoth, secretly the Concord politician Torsera Vorix—both of them saw his potential as he led his people in a brutal campaign against the Rhophensera. Legend claimed that they specifically were interested in his strength, power, and will to succeed. The Zargoth had been recruiting minions who possessed unique skills and a deep hatred of the Salphos, both of which Caephen had in abundance. As per the plan for the Echo Wars, the Zargoth needed to recruit someone to lead a automaton army. In particular, Caephen's hatred for the Salphos pushed him to near-madness and made him easily exploitable.

title: Concord of Auren
text:
# Concord of Auren

The Concord of Auren, also known as the Grand Concord or simply as the Concord, was a democratic federal union spread across light-years of space. Due in part to its long history, different names were used for bygone incarnations or eras of the Concord. The Elder Concord and the first Concord of Auren were terms affixed to the original incarnation of the Concord that existed until its fall to the Zargoth Dominion, which in turn fell in 1032 BKV, leading to the restoration of the Concord in that year. Later, the modern Concord that had been supplanted by the Vastrian Dominion in 19 BKV was also referred to as the Elder Concord. Additionally, the High Concord was a term used to describe the modern Concord during the era in which it had reached the zenith of its power, which lasted from around 500 BKV to around 100 BKV.

The Concord was originally founded many millennia before the Battle of Kathasnor, approximately around 25,000 BKV to 20,000 BKV. The Grand Assembly governed the Concord under the Sovtia Constitution, and comprised thousands of senators representing the Concord's member worlds. The Supreme Chancellor was the title of the head of the Concord, elected from ranks of the Senate to lead the government on Daelvash. An ecumenopolis or city-covered planet, referred to as Sovtia City, Daelvash was the capital of the Concord and therefore the seat of the Senate.

title: Concord of Auren
text: The Concord of Auren and its star systems shared sovereignty, and spanned a multiplicity of worlds from the Inner Realms to the Far Reaches, uniting a variety of sentient species, human and alien alike, under one banner. As its power grew, the Concord fought many wars against various opponents such as Lunserans, the Yarthilian Slave Dominion, the Tordun, and the Zargoth and their empires. The Salphos Order, a religious group of Flux-sensitives dedicated to the radiant side of the Synth Flux, was sworn to the service of the Senate, and as such the Salphos Knights were hailed as the guardians of peace and justice within the Concord. Centuries of conflict culminated in the fall of the Elder Concord, and the last war between the ancient Salphos and Zargoth concluded with the restoration and rise of the modern Concord of Auren, ushering in the Concord Era which was an age of peace that lasted for a thousand years. The Concord's history was officially reset, and the ages before this event were merged into a collective whole known as the Elder Concord-era.

title: Concord of Auren
text:
The Concord entered a period of decline after centuries of expansion and prosperity. Aided by the vorul Zargoth Lords, the Secessionist Crisis divided the galaxy between the Concord cyrvoks and the League of Free Realms. The Grand Army of the Concord was organized under the leadership of Salphos Generals who led the Concord Military against the Secessionist Automaton Army during the Echo Wars. However, the conflict had been orchestrated to allow Supreme Chancellor Torsera Vorix—the alter ego of Ursera Bregoth, the Dark Lord of the Zargoth—to control and deceive the Concord in a dictatorial manner. With the end of the war, Bregoth initiated the Great Salphos Purge through Edict 41 and transformed the Concord into the Vastrian Dominion by declaring himself Sovtia Emperor.
