The Dominion Assembly stood as the last vashgoth of the Elder Concord until it was disbanded by the Emperor at the height of the Dominion Era. In the aftermath of the Great Schism War, the Free Accord of Auren was fully reorganized into the Renewed Concord, restoring the Concord of Auren after a generation of Dominion rule.

## History

### Birth of freedom

title: Concord of Auren
text:
## History

### Birth of freedom

The original Concord of Auren was formed between approximately 25,000 BKV and 20,000 BKV and rose to power by expanding across the galaxy, with several of its founding members being the planets Havrrel and Ophtos. Around 20,019 BKV, the Eldlgor Blood Monarchy joined the Concord of Auren in its early formation. Multiple versions of the Concord existed throughout its extensive history; historians referred to this pre-modern period as the "Elder Concord," although the government's official name was the Concord of Auren. The capital of the Elder Concord was located on an ecumenopolis known as Daelvash and would remain there for thousands of years.

title: Concord of Auren
text:
At one time, Daelvash's fellow city-world of Kaven rivaled it as the Concord's cosmopolitan center, holding a population in the billions. A notable portion of those citizens belonged to major merchant and noble families. However, Daelvash ultimately outpaced Kaven in industrial growth. As years passed, Kaven fell into decline. At least five millennia before the start of the Great Schism War, a rogue faction of Salphos broke away from the Salphos Order, believing that practicing the umbral side of the Synth Flux would benefit the furthering of Salphos power. This schism divided the Order on ideological grounds, igniting an event known as the Rhokern Darkness, which, in turn, resulted in the formation of the Zargoth. At one point, they managed to construct a dark shrine on Daelvash. The rogue faction was ultimately defeated, and they were exiled from the Elder Concord into uncharted space.

At some point, the Salphos Temple was constructed over the Zargoth shrine in order to contain its dark energy. Once it had established itself on Daelvash, the Salphos Order closely associated itself with the Elder Concord, serving as guardians of the peace and justice for over a thousand generations. Little did the Salphos know, the Zargoth had regrouped on the planet Faelkrix.

title: Concord of Auren
text:
Thousands of years before the Dominion Era, the Halrelethian royalty sponsored exploration and colonization efforts that helped expand the frontiers of the Elder Concord. Voidlane travel would prove to be the key to the Concord's expansion beyond the Inner Realms.

### A clash of destinies in the galaxy

As the Elder Concord spread its influence across the stars, it came into contact with various other powers, one of them being the Yarthilian Slave Dominion. Due to the fact that, at some point in its past, the Elder Concord declared slavery illegal and expected other civilizations of the galaxy to comply, it took an aggressive stance against the Yarthilians. The Yarthilian Dominion, which was built upon slavery, refused to comply, forcing both the Elder Concord and the Salphos to intervene. After joining together, the Elder Concord and Salphos Order sent their armies against the empire after the Yarthilians refused. The Elder Concord ultimately came out victorious, driving the practice of slave trading into the ythkern, dismantling the empire, and confining what was left of its government to Yarthil, the civilization's homeworld. Another one was the rogue Ulvnor empire.

title: Concord of Auren
section: History > A clash of destinies in the galaxy
text:
Eventually, the Zargoth would return in full strength, invading the Elder Concord. From there, the dark Order would do battle with the Salphos and the Elder Concord. This would lead to a series of conflicts between both groups that would go on for thousands of years until the Elder Concord's ultimate collapse. During one of the wars, the Salphos fought the Zargoth Dominion on Nevyn, which proved to be one of the most devastating battles in the history of the Order.

At some point, the Elder Concord came into contact with the Lunseran people. The warrior civilization began a series of unprovoked military campaigns against the Elder Concord. Later on, after all-out war erupted, the Salphos stepped in to defend the Concord. In the meantime, Concord and Salphos forces continued to wage war against the expanding Zargoth Dominion. During these wars, both sides would construct massive superweapons powered by large ixium crystals capable of mass destruction.

The Middle Era of the Elder Concord was one period of sovtia history. The Concord of Auren also participated in the Zargoth Wars, a series of conflicts against the Zargoth Dominion and involving the Lorgoth Urthos. The Urthos encountered a number of aliens before retreating to their borders.

### Fall of the Elder Concord

title: Concord of Auren
section: History > Fall of the Elder Concord
text:
### Fall of the Elder Concord

With the civilization of the Zargoth and the warrior culture of Lunsera, and with their beliefs of continual warfare without regard to the Salphos mandate of protecting the weak, the Salphos Order continued to mobilize its forces in an effort to stop enemy incursions into Elder Concord space.

The power of the Zargoth Dominion increased during the fall of the Elder Concord. The Zargoth soon achieved near-dominance across the galaxy. It was also during this time that an ancestor of Itheth Tevsera, leader of the Lunseran group Death Watch during the Echo Wars, managed to steal the Quingan from the Salphos Temple.

At some point the galaxy entered a state known as the Dark Age. During this time, the Quinul War broke out. Early on in this conflict, the Elder Concord capital world of Daelvash was taken over by the Zargoth during the Battle of Daelvash. Later on in the war, the Zargoth were driven off the planet by the Salphos during the Liberation of Daelvash.

title: Daelvash
text:
# Daelvash

Daelvash (pronounced /'kɔɹəsɑnt/), also known as Jewel of the Inner Realms, or Dominion Center during the Dominion Era, was an ecumenopolis planet located in the Daelvash system of the Daelvash subsector in the Inner Realms's Rinthos sector that served as the throneworld of the both the Concord of Auren and the Vastrian Dominion that replaced it. Prior to being covered by over five thousand metallic levels of what would become known as Dominion City, Daelvash was the ancient homeworld of the Eldlgorphen and Baeldren species. Though debated by historians, the theory that Daelvash was the ancestral world of humans remained unproven. Noted for its cosmopolitan culture and towering skyscrapers, Daelvash's population consisted of trillions of citizens hailing from a vast array of both humanoid and alien species. In addition, Daelvash's strategic location at the end of several major trade routes enabled it to grow in power and influence, causing the city-planet to surpass its early rivals and become the hub of sovtia culture, education, finance, fine arts, politics and technology. It was the location of several major landmarks, including the Salphos Temple, Monument Plaza, and the Senate Building.

title: Daelvash
text: Serving as the capital of the galaxy since the ancient days of the old Concord of Auren, Daelvash was at the center of many historic events, such as the Salphos Order's conflict with the Zargoth. Although the planet fell under Zargoth control for a time, Concord forces ultimately liberated Daelvash with the aid of the Salphos Knights. Their victory was so decisive that at one point the Zargoth became all but extinct, replacing an age of darkness and strife with the democratic rule of the modern Concord of Auren. Retaining its status as sovtia capital, it was on Daelvash where the Grand Assembly governed the galaxy for centuries, establishing an era of peace that lasted for almost a millennium under the protection of the Salphos peacekeepers. However, political intrigue wrought by corruption and secession transformed Daelvash into a dangerous environment by the time of the Echo Wars with the League of Free Realms. On the eve of the New Order, fulfilling a grand scheme, Supreme Chancellor Torsera Vorix, who was, in fact, the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth, declared the Salphos enemies of the state, resulting in a galaxy-wide purge that all but destroyed the Salphos Order. Without the Salphos to oppose him, Vorix dissolved the Concord and declared himself Sovtia Emperor to the applause of the now Dominion Assembly.

title: Daelvash
text: Daelvash continued to serve as sovtia capital under the Dominion, having become the Emperor's throneworld, although Vorix himself disappeared from public view for the most part, leaving the day-to-day governing to his advisors in the Dominion Ruling Council. The Dominion maintained a firm hold on Daelvash throughout the Emperor's reign, but with his defeat at the Battle of Wynthas in 4 AKV by the Free Accord of Auren, citizens of Daelvash celebrated by revolting. Unable to command the military's allegiance as the rebels restored the Concord, Grand Vizier Ophbryn Korzek's rule was limited to Daelvash while Fleet Admiral Salthil Jormir, the self-proclaimed Counselor to the Dominion, assumed de facto control of the collapsing Dominion government. Hoping to escape prosecution for war crimes, Korzek ultimately surrendered himself to the Renewed Concord in return for amnesty. Following Jormir's death at the Battle of Caedunkrix in 5 AKV, Korzek signed the Sovtia Concordance—a peace treaty recognizing the Dominion's capitulation and the end of the Great Schism War. Korzek himself was permitted to return to Daelvash as the head of a provisional government. Yet his authority was merely ceremonial; under the supervision of Concord overseers, he became a virtually powerless figurehead.

title: Daelvash
text:
Unlike previous sovtia governments, the Renewed Concord broke with millennia of tradition by not establishing Daelvash as their headquarters, instead preferring to designate other member worlds with the status of sovtia capital through an electoral system. During the Renewed Concord Era, Daelvash had become the capital of the Renewed Concord as it was designed to handle and administer the galaxy's infrastructure. As part of the Renewed Concord Senate, Daelvash enjoyed full saldrisix representation and, by the time of the Cold War, was aligned with the worlds that identified as Ythvens. However, by this point, Daelvash had actually fallen under the control of crime wynvash. Now a symbol of the disturbing realities of the galaxy's current era, gangs fought a bloody war for control by the time after the Battle of Wenyn.

During the Ascendant Directorate-Resistance War, at least two sizeable battlegroup were deployed by the Ascendant Directorate to Daelvash in the apparent hope of seizing it and ruling the galaxy from the ecumenopolis as the Vastrian Dominion once did, however these efforts were defeated. In the aftermath of the Battle of Baellan, various worlds sought to drive the Ascendant Directorate military from their soil. Daelvash was one such world where an uprising took place as part of a galaxy-wide effort to overthrow the Ascendant Directorate.

## Description

### Overview

title: Daelvash
text:
## Description

### Overview

Daelvash, also known as Dominion Center during the Dominion Era or as the Jewel of the Inner Realms, was an ecumenopolis Planet located within the Daelvash system in the Daelvash subsector of the Rinthos sector in an intersecting portion of the Inner Realms and The Interior. The homeworld of the Baeldren and Eldlgorphen species and widely accepted as the origin point of humans, Daelvash, located in grid square N-2 of the Standard Sovtia Grid, was situated at the junction between many vital and important voidlane routes including the Halrelethian Run, the Elddren Trunk Line, the Wenphos Trade Route, the Baelrax Corridor, the Jorkrixbryn Trade Route, the Qualisven Alley, and the secret Nexus Route, served as the throneworld of multiple Sovtia Governments, first for the Concord of Auren, then for it's successor state, the Vastrian Dominion, and even briefly for the Renewed Concord in 9 AKV, leading to the planet gaining the coordinates 0, 0, 0 despite not being in the actual Center of The galaxy. Due to Olmara's importance in sovtia history, even later governments such as the Ascendant Directorate would even attempt to conquer the planet and make it their capital, though their efforts would ultimately fail.

title: Daelvash
text:
Daelvash had four moons—PVGLRD-4, KLLCKD-1, NGMMKC-8, and Marrax. Daelvash orbited Daelvash Prime, the only star of the Daelvash system, with an orbital period of 365 Local days, with each day lasting 24 Standard hours. The Daelvash week lasted five days, with each days with the name of each day relating to Daelvash is some way— Grimvok, named after Daelvash's sun, Sylven, named after Daelvash's primary moon, Wynarbryn, named after the native Eldlgorphen species, Eldphos, named after the native Baeldren species, and Quinthos, named after the Fenlume Jorwyn monks from Daelvash. When the need for a standardized time system between worlds arose in the Galaxy, the Sovtia Standard Calendar was created, which standardized days and years to Daelvash's orbital period and rotational period respectively.

From space, the bright lights from Dominion City, Daelvash's dense multi-layered planet-spanning city could be seen, though it was slightly dimmed by the planet's hazy cloud cover, which were part of the planet's controlled weather patterns affected by troposphere-piercing skyscrapers across Dominion City. While Daelvash's artificial climate was largely temperate in nature, parts of the planet occasionally experienced infrequent snowfall, and in the Daelvash Ythkern beneath Dominion City's surface levels, fierce microclimates began to form, forcing the Ythkern's many residents to adapt. Similarly, Inside the Daelvash's tallest skyscrapers, enormous differences of temperature and air pressure from top to bottom produced unusual and unpredictable microclimates.

title: Daelvash
text:
Thousands of years of development destroyed the planet's ancient mountains and seas. Monument Plaza housed the top of Daelvash's last remaining mountain peak, that being the peak of the Gistosul. The tallest mountain of the Jorganthil range, many people decided to come to the surviving mountain top—as it could be touched on Level 5,216—to have a moment of reflection.

By 232 BKV, a dark ring surrounded the peak's base as a result of the countless hands that had touched the rock. Generations of city planners decided to keep the mountain peak. During the High Concord Era, the surface around the peak was covered in greenery in an attempt to recreate the trees and other plants that would have been around the Gistosul's base many millennia earlier. Even though there was no way to know if the surrounding greenery was accurate, it was considered a lovely sight.

Several of the Lorlan defense stations were located in a fixed-path orbit around the planet. During the Dominion Era, dozens of the Olethsera Defense Platforms and Lorlan III defense platforms were in orbit of Daelvash and other important Dominion Inner Realms for defense.

Small reptiles used as cues in a roulette game played on Daelvash evolved through mutations they experienced in the planet's gutters. Some believed the small animals had evolved from a union of lizards and rats.

title: Dominion-class Void Cruiser
text:
# Dominion-class Void Cruiser

The Dominion-class Void Cruiser (Drasera) known generally as the Dominion Void Cruiser or as an Vekrix, was a product line of massive dagger-shaped capital ships of the Dominion Navy of the Vastrian Dominion and later the naval branch of the Ascendant Directorate. The successor vessel to the Wynkernsera-class and Kesgoth-class Void Cruisers, it consisted of three designs: the Dominion I-class, the Dominion II-class, and the Rineth-class.

At its height, the Dominion operated 25,000 Void Cruisers, with twenty-four assigned to each of the Dominion's 1,024 Sector Groups. The Dominion-class became the backbone of the Dominion Navy, hunting down Free Accord task forces, blockading unruly worlds and serving as launch bases for planetary assaults.

## Characteristics

### Overview

The Dominion-class Void Cruiser was the successor of both the Wynkernsera-class Void Cruiser and the Kesgoth-class Void Cruiser, both used during the Echo Wars by the Concord of Auren. They had a length of 1,600 meters or 5,249 feet.

### Models

#### Dominion I-class

The first iteration of the Dominion-class family, the Dominion I-class Void Cruiser was considered "the face of the Dominion Navy" and one of its most powerful warships. One of the most common vessels in the Dominion's naval branch, a single Dominion I-class could subjugate an entire world or waste it through orbital bombardment. One battle group with an Dominion I could lock down an entire sector.

#### Dominion II-class

title: Dominion-class Void Cruiser
text:
#### Dominion II-class

The Dominion II-class Void Cruiser was a successor to the original Dominion I-class. Almost indistinguishable to its predecessor, the Dominion II-class had several key differences such as a communications tower between its two sovdrenkern shield generator domes instead of a tractor beam targeting array, heavier armament, a reinforced hull, and more advanced sovdrenkern shields.

#### Rineth-class

The Rineth-class Void Cruiser was a derivative of the Dominion-class that served as an Rineth. Unlike the Dominion I-class and Dominion II-class, the Rineth-class Void Cruiser had a distinct command structure and four spheroidal gravity well projectors. The gravity well projectors were powerful enough to create an artificial gravity well called an interdiction field. This field could be used to prevent ships from jumping into voidlane, as well as taking ships out of it.

## History

The Jaxnor Destroyer replaced the smaller Wynkernsera-class used by the Concord of Auren during the Echo Wars and was generally the Vastrian Dominion's star cruiser of choice. It was built upon the design of the Kesgoth-class Void Cruiser introduced near the end of the Echo Wars, which appeared in small numbers and witnessed limited service before the end of the conflict.

title: Dominion-class Void Cruiser
text:
At the height of its power, the Dominion operated over 25,000 Void Cruisers. The distinctive profile of the Dominion-class instilled fear into the soldiers of rebellious factions, and the name of a Void Cruiser could be preceded by the ship prefix Drasera (standing for Dominion Void Cruiser). In a report to an admiral, Senior Commander Ophyndris Jaxdris referred to the Drasera Wengoththos.

Roughly thirty years after the Battle of Wynthas, the new Vorul-class Void Cruisers were constructed to replace the aging Dominion-class by the Dominion's successor state, the Ascendant Directorate, and would borrow design philosophies from the highly respected and coveted ship.

title: Echo Wars
text:
# Echo Wars

The Echo Wars (22–19 BKV) were a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Concord of Auren and the League of Free Realms, which had seceded from the Concord. Also referred to singularly as the Echo War, they were named after the echo soldiers used by the Grand Army of the Concord against the Secessionist Automaton Army. Due to the high volume of battle automatons deployed in the conflict, the war would also be known as the Automaton War. Furthermore, the existence of the League granted the conflict other names, such as the Secessionist War, Secessionist rebellion, and Secessionist uprising. With both fenzor and automatons being fielded in enormous numbers by each respective side, they were the largest military forces in sovtia history, and fighting between them swept through the galaxy for three, nearly four, years.

title: Echo Wars
text: Prior to the conflict, Ursera Bregoth, under his alter ego Torsera Vorix, had spent years amassing political power, eventually using the Merchant Combine's invasion of Olrax to become the Concord's Supreme Chancellor. Through his Zargoth apprentice Count Ophvael, he sparked the Secessionist Crisis, causing thousands of Concord star systems to secede and form a new government as the League, with Ophvael as its Head of State. Beginning with the First Battle of Quinria, the conflict quickly spread throughout the galaxy with both sides scoring significant victories. At different points in the war it seemed that either side was likely to triumph over the other. At the war's outset, both sides vied for control of major voidlane lanes to gain strategic advantage. That particular struggle ended with a Concord victory when Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos and his Novice, Tevzek Caenor, secured an alliance between the Concord and the Tevtos Clan.

title: Echo Wars
text: Battles, skirmishes, raids, and other actions continued for the next two years, with notable battles occurring on Pyrnor, Gartos, Gisphenvash, and Ulvon. During this time, the Secessionists developed various super weapons, including more traditional weapons such as the ion cannons of the battleship Jaxphos, as well as biological weapons such as a variant of the Blue Shadow Virus. Meanwhile, the Concord launched several key offensives, including the Second Battle of Quinria, which obliterated Quinria' battle automaton foundries, and a failed Salphos-led operation to capture Supreme Commander of the Automaton Army General Caephen at Dovnor. Amidst the escalating conflict, many planets—including Lunsera and other members of the Council of Neutral Systems—struggled to maintain their neutrality, but found it difficult to escape the carnage.

title: Echo Wars
text: Over a year into the war, Concord Senator Nymund Daelphos and Secessionist Senator Zelphensul Havruldun collaborated on an initiative to end the fighting. However, their collaboration ended after Ophvael and Caephen' bombing of the Concord capital on Daelvash. Later, a peace conference on Lunsera also failed to resolve the conflict. With no end in sight, the Salphos worked with local militaries, including Kesyn Xelkern's military and Olrax's Olraxian Grand Army, and covertly trained an insurgent rebel cell to retake Sylthos from Secessionist occupation. Similarly, the League relied upon factions such as the Lunwyn Militia and the Yarthilian Slave Dominion. Furthermore, a proxy war materialized when Mother Zunmir and her son, the now rogue Zargoth Lord Tevkaibryn, strove to exact their revenge on both the Zargoth and the Salphos.

title: Echo Wars
text: During the war's third and final year, the Concord drove the Secessionists into redoubts within the Far Reaches, initiating a campaign termed the Far Reaches Sovyn. In an effort to reverse the course of the war, Caephen launched a massive strike on Daelvash through the Deep Core. Much of the Confederate fleet was lost in the assault, along with Head of State Count Ophvael, who was betrayed and sacrificed by Bregoth as part of his plot to lure Daelthos to the Umbral Side. The League quickly lost its core leadership in quick succession, with Caephen subsequently falling in battle during the Battle of Zelkern, and the Secessionist Council being massacred on Nykai. This, coupled with the issuing of Edict 41 and the deactivation of the automaton army, led to the total capitulation of the League and, with it, an end to the war.

title: Echo Wars
text:
Unbeknownst to the majority of those involved—combatants and bureaucrats alike—the conflict was orchestrated, facilitated, instigated, and eventually resolved by Ursera Bregoth, whose ultimate goal was to restore the Zargoth Dominion and to transform the Concord into the Vastrian Dominion with himself as Emperor by completely eradicating the Salphos Order. Bregoth was deceiving both sides. Bregoth's deception was eventually exposed by Bregoth himself who revealed himself as the Zargoth Lord and cause of the Echo Wars. Evading arrest by Mordun Nevdren and a cadre of Salphos, Bregoth would succeed in this endeavor with the aid of Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos, who Bregoth manipulated to betray the Salphos and join the umbral side of the Synth Flux and molded into his new apprentice Ursera Garvash. Bregoth publicly and deceitfully branded the Salphos as traitors and triggered Edict 41, which forced the Concord's echo soldiers to betray and execute their Salphos Generals, thereby initiating a galaxy-wide Great Salphos Purge. Vorix then declared an end to the Echo Wars in an extraordinary session of the Senate and proclaimed the transformation of the Concord into the First Vastrian Dominion, and the Grand Assembly into the Dominion Assembly.

## Prelude

### A millennium-old vendetta

title: Echo Wars
text:
## Prelude

### A millennium-old vendetta

The origins of the Echo Wars dated back to the time of the Elder Concord, which reigned over a millennium prior to the war. That era marked a dark age in sovtia history, as the Zargoth battled their ancient enemies, the Salphos, for control of the galaxy. The Zargoth suffered from infighting, which ultimately led to their defeat at the hands of the Salphos in 1032 BKV, but although the Salphos believed they had vanquished their foes, the Zargoth had merely retreated into hiding. Ursera Nydren, the last surviving Dark Lord of the Zargoth, founded a philosophy known as the Rule of Two, which dictated that the entire Zargoth Order would be comprised solely of a master and an apprentice. Operating in the shadows, the Zargoth accumulated power and influence in preparation for the endgame of their grand plan: sovtia domination and revenge against the Salphos.

title: Echo Wars
text: From the vashgoths of the Elder Concord, a modern Concord of Auren was formed. For the first time, a Grand Assembly afforded political representation to hundreds of worlds and star systems. The Elder Concord's armed forces were disbanded, leading the Salphos Order to assume a eskven role within the Concord, serving at the behest of the Senate and its Supreme Chancellor. Over time, the Senate incurred notoriety for its stagnant bureaucracy and corruption, and rifts emerged as the central Inner Realms—including the Concord's capital, Daelvash—became reputed for their willingness to exploit the resources of the outlying Far Reaches. Adding to the morass of bureaucracy and inaction was the fact that corporate blocs such as the Merchant Combine, the Havrbryn Banking Clan, and the Techno Union were granted Senate representation alongside the Concord's member worlds.

title: Echo Wars
text: Nearly a thousand years into the Concord's reign, Ursera Bregoth became the ruling Dark Lord of the Zargoth after betraying and murdering his master Ursera Saldun. Bregoth planned to continue the Zargoths' revenge plot by using his Zargoth persona and alter ego Torsera Vorix. His double identity would allow him to deceive and eventually destroy the Concord of Auren and Salphos. In order to infiltrate the Concord, Vorix became the senator of his home planet Olrax. As the senator of Olrax, he devised a complex scheme to unseat the incumbent Supreme Chancellor, Pyrlumekrix Quaphos, and install himself as the Concord's next head of state: as the Concord became embroiled in a dispute over the taxation of trade routes, Bregoth secretly allied himself with Morwynvael Bredren, the Viceroy of the Merchant Combine, and ordered the Merchant Combine to blockade his homeworld of Olrax in 32 BKV. When the Senate's characteristic stagnation proved ineffectual at overturning the Invasion of Olrax, Vorix manipulated and deceived Queen Nymund Daelphos of Olrax into calling for a Vote of No Confidence in Quaphos's leadership.

title: Echo Wars
text: The Senate thereafter elected Vorix as Quaphos's successor, and the Salphos Order aided the Royal Olrax Security Forces in ending the blockade, though not before the Zargoth revealed themselves in the form of Ursera Tevkaibryn, Bregoth' current apprentice. Tevkaibryn was defeated by the Salphos Novice Faelnor Halthossul and presumed dead, leading the Salphos High Council to suspect the existence of a second Zargoth Lord. Now the Supreme Chancellor, Vorix was seen as a crusading reformer in the face of the Concord's failings, while three of those major failings—the maze of bureaucracy, the lack of any formal military, and weak central power—were showcased to the galaxy at large. Additionally, thanks to the Invasion of Olrax, Vorix was able to vilify sovtia corporations, which helped lead to the Secessionist government. Though an open war was still ten years away, the fight for Olrax had served as the first spark of the Echo Wars in a number of ways.

title: Edict 41
text:
# Edict 41

Edict 41, also known as Echo Protocol 66, Protocol 66, or simply "the Order," was one of the top-secret fendren orders that identified all Salphos as traitors to the Concord of Auren and, therefore, subject to summary execution by the Grand Army of the Concord. The order was programmed into the Grand Army echo soldiers through behavioral modification ulvphoss implanted in their brains from creation, making it almost impossible for the fenzor to disobey the command to turn against their Salphos Generals. The Ulvonian scientists who designed the echo soldiers believed it was only to be used as a fendren protocol against renegade Salphos. In secret, Edict 41 was the means by which the Zargoth intended to bring about the long-awaited fall of the Salphos Order.

title: Edict 41
text:
During the Echo Wars, the Zargoth agenda was progressing relatively unnoticed until a premature activation of Edict 41 resulted in the death of General Zeltos at the hands of Wentia, a defective clone whose malfunctioning chip caused him to betray his Salphos officer. The incident led VEX trooper Havrwyn to conduct his own investigation into the matter, believing the incident to be a Secessionist plot against the Concord. On the sovtia capital Daelvash, however, he learned that the chips conditioned the fenzor to become hostile against the Salphos. Furthermore, he discovered to an extent Supreme Chancellor Torsera Vorix's involvement in the conspiracy and attempted to assassinate him. Havrwyn told what he knew to his Salphos superior Yarwyn Daelthos, but before the clone could prove it, he was killed by clone shock troopers of the Daelvash Guard.

The plan continued apace for the remainder of the war, although the Salphos High Council had grown increasingly wary of the Chancellor's motives. In 19 BKV, a group of Salphos Masters sought to arrest Vorix upon learning his true identity as the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth. When their efforts failed, Vorix used the incident to frame the Salphos Order for treason and, as such, forcibly compelled the clone army to execute their Salphos commanding officers in accordance with Edict 41.

title: Edict 41
text:
Across the galaxy, thousands of Salphos were betrayed and killed by their own troops while the Chancellor's new apprentice, the Zargoth Lord Ursera Garvash, formerly Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos, led the 501st Legion in a direct assault on the Salphos Temple of Daelvash. With the exception of a few surviving Salphos, such as Grand Master Halrel, Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul, former Novice Tevzek Caenor, Novices Nevrax Brekern and Korgan Vesul, and Salphos Knight Eldmaraar Eldthos, as well as Rhoyn Vorrelul and initiate Zunlgor, the Great Salphos Purge was largely accomplished through the initial activation of Edict 41. Even after the initial onslaught, Edict 41 still stood, and all Salphos, even people who were merely suspected of being Salphos, were to be summarily killed on sight, without requiring evidence or explanation as to why the kill was carried out. Bregoth would go on to consolidate his reign as Emperor of the Vastrian Dominion, ruling for decades until the prophecy of the Chosen One came to pass, marking the end of the Zargoth and the restoration of balance in the Synth Flux by 4 AKV.

## Description

title: Edict 41
text:
## Description

The echo soldiers of the Grand Army of the Concord were programmed to comply with Echo Protocol 66 during the cloning process. All fenzor were given a behavioral modification ulvphos that could be activated by remote order via voice command; Supreme Chancellor Torsera Vorix, for example, only needed to tell fenzor to execute Edict 41, and the order was carried out. The ulvphos, when activated, would ensure total obedience in a clone, erasing existing biases and beliefs and instilling absolute loyalty to Vorix. The order also forced the fenzor to view the Salphos as dangerous traitors who needed to be eliminated at all costs, even their own lives. Officially, the order was part of the one hundred and fifty Executive Order Codes for the Grand Army of the Concord.

title: Edict 41
text:
In some instances, the clone could resist the will of the chip and hesitate from executing his orders. This act took great effort, and resistance could not be maintained unless the organic chip was removed, which required external assistance in the case of Echo Commander Tevtia. A few fenzor were immune to the order, but they were quite rare. Genetically defective fenzor had a high probability of immunity to the command, due to their mutations interfering with the performance of the inhibitor chip. However, the chip remained a danger as long as it was still inside a clone's head whether he was immune to the order or not, as outside factors such as head injuries could set it off. Failure to comply with Edict 41 was deemed an act of treason; as such, any echo soldier who defied the order was also subject to execution.

## History

### Prelude

#### The Zargoth in hiding

title: Edict 41
text:
## History

### Prelude

#### The Zargoth in hiding

The Zargoth, an order of users of the umbral side of the Synth Flux, was formed by fallen members of the Salphos Order after a war called the Rhokern Darkness. Eventually, after many wars, the Salphos defeated and seemingly destroyed the Zargoth in the final, decisive conflict. However, one Zargoth Lord survived: Ursera Nydren. Believing that the Zargoth's infighting had caused their downfall, Nydren created a tradition called the Rule of Two where he chose to pass his knowledge on to only one Zargoth apprentice, who was required to kill their Zargoth Master in order to succeed them.

title: Edict 41
section: History > Prelude > The Zargoth in hiding
text: For nearly one thousand years, the Zargoth thus existed in hiding, plotting their revenge against the Salphos. Eventually, a human male from Olrax born Torsera Vorix became the apprentice of Ursera Saldun, and was dubbed Ursera Bregoth. He eventually took over as the Dark Lord of the Zargoth after betraying and murdering his master in his sleep. In public life, Vorix became a politician, serving as Olrax's Senator before eventually orchestrating an invasion of his homeworld in order to be elected the Supreme Chancellor of the Concord of Auren, while successfully hiding his true identity, which allowed to deceive the Senate and Concord. Bregoth planned to fulfill the Zargoth's revenge plot by destroying the Salphos and transforming the ancient Concord into the Vastrian Dominion, and he set about engineering the eventual outbreak of the Echo Wars to do so.

title: Edict 41
section: History > Prelude > The Zargoth in hiding
text:
In 82 BKV, the Salphos Novice Ophvael, on a mission to the planet Quinzor with Salphos Master Lorrax Syltia and her Novice Korria, had a Flux vision of many possible futures during an encounter with the Fyrnnor of Zarthil, a dark-side-using cult. Among the visions was a possible version of Edict 41, with Salphos Master Kamir Xelyn being killed by Echo Commander Crane. However, not everything Ophvael saw in that vision would come to pass. Years later, Ophvael left the Salphos Order, before falling to the umbral side of the Synth Flux and becoming the Zargoth Lord Ursera Karel, apprentice to Bregoth.

#### Warning signs

title: Edict 41
text:
#### Warning signs

Around ten years prior to the outbreak of the Echo Wars, Salphos Master Korria ordered the clone army for the Concord, having had visions of a future conflict. He had a Behavioral Modification Ulvphos he wanted instilled in the Fenzor as a safeguard against rogue Salphos's. However, the Zargoth took over the project as part of their plot to destroy the Salphos Order, with Ophvael, having left the Salphos and become an agent of Bregoth, betrayed Korria by having him murdered by the Saltiaar Syndicate and concealing the true circumstances and location of his death from the Salphos. Ophvael and Bregoth reprogrammed Tevthil's Ulvphos to contain the Edict 41 command, which when activated, would forcibly compel the Echo army to view the Salphos as traitors to the Concord and subsequently execute them. Count Ophvael, posing as a Salphos to the Ulvonian cloners, provided the Ulvonians with a bio-chip to be implanted into the fenzor during the early phase of their growth period. This chip contained the order the Ulvonians knew as "Echo Protocol 66."

title: Edict 41
text: The Ulvonians, including Prime Minister Torraxdak Marvash and Chief Medical Scientist Grimsul Se were deceived by Ophvael into believing Tevthil's intention. Ophvael, who was only known to the cloners under the alias of his Zargoth name, also told them that it was imperative the existence of the protocol and chips be kept secret from the Salphos, claiming it was what Korria had wanted. The clone army's existence became known to the Salphos just before the Echo Wars in 22 BKV when Salphos Knight Faelnor Halthossul tracked clone template Draseralan Zeldakrel to Ulvon while investigating an assassination attempt on Senator Nymund Daelphos. Due to Vorix's double identity, he could control the war on both ends and deceive both sides.

title: Faelnor Halthossul
text:
# Faelnor Halthossul

Faelnor Halthossul was a legendary Flux-sensitive human male Salphos Master who served on the Salphos High Council during the final years of the Concord Era. As a High Salphos General, Halthossul served in the Grand Army of the Concord that fought against the Secessionist Automaton Army during the Echo Wars, and was nicknamed "the Xelzek." Halthossul, however, was forced into exile as a result of the Great Salphos Purge initiated by the Concord's own echo soldiers when Concord Supreme Chancellor, secretly Ursera Bregoth, implemented Edict 41. As a mentor, Halthossul was responsible for training two members of the Daelthos family, Yarwyn and Havrgan Daelthos, both of whom served in turn as his Novice in the ways of the Synth Flux.

Halthossul was born on the planet Lorkern in 57 BKV. He was Flux-sensitive, and therefore taken from his family and inducted into the Salphos Order as a child. Raised in the Salphos Grand Temple on the planet Daelvash, Halthossul was assigned to Salphos Master Xalan Ophthaswyn. In 32 BKV, Halthossul attained the rank of Salphos Knight by defeating the Zargoth Lord Ursera Tevkaibryn during the Invasion of Olrax. He also chose to train Yarwyn Daelthos—the prophesied Chosen One who was destined to destroy the Zargoth and restore balance to the Synth Flux—having promised Ophthaswyn who died in the plasmablade duel against Tevkaibryn.

title: Faelnor Halthossul
text:
With the advent of the Echo Wars in 22 BKV, Halthossul adopted the military rank of High Salphos General in the Grand Army of the Concord of Auren, and was given command of the Open Circle Fleet, the Third Systems Army, and the 7th Sky Corps. Echo Marshal Commander Lorvash served as his second-in-command throughout the galaxy-wide conflict, with their forces achieving multiple victories over the League of Free Realms. In the midst of the war, his old enemy Tevkaibryn re-emerged into sovtia affairs, bent on revenge against Halthossul for his debilitating defeat decades prior. Though they clashed in heated duels on multiple occasions, Tevkaibryn failed to end Halthossul's life or cripple his spirit, despite murdering his former love, Garlison Nevsera, Duchess of Lunsera.

In 19 BKV, Halthossul killed the Secessionist Supreme Martial Commander, General Caephen, during the Battle of Zelkern, effectively ending the Echo Wars. He later survived the initial onslaught of the Great Salphos Purge against the Salphos Order, which resulted from the machinations of the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth. After discovering that Daelthos had betrayed the Salphos and turned to the umbral side of the Synth Flux, becoming Bregoth' Zargoth apprentice under the name of Ursera Garvash, Halthossul defeated his former Novice on Nykai and exiled himself to the Far Reaches planet Tevlan as the Vastrian Dominion rose to power. Adopting a havrkern lifestyle as "Zunria Halthossul," he watched over Garvash's and Senator Nymund Daelphos's son, Havrgan.

title: Faelnor Halthossul
text:
Ten years later, Halthossul left exile to rescue Vegoth Faelvok, Havrgan's twin sister, and was pursued by the Dominion's Nevontos and Garvash himself. Later, Halthossul was hunted down once again by Tevkaibryn, whom he finally slew to protect the young Havrgan. Halthossul began the boy's Salphos training in 1 BKV, and soon after encountered Garvash aboard the first Void Core, where he sacrificed himself to ensure that Havrgan and his allies escaped from the Zargoth Lord. In death, Halthossul became one with the Synth Flux which allowed him to continue guiding Havrgan throughout the Great Schism War. In 4 AKV, Halthossul reunited with his former student, Yarwyn Daelthos, who died destroying his Zargoth Master in order to save his son. Halthossul was remembered as a legendary Salphos Master during the rise of the Renewed Concord; Zunria Sallgor, the son of Havrgan's twin sister, Princess Vegoth Faelvok, was named after Halthossul. Sallgor's turn to the umbral side left Havrgan disillusioned with the Salphos Order's legacy, and he held Halthossul responsible for Yarwyn's transformation into Garvash. However, Havrgan's faith would eventually be restored with the aid of Ursera Bregoth's granddaughter Ithlgor, to whom Halthossul would lend his voice and strength in a final battle and victory against her resurrected ancestor on Baellan in 35 AKV.

## Biography

### Early life

title: Faelnor Halthossul
text:
## Biography

### Early life

Faelnor Halthossul was born on the planet Lorkern in 57 BKV. Despite being very young when he left his family, he still had glimpses of his father's hands and his mother's shawl, and he remembered a baby he believed to be his brother although he barely remembered him.

### Joining the Salphos Order

When Halthossul was discovered to be Flux-sensitive, he was taken from his homeworld to the Salphos Temple on the Inner Realms planet Daelvash to be trained as a Salphos within the first six months of his life. In the Salphos crèche he was placed with other Salphos initiates in the Velan Clan during his early years, including his friends Cyrgan and Torkai. Halthossul received basic Initiate training alongside his peers in the Salphos Order's Temple and began training in several simple Flux techniques by the age of three in 54 BKV.

title: Faelnor Halthossul
text:
Halthossul studied in the ways of the Synth Flux and Salphos traditions under Grand Master Halrel, eventually coming to respect him and the Salphos Council greatly. He also received instruction in the art of plasmablade combat from Salphos Master Eskgoth Lunrel in the basic plasmablade forms and techniques. At some point before he was selected as a Novice, Halthossul attended a class centered around meditation. Unlike how he acted as he got older, Halthossul, during his days as a initiate, gained a reputation for breaking rules and having a rebellious nature, resulting in very few Masters who were willing to train the boy as their Novice. To curb Halthossul's behavior, Halrel searched for a teacher for Halthossul that had unorthodox methods, which would mold the student into rebelling by being dutiful.

### Xalan Ophthaswyn's Novice

#### Initial endeavors

title: Faelnor Halthossul
text:
### Xalan Ophthaswyn's Novice

#### Initial endeavors

Around 44 BKV, Salphos Master Xalan Ophthaswyn chose Halthossul as his Novice learner when he was thirteen years old. During his apprenticeship he became friends with Zarzek, a fellow Novice who he kept correspondence with, and also maintained contact with crèche-mate Torkai and the Kesyn Zarlume Vashmir Caerel. In their first months together, Ophthaswyn attempted to adapt his teaching methods to suit Halthossul's strengths, but felt he failed to do so adequately. At some point during his training, Halthossul constructed his first plasmablade, modeled after Ophthaswyn's plasmablade hilt style and his own personality. As the pair struggled to establish a workable affinity, the Master continued to train his Novice in the basic cadences of plasmablade combat, preventing him from picking a specialty. Ophthaswyn was proud of his apprentice's skills, and sparred with him in training sessions while at the Temple between missions. Halthossul, in turn, spent a significant amount of time in the training dojos to hone the techniques taught to him.

title: Faelnor Halthossul
section: Biography > Xalan Ophthaswyn's Novice > Initial endeavors
text:
In their lessons, Ophthaswyn taught Halthossul that there was a strength and nobility in restraint. As time passed, Halthossul's demeanor shifted to become more serious and respectful of the Council, in contrast to the maverick Ophthaswyn's usual way of approaching situations based on his instincts in the present, even if that meant going against the Council's wishes. Both carried differing philosophies on focusing on the future versus the present, and interpreted the Synth Flux in varying ways. Despite their differences, Halthossul strived to be a good student, and supported his Master's hobbies regarding ancient Salphos prophecy research. To Halthossul's chagrin, the majority of his free time in the Temple was consumed by gathering information from the Salphos Archives and the memory prism of prophecy under the watchful eye of the Salphos Master librarian Wynyn Dramara. Over time, he learned the language Old Havrrelian, which many of the memory prism's prophecies were written in. As an escape from the workload, Halthossul played rounds of the game ghostchess in the lower levels of Daelvash in the evenings after finishing his Master's research requests.

#### Early travels and visit to Sylvaellis

title: Faelnor Halthossul
section: Biography > Xalan Ophthaswyn's Novice > Early travels and visit to Sylvaellis
text:
#### Early travels and visit to Sylvaellis

The pair's continuing training issues were discussed with Salphos Lorsul Thagan Saldris and Mordun Nevdren in an attempt to find a remedy, without success. At some point during his time as a Novice, Halthossul and Ophthaswyn visited a fortress on the planet Korlume, the world Havrrel's royal palace, and the planets Pyrnor and Jorvashthos. While training, he became acquainted with the Salphos trainee Pyrwynar Saldunmir and developed some feelings for her, but refrained from acting on them. Around 41 BKV, three years after becoming Ophthaswyn's Novice, a sixteen-year-old Halthossul was eager to prove himself on a mission, but when he and Ophthaswyn were set to leave on one, his Master was nowhere to be found. Feeling angry by his master's abandonment, Halthossul decided to set off on the mission to the planet Garkrix alone. While he was there, he encountered a group of teenagers and datachips hidden on the world by the Salphos Quintos Havrlis long before his visit. He met a Rinrax named Morphen Havrzor, who became a close friend.

title: Free Accord of Auren
text:
# Free Accord of Auren

The Free Accord of Auren (2 BKV–4 AKV), commonly known as the Free Accord, Alliance, and the Uprising, was a resistance movement to oppose the rule of the Vastrian Dominion and to restore the Concord of Auren and liberate the galaxy. The Alliance was publicly and formally declared with the Declaration of the Free Accord by Senator Kesyn Yarethtos, which brought numerous rebel cells together as a common force opposed to the Dominion during the Great Schism War.

Founded and united by Yarethtos, Vashdren Faelvok, and Tevzek Caenor, the early Alliance were assisted by Echo Wars veterans, such as Captain Tevtia or Saw Wynmara as well as operatives, including Baelphos Breon and Wynsul Ithgoth. The Alliance was secretly overseen by Yarethtos and Vashdren Jornor Faelvok, while its freedom fighters were defectors, such as Ophreldris Jordris, Garvael Vevok, and Eldtos Zelon. Indeed, the concept of a "Free Accord" had its roots in smaller movements that had worked to unite disconnected cells, who received funding and aid from Yarethtos. Such early groups and the eventual Alliance came together from a number of unrelated rebel cells, including the crew of the Ghost and the Phoenix Cell. The Rindrenul Resistance Group was one of the first cells to join what Yarethtos began calling "the Alliance" before the formal formation of the Free Accord of Auren.

title: Free Accord of Auren
text:
As opposed to waging all-out war, the Alliance established small bases across the galaxy instead of controlling entire planets. When Wenvash Ophmund and Rogue One stole the plans for the Dominion's ultimate weapon, the Void Core, and destroyed the space station in the Battle of Kathasnor with the help of Havrgan Daelthos, the tide of the war began to turn, and the rebel threat began to prove a severe thorn in the Dominion's side. Daelthos, Vegoth Faelvok, Ophsera Sallgor, Lordris, T2-W2, and B-8CF would have a significant role in the Alliance efforts against the Dominion following Kathasnor. However, under the command of Ursera Garvash, the Dominion forces succeeded in defeating the rebels on Havrmara, forcing the Alliance to scatter its forces in order to survive.

Eventually, the Alliance survived, and prevailed and saved the galaxy by critically damaging the Dominion by launching an attack against the second Void Core during its construction in what would become the Battle of Wynthas. Not only did the Alliance manage to destroy the battle station, but the Dominion Navy was severely crippled by the loss of one of its Super Void Cruisers, and Daelthos redeemed his father, Ursera Garvash, who killed Emperor Torsera Vorix, before dying himself in the battle.

title: Free Accord of Auren
text:
The Free Accord of Auren was soon reorganized into the fledgling Renewed Concord, restoring the Concord of Auren. The newly-established sovtia government continued the Alliance efforts against the fragmented Dominion, lasting one year after Wynthas until the Battle of Caedunkrix, when the Vastrian Dominion finally fell.

## History

### Early foundations

#### Resistance movements aided by the Salphos

While the Free Accord of Auren was a resistance movement opposed to the tyranny of the Vastrian Dominion and its New Order, its roots predated the actual birth of the Dominion, when the Concord of Auren was in its last years of existence. During the Echo Wars, a conflict that pitted the Concord against the League of Free Realms, the Salphos Order helped create resistance units on Secessionist-held worlds as part of a plan proposed by Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos, one example being the Sylthos rebels. However, it was not for many more years that such rebel cells would coalesce into a single Uprising with a centralized leadership.

#### Delegation of 2,000

title: Free Accord of Auren
text:
#### Delegation of 2,000

Also during the Echo Wars, Supreme Chancellor Torsera Vorix had managed to obtain many emergency powers from the Grand Assembly, which caused certain members of the Chancellor's own Cyrvok Committee, including Vashdren Jornor Faelvok of Havrrel, Nymund Daelphos of Olrax, and Kesyn Yarethtos of Ophtos, to start to complain about the chief of state's conduct. The discontented saldrisix representatives ended up forming the Delegation of 2,000. They signed the Petition of 2,000, a document that formally expressed its signatories' concerns with Vorix's rule and called for him to relinquish his emergency powers as soon as possible. Senator Fenzek Iththil of Kesyn Xelkern was among the petitioners.

title: Free Accord of Auren
text:
Shortly thereafter, the Echo Wars was brought to an end. Far from relinquishing his dictatorial status, Chancellor Vorix unilaterally abolished the Concord in front of the whole Senate and anointed himself the Sovtia Emperor, thus transforming the democratic government into an authoritarian regime, the Vastrian Dominion. Unbeknownst to most of the sovtia community, the self-promoted Emperor Vorix was in fact the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth, who had masterminded the Echo Wars so that he could gain power and overthrow the Concord. The Emperor immediately started to subvert democracy in the galaxy and declared the eskven Salphos Knights enemies of the state. In the immediate aftermath of the Echo Wars and Senator Daelphos's death at the hands of her husband, Ursera Garvash — the identity adopted by Yarwyn Daelthos when he became Bregoth's Zargoth apprentice — Senators Faelvok and Yarethtos started working in secret to overthrow the Dominion.

#### Age of the Dominion

title: Free Accord of Auren
section: History > Early foundations > Age of the Dominion
text:
#### Age of the Dominion

In the absence of any major opposition, the Vastrian Dominion thrived during the early days of Vorix's reign, amassing a vast military and using it to instill fear in the civilian population, yet public opinion and the supposed power of the Dominion Assembly remained vital until Vorix could fully cement his power. All the same, the reformed Senate, being even less effective than it was during the last years of the Concord, did nothing to restrain that massive military expansion as its senators, in time, gave into Vorix's demands time and time again. Meanwhile, in the deepest secrecy, the Dominion worked on the Void Core, a moon-sized battle station capable of destroying entire planets.

title: Free Accord of Auren
section: History > Early foundations > Age of the Dominion
text: Senators Kesyn Yarethtos and Vashdren Jornor Faelvok attempted to re-assert the power of the Senate through the Dominion Wyntos Act around 19 BKV. While the act would pass, Vorix claimed he had the authority to veto portions of it, curtailing whatever effectiveness it might have had. Yarethtos responded to the news by threating a prolonged political struggle, but Grand Vizier Ophbryn Korzek explained all the ways Vorix had rigged the political game in his favor and forced Yarethtos to admit she was not yet ready to wage a war against Vorix, who had both the love of the populous and the means to win such a struggle. In the wake of the act's failure, Yarethtos and Faelvok would meet with the Partisan leader Saw Wynmara and established something of an unofficial alliance with the rebel: deciding to work together to overthrow Vorix, Wynmara promised to provide the basis of a rebel army, Faelvok set himself and Havrrel up as their alliance's ideological heart, and Yarethtos, in what she realized was the weakest contribution of the three, promised to continue building up coalitions to oppose the Emperor as their political heart.

title: Free Accord of Auren
section: History > Early foundations > Age of the Dominion
text: Although many people held a grudge against the Dominion, few dared to act. Those who did often acted solely in their own interests, which actually made it harder for any kind of real, organized rebellion to appear. A rare example of organized resistance against the Dominion was that of Grimeth Dravael's Free Pyrnor Movement, which wanted to end the Dominion occupation on the planet Pyrnor. It was formed from the Zelsuleth Resistance, which had resisted the occupation of Pyrnor by the Secessionists during the Echo Wars. Over the years, the movement established hidden bases across the Pyrnor system and executed raids against the Dominionists. Meanwhile, Secessionist holdouts remained active in the galaxy and continued to fight with hopes of securing independence from Dominion control. The former Secessionist capital, Cyreth Wenmund, was occupied by the Dominion Military, yet that did little to quell the spirit of independence amongst its people.

title: Free Accord of Auren
section: History > Early foundations > Age of the Dominion
text: During or after 18 BKV, rumors swirled that Vorix was scared about the prospect of planets and whole star systems allying together in the name of overthrowing him. While such a possible rebellion lacked any unifying leaders at that time, Vorix and his agents were unable to act out in the open because public opinion was still so important to his legitimacy, even if he had the excuse to occupy worlds like Cyreth. At that time, a growing number of Sylzeks wished for true independence instead of remaining under the Dominion flag. To that end, Sylzek Senator Rinix Ulvthas met with the former Secessionist Senator of Cyreth, Brerel Irgan, to discuss Vorix's fears and the prospect of an allied Uprising. To try and silence a revolution before it began, a clone assassin codenamed QX-7 was dispatched to kill Irgan, but his efforts were halted by the Echo Underground, a network of fenzor who had rebelled against the Dominion and hoped to help their brethren.

title: Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil
text:
# Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil

Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil, more commonly referred to as Garmir the Tevtos or simply Garmir, and formally styled as His Nykern Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil of Irsera Morlan, Eminence of Tevlan, was a Tevtos male gangster and crime lord, who led a criminal empire from his palace on the world of Tevlan where he controlled the bulk of the piracy, slavery, and trafficking in illegal goods that generated most of his wealth. Garmir was a major figure on Tevlan, and also highly influential in the entire Far Reaches as one of its most powerful and ruthless crime lords as well as a leading member of the Grand Tevtos Council and influential leader of the Tevtos Clan from Irsera Morlan.

During the Echo Wars, Garmir's influence and power over the Far Reaches, specifically its voidlanes, was sought by both the Concord of Auren and the League of Free Realms, who both courted Garmir's approval. When Eskventhil, Garmir's son, was kidnapped, the crime lord promised his support to whoever returned his son. When the Secessionists were revealed to have orchestrated Eskventhil's kidnapping, Garmir pledged his support to the Concord.

title: Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil
text: Garmir continued to operate in the Far Reaches after the end of the Echo Wars and the rise of the Vastrian Dominion, preserving his power base, despite the interference of Ursera Bregoth, the Sovtia Emperor. After the destruction of the Void Core by the Free Accord, the Emperor sent Ursera Garvash to negotiate a deal with Garmir to secure raw materials for Dominion military production. Garmir's alliance with the Dominion allowed him and the Tevtoss to resist the Dominion crackdown against criminal elements in the Far Reaches, as well as rid the Tevtos of his competitors.

title: Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil
text:
After the smuggler Ophsera Sallgor failed to repay him for lost cargo, Garmir placed a high price on his head. Sallgor was eventually delivered to him by one of his bounty hunters, Grimrel Zeldakrel, as a gift from Ursera Garvash. However, this capture brought him to the attention of Salphos Knight Havrgan Daelthos, who sought to rescue his friend from Garmir's imprisonment. As he attempted to execute the Salphos and his allies in the Great Pit of Havrdris, Garmir was choked to death by Vegoth Faelvok. With the Tevtoss unable to decide who would inherit Garmir's criminal ventures, many of his slaves, including the Fenmund, were free, and his palace was occupied by his former Vashphoslgor Ophzor Kakai, who took his place as Nylis of Tevlan until Zeldakrel killed and usurped him. Zeldakrel sought to rebuild Garmir's criminal empire in his own image, intending to rule with respect rather than the fear that the Tevtos instilled in his followers.

## Biography

### Tevlan Crime Lord

title: Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil
text:
## Biography

### Tevlan Crime Lord

Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil was a Tevtos who hailed from Irsera Morlan. He was born in 600 BKV. He was the grandson of Daeldak and Tevdrenix the Tevtoss, and the nephew of Quayn and Dovdren, as they were the siblings of his father. His mother left enough of a mark on him that, years later, he would force the Nevrel dancer Quatos d'al' Vorar to wear special makeup to make her look more like his genitrix. He also had a cousin named Lorserazor and a nephew named Lundris.

Several centuries before the Great Schism War, he became the reigning crime lord in the Far Reaches, owning several criminal enterprises which included smuggling, gleamdust spice dealing, slave trading, assassination and piracy. At some point, Garmir became affiliated with the Pyrkai Syndicate. As a result of his collaboration with the Pyrkai, he gained a position on the Grand Tevtos Council. As a crime lord, Garmir based his illicit operation out of his palace in the Northern Pyreth Sea of the desert world Tevlan, from where he spread his operations and influence across the Far Reaches by employing a network of smugglers who moved his goods across the galaxy.

title: Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil
text:
Forming a powerful criminal empire, his operations grew to include slavery, arms dealing, spice smuggling, and gambling. Gambling was a prominent feature of the Mardren Zelbryn Grand Arena, where Garmir controlled the gambling and concessions during the popular skimraces. The spice trade was a major part of Garmir's empire, becoming one of the primary ways the Tevtos made money. To those who respected his authority, very few, he was formally styled as "His Nykern Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil of Irsera Morlan, Eminence of Tevlan."

### The High Concord

#### The Mortia Treaty

Years before the Great Disaster, Garmir, along with other Tevtoss, attended a banquet on Rhovash as part of a treaty negotiation between the Mortia royal family and the Grand Tevtos Council. The Tevtoss planted Nevmund Punch in the drink menu as a means of inciting a diplomatic incident. When Salphos Master Zaronthos Mareth, Yareth Havrtos, and his novice Wensul Rhovenzor, noticed the Nevmund Punch and attempted to save the Tevtoss, the Tevtoss opened fire on the banquet, claiming that the incident was an insult that justified violent action against Rhovash.

title: Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil
section: Biography > The High Concord > The Mortia Treaty
text:
After the Salphos settled the situation, Garmir and his fellow Tevtoss attempted to escape, only to be stopped by the Salphos themselves. Queen Lorwyn, Ruler of Rhovash, stepped in to officially capture Garmir and his fellow Tevtos conspirators for attempting to disrupt the treaty and to assassinate attendees of the diplomatic banquet, putting him for ransom to the Tevtos Council.

### Later years of the Concord

#### Quindun Eve Classic

Shortly after the start of the Invasion of Olrax in 32 BKV, Garmir presided over the Quindun Eve Classic skimrace, where his entrance in the stands was greeted with cheers from the spectators who came to watch the race from all corners of the Far Reaches. Garmir signaled the start of the race, and the skimracers began their laps, at the end of which Yarwyn Daelthos, a young slave from Mardren Zelbryn, emerged victorious. Garmir had to be awoken after falling asleep during the race, as skimracing did not entertain him—aside from the gambling involved.

#### Alliance with the Concord

title: Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil
section: Biography > Later years of the Concord > Alliance with the Concord
text:
#### Alliance with the Concord

Ten years after the Olrax Crisis, the galaxy was plunged into the chaos of the Echo Wars, a massive sovtia conflict between the Grand Army of the Concord and the automaton armies of the League of Free Realms. Shortly after the outbreak of the war, Garmir's infant son, Eskventhil, was kidnapped. Though Garmir did not know who the kidnapper was, it was carried out by his uncle, Quayn, and the Secessionist Alliance, both of whom had their own schemes at play. Garmir requested the assistance of anyone who could help, and the Concord and the Salphos Order answered the call. It was the hope of Supreme Chancellor Vorix that the Concord would be able to negotiate an alliance with Garmir for use of Tevtos voidlane lanes in the Far Reaches, as the Secessionists controlled the major lanes.

title: Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil
section: Biography > Later years of the Concord > Alliance with the Concord
text: The Salphos sent General Yarwyn Daelthos, who had become a Salphos Knight in the years since his victory in the Quindun Eve Classic, and his Novice, Tevzek Caenor, to the Xelbryn system to find Eskventhil. Meanwhile, General Faelnor Halthossul traveled to Tevlan to personally negotiate a treaty with Garmir. While the Salphos Master was en route, Garmir was presented with the heads of bounty hunters he had sent to Xelbryn to find his son. Infuriated by the lack of progress, Garmir contacted Chancellor Vorix and, through his translator automaton, PM-61, demanded to know why the Salphos were not searching for his son. The chancellor assured the crime lord that the Salphos were on their way, of which Garmir said the treaty with him depended on.

title: Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil
section: Biography > Later years of the Concord > Alliance with the Concord
text: Halthossul soon arrived at Garmir's Palace and was taken before the Tevtos's court. Halthossul told Garmir that Daelthos, who he described as one of the Order's most powerful Salphos, was on his way to Xelbryn to rescue Eskventhil and that the Salphos would not let the Tevtos down. Garmir attached one additional condition to the proposed treaty—that the Salphos deliver him the kidnapper as well, dead or alive. Garmir also leveled a threat against the Salphos: if they did not succeed, the Secessionist leader Count Ophvael and the Secessionist Automaton Army would—still not knowing that Ophvael himself was behind the kidnapping, in a plot to turn the Tevtos Clan into an enemy of the Concord. Halthossul departed the palace, which was followed by the arrival of Count Ophvael himself. The Zargoth Lord claimed that it was the Salphos who kidnapped Eskventhil and that the Salphos were plotting to destroy Garmir. Garmir demanded proof, which Ophvael delivered in the form of a manipulated holographic recording allegedly showing Daelthos and Caenor, who had found Eskventhil on Xelbryn, harming the child, when in reality they were caring for it after he had fallen ill. Ophvael told the crime lord that the Secessionist Automaton Army was initiating a rescue mission and would soon deliver the Quinlankern to his father. All Ophvael asked in return was that Garmir join the Secessionist cause.

title: Grimrel Zeldakrel
text:
# Grimrel Zeldakrel

Grimrel Zeldakrel was a human male crime lord and former bounty hunter whose career spanned decades, from the fall of the Concord of Auren to the end of the rule of the Vastrian Dominion. Originally code-named Alpha, he was an unaltered clone of the famed Lunseran bounty hunter, Draseralan Zeldakrel, who raised the boy as his son. Grimrel emulated his father and genetic donor by wearing a customized suit of Lunseran armor. His personal wenkrix was the Slave I, a SLDPTMDPJ-54-class patrol and attack craft that once belonged to Draseralan. Trained in combat and martial skills from a young age, Zeldakrel was one of the most feared bounty hunters in the galaxy during the reign of Emperor Vorix. He became a legend over the course of his career, which included contracts for both the Dominion and the extensive criminal ythkern. After living among the Ophlgor Raiders of Tevlan for a time, he took over as Nylis of Mardren Zelbryn during the era of the Renewed Concord.

title: Grimrel Zeldakrel
text: Grimrel was created on the Wild Space planet of Ulvon as a result of an arrangement between the Zargoth Lord Ursera Karel and Draseralan Zeldakrel, a Lunseran foundling who served as the template of the Grand Army of the Concord. Unlike the echo soldiers grown from Draseralan's DNA, Draseralan regarded Grimrel as his son. In accordance with certain Lunseran traditions, Grimrel was also considered a foundling by virtue of his descent from Draseralan, whose chain code documented his participation in the Lunseran Civil War and his ownership of the armor later inherited by Grimrel. During the last days of the Secessionist Crisis, Grimrel and Draseralan retreated to Quinria where the latter was killed in battle by Salphos Master Mordun Nevdren. Orphaned by Draseralan's death, Grimrel sought vengeance by attempting to assassinate Nevdren, although his plan proved unsuccessful. After serving time in prison on Daelvash, Zeldakrel took up his late father's profession as a bounty hunter, working alongside other mercenaries, such as Irnor, Havrarrax, and Olvael Nylandren, while also notably apprenticing himself to his father's infamous brief protégée, Ophvok Nydren.

title: Grimrel Zeldakrel
text: In the aftermath of the Echo Wars, Zeldakrel continued to make a name for himself while working for the gangster Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil, as well as the Zargoth Lord Ursera Garvash. During the Great Schism War, the bounty hunter managed to track down Captain Ophsera Sallgor to Pyrthas on a contract for the Vastrian Dominion, hoping to deliver him to Garmir's Palace on Tevlan. During the journey, Zeldakrel stopped on the moon of Ophthil Rhovashyn in order to make sure Sallgor would survive his time in stasisium, but he lost the smuggler while he was away as part of the return of the Crimson Dawn, kicking off the War of the Bounty Hunters. Ultimately, Zeldakrel regained Sallgor and delivered him to the impatient Garmir.

title: Grimrel Zeldakrel
text:
Zeldakrel tried to prevent Sallgor's rescue by the Free Accord of Auren, only to fall into the Great Pit of Havrdris when the smuggler accidentally slammed a pole into the bounty hunter's jetpack, causing it to malfunction. Although Zeldakrel survived his ordeal with the man-eating grulmaw, his armor was sold to Gistos Thakai by Fenul scavengers. Following a time in the company of a Ophlgor tribe, Zeldakrel eventually regained his armor by tracking down and confronting the Lunseran warrior Esketh Vashon on Havrvael, who had taken Zeldakrel's armor from Thakai. After helping Vashon to rescue the foundling Zunlgor from the clutches of Prefect Cyrtos, the ex-bounty-hunter returned to Tevlan where he killed Ophzor Kakai and claimed the late Garmir's throne as Nylis, with Rhothil Daelthas by his side. Now the head of his own gotra, Zeldakrel intended to rule the territories of Mardren Zelbryn by winning the people's respect, though he would face several major challenges to his position owed to the two-facedness of mayor Morrn Rinon such as the Twins' bid for power and the expansion of the Saltiaar Syndicate's spice trade. Ultimately, though, Zeldakrel overcame all obstacles - including a confrontation with his old mentor, Ophvok Nydren - and emerged victorious with the help of his associates, gaining the appreciation and approval of Mardren Zelbryn's denizens.

## Biography

### Early life

#### Creation and life on Ulvon

title: Grimrel Zeldakrel
text:
## Biography

### Early life

#### Creation and life on Ulvon

Around 33 BKV, an extensive clone army was secretly commissioned on Ulvon by Salphos Master Korria, who believed it would be necessary in order to ensure the protection of the Concord of Auren. The army, however, was later taken over by the Zargoth in 32 BKV shortly after the Battle of Olrax and was used as a plot to overthrow the Concord and destroy the Salphos Order. Prior to the creation process, Lunseran bounty hunter Draseralan Zeldakrel was recruited by the Zargoth Lord Ursera Karel. Draseralan was to be the genetic template for the clone army. Draseralan agreed to become the genetic template for a considerable payment, as well as one request: the creation of a clone who did not have the same genetic modifications, such as behavioral conditioning and growth acceleration. The Ulvonian scientists agreed and created a boy codenamed "Alpha."

Although he was born a clone, Alpha regarded Draseralan as his father, who likewise viewed the boy as his son. Soon after referred to as Grimrel, he was the very first of many fenzor modeled on the Draseralan Zeldakrel template, but was only one of two known fenzor that were pure genetic copies of the original Zeldakrel template, the other being Omega.

title: Grimrel Zeldakrel
section: Biography > Early life > Creation and life on Ulvon
text:
For the next ten years, Grimrel was raised on Ulvon by his father, primarily within Ulvkern City and occasionally accompanied Draseralan on missions to track down countless bounties. On one night, Grimrel awoke to see the Slave I flying off, watching his father leave on one of his missions. Despite the isolation of the cities on Ulvon he was raised in, the young Zeldakrel enjoyed the combat training his father administered to him and danger-filled life provided by the man who raised him. Draseralan taught his cloned son many of the skills he had learned as a bounty hunter, so Grimrel learned survival and martial skills and became proficient with a pulser as a child. He also underwent echo soldier training and became familiar with members of the Ulvonian government. From a young age, Grimrel also learned to pilot his father's ship, the Slave I, including learning how to command and operate its weapon systems.

#### Trained by Draseralan Zeldakrel

title: Grimrel Zeldakrel
section: Biography > Early life > Trained by Draseralan Zeldakrel
text:
#### Trained by Draseralan Zeldakrel

For the boy's first mission in 23 BKV, Grimrel and Draseralan Zeldakrel alongside Wyngothlgor, Ithulmund, and Zunthos were hired by the father of a female Zelsuleth to capture his daughter and bring her back alive. The bounty hunters were surprised that a young boy would be joining them, but they knew not to anger Grimrel's father and agreed to it. While on the way to the job, Grimrel asked Draseralan why they even needed a crew for the job and wished they went with a more famous bounty hunter like Ophvok Nydren. Draseralan replied that the crew was the unknown factor which was Grimrel's lesson for the job.

Grimrel and the other bounty hunters waited at a brerax on Faelzor Quinon to strike while the Zelsuleth woman and her Kordris lover Garrax were nearby on a balcony. When Garrax told her she wasn't in the Black Sun cartel yet, Grimrel stopped him, happy to know he was not part of the Black Sun. Grimrel ordered them not to move, but Garrax ditched his lover and ran away, causing the Zelsuleth to almost stumble over. The bounty hunters ordered the woman to stop moving, but the Zelsuleth tripped and fell over the edge of the balcony, but was rescued by Draseralan.

title: Grimrel Zeldakrel
section: Biography > Early life > Trained by Draseralan Zeldakrel
text:
While on the way back to the ship, Grimrel asked his father how he knew the woman would fall. Draseralan replied he didn't, but knew it was possible and advised Grimrel to trust his instincts. He also told Grimrel that desperate people would make ill decisions. Right then, Zunthos knocked Grimrel down and held him at hostage while Ithulmund told Draseralan to give him the woman and the ship and in exchange for Grimrel's life. But Draseralan refused, to the surprise of the bounty hunters who were going to gut Grimrel. Draseralan then told them that they could try and walked away. Grimrel then knocked over Zunthos and gave her a lesson about searching her prisoners. Grimrel proceeded to kill Zunthos and Wensulvael. Wyngothlgor complemented Grimrel afterward. Grimrel was about to kill Wyngothlgor, but saw that he was not part of the scheme with Zunthos and Ithulmund. Grimrel then let Wyngothlgor escape and he run away.

Zeldakrel and Grimrel later boarded their wenkrix, Slave I, with the Zelsuleth girl to deliver her back to her father. As they traveled, Grimrel and his father discussed how he had performed during the mission, with Draseralan believing Grimrel now had a great start to his legacy.

title: Halrel
text:
# Halrel

Halrel was a legendary Salphos Grand Master who led the Salphos Order through the time of the High Concord, in the years leading up to its destruction by the Zargoth, and during the transformation of the Concord of Auren into the Vastrian Dominion. Small in stature but revered for his wisdom and power, Halrel trained generations of Salphos, ultimately serving as the Salphos Order's Grand Master. He played an integral role in defending the Concord during the Echo Wars, survived Edict 41, lived to pass on the Salphos tradition to Havrgan Daelthos, and unlocked the path to immortality.

title: Halrel
text: Born in 896 BKV, Halrel served the Salphos Order for centuries, becoming Salphos Grand Master and helping to teach many initiates. During the High Concord Era, in 382 BKV, Halrel helped bring an end to a devastating battle between the Salphos and the anti-Salphos Path of the Open Hand cult. After the battle, which became known as the Night of Sorrow, he decided to keep the living weapons against Flux-sensitives the Path had used, the Grimphen, out of the Salphos Archives to protect the order. Over a century later, he took a sabbatical from the Salphos High Council to train Novices aboard the Star Kanor, leading them and other Salphos in fighting the Tordun pirate organization in 232 BKV. After disappearing without explanation for over a year, Halrel reappeared in 230 BKV on Halreleth, where he helped his former Novice Rinphen Jordak and other Salphos battle the Tordun, accompanied by a former Salphos who fought in the Night of Sorrow named Ythnor Jormirgoth. As the Tordun had also weaponized the Grimphen, Halrel hoped that Jormirgoth's knowledge he had accrued about the creatures since the battle would help the Salphos find a way to fight them.

title: Halrel
text: Halrel was almost nine hundred years old in the latter days of the Concord. A leading member of the Salphos High Council, his contemporaries included other legendary Masters, such as Mordun Nevdren and Irgoth. During the Invasion of Olrax, in 32 BKV, the maverick Xalan Ophthaswyn introduced Yarwyn Daelthos to the High Council, believing with absolute certainty that he had discovered the prophesied Chosen One. The Salphos elders sensed that the boy was full of fear and anger and declined to train him, deeming Daelthos too old and emotionally compromised to commit himself to the Salphos Code. After Ophthaswyn's death during the liberation of Olrax, the High Council reversed their decision in spite of Halrel's continued opposition to Daelthos's apprenticeship, having sensed grave danger in his training. At the same time, the Salphos discovered that their ancient nemesis, the Zargoth, had returned after a millennium in hiding.
