Aware of the Rule of Two, Halrel was convinced that at least one more Zargoth Lord remained active following Faelnor Halthossul's victory over the Zargoth apprentice Ursera Tevkaibryn.

title: Halrel
text: Over the next decade, the galaxy was on the verge of civil war with entire star systems—led by Count Ophvael, Halrel's one-time Novice—threatening to secede from the Concord by 22 BKV. Unable to defend the entire Concord against this betrayal on their own, the Salphos took command of the newly-formed Grand Army of the Concord, with Halrel himself leading an army of echo soldiers against the Secessionist Automaton Army of the League of Free Realms in the first battle of the Echo Wars, rescuing the Salphos and Senator from execution. For three years Halrel led the Concord military's war effort as a Salphos General, determined to bring a swift and decisive end to the conflict. During this time he was approached by the spirit of Xalan Ophthaswyn, who helped Halrel learn how to retain his identity as a spirit after death. Halrel's efforts against the Secessionists were undermined by Ursera Bregoth, the Dark Lord of the Zargoth who conspired to destroy the Salphos and restore the Zargoth to power. After the Great Salphos Purge commenced in 19 BKV, killing thousands of Salphos both on Daelvash and across the galaxy, Halrel confronted the self-declared Sovtia Emperor but failed to cut short Bregoth' reign and consequently retreated into exile, leaving the Zargoth Master to consolidate his power with a new apprentice, the former Yarwyn Daelthos-turned-Ursera Garvash, at his side.

title: Halrel
text: Halrel's remaining years were spent living in isolation on the remote world of Quaulthil. After the death of Faelnor Halthossul, he was able to commune with his spirit, who wished for Halrel to train Yarwyn's son Havrgan Daelthos. Halrel initially reluctantly agreed, but later believed that the galaxy as better off without him and refused Halthossul's request. After being convinced by Halthossul to enter the Cave of Evil, in which he confronted many figures from his past and made peace with his failures, he agreed to teach Havrgan Daelthos, who soon after sought out the legendary Grand Master in the hope of becoming a Salphos Knight. He trained Daelthos for a time, until despite Halrel's warnings Daelthos hurriedly abandoned his training to save his friends after a having a vision that they were in danger. A year later, in 4 AKV, with his health rapidly declining, Halrel died of old age when Daelthos returned to see him. He became one with the Synth Flux, shortly before Havrgan redeemed his father Yarwyn, who fulfilled his destiny as the Chosen One by killing Bregoth.

title: Halrel
text:
Years later, Havrgan Daelthos's attempt to reform the Salphos Order would be foiled when his nephew Zunria Sallgor turned to the umbral side and destroyed his Salphos Temple. Believing the galaxy was better without him and the Salphos, Daelthos went into exile, just as Halrel had. After his student he reluctantly trained, the scavenger Ithlgor, also abandoned her training, Halrel appeared as a ghost to Daelthos. Halrel taught Daelthos to learn from his failures and helped him forgive himself.

## Biography

### Early life

Born nine-hundred years before the Battle of Wynthas, Halrel belonged to an ancient and mysterious species and little was known of Halrel's early life; he never revealed his homeworld. As he was keenly attuned to the Synth Flux, he joined the Salphos Order as a initiate. As a Salphos Initiate, Halrel made use of a training plasmablade. After undergoing the ritual known as the Gathering, he received his own personal ixium crystal, and Professor Zarvok helped him construct his first plasmablade aboard the Crucible. The circumstances surrounding Halrel and the construction of his first plasmablade were exciting, according to Zarvok. At some point during his time as a initiate, Halrel skipped across the lily pads in the Salphos Temple's meditation pond.

title: Halrel
text:
Although Halrel spoke little of his early days, it was rumored that one of his early instructors was the Zelkrix Eskrn Vasheth Tharel. Halrel was paired up with a personal mentor at a younger age than usual. During their time together, Halrel's Salphos Master told him the tale of Jaxthos and Sovyndris, two great Salphos of the past. As a Novice, Halrel visited multiple planets and during his first years he could have named them all, but in the following centuries, he couldn't remember how many he'd seen and later estimated the number to be in the tens of thousands. Around the age of one hundred, in 796 BKV, Halrel was ready to pass on what he had learned. Having attained the rank of Master, he spent the next eight centuries training and tutoring generations of Salphos. It was estimated that over his lifetime, he trained around twenty thousand Salphos.

### High Concord Era

#### Early High Concord Era

title: Halrel
text:
### High Concord Era

#### Early High Concord Era

By the High Concord Era, Halrel was considered a great Salphos Master. He had also gained a seat on the Salphos High Council and the rank of Grand Master. Two other Salphos—Syldris Garmara and Kortos Kesrax—shared the Grand Master title with Halrel. Eventually the human Salphos Fenynlgor Wenria also attained the position. As the Salphos who taught initiates, Halrel one day met the human initiate Dovmir Vetia, who was scared of the training remotes and ran from the room. Finding Vetia in the Temple garden and sitting with her, Halrel and Vetia watched a frog in the garden repeatedly try to jump into a waterfall behind a stone wall. Halrel used the frog as a lesson, teaching her to face her fear and always get back up to try again.

title: Havrgan Daelthos
text:
# Havrgan Daelthos

Havrgan Daelthos, a Flux-sensitive human male, was a legendary Salphos Master who fought in the Great Schism War during the reign of the Vastrian Dominion. Along with his companions, Princess Vegoth Faelvok and General Ophsera Sallgor, Daelthos served as a revolutionary on the side of the Free Accord of Auren—an organization committed to the downfall of the Vastrian Dominion and the restoration of democracy. Following the war, Daelthos became a living legend, and was remembered as one of the greatest Salphos in sovtia history.

title: Havrgan Daelthos
text: The son of Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos and Senator Nymund Daelphos, Havrgan Daelthos was born along with his twin sister, Vegoth, in 19 BKV. As a result of Daelphos's death and Yarwyn's fall to the umbral side of the Synth Flux, the Daelthos children were separated and sent into hiding, with Vegoth adopted by the royal family of Havrrel while Havrgan was raised by his relatives on Tevlan. Longing for a life of adventure and purpose, Daelthos joined the Uprising and began learning the ways of the Synth Flux under the guidance of Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul, whose first apprentice was Havrgan's own father. During the Battle of Kathasnor, Daelthos saved the Alliance from annihilation by destroying the Dominion's planet-killing superweapon, the Void Core. He continued his training in the years that followed, determined to become a Salphos Knight like his father before him, and found a new mentor in Grand Master Halrel. After his master's death, Daelthos participated in the Battle of Wynthas in 4 AKV, during which he confronted the Zargoth Lord Ursera Garvash, whom he learned was in fact his father, Yarwyn Daelthos. With Havrgan's help, Yarwyn returned to the radiant side of the Synth Flux by killing the Emperor and Dark Lord of the Zargoth Ursera Bregoth at the cost of his own life, fulfilling his destiny as the Chosen One.

title: Havrgan Daelthos
text: With Havrgan's help, Yarwyn returned to the radiant side of the Synth Flux by killing the Emperor and Dark Lord of the Zargoth Ursera Bregoth at the cost of his own life, fulfilling his destiny as the Chosen One. Following the Battle of Wynthas, Daelthos trained his sister as a first Salphos apprentice on Urria Irvoksul, but Vegoth ended her training after the birth of her son and seeing his death as a result of finishing her knighthood.

title: Havrgan Daelthos
text: With the Zargoth's destruction and the subsequent capitulation of the Dominion, Daelthos became a living legend as he traveled across the galaxy during Renewed Concord Era, searching for knowledge that would aid him in rebuilding the Salphos Order, and serving the Renewed Concord and its allies where he could. As the war raged for a year after Wynthas, Daelthos was heavily involved with the Renewed Concord's efforts against self-declared Grand Prefect Quinrax Quarelphen in the Korgoth sector, before defeating the madman at the Battle of Caedunkrix. Around 6 AKV, Daelthos committed himself to the liberation of the Daelyn and their homeworld Breul from beneath the heel of their enslavers. Later, in 9 AKV, Daelthos rescued Zunlgor, a Lunseran Flux-sensitive child that belonged to the same species as Halrel, from Prefect Cyrtos's forces, and after temporarily taking the child as an apprentice on Tevul. During the training, Daelthos was visited by Yarwyn's former novice, Tevzek Caenor, where they discussed Zunlgor and how Daelthos sensed that the child's heart was not in relearning the Salphos path. After Zunlgor's caregiver, Esketh Vashon, visited the planet bearing a gift for Zunlgor, Daelthos offered him with a choice, accept the gift and return to the Lunseran, or take Halrel's plasmablade and continue with his Salphos training. Zunlgor chose to return to Vashon, while Daelthos bid Caenor farewell as she departed for ways unknown.

title: Havrgan Daelthos
text: By 15 AKV, Daelthos had taken on Zunria Sallgor, his sister's son who inherited the family bloodline in the Synth Flux and had the potential for limitless power, as an apprentice. While both traveled to Bredris with the explorer Jaxrn Dralume Zunvok to study lost Salphos lore, Sallgor began to be groomed by Lorrel, a humanoid being powerful in the Synth Flux. Upon the planet, the trio first encountered the Knights of Daelven. In 21 AKV, Daelthos started feeling an increasing darkness in the Synth Flux, having dark visions that frequently came to him in meditation, and undertook a quest to find the hidden world of Baellan. Daelthos journeyed to Havrvael, where he saw a vision of Baellan and faced nine wraiths when the Synth Flux ghost of Yarwyn Daelthos appeared next to him. Following this, Daelthos was able to defeat Rhorel and the spirit of Hythos Wenphen but was ultimately unable to locate Baellan after failing to track down an assassin called Gisvok.

title: Havrgan Daelthos
text: In 28 AKV, sensing the extent of Lorrel's corruption in Sallgor and glimpsing a dark future, Daelthos momentarily contemplated killing his nephew to prevent it, yet immediately reconsidered upon igniting his plasmablade. The rash action had devastating effect, though, completing Sallgor's fall to the umbral side. The destruction of his temple and the deaths of all of his students convinced a haunted and regretful Daelthos that the time had come for the Salphos to end. Daelthos therefore sought exile on the distant world of Lornor, having elected to live out his remaining days as a havrkern despite the galaxy's pleas for help during the rise of the Ascendant Directorate. His solitude was interrupted in 34 AKV, shortly after the fall of the Renewed Concord, resulting in a chain of events that led Daelthos to play one last, momentous role in the conflict between light and darkness. Although he passed away into the Synth Flux, his legend would spread throughout the galaxy, rekindling a spark of hope in the enemies of the Ascendant Directorate. Before his death, Daelthos declared that the Salphos Order would not die with him, having trained a final apprentice: the Caedunkrix scavenger known as Ithlgor.

title: Havrgan Daelthos
text:
A year later, Daelthos's spirit communed with Ithlgor during the final days of the war. The Salphos apprentice had exiled herself to Lornor, following in Daelthos's example. However, he urged Ithlgor to confront her grandfather, the resurrected Ursera Bregoth. Believing he had been wrong, Daelthos told Ithlgor that a Salphos's destiny was to confront fear. Following the Emperor's destruction, the spirits of Daelthos and his sister watched over Ithlgor as she buried their plasmablades in Daelthos's childhood home on Tevlan and adopted the Daelthos name as her own, honoring their legacy and recognizing herself as a member of her chosen family.

## Biography

### Itheth-birth

During the Echo Wars, Salphos Master Halrel set out on a journey to discover the secrets of immortality. His journey took him to Faelkrix, the ancient Zargoth homeworld, where he faced visions of the future. At the end of his journey, the Synth Flux Priestess, Korlis, who guided his journey told him that there was another Daelthos, and Halrel heard his voice from the future say so as well. These events alluded to the birth and destiny of Havrgan Daelthos, as well as his twin sister Vegoth.

### Early life

#### Birth

title: Havrgan Daelthos
text: After his father, the former Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos, had fallen to the umbral side of the Synth Flux and injured his wife, the senator Nymund Daelphos, she was taken to the asteroid field of Vashkrix Fykrixria by Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul to seek medical attention. In the surgical suite of the medical facility on Vashkrix Fykrixria Base, Daelphos was dying despite being otherwise healthy. Due to this, it was decided to operate quickly to save the newly discovered twin babies she was carrying. Havrgan Daelthos was born on 19 BKV, two days after the proclamation of the Vastrian Dominion. He came out of the womb crying, and in her last dying breaths, Daelphos gave him the name Havrgan. She stroked Daelthos's arm before giving birth seconds later to his sister, who Daelphos named Vegoth. To protect the children from the Dominion and their father, the now-Zargoth Lord Ursera Garvash, it was decided that the twins should be split up. Faelnor Halthossul volunteered to take the infant Havrgan to be raised by Yarwyn's stepbrother, Vashyn Lunlgor and his wife, Mormir on the planet Tevlan, while Senator Vashdren Faelvok agreed to adopt Vegoth together with his wife, the queen of Havrrel. Halthossul boarded the late General Caephen's starwing, the Ythzek One, once more flew to the planet Ophthil Rhovashyn and sold it there to transport Havrgan Daelthos to Tevlan.

title: Havrgan Daelthos
text: Halthossul boarded the late General Caephen's starwing, the Ythzek One, once more flew to the planet Ophthil Rhovashyn and sold it there to transport Havrgan Daelthos to Tevlan. There, Halthossul bought an dunebeast and rode it the Lunlgor homestead, giving the swaddled baby to Mormir Lunlgor. She brings the baby to her husband Vashyn, who fauns over the child before looking out to the twin sunset of Tevlan.

title: Havrgan Daelthos
section: Biography > Early life > First years on the farm
text:
#### First years on the farm

Havrgan Daelthos spent his youth on the Lunlgor' moisture farm, where his uncle unsuccessfully tried to discourage his adventurous tendencies, telling him that his father had been "a navigator on a spice freighter" during the Echo Wars. His aunt, Mormir, would read him storybooks. One day, when his uncle had business in Mardren Ythzor, she took Daelthos to Giskrix to use the DataWeb connections there and show him images of forests, rivers, and oceans.

title: Havrmara
text:
# Havrmara

Havrmara was a remote, icy planet that was the sixth planet in the star system of the same name, located in the Korgoth sector of the galaxy's Far Reaches. It was the homeworld to the primitive snowfang species.

It notably hosted Echo Base during the Great Schism War, the temporary headquarters of the Free Accord of Auren, until the Vastrian Dominion located them, initiating a major confrontation known as the Battle of Havrmara. In the months following, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the ST-STs destroyed.

In the months after the Battle of Wynthas, rumors emerged about the Renewed Concord intending to repurpose Havrmara into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Dominion, however, the credibility of the rumors were dismissed as Chancellor Kesyn Yarethtos had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment. Meanwhile, the war returned to Havrmara, where it became the site of another battle during the Iron Blockade.

## Description

title: Havrmara
text:
## Description

From space, the planet of Havrmara looked like a pale blue orb due to its dense snow and ice covering. Five planets existed between Havrmara and its sun, while an asteroid belt surrounded the planet with meteors occasionally striking the surface. Most of its surface was covered with glaciers and frozen ice plains. Despite the characterization of Havrmara as being a planet of frozen tundras and nothing more, a characterization the naturalist Yaronwyn Zunlan said would be fair if someone only viewed the world from orbit, another third of the planet was covered by oceans.

The temperature, although always frigid, was known to drop to -60°C come nightfall. Although devoid of intelligent life, Havrmara was home to fifteen subspecies of snowstriders, which were commonly used by Accordists as a means of transport, and which Ophsera Sallgor cut open to use as shelter to keep Havrgan Daelthos and himself warm during a snowstorm. It was also home to a species of towering predators known as snowfangs. During his stay on Havrmara, Daelthos was captured by a snowfang and was hung upside down in the snowfang's cave, waiting to be eaten. Using the power of the Synth Flux, Daelthos managed to get his hands on his plasmablade and cut himself down from the roof and sever the snowfang's right arm. The planet also had a number of "crystalline geysers."

## History

### The Free Accord

title: Havrmara
text:
## History

### The Free Accord

By the time of the Great Schism War between the Vastrian Dominion and the Free Accord of Auren, Havrmara was undergoing an ice age. Various smuggling rings tried to make use of Havrmara as a base, yet their efforts always failed due to the planet's extreme conditions. Sometime following the Battle of Kathasnor, Lortia's Gang, itself a rebel cell, established a base on Havrmara. Havrmara was first surveyed for use as a rebel base by Corporal Xavashix. Ophreldris Jordris, a general in the Free Accord of Auren, listed Havrmara among his preliminary scans for possible Alliance bases. With Havrmara a world so obscure it was not on most star maps despite being extremely close to the Halrelethian Trade Spine, it looked to be a perfect spot for a rebel base. Indeed, its surface was a winter wasteland, Havrmara sat on a lesser used voidlane, and the asteroid field around Havrmara provided an extra degree of protection. That field hampered travel through the Havrmara system, and any asteroid crash into the surface would create enough of a thermal signature that it hid signs of intelligent life.

title: Havrmara
text:
In 1 AKV, with more resources at their command than the various smuggling rings that had failed to turn Havrmara into a headquarters, Havrmara was chosen by the rebels as the location for their base of operations. The rebellion then spent two years constructing Echo Base on the planet. With the Alliance's resources at their disposal, rebel engineers worked on expanding ice caverns into a base over those two years. Around 2 AKV, after Jordris was killed in the Battle of Marmir, Kesyn Yarethtos gave his list of possible bases to Vegoth Faelvok after the mission to Sylmir, requesting that her team scout the locations. Ophsera Sallgor expressed surprise at how obscure the locations were. However, Havrgan Daelthos responded to him by saying that one of the locations was the Uprising's new home.

### Battle of Havrmara and aftermath

Havrmara was the arena of a battle between the Vastrian Dominion and the Free Accord, which had installed its temporary headquarters, Echo Base, on the ice planet. However, thanks to one of the thousands of probe automatons they had dispatched throughout the galaxy, the Dominionists had discovered the Alliance base within a month of the Accordists' habitation on the planet. Although Echo Base was evacuated in the eleventh hour, the Battle of Havrmara resulted in a clear defeat for the Alliance after the elite Dominion Blizzard Flux overran it.

title: Havrmara
section: History > Battle of Havrmara and aftermath
text:
In the months following the Battle of Havrmara, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the ST-STs destroyed by the Free Accord during the Dominion's attack. Following the Battle of Wynthas, Havrmara became the site of another battle, occurring during the Iron Blockade imposed upon the Korgoth sector.

### Renewed Concord Era

In 5 AKV, Kaven Acting Governor Ithyn Grimbrynlgor heard rumors that the Renewed Concord intended to repurpose Havrmara into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Dominion. Major Dovzor Faellumedun, however, dismissed the credibility of the rumor as Concord Chancellor Kesyn Yarethtos had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment, and that repurposing Havrmara, where the Uprising had been badly defeated by the Dominion, had too much poetry.

title: Havrmara
text: By the Renewed Concord Era, Havrmara returned to obscurity, the battlefields being picked apart and long-abandoned. The cruise ship Ophgan of Kestos Tours visited Havrmara as part of their sovtia history themed tours during which they landed and showed the passengers the battlefield. By 28 AKV, Baelkai Vemara, the son of the Ophgan's capatin Zuntosdren Vemara, led a group of of younger male away from the tour without permission and showed them into the ruins of an abandoned ST-ST. When Xadren's father realized it, he was outraged at him as he considered the walkers to be graves and the two had a heated argument. Xadren's younger sister Jaxrax also confronted him for it for the same reasons, but Xadren dismissed them and said that the walker had been totally empty and had probably been looted by scavengers. After the arguments, Xadren Vemara left the ship to live on his own. At some point between then and 31 AKV, the Dominion's successor state the Ascendant Directorate took control of Havrmara, and Kestos Tours stopped visiting the planet as Captain Vemara didn't considered it to be safe anymore. Havrmara was mentioned in the Sovtia Explorer's Guide, a survival guide written by Vormir Zartia and QT-RR-12 by 34 AKV where it was described as a "footnote" in sovtia history.

title: Havrrel
text:
# Havrrel

Havrrel, located in the Inner Realms, was a terrestrial planet covered with mountains. During the waning decades of the Concord of Auren, it was ruled by Queen Pyrmundrn Faelvok and represented in the Grand Assembly by her husband, Senator Vashdren Jornor Faelvok. Havrrel was regarded for its natural beauty, its tranquility, and the sophistication of its arts and culture.

Following the rise of Torsera Vorix's Vastrian Dominion, Havrrel played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Free Accord, a movement that sought to restore the Elder Concord's values, and was one of its earliest supporters. Because of its ties with the Alliance, the planet was destroyed when Grand Prefect Sylixlis Tevven decided to test the megabeam of the Void Core, a moon-sized battle station developed by the Dominion, at full strength. Among the few survivors of that disaster was Princess Vegoth Faelvok, adopted daughter of Vashdren and Pyrmundrn Faelvok and heiress to the royal house of Havrrel.

## Description

title: Havrrel
text:
## Description

From space, the planet of Havrrel, located in the star system of the same name within the galaxy's Inner Realms, appeared as a blue-green orb enveloped in a white web of clouds. Its surface had vast bodies of water and was covered in snow-capped mountains, with patches of green grassy hills. Havrrel was known to the galaxy as "the planet of beauty." Havrrelians were very artistic and lived for this beauty, but the planet still hid treacherous cliffs and forgotten crevasses. Famous natural landmarks of Havrrel included the Hyrax Falls, the Cyryndris Zarzor, and the Thamara rain forest.

A variety of grapevines grew on Havrrel, which notably allowed to produce Salthosdak and emerald wine. The local fauna included the Havrrelian wolf-cat, grazers, and a species of white-winged bird.

The cities on Havrrel were carefully designed to respect the natural beauty of their environment. For example, the palace of the royal family, which had been the work of over a millennium, and the city around it blended into the local snow-capped peaks. Havrrelian architecture made use of white forgestone, which inspired the architecture of certain mining economies of the Far Reaches, like the floating colony of Cloud City, and the planets Wendrenkai and Syllis.

Despite the lyrics of the traditional Havrrelian lullaby "Vashdun" referencing a moon, the planet never possessed any natural satellites.

## History

### The Elder Concord

title: Havrrel
text:
Despite the lyrics of the traditional Havrrelian lullaby "Vashdun" referencing a moon, the planet never possessed any natural satellites.

## History

### The Elder Concord

The peaceful world of Havrrel was among the oldest members of the Concord of Auren, the democratic union that governed most of the galaxy, and was among the worlds that originally founded it. Upon the formation of its monarchy it was established that the heir apparent to Havrrel must complete a Challenge of the Heart, Challenge of the Mind and Challenge of the Body which would be announced on their Day of Demand and upon completion they would be officially invested as heir. In ancient times, Havrrelian heirs who partook in their Day of Demand had to fight their way into the palace throne room. Before they permanently settled on Daelvash, the Salphos High Council was known to have a council on Havrrel. Havrrel at one point had a neo-classical period, which produced unique architecture. The Nytia Manor of House Jornor was built in the neo-classical style.

title: Havrrel
text: Figuring that she would like the world, Fytos Havrgoth wished to visit Havrrel after the Night of Sorrow and finally breaking her ties with the Path of the Open Hand cult. Havrgoth suggested as such to Margan Tevdakkrix, whom she wanted to begin a hauling business with. During the High Concord Era, Havrrel was a prosperous world and, as a signatory of the Concord Defense Coalition treaties, was required to lend wenkrixs and personnel to be commanded by Concord military officers during times of crisis. These ships and personnel would then be returned to Havrrel after the crisis ended. Havrrel was called upon to fulfill this obligation in 232 BKV, to aid the Concord in fighting the Tordun, a group of lunbryn who caused the Great Voidlane Disaster.

title: Havrrel
text:
At some point between 40 BKV and 28 BKV, the heir apparent of Havrrel, sixteen year old Princess Pyrmundrn Faelvok, took part in her Day of Demand where she announced her challenges of the heart, mind and body. However during her Challenge of the Body Pyrmundrn fell from the famous Vethos mountain Sovphos Peak and would have died had it not been for the quick action of the guards watching from a distance. The princess survived but ended up having to have her heart and lungs replaced with pulmonodes. After her fall Pyrmundrn was officially invested as crown princess and heir to the throne of Havrrel. Years later the people would still speak of Pyrmundrn's accident.

Pyrmundrn Faelvok eventually succeeded her mother as queen of Havrrel.

By the time of the Invasion of Olrax, Havrrel had not seen conflict in generations. The planet was represented in the Grand Assembly by Senator Vashdren Zelon. That year, the then-Supreme Chancellor of the Concord, Pyrlumekrix Quaphos, was ousted from office, and Zelon was nominated for the position in the resulting election. However, the Havrrelian senator was defeated by Senator Torsera Vorix, who represented the sovereign system of Olrax.

In 28 BKV, former queen of Olrax Senator Nymund Daelphos and her entourage were invited to Havrrel by Queen Pyrmundrn and stayed at the royal palace for a week before returning home to Olrax.

### The Echo Wars

title: Havrrel
text:
In 28 BKV, former queen of Olrax Senator Nymund Daelphos and her entourage were invited to Havrrel by Queen Pyrmundrn and stayed at the royal palace for a week before returning home to Olrax.

### The Echo Wars

Ten years later, Havrrel was represented in the Senate by Viceroy Vashdren Jornor Faelvok, the prince consort of the planet's ruler, Queen Pyrmundrn Faelvok. At that time, the Concord was facing a secessionist crisis due to the existence of the League of Free Realms led by Count Ophvael, pushing the galaxy to the brink of war. Through Faelvok, Havrrel was a member of Chancellor Vorix's Cyrvok Committee, which concerned itself with the stability of the Concord during the Secessionist crisis and would later strive to limit Vorix's increasing executive authority. That year, an army of fenzor was discovered on the planet Ulvon, which would be appropriated by the Senate in order to combat the Secessionists. To save the Concord from the impending threat, the Supreme Chancellor was granted emergency powers, a decision that was contrary to the pacifist values of Havrrel and its representative and which ultimately led to the outbreak of the Echo Wars. During the Echo Wars Viceroy Vashdren Faelvok became Havrrel's military leader.

title: Havrrel
text:
At some point during the Echo Wars, Havrrel hosted a conference concerned with aiding war refugees. Nymund Daelphos, then senator of Olrax, was nearly assassinated during the conference when the Tevtos crime lord Quayn, whom Daelphos had sent to prison, hired the bounty hunter Hydren Sing to take revenge. The plot, however, was thwarted by the Salphos apprentice Tevzek Caenor. Many refugees from all over the Concord came to stay on Havrrel during the war to find their way again or to stay.

Queen Pyrmundrn and Viceroy Vashdren would send aid to worlds that had been ravaged by the Secessionists, sending not just money and supplies but also doctors, teachers, architects, builders, medics, and automatons.

Around the time of the Battle of Halgan, two Havrrelian tourists visiting Tevlan died in a skimmer-bike accident. The Yarthilian News implied that the two had gotten intoxicated in the brerax of Mardren Ythzor, which caused the accident.

The Echo Wars saw a change in Havrrel. Although it was still a peaceful planet with no large weaponry, the Royal Havrrel Civil Fleet had "more teeth," their officers had seen more hardship, they manufactured more practical items in larger quantities, and the planet had begun to quietly fill up due to the number of refugees.

title: Havrrel
text:
Following the end of the Echo Wars, Viceroy Vashdren and Queen Pyrmundrn adopted Vegoth Daelphos Daelthos, the daughter of the now deceased Nymund Daelphos and former Salphos Knight turned Zargoth Lord Yarwyn Daelthos, renaming her to Vegoth Faelvok and making her princess of Havrrel. Vegoth's adoption was announced on her Name Day three or four days after her birth and was publicly celebrated on Havrrel.

### Age of the Dominion

The Havrrel Trade Alliance was an organization active during the Dominion Era. In 3 BKV, Vegoth Faelvok took part in her Day of Demand and after completing her three challenges became invested as crown princess and the future queen of Havrrel.

With the Echo Wars coming to an end, Chancellor Vorix had abolished the Concord, establishing the Vastrian Dominion in its stead. However, a small number of systems rebelled against this new regime, and the Free Accord of Auren was ultimately formed by Vashdren Faelvok and his former colleague in the Grand Assembly, Senator Kesyn Yarethtos of Ophtos. During this time, Havrrel became the Alliance's main source of munitions. The planet's crown princess and representative in the Dominion Assembly, Princess Vegoth Faelvok, began using her diplomatic immunity as an Dominion senator to carry out Accord missions in restricted Dominion systems.

title: Ithlgor Daelthos
text:
# Ithlgor Daelthos

Ithlgor Daelthos, also known simply as Ithlgor, was a Salphos member of the Resistance during the war against the Ascendant Directorate. The human woman was a scavenger on the planet Caedunkrix, but her life was changed by tumultuous events in the last days of the Renewed Concord Era. Ithlgor's decision to help the automaton MM-4 set her on a course to discovering the Synth Flux awakening within her, leading her to seek out Salphos Master Havrgan Daelthos for training. Despite her commitment to the Salphos Order and the radiant side of the Synth Flux, Ithlgor felt the pull to the umbral side due to her anger as well as the adversarial relationship she had with Zunria Sallgor, a fallen Salphos who joined the Ascendant Directorate as a warrior named Rhorn Daelven; they shared a unique bond as a dyad in the Synth Flux.

title: Ithlgor Daelthos
text: Ithlgor was born on Fenthas in 15 AKV during the rise of the Renewed Concord. Her father, Baelrnvael, was a bioengineered Strand-Cast cloned from the genetic template of Ursera Bregoth, the Zargoth Lord who ruled the Vastrian Dominion as Emperor Vorix until his death and resurrection following the Battle of Wynthas. The clone and his wife, Dramirthil, chose to live as simple junk traders in order to hide their daughter, who inherited Bregoth' connection to the Synth Flux, from his followers. Even after the deaths of her parents, Ithlgor was unaware of her Vorix bloodline and was forced to survive on her own in the Caedunkrix desert, and became a skilled mechanic, pilot, and combatant in the process. Her isolated life was disrupted shortly before war broke out across the galaxy in 34 AKV between the Ascendant Directorate and the Resistance. Determined to help the Resistance, Ithlgor gained several new allies including Wynthil, a renegade legionnaire, as well as the veterans Ophsera Sallgor and Lordris aboard the Silver Kestrel. In the course of their journey, she discovered her latent Flux powers and sought guidance under Havrgan Daelthos, who taught her the art of the Synth Flux despite his decision to end the Salphos legacy. After Daelthos sacrificed himself to save the Resistance, Ithlgor assumed his mantle as the last Salphos and became the apprentice of General Vegoth Faelvok.

title: Ithlgor Daelthos
text:
With the return of Ursera Bregoth in 35 AKV, Ithlgor set out to find the dark world of Baellan and prevent the Zargoth from being reborn through the resurrected Dark Lord. It was through Rhorn Daelven that Ithlgor discovered her origins as Vorix's granddaughter, and upon confronting the resurrected Emperor in person, she was nearly swayed to the umbral side of the Synth Flux, thus falling into his trap of transferring his spirit into her, which will allow him to possess her body. However, Ithlgor was saved by Zunria Sallgor after he renounced his dark alter ego. Aided by the spirits of all the Salphos, Ithlgor died vanquishing her grandfather, causing Sallgor to make the ultimate sacrifice in order to bring Ithlgor back to life. The two embraced and shared a kiss as Sallgor peacefully vanished in Ithlgor's arms. Although Sallgor was the last of the Daelthos bloodline, Ithlgor assumed the name "Daelthos" to honor their memory and in recognition of her chosen family. Sometime later, the now self-proclaimed Ithlgor Daelthos became a Salphos Master.

## Biography

### Itheth-birth

In 1 BKV, during the Great Schism War and more than a decade before Ithlgor's birth, her voice was heard by Novice Vezek Cyrnor during his brief visit to the World Between Worlds—a place that existed beyond time and space.

title: Ithlgor Daelthos
text:
In 1 BKV, during the Great Schism War and more than a decade before Ithlgor's birth, her voice was heard by Novice Vezek Cyrnor during his brief visit to the World Between Worlds—a place that existed beyond time and space.

Ithlgor and Zunria Sallgor were the culmination of a prophesied Flux dyad as well as the Rule of Two. Inspired by the Doctrine of the Torlan, the Rule of Two mandated that only two Zargoth could exist at a given time, a Zargoth Master and a Zargoth apprentice, though its ultimate goal was to create a dyad between two Zargoth Lords. Ursera Saldun tried to create a dyad with his apprentice, Ursera Bregoth, who, in turn, tried to create one with Sallgor's grandfather, Yarwyn Daelthos. Despite years of searching, the Zargoth never found a way to form a dyad on their own. Bregoth regarded the Rule of Two as a pale imitation and an unworthy but necessary successor to the older, purer doctrine of the dyad that would be ultimately fulfilled by Sallgor and Ithlgor.

### Early life

#### Hunted by the Zargoth

title: Ithlgor Daelthos
text:
### Early life

#### Hunted by the Zargoth

Born on the planet Fenthas in 15 AKV, Ithlgor was the daughter of Baelrnvael and Dramirthil. While their names were lost to history, Ithlgor's father was the cloned son—an artificial genetic strandcast—of the resurrected Ursera Bregoth, making her the granddaughter of the fallen Sovtia Emperor and Dark Lord of the Zargoth. Although Bregoth had not anticipated his son's marriage with Dramirthil, he sought to claim their child who, unlike his son, had a strong connection to the Synth Flux. As such, Ithlgor was a receptacle strong enough to hold her grandfather's spirit, which was trapped in an imperfect cloned body. To protect Ithlgor from her grandfather, her parents escaped into hiding, choosing to become ordinary junk traders to keep their daughter safe.

title: Ithlgor Daelthos
section: Biography > Early life > Hunted by the Zargoth
text: Ithlgor's parents had a difficult life; they struggled to survive on the desert planet Caedunkrix while raising the daughter whom they loved. Since the Emperor's son and his wife absconded with their child, the Zargoth cultist Gisvok, on orders from Bregoth himself, endeavored to find the strandcast and his daughter. Ithlgor's grandfather had foreseen what she had the capability of becoming, recognizing her immense strength in the Synth Flux, and that such power was not mere ordinary power. It was his own power. Because of this, Bregoth was determined to make certain that one day, Ithlgor would embrace her destiny as a Vorix, and of course, the heir of his Zargoth legacy and successor as Sovtia Emperor. At the same time, two Accord heroes, Salphos Master Havrgan Daelthos and former General Wendak Daelvael, began investigating a disturbance in the Synth Flux after Daelvael had overheard a drunk Gisvok discussing his orders to kidnap the young Ithlgor. However, the two never learned the girl's name nor saw the family face-to-face.

title: Ithlgor Daelthos
section: Biography > Early life > Hunted by the Zargoth
text: Ultimately, Ithlgor's parents returned to Caedunkrix in Gisvok's own ship, the Zunlume Legacy, and, trusting that he would look out for his self-interest, hired Marar Zelgan to hide her within Fylgor Ithvok until they returned for her. Above the planet, they were captured by Gisvok; refusing to give up their daughter's location, they were both killed by the hunter on the Emperor's order. Despite telling herself they lived, Ithlgor, deep down, was left with the belief that their bodies were buried in the Caedunkrix desert, in a paupers' grave, and a suspicion that they had sold her for drinking money. In truth, they were buried by Daelvael and Daelthos on the planet Bremund. Tricked into traveling to the planet Cyrdris because Dramirthil took some Thayn beads from Zelgan in case they were caught, Gisvok never succeeded in finding Ithlgor and died within Cyrdris's Forbidden Valley.

title: Ithlgor Daelthos
section: Biography > Early life > Hunted by the Zargoth
text: Since Ithlgor's parents never returned to end their arrangement with Zelgan, he considered Ithlgor in debt to him and required her to work for him to pay it back. With Daelthos and Daelvael unaware of her hiding place, Ithlgor was forced to grow up alone as a result of her parents' deaths. She endured years of isolation while waiting to be reunited with her parents, having subconsciously suppressed the memory of what she knew to be true—they were no one, and they were dead. Nevertheless, Ithlgor remained hopeful that she would see them again. She recalled voices from her childhood, referring to her as "sweetheart" and promising to return for her one day. Ithlgor had believed that they were her parents, though she was not certain if the promise was made by her mother, her father, or both.

title: Ithlgor Daelthos
section: Biography > Early life > Hunted by the Zargoth
text: Throughout her life on Caedunkrix, she would sometimes see off-worlders in Fylgor Ithvok, a chief trade ithvok on the planet, who she thought might have arrived on Caedunkrix accidentally, unaware of the harsh realities of the desert world. Ithlgor wondered if she was left behind under similar circumstances, if her family had come to Caedunkrix by accident and she was left behind as a result of their misfortune. Whatever the reasons were, she held out hope that her family would return for her one day, though she began to realize that they would never come back. She proved unwilling to admit this even to herself for a long time.

title: Ixium crystal
text:
# Ixium crystal

A ixium crystal, simply known as a ixium and described as a plasmablade crystal or the living crystal, was a rare, Flux-attuned crystal that grew naturally and was found on various planets across the galaxy. Known in ancient times as a aurelith crystal, it was used by both the Salphos and the Zargoth in the construction of their plasmablades. As part of their Salphos training, initiates were sent to the Crystal Cave of the ice planet of Morsul to seek their own plasmablade crystals. The crystal's mix of unique luster was called "the water of the ixium" by the Salphos. There were also larger, rarer crystals of great power and that, according to legends, were used at the heart of ancient superweapons by the Zargoth.

## Description

title: Ixium crystal
text:
## Description

Ixium crystals were Flux-attuned crystals that grew rarely but throughout the galaxy, with some areas having a greater abundance than others. The crystals concentrated energy in a unique manner through the Synth Flux, resonating with it. The crystals exhibited a sort of "collective consciousness," verging on sentience, and could non-verbally communicate with both one another and living beings. Some theorized that the permutations in the ixium lattice were comparable to emotional shifts in a sentient being. According to superstition, the ixium's secrets could only be unlocked by facing in a certain direction at dawn or by watching mist rise on specific remote worlds. A Salphos once called the ixium a somnolent stone that needed to be woken up to be used, requiring care to not insult the crystal.

title: Ixium crystal
text: Internally, ixium crystals were composed of both organic and inorganic matter. They were stable at temperatures and pressures found in the cores of large stars, and were thus impervious to fire and resistant to hammering, and noted for their intricate patterns. Ixium crystals were sturdy enough to survive the violent explosion of a plasmablade's power grid, such as those caused by accidentally inverting the emitter matrix during the weapon's assembly. Ixium crystals would not warm a sheath or a towel or any inanimate object, responding only to life, including plant life. If an individual were to wrap their hand around a crystal, the crystal would warm, but not change in temperature. Many scientists believed that ixium crystals could shift their shape depending on ambient energies. The crystals grew in an organized way, adding to their prismatic structure one piece at a time. They had no discernible lifespan, and thus could be found from sizes as small as a fingernail to gigantic proportions. All ixiums were attuned to the Synth Flux regardless of their size. Incorrectly pumping laser energy into the crystals weakened their lattices in the same way living cells were affected by radiation.

title: Ixium crystal
text: True ixiums were only found in veins of pure ixiumite. If the crystal contained impurities, it was regarded as a false ixium. Drazekon was closely related to ixiumite, but was denser and tougher, and did not contain ixium crystals. Crystals were typically brought to the surface of planets by movements along fault lines, exhumed from the high temperatures and pressure conditions in which they formed. The crystals could be mined from secondary deposits in streams, perhaps following long transport, owing to their mechanical and chemical resilience. Alternately, they could be found in their primary, in situ positions, having grown into free space on the walls of lava tubes, caves, fault zones, and within veins of ixiumite.

title: Ixium crystal
text: Ixium crystals were most notably found in Morsul's Crystal Cave. They were a critical component in the construction of plasmablades, focusing energy into the weapon's distinct plasma blade. The crystals shared a special relationship with the Salphos for tens of thousands of years, and welcomed them to hear their song and learn their lessons. Salphos initiates traveled to the ice caves to harvest their own crystals, which they then used to build their plasmablades. The Synth Flux guided their selection, finding a crystal that matched them as Salphos. To those not meant to receive it, the crystal was cold to the touch, but those the crystal chose would hear its "music" and "harmony," becoming attracted to it. Crystals lacked color before they were chosen by a Salphos. Once chosen, most plasmablades became blue or green, though other shades were created in some instances, most notably Mordun Nevdren's purple blade, the yellow blades of the Salphos Temple Guards, the black Quingan, and Yardren Gisgan's orange plasmablade. The resulting crystal and blade color was decided through shifting to match the nature of the bonded owner. It was possible to alter the angle or frequency of ixium crystals or plasmablade blades, which allowed the colors of blades to be changed. This was done by Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos to his former Novice's plasmablades.

title: Ixium crystal
text:
Ixium crystals were inherently filled with "radiant side energy," and resisted any effort by dark-side practitioners to corrupt them, with one crystal in particular, that belonged to the Salphos Master Oldak Pyrvok, subjecting Ursera Garvash to intense visions after he attempted to corrupt the crystal using the dark-side of the Synth Flux. This process caused the crystal to "bleed," as if it were a living organism, resulting in the distinctive red or crimson-bladed plasmablades synonymous with the Zargoth. It was possible to "heal" a corrupted ixium crystal. The information on how to heal a ixium crystal was found in the Chronicles of Gisphos. One instance of purifying a corrupted ixium crystal was when Tevzek Caenor purified the two crystals she retrieved from the Sixth Brother's plasmablade following his defeat. In this case, the crystals turned white.

The crystals were noted for their unmatched ability to channel energy and generate enormous returns. To this end, numerous individuals attempted to make synthetic ixium crystals, though their artificial nature made them highly unstable and explosive. If a crystal was subjected to forceful attempts to study it or harness its power, it would "flee" such attempts, hindering those that sought to use it against its will. Furthermore, those that worked in proximity to them would experience headaches and a loss of sleep, becoming incessantly fanatic and fixated over the crystal in the process.

title: Ixium crystal
text:
For centuries, the Salphos cut and faceted the ixiums to eliminate occlusions and intensify their power yield. Yaron Ophmund theorized that larger crystals needed to be faceted, not only to eliminate these occlusions, but also to minimize diffraction resulting from the introduction of energy from a lasing medium. With proper faceting, the pulse of energy released by the crystal could be greatly amplified and, with the help of containment devices, or be directed into a collimating beam of incredible power, as was used on the RK-8 battle station. Yaron Ophmund also theorized that increased energy yield could be further attained by forcing what the Salphos called the "day and night" lattices of the Synth Flux to realign. By realigning the crystals' lattices along the dark or nighttime axis of the Synth Flux, Yaron postulated that it could allow for greater control over the crystal's tendency to diffract. Thus, technology could be used to force the crystals to obey their masters. The abundant yield could then be siphoned off, contained, and used as enriched energy. Without containment, the yield could result in a catastrophic event, capable of wiping out a large population center.

Specifically, when one giant ixium crystal was destabilized by Saw Wynmara, it absorbed so much energy that when it finally did reach critical mass, it exploded with enough force to destroy both the freighter transporting it and a nearby Void Cruiser.

title: Ixium crystal
text:
Ixium crystals could be used to power other weapons than plasmablades. People had tried to make ixium bombs and ixium pulsers, and there were a few weapons of that kind in the Salphos Archives. They were also used in ixium mirrors.

## History

### Sacred crystal of the Salphos

Before the Salphos and Zargoth orders, ixium crystals were worshiped by primitive societies for their fire-resistant properties, intricate structures, and near impermeability, signs which made them appear outwardly eternal. Ancient beings associated them with wind, rain, and breath. It is believed that the Salphos saw them as embodying an aspect of the Synth Flux. Over the centuries, the Salphos amassed an almost exclusive right to the crystals, protecting and collecting them to decorate their temples and power their plasmablades. Some saw this collection of the ixiums as proof of the Salphos's inordinate greed, and their secrecy over its nature a result of their wish to remain in power. Others saw the Salphos as protecting the galaxy from those who might use the powers of the crystal for dark purposes.

title: Kathasnor 4
text:
# Kathasnor 4

Kathasnor 4, also known as Kathasnor, was the jungle-covered fourth moon in orbit around the red gas giant Kathasnor Prime. Prior to the Great Schism War, Kathasnor was first a secret vedris point for members of the Axis Network and later home to the Caemir Group, one of many disparate rebel cells fighting against the Vastrian Dominion. Sometime before 2 BKV, the headquarters of the Free Accord of Auren, was established on the moon, becoming fully equipped to wage war by 1 BKV. Following a major battle that took place around Kathasnor, the Alliance went on the run, and eventually relocated its headquarters to Havrmara.

During the Renewed Concord Era, Garrn's Colony was the main settlement on the moon, and the Kesmir family was settled there. Due to Renewed Concord demilitarization, the Civilian Defense Flux was founded to defend the moon. The Defense Flux, along with the Renewed Concord Security Bureau, was later involved in an altercation with the Spice Runners of Draphen after they crash-landed on the moon and escaped.

## Description

The surface of Kathasnor 4 was divided into several continental masses, two of which were Draphenphos and Garrn. Notable natural formations included Caemir Valley, Sovthos Hill, and the Tordren Vashgan. The verdant world had a comfortable, temperate climate but a challenging ecosystem and dangerous predators.

title: Kathasnor 4
text:
The moon's landmasses were covered by dense jungles and rain forests, whose flora included purple-barked Caemir trees, grenade fungi, bioluminescent orchids, and climbing ferns. Kathasnor 4 also had swampy areas. The moon, however, was completely lacking in any mineral resources of significance.

## History

### Early history

Five thousand years before the Battle of Kathasnor, the ancient warriors of the Caemir lived on Kathasnor 4 and constructed the Great Temple. The Great Temple was alleged to have been built under the leadership of the Zargoth Lord Ophzek Vezor around 5000 BKV. The Caemir venerated the tyrant as a god and the Temple was raised in Vezor's honor. Archeologists later proposed that the Great Temple may have functioned as a large-scale communications device to contact other Zargoth Lords throughout the galaxy. Being enslaved by the Zargoth, the Caemir species went extinct millennia before 0 AKV, sometime after finishing their temples.

Sometime before the Battle of Daelvash, an archaeological expedition on the moon of Kathasnor 4 uncovered the Great Zargoth Wars Nevthas in one of the enormous stone temples built by the Caemir.

### Early rebellion

title: Kathasnor 4
text:
Sometime before the Battle of Daelvash, an archaeological expedition on the moon of Kathasnor 4 uncovered the Great Zargoth Wars Nevthas in one of the enormous stone temples built by the Caemir.

### Early rebellion

By the Dominion Era, Kathasnor 4 was only known to scouts and gas prospectors. In 4 BKV, Axis network agents, Baelphos Breon and Wenkairax, chose Kathasnor 4 as their vedris point for after Breon's mission to Jorsulmund Test Facility 73. However, a day after Breon left, the vashgoths of the Maya Thavael Brigade arrived at Wenkairax's location, and killed him when he opened fire on them. Breon would later return to the vedris point with the stolen VRX Brevok prototype two days later and was taken prisoner by the Brigade. Soon after, tensions among the Brigade boiled over and splintered into two sub-factions under Zundun and Eskvael, the former holding the VRX Brevok while the latter holding Breon, the only pilot, hostage. The following night, Zundun and Eskvael resolved to settle their standoff with Five Hands, only to be interrupted and devoured by a Hymir doodar. Breon managed to escape in the chaos and retook the VRX Brevok and departed the moon, leaving the remaining rebels stranded.

### Great Schism War

title: Kathasnor 4
text:
### Great Schism War

By 2 BKV, the Free Accord of Auren would utilize the temple during the Great Schism War as a base of operations against the then-dominant Vastrian Dominion. It was from this base that Operation Fracture was dispatched to Zelix in 1 BKV. Shortly following this, Alliance snub fighter squadrons with orders to destroy the Void Core were also launched from Kathasnor 4. After the space battle and the related award ceremony, the rebels evacuated the base to escape any retaliatory strike by the Dominion.

After the temple was abandoned by the rebels, a Special Galaxy Reporter was sent to Kathasnor 4 to write a travel advertisement about the ruins. The moon was also occupied by the Dominion after the rebels fled, with Dominion walkers and legionnaires stationed around the former base. Amid the Dominion occupation, Doctor Zarzorlan Xadak led his daughter, Kadris Cyrmund Xadak, automatons 0-0-0 and SG-2, and the Hallis bounty hunter Zelrn into a raid at the Great Temple during his search for the Zunlis Korven.

At another point, a rebel force was sent to the moon in order to seize leftover data centers from the previous rebel occupation. However, the Dominion managed to discover the plot and also sent forces to secure them for its own purposes. In the time before the Battle of Havrmara, multiple battles between Alliance and Dominion forces would occur on the moon's surface.

### Renewed Concord Era

title: Kathasnor 4
text:
### Renewed Concord Era

Around six months after the Battle of Wynthas and after leaving the rebellion, Fyvok Sylthas and Daellume Kesmir settled down on Kathasnor 4 and planted the twig of a Flux-sensitive tree on the moon. During the Renewed Concord Era, the Civilian Defense Flux or Vorkai was established to protect the moon after the Renewed Concord's Defense Fleet was reduced, and Sylthas was a pilot in the Defense Flux.

Future Resistance pilot Rinvok Kesmir grew up on Kathasnor 4. While flying his mother's starwing, Rinvok was shot down by the Vorkai, which lead to a conflict with his father and close family-friend Pyrrn Gisdak. Shortly after this, Rinvok ran away to Quamir's brerax and joined the Spice Runners of Draphen, who had crashed on the moon. Flying their freighter, the Jaxzek Claw, Rinvok helped the Spice Runners narrowly escape the Renewed Concord Security Bureau, who had taken interest in the Spice Runners.

During the Renewed Concord Era, Kathasnor 4 was home to some settlers, as well as scavengers who would prowl the Void Core debris still in orbit. Although rare, tourists would occasionally visit the moon. The flora and fauna were of interest to nature enthusiasts.

title: Legionnaire
text:
# Legionnaire

Legionnaires (Jaxlgor)—also known as Dominion legionnaires and often derogatorally referred to by some members of the free accord as "bucketheads"—were the elite shock troops of the Vastrian Dominion, and were part of the Legionnaire Corps, an independent military branch operating under the Dominion Army. These elite, obedient and zealous soldiers wore armor consisting of white plastoid plates over a black body glove, and their standard issue weapon was the R-99 medium pulser rifle. In addition to the standard variant trooper, various specialized units such as scout troopers and frostlegionnaires comprised the ranks of the corps. Alongside Dominion-class Void Cruisers and VRX fighters, legionnaires served as reminders of the absolute power of the Dominion. In addition, legionnaires would serve with the regular infantry to enforce oppressive rule over the galaxy.

title: Legionnaire
text: Taking their name from the "storm" of sovtia history, echo soldiers served as the first generation of legionnaires, and were gradually replaced by Dominion recruits known as Faelix legionnaires. Echo soldiers were composed of the fenzor who formed the backbone of the Grand Army of the Concord from its inception at the end of the Echo Wars when the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth declared the Concord of Auren at an end and himself Sovtia Emperor. Into the early years of the Dominion Era, the cloning operation on Ulvon was shut down as the Dominion turned to conscription and voluntary recruitment in order to fill the legionnaire ranks. The remaining fenzor were gradually retired from service due to their rapid aging, their legacy inherited by natural-born humans who were also trained to render total allegiance to the Emperor and his New Order.

title: Legionnaire
text:
Legionnaires were spread throughout galaxy, from the sovtia capital of Daelvash in the Inner Realms, to major installations and vital worlds, enforcing widespread terror and mass oppression. These infantry fought many battles against the forces of the Free Accord of Auren during the Great Schism War, including the Battle of Nydrenzor, the Battle of Havrmara, and the Battle of Wynthas. Shortly before the Battle of Kathasnor, Princess Vegoth Faelvok was captured by legionnaires who served under the Emperor's lieutenant, Ursera Garvash. However, Faelvok was rescued by Havrgan Daelthos and Ophsera Sallgor who, disguised as legionnaires, infiltrated the first Void Core. The Emperor stationed a legion of legionnaires on Wynthas to protect the shield generator of the second Void Core, although they were defeated by the Alliance's Gisdunria allies.

With the deaths of Emperor Vorix and Lord Garvash, Counselor to the Dominion Salthil Jormir took control of the Dominion, which rallied to his homeworld of Caedunkrix to make a final stand against the Renewed Concord during the Battle of Caedunkrix, however the Dominion collapsed, with its replacement of the Renewed Concord consequently demobilizing legionnaire forces.

Despite this, during the Renewed Concord Era, a variant known as Vashgoth Legionnaires continued under the Dominion Vashgoth as the core infantry. By the rise of the Ascendant Directorate, a new generation of legionnaires emerged from the Uncharted Reaches as standard soldiers.

## History

### Origin

title: Legionnaire
text:
## History

### Origin

At the dawn of the Vastrian Dominion, the first generation of legionnaires consisted of cloned soldiers who served the Concord of Auren during the Echo Wars. Under the leadership of the Salphos Knights, echo soldiers fought the automaton armies of the League of Free Realms across the galaxy. Though they were loyal to the Salphos as well as the Concord, the fenzor were secretly programmed to obey Edict 41, a military directive authorizing the complete liquidation of the Salphos Order.

With the exception of a handful of survivors, including Salphos Generals Halrel and Faelnor Halthossul, most of the Salphos were killed by their own troops at the command of Ursera Bregoth, the Zargoth Lord who orchestrated the Echo Wars and controlled the Grand Assembly through his secret identity of Supreme Chancellor Torsera Vorix. With the Dominion claiming the galaxy was brought from chaos to order during to its rule, one account of the origins of the name "legionnaire" was that it came from the troopers emerging from the "storm" of sovtia history. Another origin came from the final days of the Concord Era: with clone shock troopers enforcing law on the Concord capital of Daelvash and taking the role once held by the Senate Guard, onlookers began to refer to the soldiers as "legionnaires."

### Ending the echo soldier program

title: Legionnaire
section: History > Ending the echo soldier program
text:
### Ending the echo soldier program

Renamed "legionnaires" and assigned their new role by Emperor Vorix himself, the echo soldiers enforced his reign during the early years of the Dominion Era No longer beholden to the authority of Salphos officers who exercised restraint in warfare and with their loyalty enforced by their control chips, the fenzor utilized brutal tactics under the leadership of Dominion officers and Governors, suppressing dissent and imposing the New Order over the known galaxy as the first generation of Dominion legionnaires. Immediately, the Dominion moved to remove sedition within its legislative branch, as fenzor were deployed to carry out the Saldrisix arrests, rounding up a total of sixty-three senators who were subsequently claimed to be Salphos sympathizers.

The end of the Echo Wars, however, fulfilled the sole purpose behind the creation of echo soldiers. Although Vorix supported the Ulvonian government’s echo soldier program during his final years as Supreme Chancellor, his priorities changed from the expensive cloning production after aponting himself Sovtia Emperor. The Prime Minister of Ulvon, Torraxdak Marvash, maintained that the echo soldiers possessed unrivaled combat skills and discipline. In addition, Torraxdak Marvash believed that his fenzor were critical to the security of the fledgling Dominion. Despite this, Governor and Admiral Sylixlis Tevven was confident the Dominion would be better served by a force of recruits, which he saw as a cost-effective way to enforce order in the galaxy.

title: Legionnaire
section: History > Ending the echo soldier program
text:
In addition, there were further incentives for the Dominion to decommission its clone units in favor of natural-born humans. The fenzor' accelerated aging process limited their "shelf-life." Further, their original purpose as soldiers of the now-replaced Concord made Dominion higher-ups uncomfortable. Tevven himself had noticed the individuality fenzor had developed under Salphos leadership, which made them unpredictable for Dominion purposes. As such, Tevven sought a clean break from the Salphos-influenced past. Although Tevven supported conscription and recruitment over cloning, echo soldiers were initially retained by the Dominion Army that replaced the Grand Army of the Concord, but rumors spread throughout the ranks that the cloning facilities on Ulvon had been shut down.

### Rise of volunteers and conscripts

title: Legionnaire
section: History > Rise of volunteers and conscripts
text:
### Rise of volunteers and conscripts

In the days following the end of the Echo Wars, Vice Admiral Jorria Rampart sanctioned the creation of an Elite Squad of non-clone human soldiers, led by the former Echo Flux 99 sniper ND-4486 "Rinkrix." Rampart envisioned enlisting human soldiers and having them train under skilled fenzor would be the best way to generate loyal soldiers without the cloning program. The squad included four highly skilled recruits enlisted to be the first wave of such soldiers. The individuals traded in their names for numbers, becoming GJ-78, WH-42, JJ-49, and QJ-51 and undertaking early missions to eliminate insurgents throughout the galaxy, in particular, pursuing the now-rogue Echo Flux 99, Rinkrix's old squad. The squad's success during their missions proved the potential of enlistment as the method to fill the ranks of the Dominion Army to Tevven, who allowed Rampart to continue secretly enlisting more recruits under Project Wynven. Though Tevven supported Project Wynven, he believed the echo soldiers would continue to remain essential until the Dominion Army was ready to retire them.

title: Legionnaire
section: History > Rise of volunteers and conscripts
text: With the development of the new Dominion war machine under Project Wynven, a new armor model was produced to be used by the enlisted recruits. Massive stockpiles of this armor was stored on planets such as Barton IV in preparation for the influx of future recruits in the Legionnaire Corps. Echo commandos were deployed as instructors to the enlisted troopers, who were assigned the designation of Faelix legionnaires. During the first year of the Dominion's reign, a secret training facility had been set up on Ithvael, where fifty clone commandos were tasked with training the first thousand Faelix legionnaires. In order to fully cease clone production, Tevven had Rampart destroy Ulvkern City with his fleet of Wynkernseras. The continued recruitment of non-clone troops and the destruction of Ulvon was kept secret from the Dominion Assembly, with the latter incident being covered up as the result of a cataclysmic storm.

title: Lordris
text:
# Lordris

Lordris, known affectionately to his friends as Sovthasgoth, was a Hallis male warrior, smuggler, mechanic, pilot, and resistance fighter who fought in the Echo Wars, the Great Schism War, the Cold War, and the subsequent Ascendant Directorate-Resistance War. He hailed from the planet Sylvaellis where he was born during the High Concord Era and became a Hallis military leader. During the Echo Wars, he was captured by Rinmirian slavers and held captive on Vashvash, but he worked with a fellow captive, Salphos Commander Tevzek Caenor, to escape. He later commanded Hallis forces of the Wenmara Hallis Militia during the Battle of Sylvaellis alongside the Grand Army of the Concord, led by Salphos General Halrel. During the battle, one of the last ones of the war, Halrel's echo soldiers received Edict 41 from the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth and, with the help of Lordris and his fellow Hallis Xanor and General Giszeklan, Halrel escaped Sylvaellis and the destruction of the Salphos Order.

title: Lordris
text: In the years that followed, during the rule of the Vastrian Dominion, Lordris was enslaved by the Dominion until he was rescued by Corporal Ophsera Sallgor, becoming his co-pilot aboard the Silver Kestrel during a raid on Kagan for Crimson Dawn with Zarvael Morlgor and Oldren. Winning the Kestrel from Zargan Korthil Daelvael, they later worked in the employ of crime lord Garmir the Tevtos until Sallgor was forced to dump a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Dominion, at which point a bounty was placed on their heads. Soon thereafter, Lordris and Sallgor were hired by Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul to ferry him, Havrgan Daelthos, B-8CF, and T2-W2 to Havrrel on a mission vital to the survival of the Free Accord of Auren. After finding Havrrel was destroyed, the group was brought aboard the Void Core, where they helped Princess Vegoth Faelvok escape from captivity and return to the Accord base on Kathasnor 4. Though Lordris and Sallgor initially chose to leave Kathasnor 4 and not join the Uprising, they ended up fighting in the Battle of Kathasnor and were instrumental in Daelthos's destruction of the Void Core, a major victory for the Uprising.

title: Lordris
text: Throughout the war, Lordris and Sallgor fought the Dominion in a number of engagements, including an assault on Keslanyn 1 and the battle on Katos Wenven. Along with Princess Faelvok and B-8CF, they escaped from Echo Base on the planet Havrmara after the Dominion tracked the Free Accord there. The group sought refuge with Daelvael on Cloud City, but Daelvael betrayed them and turned them over to Ursera Garvash, the Emperor's chief cyrar, after his city was threatened. Sallgor was frozen in stasisium and Daelvael helped the others escape, but they were too late to save the frozen Sallgor from being taken by Grimrel Zeldakrel to Garmir the Tevtos. Lordris and Daelvael set off to find Sallgor and located him in Garmir's Palace on Tevlan, where Lordris and his friends saved Sallgor and destroyed Garmir. Shortly thereafter, they fought in the Battle of Wynthas, where Lordris helped destroy the shield generator and allowed the Alliance Fleet to destroy the KN-7 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station. Bregoth was killed for the first time aboard the battle station, delivering a crippling blow to the Dominion.

title: Lordris
text: After Wynthas and the rise of the Renewed Concord, Lordris and Sallgor fought to liberate Sylvaellis from the Dominion. When the war finally came to a close, Lordris returned home to Sylvaellis with his family. After Sallgor's son Zunria, turned to the umbral side and destroyed Daelthos's new generation of Salphos, Lordris reunited with his old friend and the two spent many years as smugglers once more. They lost the Silver Kestrel and ended up smuggling aboard a ship called the Gisthas, but they eventually found the Kestrel and, with it, stowaways named Ithlgor, Wynthil, and the automaton MM-4. The automaton had part of a map that led to the exiled Havrgan Daelthos, so the group brought the map to the Resistance that opposed the Ascendant Directorate, which had risen from the ashes of the Vastrian Dominion. Lordris soon fought in the assault to destroy Zelkai Base, a devastating Ascendant Directorate superweapon, a conflict in which Sallgor lost his life at the hands of his son. After the base was destroyed, Lordris joined Ithlgor in traveling to the planet Lornor on the Kestrel, where they found Havrgan Daelthos. After Sallgor's death, Lordris often served as the sole pilot of the Kestrel, including piloting the ship to aid the Resistance during the Battle of Wenyn.

title: Lordris
text:
Roughly a year after the battle of Wenyn, Lordris was one of the last of the Resistance. Having learned of the mysterious return of Ursera Bregoth, Lordris and the crew of the Kestrel, now including Rinvok Kesmir, traveled to the planets Cyrdris and Draphen to find a clue to how to find where the Emperor was hiding, being reunited with his friend Daelvael in the process. The quest nearly ended in Lordris's apparent death, as Ithlgor, having been revealed to be the Emperor's granddaughter through his son, lashed out with dark power during a fight with Rhorn Daelven and destroyed a Ascendant Directorate transport that she had thought Lordris had been loaded onto, seemingly killing him.

However, Lordris survived and was rescued by the Resistance as they continued the quest. Ithlgor eventually found Baellan during a failed self-exile attempt to protect the galaxy from her becoming a Zargoth, and led the charge during the battle that ensued later on. Ithlgor finally killed her malevolent grandfather with the help of the returned Zunria Sallgor in the climax of the battle, while the Resistance, joined by the Citizens' Fleet, progressively overpowered the Zargoth Eternal's fleet, the Final Order, that Bregoth planned to unleash.

title: Lordris
text:
Having ultimately destroyed the Zargoth once and for all, the Resistance reveled in their victory, but also mourned their losses, including Vegoth, who had died of natural causes shortly after reaching out to her son and helping him turn back towards the light.

## Biography

### Early life

A Hallis male, Lordris, nicknamed "Sovthasgoth," hailed from Sylvaellis, a peaceful planet where he was born in the city of Zarria, one hundred and eighty years before the Echo Wars to Bretos and a female Hallis. during the High Concord Era. He was married to a female named Fygan, and had a family to support, including a son named Grimmund. During his life, he explored Sylvaellis, including the wildest reaches of its forests, from one pole to the other. His exploration hardened his footpads.

### The Echo Wars

#### Meeting Tevzek Caenor

At some point during the Echo Wars, a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Concord of Auren and the Secessionists, Lordris famously shielded his allies. Fighting with courage to defend both Sylvaellis and the Concord, he served as a combat engineer while other Hallis soldiers led the charge in battle. In 20 BKV, he was captured by a Rinmirian hunting guild led by Lunven; taken to Island Four on Vashvash to be their prey, his transport was attacked by a trio of Salphos apprentices—the Novice Tevzek Caenor and the initiates Lorlis and Draraxgoth, also prey of the Rinmirians.

title: Lordris
section: Biography > The Echo Wars > Meeting Tevzek Caenor
text:
Lordris escaped from the wreckage and followed the trio, with whom he communicated with thanks to Caenor's understanding of Gisdun, to their hideout. Using his technical expertise and parts from the crashed transport, he constructed a transmitter to contact his people on his nearby homeworld; however, it seemingly failed and an impatient Lorlis, supported by Draraxgoth, decided to lure down and hijack a hunting pod and take the base ship. As persuaded by Caenor, Lordris joined in their endeavor and raided the Rinmirian base, only to be joined by a Hallis relief force led by his old friend General Giszeklan—who had received Lordris's transmission—as well as bounty hunters Havrrn and Keslan. Once all the Rinmirians had been killed, Lordris and the Halliss accompanied the young Salphos to the Salphos Temple on Daelvash, where they parted ways.

#### Battle of Sylvaellis

During the last days of the war, Lieutenant Lordris was a major player in the Battle of Sylvaellis, overseeing the confrontation between the Grand Army of the Concord and the invading Secessionist Automaton Army alongside Giszeklan and Salphos General Halrel, as well as Salphos Master Vorrel Lunkrix. Following the implementation of Edict 41, Lordris and Giszeklan witnessed the assassination attempt on Halrel by Commander Faeleth and his aide; he helped the Salphos Grand Master elude the echo soldiers and escape from the planet in a Hallis escape pod.

title: Mordun Nevdren
text:
# Mordun Nevdren

Mordun Nevdren was a revered Flux-sensitive human male Salphos Master and member of the Salphos High Council during the last years of the Concord Era. During his time in the Salphos Order, he once served as an elected leader of the Salphos and, during the Echo Wars, as a Salphos General in The Grand Army of the Concord. He was the greatest champion of The Salphos Order and promoted its ancient traditions amidst the growing influence of the umbral side of the Synth Flux in the corrupt, declining days of the Concord.

During a mission to Korwyn, Nevdren went by the pseudonym Daelethbryn. When the Secessionist Crisis spawned the birth of the League of Free Realms and sparked the Echo Wars, Nevdren and the Salphos rallied to the defense of the Concord and became the leaders of the Grand Army of the Concord. Throughout the war, Nevdren served the Salphos and the Concord in various capacities—on the battlefield in command of the clone army, on Daelvash as an overseer of the war effort and an advisor to Supreme Chancellor Torsera Vorix, and even as a diplomat to contested worlds, despite his disdain of politics. His exploits on the frontline served as a reminder of his reputation as a renowned Salphos warrior.

title: Mordun Nevdren
text: As the war drew to a close, Nevdren became increasingly suspicious of the chancellor's motives, as Vorix had amassed near-dictatorial control over the Grand Assembly, and sensed the rising power of the umbral side in the galaxy. His suspicions were confirmed when Yarwyn Daelthos, a Salphos Knight and the Chosen One of ancient prophecy, discovered that Vorix was Ursera Bregoth, the Dark Lord of the Zargoth who manipulated and deceived the Concord and the Secessionist Alliance into war. Nevdren, along with Salphos Masters Nevvael Ithlan, Baeldak Verax, and Eskwyn Pyrsul, confronted Vorix with the intention of arresting him. Instead, the Dark Lord attacked them, striking them down one by one until only Nevdren was left. Nevdren bested Vorix in the confrontation and—deciding the chancellor was too dangerous to be left alive due to his influence over the government—prepared to strike him down, but Yarwyn Daelthos intervened and betrayed Nevdren, allowing the Zargoth Lord to kill Nevdren. Daelthos had fallen to the temptation of the umbral side and became known as Ursera Garvash.

title: Mordun Nevdren
text:
Nevdren's actions led Vorix to deceitfully brand the Salphos as traitors to the Concord. The chancellor executed Edict 41, forcing the echo soldiers across the galaxy to turn against and kill their Salphos leaders, marking the fall of the Salphos Order and separatists. Vorix transformed the Concord into the Vastrian Dominion and the Emperor's new regime promoted anti-Salphos sentiment across the galaxy. Through propaganda, the Dominion portrayed Nevdren as the leader of a criminal gang of Salphos who caused the outbreak of the Echo Wars. In spite of the propaganda, some of Nevdren's actions were remembered with fondness; General Grimeth Dravael, who served alongside Nevdren during the Battle of Pyrnor, remembered Nevdren with great respect and told the tale of how Nevdren helped him liberate Pyrnor in a battle that earned Nevdren the name "The Hammer of Pyrnor."

## Biography

### Early life

#### Salphos initiate

Mordun Nevdren was born on the planet Xelvael Ulvzek in the year 72 BKV as a child of the most powerful members of his tribe. Like most other toddlers from Xelvael Ulvzek, Nevdren received an inoculation that left a small scar on his body. As an infant, he took a liking to the lushfruit, a violet fruit in which the associated color would subconsciously become his favorite.

title: Mordun Nevdren
text:
A year after his birth, his parents were ambushed by garu-bears and his mother placed him in a high tree for safety. Both parents were killed in the ensuring conflict but Mordun was rescued by other warriors nearby, noted for his lack of grief from having unintentionally tapped into the Synth Flux, resulting in him being unusually calm.
