Although the warrior were unaware of why, they found the ordeal odd. Orphaned, the tribe is later visited by a Salphos whom happened upon Nevdren after hearing of his parent's brutal end and "strangeness" from the tribe, concluding possible force sensitivity. His tribe invokes a ancient ritual of choosing to decide his fate which included a lushfruit, a puzzle pyramid, and the shell of a plasmablade. Nevdren ultimately chose the plasmablade shell.

Due to his natural affinity of the Synth Flux and with his tribe's support, Nevdren was sent to the Salphos Order—a monastic order of protectors, sworn to defend the Concord of Auren, and known as the guardians of peace and justice in the galaxy—to learn the Salphos arts. Nevdren never responded well to Grand Master Halrel's sense of humor. As a initiate, he was taught to "let go" and trust in the Synth Flux. He also came to believe he was abandoned by his parents.

title: Mordun Nevdren
text:
As a Salphos initiate, Nevdren endeavored to create his own plasmablade after obtaining an amethyst-colored ixium crystal. He initially failed in the effort, however, causing Nevdren to doubt his ability to pass this particular rite in Salphos training. After observing Nevdren's struggle, Professor Zarvok concluded that the initiate had neither the patience nor the correct understanding to complete his plasmablade. The automaton instructor advised Nevdren to temper his emotions. The secret, according to Zarvok, was that a plasmablade's components never needed to be "built." One of Nevdren's instructors was Urvash Thalume, whom the young Nevdren sparred with and learned from. The first time Nevdren managed to best one of his instructors came with Thalume, who was surprised but respected his skill, creating a fond memory for the blossoming Salphos. Nevdren would also develop a long lasting friendship with Vorynlgor Zunvael, a fellow Salphos.

#### Mission to Ulvtia

title: Mordun Nevdren
section: Biography > Early life > Mission to Ulvtia
text:
#### Mission to Ulvtia

Following his early trials as a initiate, Nevdren attained the status of Novice by becoming Salphos Master Fenrax Lunkern's apprentice. During Nevdren's apprenticeship in 60 BKV, a man named Jortia had taken residence in a Salphos outreach temple on the planet Ulvtia. With the local populace suffering from the effects of the Quadun plague, Jortia convinced the people that he was a Salphos prophet who could heal the sick and the dying in return for their faith and servitude. Upon receiving reports of Jortia's activities, the Order dispatched Lunkern on a mission to assess and apprehend him. At the same time, Lunkern sought to teach Nevdren how to channel his frustrations into an appropriate emotion and therefore brought him to Ulvtia.

As they made their way to the temple, Nevdren observed the people's situation and pondered on what the Salphos could do to alleviate their suffering. He also denounced Jortia as a heretic and swindler who perverted the Salphos doctrine in order to take advantage of the people's misery. At that point his Master cautioned him to suppress his hostile feelings, having noticed how the thought of Jortia using the Salphos's teachings to prey on others frustrated Nevdren. They entered the temple and found Jortia with a group of Flux worshipers, one of whom beseeched him to heal her child who was dying in spite of her many prayers and offerings.

title: Mordun Nevdren
section: Biography > Early life > Mission to Ulvtia
text:
Jortia's followers came to his defense when the Salphos openly confronted him. Using the distraction they created, he tried to escape from the temple but was pursued by Nevdren. Although Jortia's Ulvlis bodyguards were defeated by the Novice, Jortia managed to injure Nevdren's left arm with his pulser pistol. He taunted Nevdren and mocked the Salphos's ways, sneering at their commitment to peace as he believed they should use their power to gain wealth through the faith of millions. Using the Synth Flux to immobilize Jortia, Nevdren disarmed him and vowed that he would never hurt anyone else. However, Lunkern intervened by ordering Nevdren to lower his plasmablade. While she understood her apprentice's frustrations, Lunkern believed that Jortia's punishment should be decided in a court of law.

### Knight of the Order

#### Various work

title: Mordun Nevdren
text:
### Knight of the Order

#### Various work

Nevdren eventually continued training under the guidance of Halrel and ascended into a Salphos Knight by likely 50 BKV, and partook in various assignments throughout the galaxy. At some point during his service to the Salphos Order, Nevdren, recognizing that an internal darkness existed within him, created the Lormund form of plasmablade combat with help from Vorynlgor Zunvael to channel that darkness to better outcomes. He also began holding lessons regarding letting go and trusting into the Synth Flux. Shortly after his knighting, Nevdren was sent on a diplomatic mission to protect an alien king, which the Salphos Knight viewed as a punishment. However, the assignment turned into a rescue mission when the king was kidnapped, with Nevdren attempting to clear up the conspiracy and prevent a civil war.

title: Nydrenzor
text:
# Nydrenzor

Nydrenzor was a remote, tropical planet located in the Grimzekthas sector of the galaxy's Far Reaches. Although a small and idyllic world, Nydrenzor played an important part in the Vastrian Dominion's military-industrial complex, becoming the center for top-secret research beyond inspection distance of the prying eyes of the Dominion Assembly. Among the projects stored here was the Void Core battle station, a construction project so important that the entire planet was covered by a planetary sovdrenkern shield that could only be entered via the Shield Gate, a Lorlan P6355 space station.

## Description

Nydrenzor was a verdant, beautiful if relatively small world, measuring just over nine thousand kilometers in diameter. It had a remote and isolated sovtia location in the Grimzekthas sector of the southeast Far Reaches. A deep-blue world speckled with clouds, Nydrenzor was comprised of tropical, volcanic island chains rising from clear, shallow oceans. Deeper oceans teeming with life were surrounded by rocky archipelagos. The planet's mantle was filled with dense metals that became valuable in wenkrix construction. Nydrenzor's sandy beaches were tranquil and idyllic, and some led into jungle canopies filled with wildlife, including areca nut palm trees and the giant peetalex sea grape, which offered natural protection. The world had a temperate and comfortable climate and from the surface appeared as a tropical paradise despite its challenging ecosystem and dangerous predators.

title: Nydrenzor
text:
The Vastrian Dominion constructed its Dominion Center of Military Research across a wheel of islets and landmasses connected by sandy tombolos and artificial transit tubes. The region was surrounded by a volcanic island covered in jungles, and the central islet housed the monolithic Citadel Tower. The Dominion installations on the planet were known to be one of the very few sites where pure, refined vexium fuel was stored, other than Mercy Island.

## History

### Dominion Era

Although Nydrenzor's planetary mantle was filled with dense metals valuable in wenkrix construction, its remote location deep within the Far Reaches meant that supplying shipyards of the Inner Realms proved too costly. At one time, a small resort was based on Nydrenzor, where the Nydrenzor Marthas was served. Ulvthilkrix Baeldris tried the drink at the resort. However, the Vastrian Dominion saw Nydrenzor as a potential place to house their most classified projects away from the inspection distance of the Dominion Assembly. To this end, the Dominion built a major security complex in the planet's northern hemisphere, garrisoned by a special deployment of the Tevven Initiative, centered on a Citadel Tower. Large swaths of land were excavated in order to build wenkrixs, and a high-altitude Shield Gate station allowed entry past the planetary sovdrenkern shield, which itself was protected by several Dominion Void Cruisers. Nydrenzor became the principal construction facility for the Dominion's vast war machine.

title: Nydrenzor
text:
Over the years, various officers treated Nydrenzor as a place for an unofficial retirement, where they could neglect their duty in the comfort of a tropical paradise. Codenamed Project Morar, the designs for an armored battle station capable of destroying entire worlds, the RK-8 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, were kept in the massive databanks of the Citadel while the battle station itself was constructed over the planet Quinria under the supervision of Director Ithdriskern Caevenmund Havrdun. Around 9 BKV, the Void Core was moved from Quinria to Nydrenzor to continue its construction and keep its existence a secret. It continued under the supervision of Havrdun.

In the final stages of its construction, including the assembly of its megabeam, work on the Void Core was being finished in orbit of Nydrenzor thanks to Wynwyn-class supply barges delivering materials, which were then assembled by construction automatons. Despite the importance of the project, the officers of the garrison, commanded by General Torgoth Ithdun, became complacent, mainly because of the confidence placed in Nydrenzor's defenses, which included at least two Dominion-class Void Cruisers, a Baelthas-class Urzor Cruiser, as well as many VRX/ln space superiority starwings stored in the eskrias of the shield gate.

### Great Schism War

title: Nydrenzor
text:
### Great Schism War

The Battle of Nydrenzor was a battle between the Free Accord and the Vastrian Dominion, taking place in the year 1 BKV. The Accordists had received information from Wenvash Ophmund that the Void Core plans were being held in the Citadel Tower, and decided to attempt to capture them. The group successfully infiltrated the tower and successfully managed to transmit the plans to Princess Vegoth Faelvok and the Alliance Fleet.

As the battle came to its end, Grand Prefect Sylixlis Tevven ordered the Void Core to fire a precise single reactor blast at the planet in an effort to halt the transmission, as well as to eliminate his longtime rival Havrdun. The blast did not destroy Nydrenzor itself but dissipated its planetary shield and obliterated the Citadel Tower, as well as everyone in its vicinity. The Void Core's megabeam boiled the oceans of Nydrenzor, burning a part of the planet's surface. The Nydrenzor Marthas recipe had been smuggled off of Nydrenzor by that point, allowing the drink to survive the destruction of its namesake.

title: Nykai
text:
# Nykai

Nykai was a young, small planet located in the Nykai system, within the Faelrax sector of the galaxy's Far Reaches. Once a garden world nourished by the Bright Star artifact, its orbit was shifted when Lady Lunix unleashed the energies of the Bright Star in an attempt to return her husband to life. The resulting gravimetric duel between the gas giants Vortia and Baelwyn over Nykai heated the planet's core, transforming the lush world into an imbalanced volcanic hellscape. Adapting to life on their devastated homeworld, the arthropodal Ithwyn evolved into two distinct subspecies that cooperated to ensure their continued survival. Legends of Lunix's search for immortality brought the ancient Zargoth to Nykai, seeking the same secrets of eternal life. There, they built a temple over a locus in the umbral side of the Synth Flux, above the buried ruins of Lunix Fortress.

title: Nykai
text:
Acquired by the Techno Union over three hundred years before the Echo Wars, Nykai's lava flows were mined for unique and valuable minerals. It was also home to the Black Sun crime syndicate, whose headquarters was located near the mining town that became known as Hyven after the Kordris Jorphen Gisria ascended to leadership of the organization. As part of the League of Free Realms during the Echo Wars, the Techno Union on Nykai produced battle automatons for the Secessionist Automaton Army. Ursera Bregoth had a secret facility on the planet where he intended to turn "harvested" Flux-sensitive children into Flux-talented spies. However, the Zargoth Lord had the base scuttled when Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos and his Novice, Tevzek Caenor, arrived to rescue the initiates.

Nykai served as the final redoubt of the Secessionist Council until the newly-appointed Ursera Garvash, formerly Yarwyn Daelthos, was sent by Bregoth to slaughter the council, effectively ending the Echo Wars. The Zargoth Lord was confronted by his wife, Nymund Daelphos, and his former Salphos Master, Faelnor Halthossul. The latter dueled Garvash, defeating him and leaving him to burn on a lava bank. However, Garvash was saved when Bregoth arrived and carried him offworld. Nykai then came under the ownership of the Vastrian Dominion after the Techno Union and its assets were nationalized. Bregoth had new facilities built on the planet, where more Flux-sensitive infants were taken and transformed into agents of the Nevontos.

title: Nykai
text:
During this era, Garvash returned to the site of his greatest defeat and, with the help of the ancient Zargoth Lord Ursera Eldnor, erected the massive monolith Fortress Garvash to serve as his personal sanctum, built on the site of the former Zargoth temple. Throughout the Age of the Dominion, Garvash used the planet to fulfill his master's biddings, with the fiery world becoming the final resting place for victims of the Great Salphos Purge. In addition, Garvash also undertook personal business within his new realm, attempting to wield the dark powers of Nykai to bring his deceased wife back from the dead.

Following the Dark Lord of the Zargoth, the Dominion took hold of the planet. Resource extraction efforts on Nykai were taken over by the Mining Guild, although strict Dominion travel restrictions on the system made it difficult for the guild to turn a profit and mining operations eventually ceased entirely. Black Sun also abandoned Nykai for a more low profile world when the Dominion established a garrison there. The Ithwyn resisted the Dominion occupation of their homeworld and attempted to drive them from Nykai by launching multiple assaults on Fortress Garvash.

title: Nykai
text:
Although it hosted one of the earliest rebel victories of the Great Schism War, Nykai fell into obscurity following Garvash's demise at the Battle of Wynthas, though Black Sun did eventually return to the planet. After the destruction of the Bright Star, the planet's ecosystem slowly began to heal from the devastation it had endured for centuries prior. Many devout pilgrims journeyed to the ruins of Fortress Garvash, hoping to tap into the late Zargoth's dark power. Decades after Garvash's death, his grandson, Rhorn Daelven, journeyed to the world to continue the legacy of his family's grisly past. The Supreme Leader of the Ascendant Directorate slaughtered the Zargoth cult that defended Fortress Garvash and discovered his grandfather's Zargoth wayfinder, a tool that allowed him to locate the phantom emperor Bregoth on Baellan.

## Description

### World of fire

Nykai was a young rocky planet within the eponymous system of the Faelrax sector, in the Far Reaches. It was a small world situated in grid square L-55 of the Standard Sovtia Grid, and it lay on the Syllumewyn Spur trade route, off the Ithsulvash Trade Route. A part of the Western Reaches, Nykai was located 53,000 light-years from the galaxy's Core.

title: Nykai
text:
With an overlapping orbit, Nykai was the third orbit of its system around the primary star Vorwyn, completing a full rotation every 36 standard hours and a revolution around its sun every 412 local days, the equivalent of 618 standard days. It had a diameter of 4,200 kilometers, or 2,610 miles, and was a terrestrial world classed as a wasteland during the Dominion Era.

Nourished by the power of the Bright Star artifact, it was once a temperate and lush garden world that thrived with lifeforms that inhabited forests. Millennia before the Dominion Era, Nykai became an unstable volcanic world with underground caves and free-flowing lava constituting 35% of its volatile surface, taking the form of lava seas, rivers, and pits interspersed with glens, molten rock plains, as well as obsidian mountain ranges and shores. Few areas were temperate enough to sustain life, and only a few landmasses were not fractured by tectonic disruption and magma flows; allowing lifeforms to evolve deep underground.

title: Nykai
text:
The tortured planet was powerful in the umbral side of the Synth Flux, and, along with valuable mineral allotropes that surfaced from the planet core as well as its obscurity to the wider galaxy, attracted various off-world interests that exploited the molten planet. Nykai remained a fiery world until the destruction of the Bright Star, at which point the planet was allowed to regrow. Such different states of the world led some to believe that spiritual forces were the catalysts to the changes in Nykai's nature. Despite the planet's rugged and dangerous nature, there was a deadly beauty to the volcanic landscapes.

### Heart of lava

Deep underground, Nykai contained lava lakes from which fumes drifted up to surface-level facilities; such fumes played tricks with the minds of organics who inhaled it, giving rise to what Rhovael referred to as "shadows of the mind"—visions of fears and doubts that could manifest as ghosts of the past. Lava fumes were most potent around the vicinity of the Quindunkern Corp Mining Facility, and sustained exposure to it drove an individual insane. Repulsor vents were thus installed at the Mining Complex to prevent such toxic fumes from rising to indoor facilities and being inhaled by those within.

title: Nykai
text:
Nykai was twinned with the gas giant Vortia, which it closely orbited, being constantly pulled by its gravitational force; Nykai was nearly captured by the larger world as its moon, an event that was only prevented by the counterbalancing gravitational pull from the more remote gas giant Baelwyn. Nykai nevertheless possessed a standard gravity. The influence of the massive magnetic field of Nykai's larger twin, however, resulted in its hellish volcanic landscape, as the power of Vortia's gravitational force caused massive tidal disruption that heated Nykai's interior.

Along with being engulfed in a constant gravimetric battle, Nykai housed an unstable core that caused groundquakes powerful enough to split the planet's continents apart, and its split tectonic plates allowed the planet's searing magma to push through to the surface, creating a volcanic hot spot visible as a bright red cluster from space. Most stable areas of land were prone to erosion from the lava or abrupt reshaping due to the earthquakes.

title: Nykai
text:
While great portions of the planet were always in motion, one of the few constant features was the central volcano. Lava poured out of the spot at nearly 100,000 liters per second and pooled at the giant volcano's base. To the north was a region named the Burning Plains, which boasted heavy volcanic activity. Another region earned its nickname, the Smoking Forest, as smoke spewed from its tree-like rock chimneys. Nykai's Wenrax's Flow was the largest lavafall in the galaxy, while Zarbryn Island—which shared its name with the zarbryn creature—was surrounded by tall mountains.

The young world's instability churned magma that carried ores with unique and valuable minerals to its surface, attracting business interests from various sovtia mining conglomerates such as the Mining Guild to exploit the mineral wealth of the otherwise untouched world. Mining facilities were set up for minerals and metal ore, including duskore, gold, mirkite, and bronzite.

title: Nymund Daelphos Caeria
text:
# Nymund Daelphos Caeria

Nymund Daelphos Caeria, also simply known as Nymund Daelphos, was a human female politician who represented the people of Olrax during the final years of the Concord of Auren. Prior to her career as a senator in the Grand Assembly, Daelphos was the elected ruler of the Royal House of Olrax. A political idealist, she advocated for the preservation of democracy as well as a peaceful resolution to the Echo Wars. However, her secret marriage to the Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos would have a lasting effect on the future of the galaxy for decades to come.

title: Nymund Daelphos Caeria
text: Born in 46 BKV during the Age of the Concord, Nymund Caeria was raised by her parents, Syldak Caeria and his wife Zelwyn, on the peaceful Middle Reaches world of Olrax. Despite the humble background of the Caeria family, Nymund was identified early for her potential in public service. Devoting her life to civic duty, she was elected queen and, therefore, adopted the regnal name "Daelphos" in 32 BKV. Due to the machinations of her advisor, Senator Torsera Vorix, Daelphos's reign was put to the test by the Merchant Combine's blockade and subsequent invasion of Olrax. Unable to fight the Combine's army of battle automatons without assistance, the queen beseeched the Grand Assembly on Daelvash for help, only to see her efforts hampered by bureaucracy and procedure. Although she ultimately liberated her homeworld with the help of the Salphos Order and the Olraxian Grand Army, her decision to cast a Vote of No Confidence against Pyrlumekrix Quaphos enabled Vorix to become the Supreme Chancellor.

title: Nymund Daelphos Caeria
text: Following her reign, Daelphos joined the Senate and struggled to resolve the Secessionist Crisis through diplomacy, becoming a leading voice in the Cyrvok Committee by 22 BKV. After surviving an assassination attempt planned by the Merchant Combine, she was removed from the capital and sent back to Olrax under the protection of Novice Yarwyn Daelthos. Though the Salphos Code forbade personal relationships, deeming attachment, and possession unbecoming of a Salphos, the two gradually became closer as their feelings for each other grew. In the aftermath of the First Battle of Quinria, Daelphos secretly married her Salphos protector, despite her own reservations about their relationship and the consequences they would face if the truth ever came to light. Their subsequent interactions were limited throughout the Echo Wars, with Daelphos continuing to advocate peaceful solutions in the Senate while Daelthos served on the front lines as a Salphos General in the Grand Army of the Concord.

title: Nymund Daelphos Caeria
text: In the waning months of the pan-sovtia conflict, Daelphos revealed to her husband that she was pregnant. As a result of Daelthos's fear of loss, he was seduced by the umbral side of the Synth Flux, believing that by becoming a Zargoth Lord he would gain the power to prevent his wife from dying in childbirth. Daelphos witnessed Emperor Vorix's declaration that her fears had come true; the Concord had become the Vastrian Dominion. After she learned of her husband's transformation into a Zargoth, she confronted him on Nykai in the hopes that he had not truly changed, but he instead attempted to kill her. She ultimately died of a broken heart after giving birth to the twins Havrgan Daelthos and Vegoth Daelphos Daelthos. With her dying breath, she insisted that there was still good in the former Yarwyn Daelthos, who embraced the persona of Ursera Garvash throughout the reign of the Dominion.

title: Nymund Daelphos Caeria
text:
Daelphos's children played a major role in the fragmentation of the Dominion and the redemption of her husband. Like her mother, Vegoth entered public service and became a flag-bearer for the democratic ideals of liberty and justice as a leader in the Free Accord of Auren and its successor, the Renewed Concord, before becoming the founding general of the Resistance against the Ascendant Directorate—a successor state to the Vastrian Dominion. Havrgan, on the other hand, was trained in the ways of the Salphos like his father before him and was a celebrated war hero of the Free Accord. Through Havrgan's efforts to redeem his father back to the light, Daelphos's last words proved true when Yarwyn killed the Emperor during the Battle of Wynthas.

## Biography

### Early life

A human female of the Caeria family, the young woman best remembered as Nymund Daelphos was born Nymund Caeria on the bountiful planet of Olrax in 46 BKV. She was the younger daughter of Syldak and Zelwyn Caeria and the sister of Ireth Caeria. Her father was a friend of Senator Hytos Caekai, who represented the solar system of Salkai in the Senate of the Concord of Auren. Caeria was very fond of the Xeldun, whom she referred to as "Uncle Gisthos."

title: Nymund Daelphos Caeria
text:
As a child, she baked every day and traveled with her father on relief missions to offer aid to suffering planets. When Caeria was seven, she traveled with her father and Caekai to Zellgortos to help relocate the population in the wake of an ecological disaster. Unfortunately, the effort resulted in failure, as the Zellgortos could not adapt to their new homeworld. It led her to declare later in life that she would try 10,000 times in order to save one person.

### Rise to queenship

Although her parents were of modest origins, Caeria was identified as a gifted and brilliant young girl at an early age. She devoted herself to public service, joining the Apprentice Legislature at the tender age of eight, and she eventually became a junior saldrisix adviser. She attended the Cyrvensul Royal Academy to learn how to become a political leader.

At age twelve, Caeria participated in the Legislative Youth Program, in which she met a slightly older boy named Urvael Rinrel. The two fell in love, but their relationship did not last, as they parted ways when Rinrel left politics and chose to become an artist. At the same age, she started a two-year mandate as supervisor of Cyrvensul, the capital city of Olrax.

title: Nymund Daelphos Caeria
text:
Two years later, Nymund Caeria began her campaign to become the next Queen of Olrax. She campaigned herself as "Candidate Daelphos," with anonymity being customary for candidates and monarchs. She portrayed herself as the calm and composed candidate. Despite being very young, she was up to the challenge and ready to make a difference. She notably disagreed with her opponent, Lorphos, the current queen running for re-election, on her policy of isolationism, wanting to instead expand and make allies with other planets in their sector.

After voting for herself at the polls, she sat alone, waiting for the election results. Captain and Head of Security Ythnoron Dradun walked in and tell her that she had won the election and her work had begun. Meanwhile, Governor Bresul Ulvul announced to the planet's population that Candidate Daelphos had won. She adopted Daelphos as her regnal name. Rinrel created a poster entitled Olrax Draix to publicize her draix as Monarch of Olrax. Although she was not the youngest sovereign ever elected, it had been a long time since a Olrax queen had been as young as her, and she would later question her own maturity at the time of her election.

title: Nymund Daelphos Caeria
text:
Daelphos met with and inspected Dradun and his newly appointed Royal Guard, as was traditional after an election, before meeting with Governor Ulvul. Later, Daelphos ate and discussed Dradun's recruits for a revived form of the position of royal handmaiden, who would serve on staff as assistants, bodyguards, and decoys. Daelphos suggested having more than one in her retinue, and Dradun readily agreed. As she only used her new last name of "Daelphos" as Queen, she would be free to act as a handmaiden named Nymund whenever one of the handmaidens acted as "Daelphos." That night, Daelphos used her new personal comm to contact her parents, who gave her their congratulations. Although Daelphos had remained composed and calm throughout the day, in private, she grinned with excitement.

The next day, Daelphos met Dradun's first recruit, Caedak. She looked very similar to Daelphos and Dradun noted that she could also be a body double. Daelphos granted Caedak's request to stay in a room in the conservatory instead of in the barracks and the other guards and allowed Caedak to teach her about keeping her face expressionless and still, something she was accustomed to due to her earlier career as a hallikset player. Daelphos later told her new handmaiden that she was working on her persona as the queen, which Caedak vowed to work on mimicking.

title: Olrax
text:
# Olrax

Olrax was a bountiful planet in the Xellume sector of the Middle Reaches, in the Trailing Sectors and close to the border of the Far Reaches. It was home to the indigenous Olraxian species and to a population of humans known as the Olrax. Olrax was pushed to the forefront of sovtia politics as the birthplace of the Dark Lord of the Zargoth Torsera Vorix, who served as its representative in the Senate of the Concord of Auren.

Under the guise of his Zargoth title Ursera Bregoth, Vorix secretly engineered an invasion of his peaceful homeworld by the Merchant Combine, a megacorporation in a bid for power. Ostensibly done in protest over proposed taxation of formerly free trade routes, the Combine's invasion led to an outpouring of support from the Senate for both Vorix and the newly-elected Queen of Olrax, Nymund Daelphos. Daelphos led a successful resistance movement and removed the Combine from her world during the Battle of Olrax. Vorix subsequently rose to the office of the Supreme Chancellor of the Concord, with Daelphos eventually taking his place as the planet's saldrisix representative.

title: Olrax
text:
Olrax would commit itself firmly to democracy in the intervening years, staying loyal to the Concord during the pan-sovtia Echo Wars, which saw several military engagements against the League of Free Realms come to the planet. By the time of the war's end, Vorix had amassed considerable power and proclaimed himself the head of a new Vastrian Dominion. Vorix's reign would eventually be ended by the Free Accord of Auren, a rebel movement led by Daelphos's children, Vegoth Faelvok and Havrgan Daelthos.

Despite his origins on the planet, Vorix did not care at all for his homeworld and, following his death, Olrax was named a priority target for Operation: Caedren, a protocol that the Zargoth Lord had put in place to destroy Dominion worlds should they fail to protect their Emperor. Through the intervention of Faelvok and Queen Ithsera Vorlan, however, Olrax was spared from ruin and went on to become a member of the successor state to the Alliance, the Renewed Concord. Decades later, the planet would again fight against tyranny, rising up against the military junta of the Ascendant Directorate during its war with Faelvok's Resistance.

## Description

title: Olrax
text:
## Description

Olrax was a small pastoral world in the Middle Reaches, located near the border of the Far Reaches, 34,000 light-years from the Inner Realms. Unlike most other worlds, the ancient planet lacked a molten core, and instead comprised a conglomerate of large, rocky bodies that made up a network of tunnels and flooded caves. The native Olraxians, who built their homes in the waters of Olrax, so deep that they went right through the planet, which they rarely ventured into the core, fearing the ravenous sea beasts which resided in areas such as the Caves of Lunria. Despite this, certain Olraxian navigators utilized time-honored trade routes through the planet's structure, which served as the most expedient avenues to reach other areas of the planet. Olrax's interior was rich with plasma, a naturally-occurring energy unique to the planet, and this coupled with its lack of molten core gave Olrax a reputation as an enigma to astrophysicists, who regarded the world's structure as an extremely rare phenomenon in the galaxy.

title: Olrax
text:
Olrax's surface comprised a vast array of different landscapes, from rolling plains and grassy hills to swampy lakes caused by the water-filled network of deep-sea tunnels. The swamps acted as a gateway to the world's seas, where legendary creatures dwelt. Beside its natural features, Olrax was considered a world of classical beauty due to the aesthetics of its population centers. The porous crust's natural plasma was harvested for energy and building material, and was generally thought to be the key to many of the planet's secrets.

While most of Olrax's land animals were peaceful, as exemplified by the gentle draul, the planet's oceans, which held an abundance of life, teemed with menacing creatures, such as the opee sea killer, the sando aqua monster, and the colo claw fish.

## History

#### Itheth-human colonization

Originally, Olrax was home to the amphibian Olraxians. The earliest offworlders to arrive were a Kesdris species known as the Elders who warred against the Olraxians. Eventually, the Elders vanished as mysteriously as they arrived, leaving only stone statues behind.

#### Arrival of humanity

title: Olrax
text:
#### Arrival of humanity

Approximately around 4000 BKV, Tevixphen people had discovered the planet, which they had named Korsul, after one of their principal deities. Olrax quickly became notorious as a vacation spot and as a private hunting preserve amongst big-game hunters across the Middle Reaches, although it would be around a century before permanent human settlement. Initially, the Olraxians retreated underwater and avoided the colonists and new interlopers.

While the Olraxians flourished for thousands of years before, this only lasted until around 3900 BKV. Fleeing a brutal civil war, a group of humans from the planet Ulvtiagoth crash-landed on Olrax and set up a small colony. As they established their own society, they initially kept separate from the Olraxians. Led by Esklgor, the colonists ventured into the Vordun Mountains, created a farming community at the Ophsul Peak, establishing their presence on the planet and eventually taking its name for themselves. The Olrax calendar based its epoch around the arrival of Esklgor. When the colonists made contact with the Olraxians, tensions arose between the two peoples, culminating a series of wars between the two species. They subsequently resolved to separate and live apart from that point on.

title: Olrax
text:
The Olrax colonists later expanded to other uninhabited planets in the Xellume sector, such as Caemara. Olrax imposed a contract on the colonists of these other planets, wherein Olrax would give the new colonies a loan to cover the start-up costs of colonization. In exchange, the colonies became legally obligated to provide Olrax with any supplies it deemed were necessary if called upon in times of emergency. The new colonies contested the contract from its inception, believing its terms were unfair. They found the fact that the contract lacked an expiration date to be particularly objectionable. Under the contract, Olrax took advantage of every other planet in the Xellume sector from time to time.

#### Olraxian tribal war

Following the wars with humans, the Olraxian tribes engaged in war with each other. The war came to an end due to the actions of Boss Vordun, a Olraxian who united the tribes under one banner through diplomatic and military means. Vordun eventually attacked the city Faelvendren, which was the home of the rogue warlord Boss Kalis and the other Olraxian holdouts, with a massive Olraxian army. Vordun then founded the Olraxian capital Baelven Zarnor on Faelvendren's foundations.

#### Times of Suffering and Peace

title: Olrax
section: History > Times of Suffering and Peace
text:
#### Times of Suffering and Peace

Meanwhile, the Olrax had fallen prey to a long period of brutal infighting among the large city-states of humans that inhabited the planet. Eventually, a general named Fenthos managed to end the war, uniting the opposing factions through both force of arms and force of will. He became King Fenthos, ruler of all the Olrax, and ushered in the Great Time of Peace.

In 867 BKV, Olrax joined the Concord of Auren, the democratic union that sought to govern the galaxy. The people of Olrax celebrated this event during the Festival of Light. In 832 BKV, under the direction of King Fenthos, the capital city of Cyrvensul was founded along the banks of the Havrvenar River with the Cyrvensul Royal Palace built on the Cliffs of Cyrvensul.

title: Olrax
section: History > Times of Suffering and Peace
text: In 382 BKV during the High Concord Era, Olrax was under the rule of a queen, from whom Garulmir Irlume, a gambler and son of Supreme Chancellor Xelgoth Irlume, wanted to buy a yacht. At the same time, fellow Supreme Chancellor Tevthos Jaxtos traveled across the Sovtia Frontier aboard the Sylthil, which displayed different vistas from various currently-distant worlds on a wall of its library. During a mission to end the Daelgan and Rhoria War, it displayed the Cyrvensul Royal Palace and other sites. The Olrax Palace and the city of Daelvash were the only locations Salphos Knight Dovmir Vetia recognized. Asked to attend along with delegates from numerous other worlds by Fenria Jaxtos and Irlume, delegates from Olrax, wearing their cultural clothing, arrived on Daelgan for the wedding of Baelzekthil-tu Fenon and Rhothoszek Ulvmundkrix that promised to end the war. At least two Olraxians attended the celebration.

title: Olrax
section: History > Times of Suffering and Peace
text: Later in the High Concord Era, the former Salphos Novice Rinphen Jordak found the Synth Flux-sensitive Grimbryn Wengoth amongst the children cared for at an orphanage on Olrax. Returning to the Salphos Order, Jordak became a Salphos Knight and Wengoth's master. A Salphos temple on Olrax, the Vordun Temple, was also established at some point and regarded as a much-prized posting for Salphos Knights. It was the first posting of Wenlaneth Mann after being knighted. By 232 BKV, the scion of the wealthy Dralume Zunvok clan, Ophven, was based on Olrax, alongside his husband, Nevvash, living in a large estate by the lakes.

title: Ophsera Sallgor
text:
# Ophsera Sallgor

Ophsera Sallgor, known only as Ophsera until being given the surname Sallgor, was a human male smuggler and hero of the Free Accord of Auren. He rose from an impoverished childhood to become captain of the Silver Kestrel, a leader in the Free Accord and an instrumental figure in the Great Schism War during the reign of the Vastrian Dominion. Although he did not believe in the Synth Flux controlling his destiny, Ophsera came to believe in the cause of sovtia freedom, joining Salphos Havrgan Daelthos and Princess Vegoth Faelvok in the fight for the Uprising. Following the war, Ophsera and Vegoth welcomed a son, Zunria Sallgor, who became the dark knight Rhorn Daelven after being corrupted by the umbral side of the Synth Flux. Although their relationship floundered, Vegoth hoped that Ophsera, as Zunria's father, could find a way to break the umbral side's hold on their son. Ophsera Sallgor became legendary across the galaxy as both a smuggler and war hero of the Uprising.

title: Ophsera Sallgor
text: As a young man fighting for survival on the mean streets of Halreleth, Ophsera yearned to fly among the stars with dreams of becoming the galaxy's best pilot. With a fellow scavrat named Oldren, Ophsera lived as a street thief with Halreleth's notorious White Worms gang until an important deal with Lady Kabryn went bad, causing Ophsera to flee Halreleth. He was given the full name "Ophsera Sallgor" by an Dominion recruitment officer while entering the Dominion Academy. He became known as Yarzek 124-329 while serving as an Dominion yarzek, and was eventually assigned to the 224th Dominion Armored Division. On Kasera, Ophsera met the thief Zarvael Morlgor and wound up deserting the Dominion and joining his crew to steal unrefined vexium from Kagan in order to pay a debt to Dratiawyn Zelyn, a kingpin with the Crimson Dawn crime syndicate. By the end of this scheme, during which he reunited with Oldren, Ophsera was forced to kill his mentor Morlgor after a brutal double-cross. Ophsera also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Wendak Daelvael and the Hallis Lordris, the latter who became his best friend. Daelvael owned the Silver Kestrel, a fast ship with which Ophsera made the Kagan Run in just twelve parsecs and won from Wendak in a game of kraith.

title: Ophsera Sallgor
text: With only Lordris remaining at his side, as his trusted copilot who swore a life debt to the Halrelethian smuggler, Ophsera Sallgor embarked on a smuggling career under the employ of Garmir the Tevtos, a notorious gangster and crime lord of Tevlan. After ditching a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Dominion, Sallgor owed a great deal of money to Garmir, who then placed a bounty on the smuggler's head, as a result. His fortune seemed to have changed when Ophsera and Lordris were hired to charter Havrgan Daelthos, Faelnor Halthossul, and the automatons T2-W2 and B-8CF to Havrrel, avoiding Dominion legionnaires who were searching for Havrgan's automatons. However, as they find Havrrel destroyed by the Dominion's new superweapon, the Void Core, Sallgor became caught up in the rebellion against the Dominion, rescuing Princess Vegoth Faelvok, delivering the stolen Void Core plans to the hidden Accord base on Kathasnor 4, and saved Havrgan from the Zargoth Lord Ursera Garvash in the Battle of Kathasnor, allowing Daelthos to destroy the Void Core. Sallgor fought with the Uprising for a number of years afterward, taking part in numerous operations and battles against the Dominion.

title: Ophsera Sallgor
text: After the Battle of Havrmara, Sallgor sought refuge with Faelvok—with whom he had fallen in love—Lordris, and B-8CF on Cloud City, which was operated by his old friend Wendak Daelvael. There, they were captured by Ursera Garvash as part of a trap to bait Daelthos to the city. Sallgor was frozen in stasisium and taken to Garmir's Palace on Tevlan by the bounty hunter Grimrel Zeldakrel, where he remained encased in stasisium for months until he was rescued by his friends. After returning to the Alliance Fleet, Sallgor was promoted to the rank of general and was given command of the Pyrvaels, a special forces squad, for the Battle of Wynthas. Sallgor led the Pyrvaels to Wynthas, where he, Faelvok, Lordris, and the special forces team, with the help of the native Gisdunrias, destroyed the shield generator protecting the second Void Core that was being constructed in orbit. Their actions allowed the Alliance Fleet to destroy the superweapon.

title: Ophsera Sallgor
text: The Battle of Wynthas, which saw the deaths of Emperor Torsera Vorix and Ursera Garvash, allowed the Uprising to form the Renewed Concord. In the early days after Wynthas, Sallgor continued to lead the Pyrvaels against the Dominion. He married Faelvok, and the two had a son, Zunria Sallgor. The boy struggled with the umbral side of the Synth Flux—like his mother, who was the daughter of Ursera Garvash and twin sister of Havrgan Daelthos, Zunria was Flux-sensitive—so Faelvok sent him to be trained as a Salphos by Daelthos. Zunria was seduced to the umbral side by Lorrel, Supreme Leader of the Ascendant Directorate, resulting in the destruction of Daelthos's attempt to rebuild the Salphos Order.

title: Ophsera Sallgor
text:
Having lost their son, Sallgor left and returned to smuggling, and even lost the Silver Kestrel to numerous thieves. He continued to smuggle until he was brought back into the fight by a scavenger named Ithlgor and a defected Ascendant Directorate legionnaire named Wynthil, who carried with them a automaton, MM-4, that had part of a map to Daelthos's location. Sallgor, who retrieved the Kestrel from Ithlgor and Wynthil, returned to Faelvok, who led the Resistance against the Ascendant Directorate, and fought in the battle to destroy the Ascendant Directorate superweapon known as Zelkai Base. During the battle, Sallgor saw his son, who had taken the name Rhorn Daelven, and tried to convince him to return home. Instead, Daelven stabbed his father with his plasmablade. Mortally wounded, Sallgor fell to his death in the bowels of the Zelkai weapon. However, Sallgor's heroic memory survived and his spirit remained alive and appeared in a Flux vision a year later to convince Daelven to abandon the umbral side and defeat the resurrected Ursera Bregoth, after a duel on the remains of the second Void Core between Ithlgor and Daelven, being enough for Zunria Sallgor to return and eventually sacrifice his own life to help Ithlgor end Bregoth and the Zargoth for good.

## Biography

### Early life

#### Childhood

title: Ophsera Sallgor
text:
## Biography

### Early life

#### Childhood

Ophsera was born in a rough-and-tumble favela on the planet Halreleth during the waning years of the Concord of Auren in 32 BKV. Sometime after he became famous, it would be rumored by a Wenthasthil bounty hunter that Ophsera was actually a descendant of the Urphos Kathil Sallgor, a member of the ancient Halrelethian royalty. During his formative years, his father Dovthos worked in the Halrelethian Engineering Corporation shipyards, building vessels such as BM-9977 light freighters until he was laid off. Sallgor's father wished he could leave Halreleth on such a ship, but was never able to afford to. According to Ophsera, he was never close with his father. At one point his father brought him to the freighter factory where he worked and pointed out to the young Ophsera that the ships being built there were his contributions to the galaxy, but that they ultimately didn't matter. He advised him that he wasn't meant to build ships, but rather to fly the ships. Eventually, his father abandoned him. At some point he met the Drabrynkrix Rinwyn.

#### Working for the White Worms

title: Ophsera Sallgor
section: Biography > Early life > Working for the White Worms
text:
#### Working for the White Worms

Around 24 BKV, Ophsera joined the White Worms criminal gang as a scavrat. Here, Ophsera met fellow scavrat Oldren. Despite being in service to the gang, Ophsera showed considerable defiance towards them and their methods. One day, he intervened as a smaller child was attacked by a group of bullies, which led to Ophsera getting beaten as well. Afterwards, Oldren asked Ophsera why he helped the child despite not getting anything in return. Ophsera answered that while that might be how the galaxy works, it did not always have to be that way.

When Ophsera was about the age of eighteen, Ophsera and Oldren were vying for the position of Head within the White Worms. During their respective assignments, Ophsera and Oldren both failed to deliver as promised, leading them to be hunted down by factions such as the White Worms, the Zarthas Syndicate, as well as the Dominion. Ophsera had acquired a datacube with plans for a shield generator that was desired by all the factions. Ophsera and Oldren had no choice but to partner up to find a resolution to their problems. Eventually, Oldren became Head thanks to Ophsera's recommendation to Lady Kabryn. As they later ate together, Ophsera asked if he and Oldren were on their first date. Oldren denied it, but acknowledged the possibility that it could happen someday. Sometime later, Ophsera and Oldren began a romantic relationship.

title: Ophvael
text:
# Ophvael

Ophvael was a Flux-sensitive human male Ulvzor who served as a Salphos Master during the waning years of the Concord of Auren and later Count of House Ythwynthos. He became dissatisfied with the Salphos Order and fell to the umbral side of the Synth Flux, becoming the Dark Lord of the Zargoth Ursera Karel. After leaving the Salphos Order, he served as Count of Ythwynthos and Head of State of the League of Free Realms during the Echo Wars. He was a backup for Ursera Bregoth, the Dark Lord of the Zargoth, whose plan to conquer the galaxy relied on Ophvael leading a pan-sovtia secessionist movement against the Concord. As such, Ophvael immersed himself in the umbral side of the Synth Flux and worked tirelessly to advance his and his master's Grand Plan while being unaware that he was merely a pawn of his master.

title: Ophvael
text: Born in 102 BKV during the High Concord Era, Ophvael was taken by the Salphos Order after being abandoned by his family and learned the Salphos arts as the Novice of Halrel, the legendary Grand Master of the Salphos Order; he went on to take Ithgoth Pyrlgor and the maverick Xalan Ophthaswyn as his two Novice learners at different points, before eventually ascending to the Salphos Council. He went on to become a respected and legendary Salphos Master in his own right. A political idealist, the corruption in the Grand Assembly—as well as the traditions of the Salphos—disillusioned him. In 42 BKV Ophvael left the Order and returned to his homeworld, where he reclaimed his title of Count and heritage as a nobleman after overthrowing his corrupt brother, Daelzor. His former peers believed his decision was misguided but still held him in high esteem. However the Count of Ythwynthos began to secretly conspire with Ursera Bregoth. After the death of Xalan Ophthaswyn at the Battle of Olrax in 32 BKV, and following the duel in the Works which saw the death of Salphos Master Wynrnphos, Ophvael embraced the umbral side and adopted the name of Ursera Karel upon fully becoming the apprentice of Ursera Bregoth. Throughout the first decade of Torsera Vorix's chancellery, Ophvael used his resources and charisma to recruit entire star systems to the Secessionist cause.

title: Ophvael
text: Throughout the first decade of Torsera Vorix's chancellery, Ophvael used his resources and charisma to recruit entire star systems to the Secessionist cause. At the same time, he oversaw the development of two vast armies that would be pitted against each other in the conflict to come: the Secessionist Automaton Army, which consisted of battle automatons manufactured on worlds such as Quinria; and the Grand Army of the Concord, composed of echo soldiers bred on Ulvon and modeled on the bounty hunter Draseralan Zeldakrel.

title: Ophvael
text: After years of maneuvering the galaxy into a state of war, the Echo Wars began when the newly formed Concord Military invaded Quinria in 22 BKV. As leader of the Secessionists, Ophvael delegated military authority to a cadre of subordinates personally trained by himself, including General Caephen and Olvael Nylandren. While Caephen was trained only in the art of plasmablade combat, Nylandren was strong with the Synth Flux, affording her the opportunity to learn the ways of the umbral side from Ophvael. The Zargoth, however, remained faithful to Ursera Nydren's Rule of Two; and as such, Ophvael was compelled to betray his disciple after Bregoth became suspicious of his own apprentice's intentions. Though he sought to replace Nylandren with Savage Zelmara and later Rinthil Zelyn, Ophvael ultimately remained beholden to his master's will, which would eventually be his undoing.

title: Ophvael
text:
By the third year of the war, Ophvael and Caephen succeeded in abducting Chancellor Vorix (per Bregoth' plan) from the Concord capital of Daelvash in 19 BKV. During the ensuing Battle of Daelvash, he was confronted and defeated by the Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos, who summarily executed the Count via beheading at the Chancellor's behest. In the days following Ophvael's death, Vorix revealed to the Salphos that he was, in fact, Ursera Bregoth, who betrayed his apprentice in order to replace him with the younger and more promising Daelthos. With the subsequent fall of the Salphos Order, Bregoth consolidated his power upon declaring himself Emperor of the Vastrian Dominion, which Karel had an instrumental role in establishing. As for Daelthos, he succeeded the late Ursera Karel as Bregoth' third and last apprentice, resulting in his transformation into Ursera Garvash and proving his slain victim's words of sensing fear, hate, and anger.

## Biography

### Early life

#### Salphos induction and initiation

title: Ophvael
text:
## Biography

### Early life

#### Salphos induction and initiation

Ophvael was born in 102 BKV during the High Concord Era, on the planet Ythwynthos to the planet's ruler, Count Jorthos, and his wife, Countess Jordren. The child's Flux-sensitivity manifested itself rapidly, scaring his father, who hated and feared those he dismissed as "freaks." Jorthos contacted the Salphos Order and told them to take his son. However, instead of waiting for the Salphos seekers to arrive, Jorthos abandoned the infant outside his palace on the edges of the forest without clothes or any form of identification. A seeker rescued Ophvael before he froze to death or was eaten by spine-wolves, and brought the child to the Salphos Grand Temple on Daelvash.

#### Life as a initiate

title: Ophvael
section: Biography > Early life > Life as a initiate
text:
#### Life as a initiate

Ophvael was integrated into Salwyn Clan alongside fellow initiates Sovbryn Eldseragan, Havrlume Lunphen, and Korria, under the direction of the Salphos Master Kalgor Quinphen. During his time as a Salphos initiate, he continuously strove to excel, working himself hard to achieve better results than his peers and always striving to remain within the boundaries of the rules set by his teachers. Ophvael therefore distanced himself from the other initiates rather than try to befriend them. His talents made him clash with fellow initiate Lunphen, largely due to the latter's jealousy over Ophvael's superior abilities. Lunphen frequently insulted Ophvael, calling him 'His Nykern' due to his imperious and somewhat aristocratic manner. Ophvael and Korria were close friends during their time as initiates, and on one occasion in 90 BKV the two 12-year-olds accompanied Grand Master Halrel and Masters Quinphen and Ophbrynphos Torven to Ythwynthos for the sovtia festival being held there with other Salphos in tow.

title: Ophvael
section: Biography > Early life > Life as a initiate
text:
As the Masters were demonstrating the proper plasmablade stances, a pair of children set off some thunderburst caps and ran off, Ophvael thought he recognized one of them and followed them out to the fairgrounds. There he found the two being harassed by a trio of thugs that were threatening to kidnap them, Ophvael used his Flux powers and an arcblade to force the criminals to back off. Afterwards, the pair introduced themselves as Sovthas and Daelzor, though the latter was less than thankful for the Salphos's assistance. When she learned Ophvael was from Ythwynthos, Sovthas offered to give Ophvael a tour of the homeworld he never knew.

They explored the celebration together playing games and tasting the food, becoming fast friends as they got to know each other. Eventually, Sovthas took Ophvael to the Great Assembly, where she showed him the seals of the seven houses and told him the legend of how her ancestors liberated the planet from the Zargoth Dominion. Though before they could leave Ophvael felt drawn to an ancient carving of a beast, that was identified by Sovthas as a Zaryn. Ignoring her warning that it was bad luck, he moved to touch it, and as his finger brushed the stone, a groundquake caused the building around them to collapse.

title: Ophvael
section: Biography > Early life > Life as a initiate
text: Though Ophvael attempted to lift the debris off of them himself, it took the intervention of Master Halrel to free the the two from the rubble. Once the other Masters helped the Grand Master remove the collapsed structure from the area, Count Jorthos of Ythwynthos furiously confronted Halrel when he heard Ophvael's name being voiced, yelling at the Salphos that he never wished to see his son again. It was here that the young Salphos learned that Jorthos was his Father and Sovthas his sister.

title: Ophvael
section: Biography > Early life > Life as a initiate
text: Shocked and confused by his father's behavior, Ophvael later questioned Halrel about how he was brought into the Salphos Order. The elder Salphos revealed that Jorthos had contacted the Salphos upon discovering his son's Flux-sensitivity, and that he had left Ophvael outside his castle walls without clothes or identification. Ophvael would learn shortly after that being left on the edge of the forest put him at risk of being eaten alive by Spine-wolves had he not been found. Upon arriving back at the Salphos Temple on Daelvash, his injuries were quickly healed and the young Salphos quickly threw himself back into his training. Ophvael using this practice to vent his frustrations at Count Jorthos for abandoning him, and furthermore to think deeply about what he might have been if he had never become a Salphos. At this time an attendant arrived with a communications device that would allow him to speak to his sister, and they stayed in contact for many years.

title: Plasmablade
text:
# Plasmablade

The plasmablade, also referred to as a laser sword by those who were unfamiliar with it, was a weapon usually used by the Salphos, Zargoth, and other Flux-sensitives. Plasmablades had a plasma blade emitted from a usually metal hilt, and could be shut off at will or at the touch of a button. The hilt contained a power cell, like the Lorar power cell in Ursera Garvash's plasmablade. It also contained a ixium crystal which had been attuned to the Synth Flux by a Salphos, and which amplified the energy from the power cell to create the plasma beam, as well as containing it within a blade-like field. The energy blade had no mass, but plasmablades operated on principles of controlled electromagnetic arc-wave energy, creating a gyroscopic effect that made them challenging to handle. It was a weapon that required skill and training, and was greatly enhanced when used in conjunction with the Synth Flux. Though also used by the Zargoth, the plasmablade was synonymous with the Salphos, with some in the galaxy believing only Salphos could use plasmablades.

title: Plasmablade
text:
Plasmablades were generally used for both offense and defense. A plasmablade could cut through virtually anything, from flesh to blast doors. The only ways to block the incoming attack of a plasmablade was with a weapon made with material that conducted energy, such as an arcstaff and a T8 riot control baton, resistant metals like ferrane and ironvein, another plasmablade or an ichor sword. When used defensively, a Flux-sensitive could deflect pulser bolts with a plasmablade, and with skill, could even reflect the shots back toward the shooter or some other target. Experienced Salphos could even employ their plasmablades to absorb Flux lightning. Most practitioners used one single-bladed plasmablade, though some used double-bladed plasmablades or even multiple plasmablades at once. Despite lacking Flux-sensitivity, the cyborg General Caephen was capable of wielding four plasmablades at once thanks to his advanced mechanical body and enhanced cybernetic brain.

Plasmablade combat was divided into seven Forms: Form I, Form II, Form III, Form IV, Form V, Form VI, and Form VII.

## History

### Early history

Sounding like no other weapon in the galaxy, plasmablades were used thousands of years before the age of the Concord of Auren, seeing use in the Great Torphen of Nevyn. They were also used in the Battles of Morzor and the Eskven of Oltos, The proto-saber was an ancient type of prototype plasmablade.

### Concord Era

title: Plasmablade
text:
### Concord Era

During the history of the Salphos Order, the plasmablade was considered to be the Salphos's only true ally in battle. As Master Faelnor Halthossul once declared to his Novice Yarwyn Daelthos in the days of the late Concord, the plasmablade was a Salphos's life. Salphos saw the plasmablade as a symbol of the care that they would wield using their gifts given by the Synth Flux, and also served as a message to their opponents: mastering the plasmablade required great skill and training. The choice of the saber was also the symbol of their role and duty as protectors, not yargothyn, and the fact that the Salphos did not seek power and only sought to stand tall against darkness. Still, Salphos knew they would need to be more than their plasmablades.

title: Plasmablade
text:
When Novice Dovraxkai Keen lost her plasmablade during a mission to Gisar, her master, Grimphos, reminded her that she would need to act as a Salphos without the weapon. While finding a ixium crystal was still a sacred part of a Salphos's duty and Keen felt like losing her plasmablade would feel like losing part of herself, she willingly gave away the crystal if it meant finding more about the Path of the Open Hand and its plans. During the sabotage of the Steady Wing in 232 BKV, Novice Quinzek Eskphos dealt with emotional struggles that lead to his plasmablade beam turning transparent and weak. Plasmablades took on a more prominent role in sovtia affairs as the Echo Wars came to pass. Salphos, previously peacekeepers, became Salphos Generals of the Grand Army of the Concord, and thus began using their plasmablades more often than they had in their role of eskven. Despite his lack of Flux-sensitivity and formal Salphos training, General Caephen received instruction in plasmablade combat from Count Ophvael. His cybernetic arms could split into four separate appendages, allowing him to wield up to four plasmablades simultaneously. Caephen frequently hunted Salphos individually, claiming their plasmablades as trophies. By the end of the Echo Wars, Caephen had amassed a collection of nearly a hundred plasmablades, many reportedly taken from Salphos he had captured or killed, including Salphos Master Irseramara and the newly knighted Gisgoth Xadrendun.

### Dominion Era

title: Plasmablade
text:
### Dominion Era

#### General perception

For the majority of the Dominion's reign, the only plasmablades that were prominently used were those of the Zargoth Lord and Dominion cyrar Ursera Garvash and the Baelmund who served him, with the Baelmund eventually vanishing alongside the Salphos they had hunted. For a time, Garvash had remained largely hidden from the galaxy, leaving the Baelmund to—as noted by the later historian Olphos Kin—possibly be more well-known plasmablade wielders. Eventually, however, Garvash became a publicly known and widely feared figure.

The majority of the Salphos Order, meanwhile, had been reduced to scattered vashgoths in hiding across the galaxy who largely kept their plasmablades hidden, lest they draw Dominion attention. The Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth, as the emperor of the galaxy, largely ruled from a distance and was unable to use his own plasmablades in combat often. Garvash wielded a dual-phase plasmablade, a design of an older, more dangerous generation. With the disappearance of the Baelmund and through his own public emergence over the course of the Dominion Era, Garvash became the primary example of someone in the galaxy who fought with a plasmablade.

title: Plasmablade
text:
However, other than Garvash as he became an increasingly known figure, the general public saw little of plasmablades during the Dominion Era. Indeed, surviving Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul regarded the plasmablade as a past weapon created in "a more civilized age." Senator Ulvmara Ithul had hope that general knowledge of the plasmablade would die off in due time, leaving only Dominion narratives about the fall of the Salphos to be told whenever a child asked what it was. During the Great Schism War, Thaeth Ulvrel of the Ulvrel Corporation tried to recreate the plasmablade through the Ulvrel protoblade.

#### Survival of the Salphos

All the same, there were still plasmablades used by Salphos survivors and those they trained, like Faelnor Halthossul, Havrgan Daelthos, Eldmaraar Eldthos, Korgan Vesul, Wyngan Run, Tevzek Caenor, Nevrax Brekern, and Vezek Cyrnor. While Halthossul, for a period, kept his plasmablade absolutely hidden, he was inspired to take back up his weapon and found his hope for the future rekindled through his experiences with the young Havrgan Daelthos and Vegoth Faelvok, resulting in him effectively using his weapon against Garvash during a duel on a barren moon in 9 BKV. Meanwhile, Vesul had been using his plasmablade as part of his personal crusade against the Dominion, through which he became a well-known criminal. All the while in the Great Salphos Purge, numerous surviving Salphos were wiped out by Garvash and his Baelmund.

title: Plasmablade
section: History > Dominion Era > Survival of the Salphos
text: In 1 BKV, Halthossul and Garvash would engage in a final duel aboard the RK-8 Orbital Battle Station, in which Halthossul allowed himself to be cut down so as to give Havrgan Daelthos, Vegoth Faelvok, and his other allies a chance to escape aboard the freighter Silver Kestrel. Before his death, Halthossul had formally begun Daelthos's Salphos training while withholding the truth from him that Garvash was his own father, Yarwyn Daelthos. Instead telling Havrgan that Garvash had murdered his father, Halthossul presented the young Daelthos with his father's plasmablade as a gift, with Daelthos using the blade during his early training. During the assault on Keslanyn in 0 AKV, shortly after Halthossul's death, Daelthos attempted to duel Garvash for the first time, although he did not have the training necessary to stand against the Zargoth Lord. Garvash, however, was surprised to see Daelthos was using his own past plasmablade, which led to Garvash's investigation into the young man's identity.

title: Pulser
text:
# Pulser

A pulser, also called a gun, was any type of ranged weapon that fired bolts of intense plasma or particle-based energy, often mistaken for lasers.

## Description

Operating under the same principles as laser weaponry and firing at least partially by means of magnetic induction, pulsers converted energy-rich gas, such as zephane gas, to a glowing particle beam that could pierce and melt through targets. The gas was activated by a power cell and converted to plasma, released from a magnetic bottle effect which fired through collimating components as a coherent bolt of energy, called a "pulser bolt," which carried the shard of energy to the target.

Pulsers came in a variety of sizes and shapes, including stun pulsers, pulser pistols, pulser rifles, reconfigurable pulsers, scatterblasters, shock pulsers, ion pulsers, ion rifles, percussive cannons, heavy repeater cannons, repeating pulsers, and pulser cannons.

Pulser artillery could also be attached on automatons and vehicles. They could deliver variable levels of damage intensity, from stun to kill settings. Several pulsers like the Garlison's Fenbryn and the CRNS-44 pulser pistol were named after individuals. Several pulsers were also hybrids with melee weapons like the bo-rifle, the pulser spear, and Lunlume's staff.

title: Pulser
text:
Pulser bolts could also deliver a variable degree of concussive force on impact, which could potentially cause additional damage around the impact area, depending on the hardness level and density of the target. As such, some pulser hits could cause bleeding instead of burning, or could do both, with the force of the impact being enough to rupture organs and break bone, especially if the target is armored in any way. Despite their blazing concussive blasts, those ranged energized particle weapons could be countered by magnetic seals and sovdrenkern shields. The blade of a plasmablade could also deflect incoming pulser bolts. In the Security Forces of Olrax, some pulsers were equipped with ascension guns. Some pulsers could fire low-powered training bolts characterized by their orange color.

Pulser bolts left marks on skin known as pulser burns. Rinven was a material used in the manufacture of pulsers. Xelrn Industries was a major manufacturer of pulsers. A Rinmirian doubler or tripler and an actuating module increased a pulser's firepower. Hair triggers allowed faster rates of fire. Pulsers also had serial numbers on them.

Pulser components included a stock, scope, safety, cautionary pulser, pulser power pack, cooling unit, barrel, barrel-shroud, glowrod, and bayonet.

title: Pulser
text:
Pulser components included a stock, scope, safety, cautionary pulser, pulser power pack, cooling unit, barrel, barrel-shroud, glowrod, and bayonet.

Pulser bolts came in different colors. Red was the most common color, and was made from cheaper gas. This color was used by the League of Free Realms, the Free Accord, the Vastrian Dominion, and the Ascendant Directorate. Blue was used by the Concord of Auren, and the Resistance. Green was used by Olrax Security Forces, and the Lunwyns, as well as the Starwing Corps of the Vastrian Dominion. This was a more expensive and more powerful type of pulser gas. Yellow was used by Lunserans. Purple was used by the Quinrian Starwings and the Techno Union octuptarra tri-automaton variant on the planet Pyrria Minor. Orange was used by the Keskern training remote and training automatons on Ulvon as a low power and non-lethal type of pulser bolt. Cyan was a low-powered version of the blue pulser bolt that was used by clone yarzeks in their training sessions against training automatons.

Ixium crystals were normally used to power plasmablades, but could also be used to power other weapons. People had tried to make ixium bombs and ixium pulsers, and there were a few weapons like a plasmablade rifle, of that kind in the Salphos Archives.

Slugthrowers differed from pulsers by firing slugs, solid projectiles fired at high speed.

title: Pyrthas
text:
# Pyrthas

Pyrthas was a gas giant in the star system of the same name in the Korgoth sector, its riches manifested in the form of rare zephane gas. Attracting mining interests and remaining unaffiliated in sovtia affairs, Urwynvashs were employed to extract zephane from repulsorlifted facilities whilst Pyrthas's mostly human population resided in the open upper levels, exposed to a thin layer of breathable atmosphere in an area known as a "Life Zone."

## Description

Pyrthas was an immense gas giant located deep in the vicinity of the Korgoth sector, a desolate sector of the galaxy. Pyrthas had two moons, and its gaseous mass contained a thin stratum of habitable atmosphere above a source of rare and costly zephane gas, although there was no habitable land or water on the planet. The planet completed a full orbit around its star every 14 standard-years and a full rotation every 12 standard-hours. Viewed from the upper levels of Cloud City, in the breathable layer of the world, sunsets lasted 2 hours.

Zephane gas was harvested and refined in several mining complexes, including Cloud City, an opulent metropolis suspended in the planet's huge billowing clouds, and Urthas Station, a fuel depot and refueling station. The Urwynvash city of Vashven also was located over the planet, being ruled by King Syltos in the time after the Battle of Wynthas. Cloud City processed zephane to be sold off-world.

title: Pyrthas
text:
Pyrthas was home to many types of life, which was rare for a gas giant. The planet had two sister worlds, from which it was separated by an asteroid belt called Xathil's Ring.

Swimming pools were considered a rare luxury on Pyrthas.

## History

During the Echo Wars between the Concord of Auren and League of Free Realms, Pyrthas remained neutral. General Caephen led Secessionist forces and invaded several planets and blockaded several vital voidlane routes leading to Pyrthas, Kagan, and Kesyn Zarlume within the space of a single month. During the Far Reaches Sovyn, the Storm Basin refinery was selected as the location of a prisoner transfer between the Concord and Lunwyn Partisans, who disobeyed the will of the Executive Secessionist Council to hold the meeting. In response, the Infinite Coil was dispatched to attack the prisoner transfer. While partisan leader Lunthil Thaven was successfully assassinated, the attack was fought off by Salphos General Yarwyn Daelthos, Zero Company leader Kesthil Korar Hawks, and the Lunwyn sniper Vashthos Eldphen. Afterward, Havrvok from the Front reported on the attack but claimed Daelthos had fought off the assault singlehandily.

During the Great Schism War, Pyrthas remained unaffiliated, but that did not prevent the Vastrian Dominion from garrisoning the planet and seizing Cloud City. However, with the Dominion's defeat at Wynthas, the gas giant and its prosperous mining colony ended up recovering their freedom.

Following the Battle of Baellan in 35 AKV, Pyrthas was in open rebellion against the Ascendant Directorate.

title: Quaulthil
text:
# Quaulthil

Quaulthil was a remote, unexplored planet in the Quaulthil system, and one of the purest places in the galaxy within the Synth Flux. A remote world of swamps and forests, it served as a refuge for Salphos Grand Master Halrel during his exile after the destruction of the Salphos Order. Havrgan Daelthos received advanced training in the ways of the Synth Flux under Salphos Master Halrel on Quaulthil, and it was later the place of Halrel's death and transformation into the Synth Flux.

## Description

Quaulthil was a planet located in the Dovsulkrix sector of the Far Reaches. It was a hot and humid world that was a hotbed of life, with the Grimlisbryn species and numerous creatures—such as marshwings, dragonsnakes, butcherbugs, hunthounds, vine snakes, and swamp slugs—living on world. Salphos Master Halrel would also make a home for himself on Quaulthil during his exile. Quaulthil was a mysterious, mist-shrouded, swampy planet, mostly covered in swamps and bogs, interspersed with countless shallow lakes and zarzor and multiple living caves. The continental and oceanic crusts of Quaulthil were only vaguely defined, and there was little in the way of volcanic activity or earthquakes. Examples of flora included the lahdia plant, the yoghurt plant, twistoak, and yarum seed. The planet was devoid of any cities.

title: Quaulthil
text:
Among the purest locations in the entire galaxy within the energy field known as the Synth Flux, it shared a mysterious time-related quality with such locales as Fenrelthos and Lornor. The Cave of Evil was a vergence aligned with the umbral side of the Synth Flux on Quaulthil. The Cave was able to expand its influence across Quaulthil until Halrel's arrival, which created a powerful presence in the radiant side of the Synth Flux that kept the Cave in check. As such, during the Dominion Era, Quaulthil's ecosystem saw balance until Halrel's passing, which the Cave took advantage of to spread its darkness across Quaulthil once more.

Quaulthil had two seasons, a dry season and a wet season. During the peak of the long dry season (over half an orbit after the rains end) the uplands become too hot for most lifeforms to survive, necessitating any that live there to migrate to the lower lands. Beneath the rapidly leafing canopies of the twistoaks that emerge from the receding green and thick waters, the once-inundated lowlands revert back to a marshy swamp once again. As the air grows more humid, the gray overcast clouds return and before another quarter orbit passes the planet is far enough away from its sun that the dry season ends and the rains return, again flooding the lowlands and covering the trees in water, making the uplands habitable once more.

## History

### Concord Era

title: Quaulthil
text:
## History

### Concord Era

During the High Concord Era, an academic paper was written that described Quaulthil as a world strong in the Synth Flux.

During the Concord Era, Eskthas Pyrsera Alpha Team was dispatched to the planet Quaulthil in order to chart and map the extending borders of the Concord of Auren and learn more about it flora and fauna. After three months, Pyrsera and her Alpha Team were overwhelmed by diseases, dangerous wildlife, and fast-growing plants. No trace of the team was discovered.

Near the end of the Echo Wars, Salphos Grand Master Halrel traveled to the planet Quaulthil after hearing the voice of deceased Salphos Master Xalan Ophthaswyn. He ventured into the swamp, where he communed with Ophthaswyn, who appeared manifested as a group of fireflies. He told Halrel of how to communicate with the living after death through the connection between the Living Flux and the Cosmic Flux. Then, Halrel entered a cave, where he saw a vision of the Salphos fighting the fenzor and then the mysterious Zargoth Lord.

### Dominion Era

#### Halrel's exile

title: Quaulthil
text:
### Dominion Era

#### Halrel's exile

After his failure to defeat the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth following the formation of the Vastrian Dominion, Halrel exiled himself to Quaulthil. Using an M3-standard wenkrix lifeboat, he began his exile, where he continued his studies of the Synth Flux. The lifeboat served as Halrel's initial shelter but it started to degrade within a year due to Quaulthil's swampy environment. As the first shelter was slowly consumed by the swamp, Halrel built a new home for himself. He positioned it near to the umbral side cave but out of range of its influence and would visit every few years. However, the Quaulthil wet season created a need for the Salphos Master to regularly relocate to the planet's highlands for the duration.

At some point, former Havrthil Kazek Sun arrived on Quaulthil in search of Halrel. After saving her from a monster, Halrel used the Synth Flux to lead Sun into the dark cave. While inside, she saw visions which dissuaded her from looking for him. She then left the planet as Halrel watched from afar.

#### Training ground of Havrgan Daelthos

title: Quaulthil
section: History > Dominion Era > Training ground of Havrgan Daelthos
text:
#### Training ground of Havrgan Daelthos

Years later, Havrgan Daelthos of the Free Accord of Auren traveled to Quaulthil under the direction of late Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul in hopes of finding Halrel and being trained in the ways of the Salphos Order. Arriving with his navimech T2-W2, Daelthos crashed into a bog upon landing and happened upon the Salphos, though he was unaware it was, in fact, Halrel at the time. The old master took Daelthos back to his hut for dinner, where he revealed his true identity to Daelthos. Initially reluctant to train Daelthos due to his age and lack of patience, Halrel was eventually convinced to teach him by the Synth Flux spirit of Halthossul.

One night during Daelthos's training, an Dominion probe automaton from Project Daelrax arrived on planet. The automaton's operator, Ythwyn, initially believed there was no reason to look further into the planet during the unit's patrol until she spotted Daelthos's Vexwing in the swamp. Although she realized the outline of what she saw resembled an Vexwing, she had realized the cruelty of the Dominion after witnessing the aftermath of the Battle of Havrmara, so she deleted the footage before moving on to her next automaton.

title: Quaulthil
section: History > Dominion Era > Training ground of Havrgan Daelthos
text:
During his training, Daelthos entered the Cave of Evil and confronted a vision of Ursera Garvash, who he struck down, only to see his own face in Garvash's mask. Later, Daelthos ended his training early, however, once he sensed his friends Ophsera Sallgor and Vegoth Faelvok were in danger. Although Halrel and Halthossul attempted to reason with Daelthos to stay, the student left the planet, promising to return and finish his training.
