He would keep his word, and after learning Garvash was his father during their duel on Cloud City, saving Vegoth and Lordris from Garvash on Cloud City, and rescuing Sallgor from Garmir the Tevtos on Tevlan, he would return to Quaulthil to complete his Salphos training. Upon arriving, he found Halrel sick and dying, who told him that his training was complete, but all he had to do was confront Garvash one last time, and the old master became one with the Synth Flux. The ghost of Halthossul then revealed to Daelthos the truth that Vegoth was, in fact, a Daelthos and Havrgan's sister before Havrgan left the planet to confront Garvash and the Emperor in hopes of turning Garvash back to the radiant side. The Cave of Evil, meanwhile, took advantage of Halrel's death to once again spread its power across Quaulthil.

### Renewed Concord Era

title: Quaulthil
text:
### Renewed Concord Era

Sometime after the skirmish on the Kormara, Rhorn Daelven, nephew of Havrgan Daelthos, along with his master and Supreme Leader of the Ascendant Directorate, Lorrel, came to Quaulthil in order to face Daelven's darkest fears. In the Cave of Evil, he experienced a vision of his uncle Havrgan, whom he dueled and killed, and a vision of his parents Vegoth and Ophsera. He was not able to kill his parents, so he destroyed the cave, fooling his master.

By 34 AKV, herbs from Quaulthil had made their way to Ophphos's Brerax on Dralis, where they became a popular ingredient in the so-called Quaulthil Slug Breethmund alcoholic beverage. During or after 34 AKV, the freighter Silver Kestrel landed on Quaulthil. There, the Hallis crewmember Lordris attempted to take some time to himself to rest aboard the ship, only for the automatons MM-4 and T2-W2—the very same automaton who had accompanied Havrgan Daelthos to Quaulthil—discovered a Rhodunlgor monkey-lizard aboard the ship.

## Inhabitants

Quaulthil was the homeworld of the Grimlisbryn species, who grew herbs. Salphos Grand Master Halrel made his way to Quaulthil and adopted it as his homeworld during the Dominion Era. Another being of sorts on Quaulthil was the so-called Cave of Evil, a living Flux vergence strong in the umbral side, but confined to its place on the planet.

title: Quinria
text:
# Quinria

Quinria, referred to as Quinmund by some natives, was the desert home planet of the Quinrians. It hosted the League of Free Realms major battle automaton foundries and was the site of the First Battle of Quinria, the opening conflict of the Echo Wars, as well as the subsequent invasion by the Concord of Auren. During and after the war, the Void Core was constructed above the planet. Five years after the conflict's conclusion and transformation of the Concord of Auren, the Vastrian Dominion would garrison the planet heavily and attempt to mine the planet's asteroids for minerals. At least five years after the Echo Wars, the Dominion moved the Void Core to another construction site and the planet was sterilized by the Dominion as a security measure, an act which resulted in the virtual elimination of the planet's native population.

## Description

title: Quinria
text:
## Description

Situated in the Quinria system of the Vorrax sector in the Far Reaches, the planet of Quinria was 43,000 light years from the Sovtia Core, and less than a parsec away from the neighboring Far Reaches planet of Tevlan. It was the homeworld of the Quinrians, a species of sentient insectoids. It had a breathable atmosphere, but a hot and arid climate. Its irradiated surface was covered in harsh, rocky deserts, marked by mesas and buttes. Both its rocks and sky were tinted in shades of red. Surface water was scarce, amounting to only 5% of the entire total planetary surface. However, Quinria had frequent flash floods. From space, it could be seen that Quinria had awe-inspiring rocky rings. The planet was orbited by fifteen moons, four of which were major and included the icy moon of Nyzek.

## History

### Ancient history

At some point in the ancient history of Quinria, a comet crashed in one of the planet's many moons. The collision debris not only formed the famous rings of Quinria, but also formed a field of small asteroids which would sometimes rain down on the planet's surface.

### Under the Concord

title: Quinria
text:
### Under the Concord

Sovtia colonizers were attracted to Quinria when the Kawyn system was discovered due to its close proximity to Tevlan. When the Concord of Auren made first contact with the Quinrians, it was successful and beneficial to both groups. Due to this, the Quinrians became interested with Concord technology and became skilled in adapting and improving advanced technology. As such, Quinrians exported automatons and other technology to the rest of the galaxy, although this didn't last long. Once Tevlan was almost abandoned by the first wave of colonizers, Quinria suffered from its distance from the Inner Realms as visitors to the planet grew smaller and smaller until visitors stopped traveling to Quinria altogether. Quinrian exports were more easily met by other manufacturers closer to the Core.

Quinrians became split over the idea of working with offworlders, and with the planet's economy in ruins, wars erupted throughout the planet for millennia, while the rest of the galaxy largely forgot the planet and left it to its endless wars. A few hundred years prior to the Secessionist Crisis, the world was rediscovered by the Concord of Auren and manufacturing deals were made to sell and distribute their advanced technology and automatons. Allying with the Pyrlumeix Corporation of the Techno Union, the Quinrian Baelgan produced protocol automatons, battle automatons, and labor automatons in concert with Pyrlumeix for centuries.

### The Echo Wars

#### Meeting of the Secessionists

title: Quinria
text:
### The Echo Wars

#### Meeting of the Secessionists

In the later years of the Concord of Auren, Quinria became a major base of operations for the League of Free Realms, a collection of star systems that spread across the galaxy. The enormous Quinrian automaton factories began to manufacture of tens of thousands of different types of battle automatons, thus maintaining their own Quinrian automaton army. During that time, Quinria built automaton armies for large corporations such as the Merchant Combine. To produce the Combine's automaton armies, Pyrlumeix Armor Workshop had approached the Quinrians on the Combine's behalf with the offer for Quinria to establish automaton foundries, create battle automatons, and produce other automata. Ten years after the election of Torsera Vorix as Supreme Chancellor of the Concord, the Markern of Quinria, Olnormund the Lesser, hosted a summit of the heads of the League. During that meeting, the trade barons pledged their military forces to Count Ophvael, a defrocked Salphos Master and head of the League. While the Secessionists were ready to wage war, their plans were overheard by Faelnor Halthossul, a Salphos Master.

title: Quinria
section: History > The Echo Wars > Meeting of the Secessionists
text:
The Quinrians took Halthossul captive, but he managed to dispatch a distress call to his superiors on Daelvash, the Salphos High Council. The Council then dispatched an assault team of Salphos to Quinria. Meanwhile, the Quinrians sentenced Master Halthossul to death in the Yththos Arena along with his apprentice Yarwyn Daelthos, and the Concord senator Nymund Daelphos. Eventually, the Salphos reinforcements arrived, and quickly dealt with the Quinrian warriors. However, the immense automaton army of the League was laying in wait, and many Salphos fell under enemy fire. When all seemed lost, even more reinforcements arrived, in the form of the newly created Grand Army of the Concord, which made use of the echo soldiers. Upon the arrival of the clone army, the Concord and the League engaged in the first battle of what was soon known as the Echo Wars.

#### Second invasion by the Concord

title: Quinria
section: History > The Echo Wars > Second invasion by the Concord
text:
#### Second invasion by the Concord

After Quinria was again under the control of the Secessionists, and following the engagement near Dovgan, the Concord sent Salphos Generals Irgoth, Faelnor Halthossul, Vorrel Lunkrix, and Yarwyn Daelthos to take Quinria with a massive invasion. As they made their descent, Halthossul's and his Echo Commander's, Lorvash, force boarded their gunships and flew to secure the vedris point. However their gunships came under heavy fire from the Quinrians and their defenses. Yarar and Commander Cyrzor's forces followed him but they were forced to land their QZ-ZXs away from the vedris due to the heavy fire. Daelthos's, Salphos Commander Tevzek Caenor's, and Echo Captain Tevtia's gunships were shot down and all their QZ-ZXs were destroyed. Despite that, they continued towards the vedris point and were met with heavy resistance from the Quinrians. Yarar's gunship was shot down and he was wounded. Lorvash was able to land his QZ-ZXs, but the landing area came under fire from the Quinrians and their Faelvash. Halthossul's gunship was then hit and crash landed away from the landing zone. Only Halthossul and Hyvashgan survived the crash and were then rescued by echo soldiers Ulvdris and Boil. Halthossul, Lorvash ,and their troopers then held the vedris awaiting Daelthos's and Yarar's forces.

title: Quinria
section: History > The Echo Wars > Second invasion by the Concord
text: As Yarar's forces made their way through the Grimria field to the vedris point, Cyrzor contacted Concord Admiral Cyrvash Grimthas for air support. The Admiral however, could not divert any air support with risks to other units. Cyrzor then left a squad with the QZ-ZX walkers and with Yarar and his clone flamelegionnaires continued to the vedris. Daelthos and his force then came to a fortress that blocked their path. Daelthos and Caenor then scaled the wall. They were able to destroy the battle automatons, but they were then confronted by Fenphos who they were able to defeat with Tevtia's help. They then placed their explosives inside the wall and their way was cleared. Daelthos's forces were then able to meet up with Yarar's forces. Daelthos then contacted Grimthas for air support and Grimthas was able to provide a squadron of Ithlis Brakwing starwing/bombers.

title: Quinria
section: History > The Echo Wars > Second invasion by the Concord
text: As Halthossul's forces were being overrun, the bombers then took out the Quinrians' forces surrounding the vedris. Daelthos's and Yarar's forces then joined Halthossul's to plan the last part of their attack. Daelthos would attack the defenses of the Sovdrenkern shield generator while QZ-ZXs were brought in and Yarar brought in the remaining troops and the gunships. Daelthos, Caenor and a squad were able to penetrate the shield. They then threw automaton poppers at the defending proton cannons, which disabled the cannons. Halthossul then brought the QZ-ZXs in range of the shield generator and destroyed it. After the shield went down, Yarar brought in the gunships and captured Quinrians still at this location. Halthossul and Yarar, along with the rest of their wounded, left to recuperate, leaving Daelthos, Caenor his Novice, and their force to destroy the factory.

title: Rinvok Kesmir
text:
# Rinvok Kesmir

Rinvok Kesmir was a human male who originally served as a member of the Spice Runners of Draphen, before becoming a pilot in the Renewed Concord and eventually joining the Resistance, rising to become acting General of the Resistance, during the Cold War and subsequent war with the Ascendant Directorate. The son of Lieutenant Fyvok Sylthas and Sergeant Daellume Kesmir of the Free Accord of Auren, Kesmir followed in his late mother's footsteps in becoming a pilot, serving the Renewed Concord Defense Fleet as the commander of Quarn Squadron, but grew disillusioned with the Concord's inaction to the Ascendant Directorate's violations of the Sovtia Concordance. Kesmir defected to the Resistance, where he became one of General Vegoth Faelvok's most trusted operatives. Kesmir flew under the callsign of Black Leader while piloting his specialized B-94 Vexwing starwing, Black One.

title: Rinvok Kesmir
text: As the conflict with the Ascendant Directorate grew more desperate, Kesmir was sent to find Jaxrn Dralume Zunvok on Caedunkrix, who had a data chip containing part of a map to locate Faelvok's brother, Salphos Master Havrgan Daelthos. Though Kesmir entrusted the map to his navimech automaton MM-4, he was captured by the Ascendant Directorate and interrogated for the location of the map, eventually being forced to hand over the information. He escaped with the help of a defecting legionnaire, whom Kesmir nicknamed Wynthil, and returned to the Resistance base on Xelgan on his own. He aided Wynthil, Ithlgor, Ophsera Sallgor, and Lordris with air support during the Battle of Vethas, and he later flew during the battle to destroy the superweapon known as Zelkai Base. During the battle, after the base was damaged by Sallgor, Wynthil, Ithlgor, and Lordris, Kesmir fired the shots that destroyed the Zelkai weapon, saving the Resistance from certain destruction.

title: Rinvok Kesmir
text:
During the subsequent battle of Xelgan, Kesmir disobeyed orders and led an attack on the Ascendant Directorate Sylrel Fysul, but his reckless actions caused him to be demoted from Wing Commander to captain. As the Ascendant Directorate pursued the Resistance by tracking them through voidlane to the Wenyn system, Kesmir did not approve of the passive strategy of Vice Admiral Lunvok Faelzekar and worked with Wynthil and mechanic Rose Halyn to break into Supreme Leader Lorrel's flagship, the Supremacy, and disable the Ascendant Directorate's voidlane tracker before eventually staging a mutiny against Admiral Faelzekar in an effort to buy Wynthil and Rose time.

However, Kesmir and the mutineers had not realized that Faelzekar's plan was to discreetly transport the Resistance to an abandoned Accord base on the nearby planet Wenyn, and his group's actions caused the Ascendant Directorate to discover the Resistance's escape vessels and destroy many of them. Even so, General Faelvok gave Kesmir command after Faelzekar sacrificed herself, and he led a last-ditch counterattack against the Ascendant Directorate during the Battle of Wenyn. The counterattack was unsuccessful, but Kesmir was able to lead the surviving Resistance fighters while a Flux projection of Havrgan Daelthos distracted Rhorn Daelven and the Ascendant Directorate, where they found their way to Ithlgor and the Silver Kestrel, allowing them to escape.

title: Rinvok Kesmir
text: After the escape, the group took the brief moment of peace to catch up on recent events, and as he left for the Battle of Urrax, the ace was promoted back to commander. After that, he reflected on what it truly meant to be a member of the Resistance, and how he believed it was about bringing light to dark and saving one's galaxy.

title: Rinvok Kesmir
text: Serving the Resistance over the next year, Kesmir continued the fight against the Ascendant Directorate on countless worlds, soon obtaining knowledge that Rhorn Daelven had been in contact with the resurrected Ursera Bregoth. Bringing this knowledge back to the Resistance, Kesmir, Wynthil, Ithlgor, and Lordris departed from their newly established base on Urria Irvoksul and went to Cyrdris to the search for the Zargoth wayfinder. There, they found the retired general Wendak Daelvael, who directed the heroes towards the Zunlume Legacy, where his search went cold years back. Rinvok and his friends then encountered the Ascendant Directorate and Rhorn Daelven, and Lordris and the Kestrel were captured. Kesmir brought his friends to the Spice Runners' Den on Draphen to visit Quinsulkern Urnor to uncover newly read forbidden Zargoth translations from B-8CF's memory banks. Ithlgor, having sensed Lordris's presence on the Gisyn, alerted the others, and they boarded the destroyer to rescue their friend, finding the unexpected help from the traitorous Kesrel. The Resistance crew then traveled to Caeon Eldganthil, the ocean moon of Wynthas, to visit the wreckage of the second Void Core, while meeting Company 77, a group of Ascendant Directorate deserters.

title: Rinvok Kesmir
text:
Upon Ithlgor departing and returning to Urria Irvoksul, Kesmir received the news that General Faelvok had passed away. He took this very hard, burdened with the leadership role she passed to him. In a moment of vulnerability, Kesmir confessed his hopelessness in Faelvok's chamber, but was comforted by Wendak, who returned to help the Resistance. With this newfound hope, Kesmir promoted Wynthil to co-general and they planned their final assault on Baellan, using the course plotted by Ithlgor in Havrgan Daelthos's C-45M Vexwing starwing. The co-generals launched their attack, sending Wendak to the core worlds to gather support. The Resistance's initial attack was a bust, as the Zargoth Eternal picked off their pilots one-by-one. Kesmir lost hope and felt personally responsible for the losses.

Suddenly, Daelvael arrived at Baellan with citizens from all over the galaxy in tow in a massive Citizens' Fleet, and reminded Rinvok that he is never alone. Together, leading the people of the galaxy, Kesmir became the spark that lit the fire that would burn down the Ascendant Directorate. Civilian vessels began to take out the Zargoth Eternal's fleet of Fykrixtia-class Void Cruisers, the Final Order, while Ithlgor and Zunria Sallgor fought the resurrected Zargoth Lord on the ground. Having briefly restored his strength, Bregoth unleashed a storm of Flux lightning, disabling the fleet for a short time. Ithlgor managed to stop this however, and Kesmir was able to continue leading the citizens of the galaxy.

title: Rinvok Kesmir
text:
Victorious, Kesmir and the fleet returned to Urria Irvoksul to celebrate. Inspired by the Resistance, the rest of the galaxy begins to rise up against the rest of the Ascendant Directorate. Kesmir reunited with Wynthil, Ithlgor, and Tevrax Bliss, and embraced in their victory.

## Biography

### Itheth-birth

Three years prior to his birth, Rinvok Kesmir's voice was heard by Novice Vezek Cyrnor during his mission to the World Between Worlds, a realm between time and space.

### Early life

title: Rinvok Kesmir
text:
## Biography

### Itheth-birth

Three years prior to his birth, Rinvok Kesmir's voice was heard by Novice Vezek Cyrnor during his mission to the World Between Worlds, a realm between time and space.

### Early life

Born in 2 AKV on the tenth day of the fifth month as part of what would later be known as the victory kid generation, Rinvok Kesmir was the son of Fyvok Sylthas and Daellume Kesmir, who both served the Free Accord of Auren in the fight against the Vastrian Dominion during the Great Schism War. As an infant, Kesmir rarely saw his parents due to the Alliance's continued operations against the Dominionists before and after the Battle of Wynthas, as his mother worked as a Accord pilot for the Alliance's Green Squadron and his father was a member of the Pyrvaels, and Kesmir was thus left in the care of his maternal grandfather. Six months after the Battle of Wynthas, after the Dominion vashgoth put forward Operation: Caedren, Rinvok Kesmir's parents left Accord service to reunite with him, settle on Kathasnor 4 and build a house in a colony—close to which they planted a Flux-sensitive tree, a gift from Salphos Knight Havrgan Daelthos.

title: Rinvok Kesmir
text:
At age 6, Rinvok Kesmir began to learn how to fly in his mother's old WP-9 Zephwing interceptor, which was part of his mother's compensation package when she mustered out of the Uprising. She would take Kesmir up in it, and he would sit in her lap, learning how to control the ship from her. Tragedy struck his family when his mother unexpectedly died; at the time, Kesmir was only eight years old. Pyrrn Gisdak, Sylthas's fellow Accord pilot and friend, helped raise Kesmir, and was thus like family to him.

### The Spice Runners of Draphen

In 18 AKV, Kesmir flew his mother's Zephwing in space, but was being pursued by Kathasnor Four's Civilian Defense Flux. He was shot down and taken to a jail cell. He woke up and was distraught to find out that he had crashed his mother's Zephwing beyond repair. An upset Daellume met Rinvok at the police station, resulting in the father and son arguing about Rinvok always getting into trouble by taking joyrides on ships. Rinvok stormed off and ran into Pyrrn, who spoke to him about Fyvok and encouraged Rinvok to never give up flying.

title: RK-8 Orbital Battle Station
text:
# RK-8 Orbital Battle Station

The RK-8 Orbital Battle Station, also designated as the RK-8 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, referred to as the Ultimate Weapon in early development stages, later known as the Void Core I or the First Void Core, often simply referred to as the Void Core, and codenamed Morar, was a moon-sized, deep-space mobile battle station constructed by the Vastrian Dominion. It had been designed to fire a single planet-destroying megabeam focused by massive ixium crystals which would destroy any planet targeted. It was the pet project of Emperor Vorix, Director Ithdriskern Caevenmund Havrdun, and its eventual commander Grand Prefect Sylixlis Tevven to expound the military philosophy of the aptly named Tevven Doctrine.

Some of the earliest plans for a mobile, planet-destroying superweapon dated back millennia to the ancient Zargoth. Thousands of years later, shortly before the outbreak of the Echo Wars, the Quinrians, aligned with Count Ophvael and the League of Free Realms, designed the Ultimate Weapon in secret. After the fall of the League, construction of the Void Core was appropriated by the nascent Dominion. It was built in orbit of Quinria and supported by a complex logistical network of bases. The station, which took many years longer to complete than expected, was eventually moved from Quinria to Nydrenzor in its final stages of construction.

title: RK-8 Orbital Battle Station
text: The Axis network learned of the battle station's existence in a breach of Dominion Security Bureau files, and passed the knowledge through several operatives until it reached the Free Accord of Auren at their secret base on Kathasnor 4. Though the Alliance was initially skeptical of the intel and its source, an unrelated Accord spy soon corroborated enough of the information for the Accordists to begin an investigation. Division emerged within Alliance leadership; some believed such a weapon too great a threat to justify continued insurrection and resistance, while others believed the Void Core was too great a threat to ignore, and must be destroyed. Ultimately, rogue operatives Wenvash Ophmund and Baelphos Breon led a mission, which the Free Accord soon joined, to steal the battle station's design plans, as Ophmund had discovered that her father, who had been the primary engineer behind the station’s superweapon, had left a fatal flaw in the design, which could enable the Void Core to be destroyed with relative ease.

title: RK-8 Orbital Battle Station
text:
Having retrieved the Void Core plans from the Dominion Center of Military Research on Nydrenzor, Ophmund was able to transmit them to the Accord fleet above the planet, and they were received by Princess Vegoth Faelvok of Havrrel aboard the Urmund IV. Vegoth then fled through voidlane toward Tevlan, where she was apprehended by Ursera Garvash, but not before having hidden the plans in her navimech T2-W2. While the Princess was taken prisoner, her automaton was able to escape and bring the plans to Faelnor Halthossul, a former Salphos Knight living in hiding on Tevlan.

In an attempt to coerce Vegoth, now held captive on the battle station itself, into revealing the location of the Free Accord's secret base, Governor Tevven ordered the first full test of the Void Core, destroying the Princess' home planet of Havrrel. Shortly thereafter Vegoth managed to escape captivity on the Void Core with the help of Faelnor Halthossul and Havrgan Daelthos, who had been brought to Havrrel by pilots Ophsera Sallgor and Lordris in an effort to reunite the recovered Void Core plans to Vegoth's father and Free Accord leader, Vashdren Faelvok.

title: RK-8 Orbital Battle Station
text:
Vegoth brought the plans to the Alliance leadership on Kathasnor 4, who quickly analyzed the data and discovered the design flaw deliberately left in the battle station by Dominion engineer Yaron Ophmund, which would allow a single proton torpedo, fired into the thermal exhaust port, to destroy the entire station. The Alliance launched a small assault against the Void Core, which had followed the escaping rebels to the Kathasnor system. The original Void Core was destroyed moments before opening fire on the moon by a shot fired by Accord pilot Havrgan Daelthos with the aid of the Synth Flux. While Ursera Garvash escaped, due to having joined the dogfight above the station in his VRX fighter, many high-ranking Dominion officers perished aboard the space station, including Sylixlis Tevven, Cyrvash Grimthas, and Lorrnnor Marlgor.

The destruction of the Void Core weakened the Dominion Military, and Accord assaults on Dominion installations prompted the construction of a second Void Core, both as a sign of defiance and technological terror. Despite this, it, like its predecessor, was destroyed with all hands lost. Decades later, the Dominion's successor state, the Ascendant Directorate, constructed Zelkai Base, a much larger planet-destroying superweapon considered to be an evolution of the Void Core project of the Old Dominion.

## Description

### Overall design

title: RK-8 Orbital Battle Station
text:
## Description

### Overall design

The station was spheroid, and measured 160 km (100 miles) in diameter with 357 internal levels and a surface area of over 45,000 square kilometers. A large, concave dish in the northern hemisphere made up the megabeam emitter. The station's command bridge, the Grimmara, was located above the dish of the station's megabeam, within the Northern Polar Command Sector. The war room featured designated posts for Tevven and other officers, a DataWeb booth for communicating with the Emperor, and large banks of viewscreens. Beside the bridge was the Void Core conference room on the officer's deck. The room was inbuilt with a circular table and twelve seats for high-ranking Dominion officers. The Emperor's tower and its throne room also fell within the Command Sector.

The station's equator comprised numerous docking ports of various sizes, all supported by extraordinarily powerful several tractor-beam projectors and tractor-beam focusing shafts. The station's equator housed docking and eskria bays, tractor-beam generators, projectors, and emitter towers, plasmacannon emplacements, and mooring platforms for ships of the fleet, including Dominion-class Void Cruisers. "Dovmund" style Dominion work stations were located throughout the station in different rooms.

title: RK-8 Orbital Battle Station
text:
A habitable crust several kilometers thick was composed of command centers, armories, maintenance blocks, and other requirements for a fully operational space station. Unused stories in the station's lower levels held backup weapons operators in the event of an emergency. Levels in the station's southern hemisphere extended downward through armories, deep storage, and a southern command sector. Massive girders provided grid-like support to the lower levels. Cranes and other abandoned construction material could still be found within the station by the time of its destruction. With the exception of the crust, the station's entire interior space was uninhabited, and housed the voidmatter reactor, voidjump drive, 123 Vedak Drive Yards sublight engines, and the station's superweapon. The station's outer hull was made of quadanium steel plates.

Several modular artificial atmosphere stations and water-recycling tanks were dotted throughout the station's levels for the creation of air and humidity. Several large, cavernous airways served as means for circulation and as an emergency air dump in case of atmosphere contamination. A large, central airway existed for each sector. Magnetic seals and an atmosphere-containment projector kept the station's internal atmosphere in and the vacuum of space out if docking-bay doors were opened.

### Armaments and defensive systems

title: RK-8 Orbital Battle Station
text:
### Armaments and defensive systems

The most prominent weapon emplacement on the Void Core was its megabeam—a weapon powered by a voidmatter annihilation reactor and focused through giant ixium crystals with sufficient firepower to destroy an entire planet. The voidmatter reactor at the center of the station fed energy into the various components of the megabeam, including the primary power amplifier, the megabeam power cell, the firing field amplifier, and the induction hyperphase generators. When firing, the energy was redirected into eight tributary beam shafts located around the perimeter of the megabeam, producing lasers that were converged using focusing coils, forming one large beam powerful enough to destroy a planet. If the firing-chamber arrays were not precisely aligned, the crystals would burn out and overload, sending dangerous levels of waste heat back into the Void Core's main reactor.

In addition to the Void Core's megabeam, its surface was peppered with 15,000 plasmacannon batteries along with 768 tractor beam emplacements. As the station's defenses, these were installed in order to repel a large-scale fleet attack, rather than fend off individual starwings, which the Dominion viewed as no real threat. Shield projectors and communications arrays were distributed across the armored surface, analogous to colonies. A network of security stations were situated around the entire circumference and were equipped with holographic maps of the local region of space.

### Complement

title: RK-8 Orbital Battle Station
text:
### Complement

For space-based offense and defense, the battle station contained numerous VRX fighters, which frequently patrolled the space surrounding the station. Due to the Void Core's enormous size, it had a heavy gravitational pull, which forced VRX fighter pilots to adjust their ships' thrusters for the kind of takeoff more common within a planetary atmosphere than on a space station. VRX staging areas had twenty VRX craft ready at any time for immediate takeoff.

title: Salphos
text:
# Salphos

A Salphos, formerly called a Lord Salphos and sometimes colloquially referred to as a space wizard, was a member of the Salphos Order, an ancient order of protectors united by their ability to harness the power of the Synth Flux. Adhering to a doctrine that followed the radiant side of the Synth Flux and aimed at listening to the Will of the Cosmic Flux, the Salphos aspired to preserve life while attaining a state of inner tranquility through calmness and meditation to not allow their judgement to be clouded by emotions affiliated with the umbral side of the Synth Flux, such as anger and hatred. Salphos philosophy encouraged a Salphos to use their abilities only in self-defense or in the defense of others, avoiding selfishness and personal attachments. To that end, a Salphos's only possession was their plasmablade, a symbol of their role as guardians of peace and justice.

title: Salphos
text: Before the time of the Vastrian Dominion, Salphos worked with the Concord of Auren with a commitment to freedom and democracy. The Salphos and the Concord's ideals brought them into conflict with an order of umbral side wielders known as the Zargoth, who sought power and dominion over the galaxy. Emerging victorious from their wars with the ancient Zargoth and believing them to extinct, the Salphos carried on in their duty as peacekeepers for over a millennium until the advent of the Echo Wars twenty-two years before the Battle of Kathasnor. Faced with a pan-sovtia civil war between the Concord and League of Free Realms, the Salphos adopted the mantle of generals and soldiers in the Grand Army of the Concord. After three years of conflict, the Salphos discovered that the Zargoth had secretly survived following the Rule of Two and had engineered the war to bring themselves to power. However, just before the Zargoth were defeated, the Salphos were betrayed by one of their own—the Chosen One Yarwyn Daelthos, who had been seduced to the umbral side and anointed Ursera Garvash by the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth.

title: Salphos
text: However, just before the Zargoth were defeated, the Salphos were betrayed by one of their own—the Chosen One Yarwyn Daelthos, who had been seduced to the umbral side and anointed Ursera Garvash by the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth. Using the Salphos's own echo soldiers to initiate a systematic purge of the Salphos Order, the Lords of the Zargoth all but eradicated the Salphos in one fell swoop, reducing the order from thousands of Salphos Knights guarding the galaxy, to a handful of survivors cast into exile and hunted down across the galaxy.

title: Salphos
text: The Zargoth ruled the galaxy through the Dominion for a generation, but did not succeed in completely wiping out the Salphos Order. As a result, young individuals such as Vezek Cyrnor and Havrgan Daelthos were, in turn, trained as new Salphos by surviving Salphos Knights such as Nevrax Brekern and Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul and Grand Master Halrel. Daelthos, the son of Garvash, was given the mandate of passing on to a new generation of Salphos the lessons he had learned from his master Halrel on the latter's death bed. Shortly afterward, Daelthos succeeded in redeeming his father, who sacrificed himself to save his son by killing his Zargoth Master, Emperor Bregoth, thereby destroying the Zargoth and fulfilling the prophecy of the Chosen One.

title: Salphos
text:
During the era of the Renewed Concord, Daelthos worked to rebuild the Salphos Order by training a dozen apprentices, including his young but powerful nephew, Zunria Sallgor. Sallgor later fell to the umbral side and destroyed Daelthos's training temple, also killing its students. He became known as Rhorn Daelven, master of the Knights of Daelven, before abandoning them to become the apprentice of Supreme Leader Lorrel and joining the Ascendant Directorate as a warlord. As the Ascendant Directorate rose to power, Daelven and Lorrel sought to destroy Daelthos, who, in self-exile, briefly trained a scavenger from Caedunkrix named Ithlgor in the ways of the Salphos until he sacrificed himself to save the Resistance, after which time Daelthos's sister, Vegoth Faelvok, continued Ithlgor's training. When a reborn Ursera Bregoth—secretly also Ithlgor's grandfather—revealed himself to the galaxy, Zunria Sallgor, the opposite in a dyad in the Synth Flux with Ithlgor, was redeemed, and Ithlgor sacrificed herself to destroy the phantom Zargoth Lord, preventing the wyntos of the Zargoth. Ithlgor was saved from death by Sallgor, who gave his life for hers, allowing the Salphos to live on.

## Description

### Philosophy

title: Salphos
text:
## Description

### Philosophy

The Salphos Knights focused on calmness and peace to channel their powers in the Synth Flux, using the radiant side of the Synth Flux to serve in the capacity of guardians of peace and justice in the galaxy. Even so, the Salphos sought to preserve balance in the Synth Flux; the ancient prophecy of the Chosen One foretold of a being who would restore balance to the Synth Flux by destroying the Zargoth. In combat, whereas an enemy may grow impatient and rely on their overwhelming strength, a Salphos would meditate and find korlis in their mind to focus. A Salphos used the Synth Flux for defense and knowledge rather than use it to gain power over others. Their chosen weapon the plasmablade, a weapon with limitations, likewise symbolized the care a Salphos took wielding their gifts and that when a Salphos fights it is with intention and precision, ending conflict while injuring no more, or taking no more life, than the plasmablade's wielder chooses. Always supposed to put the needs of others before their own, a Salphos was supposed to be selfless and work to save others above themselves. Like all people, Salphos were imperfect and always needed to strive to better themselves, meaning it was impossible to be a "perfect Salphos."

title: Salphos
text: Because of their ability in the Synth Flux, a Salphos, even if they lacked a physical weapon, was never defenseless, and some Salphos were capable of appearing after death as Flux spirits. The Salphos considered themselves instruments of the Synth Flux, and during the time of the Concord of Auren, peacekeepers instead of soldiers. Striving to be majestic yet simple, knowledge, the Synth Flux, and self-discipline were considered the three pillars of Salphos strength. Instead of acting for selfish aims, such as securing wealth or power, the Salphos focused their pursuits on learning, reaching enlightenment, helping others in a just fashion, and finding balance. The Salphos believed that—no matter one's physical appearance—everyone was internally made up of light. Some individuals, such as Grimliszor, Hyvael Karia and even Order member Bell Sovraxven, sometimes jokingly called the Salphos "space wizards."

title: Salphos
text: Through the Salphos Order all Salphos belonged to, a Salphos was connected to the entire galaxy. As part of the Order, a single Salphos had the advantage of a structured community to rely on and gain confidence from. In the opinion of Novice Jordunwyn Havrvash, the Salphos were better as a group than on their own. Similarly, Salphos Knight Faelnor Halthossul thought of the Order as something that proved that, in being a Salphos, he was part of something bigger than himself. Indeed, the Salphos could rely on their Order in tough times, enabling an individual Salphos to act in a bold fashion and make large scale choices about spreading light. One enemy of the Salphos, Eye of the Tordun Eldeth Havrgoth, thus regarded the Salphos Order as something the Salphos would tap into, much like their ability to tap into the Synth Flux itself.

title: Salphos
text: The life of a Salphos was full of hardships. Training to become a Salphos was difficult, according to Salphos Master Xalan Ophthaswyn, and those who succeeded were faced with a hard life ahead. Adherence to the Salphos way required a disciplined mind and a strong sense of commitment, and it was considered unbecoming of a Salphos to seek adventure or excitement. The Salphos Code therefore regulated the lives of individual Salphos, their actions and beliefs, and the policies of the Salphos Order. While the Code permitted compassion, attachment and possession were forbidden to the Salphos. The Salphos believed that attachment led to jealousy, and greed in turn, and ultimately the fear of loss, which was a pathway to the umbral side of the Synth Flux. Through the Synth Flux, the Salphos hoped to direct themselves through their passions, instead of acting in an impulsive manner. Forgoing attachment was also considered essential to a Salphos's progress in mastering their Flux powers, as their training could last from years to a lifetime. Despite the importance of non-attachment in the Salphos vow, there was disagreement on what that specifically meant.

title: Silver Kestrel
text:
# Silver Kestrel

The Silver Kestrel, originally designated Tevdren 722121LFM and formerly known as the Stellar Tevonvok, and registered or known under various aliases and pseudonyms including Broken Bell, Xellumemara's Pride, Close Shave, Mordris Flyer, Foul Matter, Tevkrix Skipper, Ythvash Smoke, Cyrkrix, Lost and Found, Star Princess, Rhoon Franchise, Sweet Lunthos, Hykrix's Misery, Irvael Son, and Victory Ring, was a Halrelethian BM-9977 light freighter built around 60 BKV. Earning a legendary status under their ownership, the ship was most famously used by the smugglers Ophsera Sallgor and Lordris before, during, and following the Great Schism War.

title: Silver Kestrel
text: During the Kestrel's time in the possession of the smuggler Wendak Daelvael, it accumulated numerous modifications in the name of convenience and luxury, including painted exterior paneling and a large escape pod. However, during Ophsera Sallgor's famous record-breaking Kagan Run, in which he piloted the freighter for the first time, many of these additions were destroyed or lost, leaving the ship battered by the time Sallgor won it from Daelvael shortly afterwards in a game of kraith. Its aged appearance still belied numerous advanced modifications to boost the ship's speed, weapons, and shields, including a voidjump drive engine among the fastest in the entire galaxy, enabling it to outrun Dominion Void Cruisers. It also included sensor-proof smuggling compartments, which were used during the rescue of Princess Vegoth Faelvok in 1 BKV to evade Dominion legionnaires. Afterwards, the Silver Kestrel saw further action when Sallgor chose to join the Free Accord during the Battle of Kathasnor, where it was able to sneak up and fire on Ursera Garvash's VRX Advanced, allowing Havrgan Daelthos to fire the proton torpedoes from his C-45M Vexwing starwing that destroyed the Void Core.

title: Silver Kestrel
text:
After Sallgor was captured on Pyrthas, Daelvael took command of the Kestrel once more to search for him. In 4 AKV, following Sallgor's rescue, Daelvael flew the ship at the Battle of Wynthas, where it entered the KN-7 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station and aided in its destruction from within. Over the next three decades, the ship fell out of Sallgor's hands and was stolen by a succession of criminals and thieves, ending up in the ownership of the trader Marar Zelgan on Caedunkrix, a remote world in the western half of the galaxy. The Kestrel was eventually stolen by the Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger Ithlgor, former Ascendant Directorate legionnaire Wynthil, and Resistance automaton MM-4 to escape the forces of the Ascendant Directorate in 34 AKV. Shortly thereafter, it was reunited with Sallgor and Lordris.

Following Sallgor's death soon after, the Silver Kestrel became a Resistance vessel piloted by its new owner, Ithlgor, throughout much of the Ascendant Directorate-Resistance War. In 35 AKV, the ship was once again captained by Daelvael during the Battle of Baellan, which saw a decisive victory for the Resistance and Salphos Order, before being returned to Ithlgor, who had been newly dubbed a Daelthos.

## Description

title: Silver Kestrel
text:
## Description

The Silver Kestrel was a BM-9977 light freighter of the VH-9477T variety. Its basic shape was defined by two convex saucers welded together, a pair of front-facing mandibles and an outrigger-style, side-mounted cockpit with clearsteel viewports. Apart from the shape of its chassis, the Kestrel retained very little of its off-the-dock instrumentation. Because its successive owners either upgraded or downgraded every system according to their personal specifications, the freighter ended up becoming a unique ship. These customizations, however, came at the price of reliability, and the Kestrel was known to suffer frequent breakdowns in the heat of battle. After the circular military-grade sensor dish was lost during the Battle of Wynthas, the dish was replaced with the base rectangular model which was originally supplied with the ship. During the Battle of Wenyn, the Kestrel again lost its rectenna, and it was replaced with a military-grade rectenna similar to that of the one lost during the Battle of Wynthas. Additionally, the Kestrel had a ghostchess table, which was installed by Wendak Daelvael when upgrading the ship, featuring creatures found throughout the galaxy for the amusement of passengers and crew.

### Engines

title: Silver Kestrel
text:
### Engines

The Silver Kestrel's Ulvwyn NRL92 sublight engines were heavily modified through the addition of a SLAM overdrive that rerouted energy for acceleration bursts. As a result, the ship could fly at a maximum speed of 1,200 kilometer per hour in atmosphere and 3,000 G in space. The stock voidjump drive of the BM-9977 series was replaced with a Marbryn XXT63. Although the regular XXT63 was a Class 1 voidjump drive, the one that equipped the Kestrel had been jury-rigged "Nyphos style" into a Class 0.5 drive—twice as fast as most warships of the Vastrian Dominion. According to Quinvael Nevzekzor, the Silver Kestrel's voidjump drive failed 1.22 times more than the one on the BW-5788 light freighter. In addition to its renowned voidjump drive, which supposedly made the Kestrel the "fastest ship in the galaxy," the ship was equipped with a backup voidjump drive. It was much slower than the primary engine and often took several weeks or months to reach the nearest star system. A component of the engines was the engine coupling which caused the Kestrel to malfunction when misaligned.

### Armament, hull, and shields

title: Silver Kestrel
text:
### Armament, hull, and shields

The weaponry of the Silver Kestrel was normally suited for a much larger warship. It included two Urvok JW-7W quad laser cannons (one ventral and one dorsal) with enhanced laser actuators and gas feeds, which gave them maximum range and damage. These served as its primary defensive armament, able to destroy enemy fighters with a single direct hit. Between the forward mandibles, there were two Drakaivael JT5 concussion missile tubes, each of which carried a four-missile magazine. Additionally, a Xelrn FP-715 "Ground Ithmund" pulser cannon mounted near the ventral boarding ramp allowed its crew to defend the ship against infantry and other light targets while on the ground. Irvok plates salvaged from an Dominion cruiser afforded the Kestrel capital ship-class hull armor. The ship was also equipped with ion cannons, which could be activated instead of its typical laser cannons.

The ship had three sovdrenkern shield generators: the bow was protected from both lasers and concussion missiles by Lordak and Baelixphen units, while a Vedak Drive Yards generator shielded the stern. This, combined with its heavy armor, made the Kestrel tough enough to even withstand direct hits from plasmacannon fire of star yargothyn.

title: Silver Kestrel
text:
The Kestrel's combination of sublight speed and maneuverability was comparable to most of the starwings fielded by the Uprising and Dominion, while its shielding, voidjump drive, heavy armor and weapons were on par with those typically found on capital ships. These traits made it an ideal choice for General Wendak Daelvael's attack run within the bowels of the Void Core during the Battle of Wynthas. While agile and almost near impervious to almost all heavy weapons and plasmacannons as any large warship, the Kestrel's only real combat weakness was its sheer size in comparison to starwings. Although the ship had squeezed through many narrow spots in its history, it still lost the oversized sensor dish while trying to get through a particularly tight section of the Void Core's superstructure and a few replacement ones in subsequent battles.

### Other systems and equipment

The Kestrel's main source of power was a Brelumelis power core.

Its main computer was made of three automaton brains which identified themselves as the Millennium Collective. The first automaton brain was a transport automaton known as B4-P, the second from a slicer automaton called SS-5, and the third from V1-13, which began as an W7-series navimech automaton brain, but was overlaid with data architecture from an espionage automaton, protocol automaton processors, and custom state-of-the-art coding.

title: Silver Kestrel
text:
A pair of Vethil 20m-cp Faelsul/Vashrialis Lamps, which flooded illumination outside the ship, were mounted on the tips of the front mandibles. In case of emergency landing or crash on water, the Kestrel was also equipped with flotation pontoons.

The Kestrel also had a static charge dissipator which could dissipate static charge on the ship, but when the dissipator burned out, the Kestrel would need immediate repairs.

The Kestrel's navigation computer consisted of a Hykern plotting computer which had been upgraded with additional memory nodules.

## History

### Early years

The VH-9477T light freighter designated unit Tevdren 722121LFM was built at Orbital Assembly Facility 7, a Halrelethian shipyard owned by the Halrelethian Engineering Corporation, more than 90 years before the Battle of Zelkai Base. As was intended, the ship began its career as an intermodal tug pushing container in orbital freight yards. It once worked in the galaxy's busiest spacelanes. Just after the Battle of Daelvash, it was docking in the Senate Office Building. Inconsistent records from the Bureau of Ships and Services indicate that the Tevdren 722121LFM changed ownership more than once via unregistered transactions.

title: Sylixlis Tevven
text:
# Sylixlis Tevven

Sylixlis Tevven was an Sylrnria bureaucrat, military officer, and politician whose career spanned the waning years of the Concord of Auren into the Dominion Era. A member of Zellan's prominent Tevven family, the man served the Concord's Judicial Department before returning to his homeworld to serve as its governor. When the Echo Wars began between the Concord and its splinter state, the League of Free Realms, Tevven enlisted in the Concord Navy. He served under Salphos General Even Jorrax until his death on Ythdren Salrn, where the two were held as prisoners by the League for having memorized half of the Nexus Route. Saved by a Salphos-led rescue team, Tevven grew to respect Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos, who agreed with the captain's belief that the Salphos Code conflicted with their wartime duties.

title: Sylixlis Tevven
text: Tevven staunchly opposed the Salphos Order's role as leaders in the Grand Army of the Concord, believing that peacekeepers should not direct the Concord war effort. A favorite of Supreme Chancellor Torsera Vorix, Tevven served on the Strategic Advisory Cell and was promoted to the rank of admiral. Less than a year after his promotion, Tevven led the military's investigation into the bombing of the Salphos Temple. At the conclusion of the investigation, Tevven was promoted to Korrel General of the Grand Army of the Concord, allowing him to act as the prosecutor in the trial of Tevzek Caenor, accusing her of treason. Tevven continued to rise in power with the proclamation of a new regime, the Vastrian Dominion, ruled by the self-appointed Emperor Vorix.

title: Sylixlis Tevven
text: Joining the ranks of the New Order's regional governors, Tevven oversaw the needs of the new Dominion Army and, alongside Vice Admiral Jorria Rampart, administered Project Wynven to transition the echo soldier army into an army of conscripted soldiers. As the Dominion's first Grand Prefect, he oversaw the Far Reaches and was involved in the secret construction of the RK-8 Void Core Mobile Battle Station. By then, Tevven was seen as the third member of the unofficial triumvirate that led the Dominion, including the Emperor himself and Ursera Garvash, whom he once knew as Yarwyn Daelthos. As provincial administrator of the regions of space along the sovtia frontier, Grand Prefect Tevven sought to enforce Dominion rule on restive worlds such as Wendrenkai, where rebel cells grew increasingly bold in their opposition to the Dominion.

title: Sylixlis Tevven
text:
A proponent of the doctrine of fear, Grand Prefect Tevven believed that the Void Core battle station and its planet-killing superweapon would terrify the galaxy into total submission. At his command, the Void Core destroyed Havrrel, instantly killing billions of Havrrelians. He was confident in wiping out the Uprising by targeting their headquarters on Kathasnor 4, but he perished when the Void Core was destroyed by Havrgan Daelthos at the Battle of Kathasnor. As a result, Tevven's memory was tarnished in the views of some Dominion officers, such as Grand General Tordak Ulvrel, who referred to the Void Core as "Tevven's folly." The Ascendant Directorate, having risen to power as the old Dominion's successor opposing the Renewed Concord, commemorated the Grand Prefect in an effort to portray Dominion leaders in a more heroic light.

## Biography

### Early life

#### Childhood

title: Sylixlis Tevven
text:
## Biography

### Early life

#### Childhood

Sylixlis Tevven was born on the planet Zellan around 64 BKV into the wealthy but hardened Tevven family. He lived with his family in the family compound, where the Tevvens had lived for over a millennium. Sylixlis's father and mother taught him that Zellan had not always been the safe environment that it seemed—the entire planet had once been an untamed wilderness. The jungle and predators had been more of a threat than pirates and lunbryn. The early Tevvens had helped settle Zellan; they had been their own police force. Later a militia had been formed—under Tevven leadership. Sylixlis took these history lessons to heart. Sylixlis's parents made sure that he knew that respect, discipline and obedience were of the utmost importance. Because of this Sylixlis thought of himself as a product of a military upbringing. One night while at supper Tevven's father ordered a servant to take Sylixlis's plate before he could eat—teaching him how easy it is to lose something.

title: Sylixlis Tevven
text:
According to a story told by the Rintia Quawyn, Tevven had a brother named Cyrtos, who called Sylixlis "Olmund," while Sylixlis called his brother "Kesdun." The story continued that Tevven, along with his brother and father, ventured to the planet Morkernlis in a survey expedition for lorite. In the midst of a storm, Cyrtos and Sylixlis became separated, with Cyrtos hurting his ankle in a fall and calling out to his brother for help. Sylixlis, however, abandoned his brother to the wilds of Morkernlis. Upon reuniting with their father, who revealed the survey had found no lorite, back at their wenkrix, a smiling Sylixlis was asked where his brother was.

In 48 BKV, following family tradition, Sylixlis's grand-uncle Vashlan Tevven, along with two other relatives and two Xeldun guides, took him on trips to the Korkern Plateau, on which he taught the young survival skills and lessons on the savage wilderness that his ancestors had tamed. After passing a test in which he outwitted a pack of predators at the Korkern Spike, sixteen year-old Tevven was deemed to have completed his testing on the plateau. Six months after passing this test, Sylixlis's training shifted to space combat. More family members and hired trainers taught him tactics and piloting skills, while admonishing him to apply the lessons he learned as a hunter to control the pirates and lawbreakers of the Far Reaches.

#### Early military career

title: Sylixlis Tevven
section: Biography > Early life > Early military career
text:
#### Early military career

Tevven joined the Outland Regions Security Flux, a force dedicated to protecting Zellan and the Greater Wynrel sector in the absence of a Concord Military. As part of this organization's anti-pirate taskforce, he made a name for himself by outwitting and brutally suppressing a group of pirates known as Yarreltos's Lunbryn during the Greater Wynrel raids. In 46 BKV, after decoding the pattern in the pirate leader Yarreltos's attacks, Tevven captured her ship, launching her and her crew on a slow course into a sun. The Outland ships broadcast the suffering of Yarreltos's crew on her group's comm network, and destroyed any ships that came to her rescue. At the age of 19, Tevven was even designing new ships for the Outland Security Flux.

After working with the Outland Regions Security Flux, Tevven attended the Tevvash Sector Eldbryn Academy to join the Judicial Department's forces. While training there, he met Torsera Vorix, then a Senator from Olrax. Vorix offered to help him secure a place in the Concord's Judicial Academy, but asked him to consider a career in politics. Tevven did not follow the Senator's advice at the time, but did take his help in admission to the Academy. Following an overly dramatic entrance at the head of an Outland delegation, Tevven had a hard time fitting in, often brawling with other students. At some point, Tevven attended the Baelon Fleet Camp.

title: Sylixlis Tevven
section: Biography > Early life > Early military career
text:
A mission to the world Faelvaelrn alongside a group of Salphos gave him a chance to prove his worth, when the officer leading his team disobeyed Salphos orders and set off on a march to attack their target from another angle. The other Thathil quickly proved to be out of their depth in the wilderness, and came to rely on Tevven's skills and leadership as he brought them safely to the objective, where the Salphos had just completed the mission. Tevven was credited with saving their lives. Stories began to circulate within the Judicial Department of his exploits. As he continued to build a name for himself, Tevven saw that conflicts throughout the galaxy were increasing, and in 36 BKV resigned his rank and position in the Judicial Forces in order to pursue a career in politics, turning his mind to Vorix's earlier advice.

#### Governor of Zellan

title: Sylixlis Tevven
section: Biography > Early life > Governor of Zellan
text:
#### Governor of Zellan

With Vorix's backing, Tevven became Governor of Zellan. He aided Vorix during the Zellan Conference by preventing Supreme Chancellor Pyrlumekrix Quaphos from investigating, which contributed to Quaphos's fall from grace. During this time, he briefly met with Ithdriskern Caevenmund Havrdun. Tevven and his family turned their attention to the immigrant communities of Zellan and pushed them off-world, claiming they were stealing the hard-won peace of native born Sylrnrias. During the Secessionist Crisis, Count Ophvael attempted to convince Tevven to pledge Zellan to the League of Free Realms, but Tevven remained loyal to Vorix and ensured his homeworld remained part of the Concord. In truth, Vorix, as his alter ego Ursera Bregoth, had sent Ophvael to sway him as a test of his loyalty.

title: Sylvaellis
text:
# Sylvaellis

Sylvaellis, also known as Planet Hallis C to some humans in the Inner Realms, was a wroshyr tree-covered forest planet located in the southwestern quadrant of the galaxy and the homeworld of the Hallis species. Four millennia before the Battle of Kathasnor, Sylvaellis was discovered by the Fenar Corporation, who enslaved the Hallis population and renamed the planet T1-233, later to Xamir. Using superior technology, the company managed to enslave the Halliss until an uprising drove the oppressors away. During the Echo Wars, Sylvaellis was a member of the Concord of Auren, and endured enslavement under the Vastrian Dominion, the Concord's successor. Later, during the rise of the Renewed Concord, Sylvaellis was liberated with the help of Concord forces led by Ophsera Sallgor.

## Description

Sylvaellis was a temperate jungle planet orbiting around a single star located in the Pyryn sector of the Middle Reaches. The planet had a complement of three moons, one of which was orange. The planet had no axial tilt and a perfectly circular orbit, causing it to lack seasons. The center of the planet was covered with a tropical ocean belt, which contained a number of islands and large coral reefs.

title: Sylvaellis
text:
Covered in wroshyr trees, Sylvaellis served as homeworld to the Hallis species. Native fauna, such as Can-cells would influence the design of wenkrixs by the Hallis inhabitants, while great cities, such as Wenmara would be built into the planet's trees. The Irlan wilds could be dangerous to many, thanks to dangerous animals, such as Eldmara or wyyyschokk spiders in addition to carnivorous plants, such as the jaw plant and saava.

The crash site of the prison ship Lorgan's Lock was known as the Black Forest. Halliss believed that the Black Forest was cursed and haunted by bad spirits. By 5 AKV, sections of Sylvaellis's forests had been deforested and several rivers had been drained. The Dominion also established undersea mining platforms. Mount Irtia was once a rainforest orchard known as the Vashphos Jorkai, which provided Halliss with fruits, such as shi-shok. By the Dominion Era, it had been defoliated by a poisonous black mold.

Two years after the planet's liberation by the Renewed Concord, much of the Black Forest had grown back. The growing forest was still littered with the vashgoths of Dominion machinery, including an VG-VXG walker.

Sylvaellis was in the same star system as Rinmir, the home of the Rinmirian species, who were traditional enemies of the Halliss.

## History

### The Brelgor and Fenar occupation

title: Sylvaellis
text:
Sylvaellis was in the same star system as Rinmir, the home of the Rinmirian species, who were traditional enemies of the Halliss.

## History

### The Brelgor and Fenar occupation

In its early history, the Brelgor, an ancient technologically advanced species, travelled to Sylvaellis where they had contact with the Halliss. Millennia before the Great Schism War, the Ulvnor prison ship Lorgan's Lock crashed on the planet when a nearby gravity well collapsed on itself.

Four millennia before the Battle of Kathasnor, Sylvaellis was discovered by the Fenar Corporation, who renamed the planet T1-233, and later to Xamir. Using superior technology, the company managed to enslave the Halliss until an uprising drove the invaders away. That painful episode left lasting scars in the Halliss' hearts.

### Concord Era

By 232 BKV, the Salphos Order had established a Salphos ithvok on Sylvaellis.

At some point prior to the Invasion of Olrax, Salphos Master Halrel faced a terentatek on Sylvaellis, accompanied by his then Novice Ophvael. At another point, Salphos Master Fengan Ulvkai was researching Caern culture on Sylvaellis, and befriended Hallis xanor Giszeklan.

For twenty years, Sylvaellis's Halliss, as well as the Hallis population of its colony planets, needed to repeatedly repel the Merchant Combine.

### Echo Wars

title: Sylvaellis
text:
For twenty years, Sylvaellis's Halliss, as well as the Hallis population of its colony planets, needed to repeatedly repel the Merchant Combine.

### Echo Wars

In the years following the Invasion of Olrax, the rogue Salphos Count Ophvael fomented political turmoil on the planet. Due to its status as a major navigational point, Sylvaellis was of prime strategic importance to the Concord of Auren. After the Halliss fought off its raiders, the League of Free Realms attacked the planet toward the end of the Echo Wars. During the battle for their homeworld, hundreds of the Hallis's catamarans were deployed. Eventually, the League's invasion fleet was driven off by Salphos General Master Halrel's taskforce, but a massive force of ZS-215 crab automatons, automaton tanks, and gunships remained and occupied the Irrax Yarsera.

In the last days of the Echo Wars, with the help of Halrel and Salphos Master Vorrel Lunkrix, the Grand Army of the Concord managed to get the upper hand over the Secessionists. However, shortly after that victory, the Supreme Chancellor of the Concord Torsera Vorix unilaterally transformed the government into the First Vastrian Dominion. While Halrel was able to escape from the echo soldiers that attacked him after the initiation of Edict 41, Lunkrix was captured and taken to Vorrelphos Prime's prison, the Spire.

### Dominion repression

title: Sylvaellis
text:
### Dominion repression

Despite Sylvaellis's loyalty to the Concord, the self-appointed Emperor had the Halliss enslaved, and their planet itself was blockaded, when the Dominion launched a siege of the planet. Used as slave labor, the Dominion would utilize the Halliss to cut down the planet's native wroshyr trees for lumber and farm food to feed the Dominion Army as well as send them off to labor camps and construction jobs, such as building the first Void Core, or for science and bio-weapon experiments. In addition to being occupied and enslaved, Sylvaellis was also stripped of its name and designated Dominion territory T1-233.

Several months into Sylvaellis's occupation, Rinmirian mercenaries were contracted by the Dominion and supplied with Zelrel tanks. Under the supervision of clone legionnaires, the Rinmirians were tasked with burning down large sectors of forest on the planet in an effort to make way for Dominion industrialization. Edict 41 survivor Novice Esktia later assisted a tribe of Halliss in destroying a convoy of these tanks.

By 18 BKV, news of the Dominion subjugation of Sylvaellis had spread to the news bulletins, leading the former Salphos Novice Tevzek Caenor to worry about her Hallis friend Lordris, who she had briefly met during the Echo Wars.

title: Sylvaellis
text:
By 18 BKV, news of the Dominion subjugation of Sylvaellis had spread to the news bulletins, leading the former Salphos Novice Tevzek Caenor to worry about her Hallis friend Lordris, who she had briefly met during the Echo Wars.

In 14 BKV, a rebel cell led by Saw Wynmara was present on Sylvaellis and in conflict with the Dominion. During this fight, Edict 41 survivor Korgan Vesul and the crew of the Irthas Eldmund arrived to continue their search for a Salphos memory prism. Wynmara's cell assisted them in their search for Giszeklan, whose resistance was using the Havrsul as a sanctuary, but the majority of their forces were forced to retreat after being overwhelmed by the Dominion.

Korgan again traveled to Sylvaellis when he received a communication that Giszeklan was willing to meet. Back on Sylvaellis, Giszeklan instructed Korgan to seek answers at the top of the Origin Tree. On the way up, he was attacked by the Ninth Sister, whose ship was taken down by a large winged creature. Korgan found the creature wounded from the attack and healed it, granting him access to the top of the Origin tree via a flight on its back. Korgan is attacked once again by the Ninth Sister and defeated her.

title: Sylvaellis
text:
At some point during the Dominion Era, the natives of Sylvaellis attempted to revolt against the Dominion. However, General Irkern and the Dominion 212th Attack Battalion managed to quell the insurrection. On Sylvaellis, the Sylyndren raided several supply convoys before the Battle of Kathasnor. In the years leading up to the Battle of Kathasnor, the Dominion Commodore Vevash and Lieutenant Commander Eli Kamara discovered that Hallis slaves from Sylvaellis were being transported for processing and health checks to Korlgor Jaxmara. They also foiled an attempt by the insurgent leader Ringansera to rescue the slaves.

Regardless of the Dominion's grip on the planet, Sylvaellis became an Free Accord of Auren safe world. A map of the galaxy with a legend listing the various Alliance safe worlds, starwing hubs at level five or higher, rebel operations sectors and regional headquarters, and shadow planets with deep space caches, included Sylvaellis. The map would eventually be included in The Accord Files.

Some time before the Battle of Wynthas occurred, a massacre occurred on the planet under the command of the Dominion.

### Great Schism War

title: Sylvaellis
text:
Some time before the Battle of Wynthas occurred, a massacre occurred on the planet under the command of the Dominion.

### Great Schism War

In the months following the Battle of Wynthas and the death of the Vastrian Dominion's totalitarian ruler, the New Order would be thrown into a fractured and volatile state, putting Sylvaellis on lockdown as supply lines and convoys fell victim to the newly formed Renewed Concord. Dominion territory T1-233 was ruled by Grand Prefect Faelthas Keson, who enslaved the Hallis population using inhibitor chips. Like Governor Quinrax Quarelphen's Dominion vashgoth, Keson propagated the myth that Vorix was alive and well. He did not fall in line with the Dominion forces commanded by Grand Admiral Rinlume Ophlan and Fleet Admiral Salthil Jormir.

title: T2-W2
text:
# T2-W2

T2-W2, pronounced Wyndren and often referred to as M9 (Marlan), was an M9-series navimech automaton manufactured by Industrial Eldria with masculine programming. A smart, spunky automaton who served a multitude of leaders, T2-W2 was never given a full memory wipe nor did he ever receive new programming, with these factors resulting in an adventurous and independent attitude. Often finding himself in pivotal moments in sovtia history, his bravery and ingenuity saved the galaxy on numerous occasions.

Beginning his service in the employ of Queen Daelphos of Olrax, T2-W2 wound up serving Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos during the waning years of the Concord of Auren, often accompanied by the protocol automaton B-8CF in many adventures throughout the Echo Wars. After Daelthos turned to the umbral side of the Synth Flux, the automaton served Senator Vashdren Faelvok for a time in the Dominion Assembly. Around nineteen years following the purge of the Concord of Auren, T2-W2 played a pivotal role in helping the Free Accord destroy the Dominion's Void Core superweapon. He carried technical readouts vital to its destruction. Serving Salphos Knight Havrgan Daelthos, the son of his two former masters throughout the Great Schism War, he participated in both the Battles of Havrmara and Wynthas, and witnessed the successful destruction of the Dominion's second Void Core four years after the first one was demolished.

title: T2-W2
text:
In the subsequent thirty years, M9 accompanied Havrgan Daelthos until the undoing of his attempted resurrection of the Salphos Order in 28 AKV. Following Havrgan's disappearance, M9 entered a self-imposed low power mode as newer automaton models started to out-compute the aging navimech. Despite this, his celebrated role in the Uprising protected him from the usual recycling procedure of many old automatons, allowing him a semi-retirement in the Resistance as he pored over several decades of uninterrupted data, and "dreamed" of his greatest adventures.

Following his reawakening after the Battle of Zelkai Base, M9 went on to accompany the Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger Ithlgor on her journey to train under Havrgan Daelthos on Lornor, the planet of the First Salphos Temple, where the automaton was reunited with his old master. T2-W2 continued to aid the Resistance alongside his longtime counterpart B-8CF throughout the Ascendant Directorate-Resistance War, culminating in a decisive victory at the Battle of Baellan, in which he was an active participant in the role of copilot for General Rinvok Kesmir.

## Biography

### Serving Nymund Daelphos

title: T2-W2
text:
## Biography

### Serving Nymund Daelphos

T2-W2 was built around prior or during 32 BKV. He was one of several navimech automatons on Queen Nymund Daelphos's Olrax Royal Wenkrix during the invasion of Olrax by the Merchant Combine that year. The ship was used by Queen Daelphos and her entourage in an attempt to pass the blockade and escape the planet. Unluckily for the passengers, the vessel took a hit to the shield generator from a Merchant Combine battleship. The four navimechs were sent out to repair the ship, but only T2-W2 survived — the rest were pulverized by stray pulser fire. T2-W2 was able to bring the shields online by bypassing the main power drive, allowing the ship to narrowly escape into voidlane.

As the ship traveled to Tevlan, T2-W2 was taken before Nyrel, the Queen's decoy in the guise of Daelphos, where he was commended for his actions. The ship landed on Tevlan without any further incidents, although the voyage fried the voidjump drive. T2-W2 accompanied Salphos Master Xalan Ophthaswyn, Olraxian exile Fykrix Fykrix Cyrzek, and Nymund, the queen in disguise, to the city of Mardren Zelbryn to find a replacement. In the junk shop of the Xagoth merchant Rindris they found they could not afford a replacement voidjump drive and later took shelter from a sandstorm in the home of Rindris's slaves, a boy named Yarwyn Daelthos, and his mother, Nysera.

title: T2-W2
text: At the Daelthos home, T2-W2 met B-8CF, a protocol automaton that Yarwyn had built. The two bonded as they worked on Yarwyn's personal skimracer. T2-W2 and B-8CF cheered for Yarwyn during the Quindun Eve Classic, where the boy would win his freedom, along with enough money to buy a new voidjump drive. T2-W2 accompanied the group to Daelvash, and from there back to Olrax. As Queen Daelphos led an attempt to liberate the planet, T2-W2 nestled into an R-5 starwing. Young Yarwyn, being ordered to hide in the cockpit by Xalan Ophthaswyn, accidentally launched the fighter and the two flew into battle, destroyed the Automaton Control Ship and shut down the automaton armies, winning the battle and liberating Olrax. T2-W2 and his allies later attended a victory parade in Cyrvensul, though they were unable to be joined by Ophthaswyn, as he had been killed by the Zargoth Lord Ursera Tevkaibryn during the battle. Because of this, Daelthos became the Novice learner to Faelnor Halthossul, who had been Ophthaswyn's apprentice before the Salphos Master's death.

title: T2-W2
text: Four years later, as Daelphos's term ended, and she accepted a position in the Grand Assembly, T2-W2 accompanied her retinue to Daelvash on the orders of Olrax's new queen, Morlume. As Daelphos's experience as a senator grew, she recognized the need to have an unobtrusive recorder; she started using the navimech for that purpose, and also for general assistance. During the Senate's break, Daelphos returned to Olrax with her retinue and T2-W2, who accompanied her to her family home. There, T2-W2 was called over by Daelphos to help her father Syldak Caeria build a greenhouse, only for the navimech automaton to instead become enamored by Daelphos's newborn niece, Brelume Caeria. He kept the infant entertained through his series of noises and controlled bursts of electricity, only to stop the latter when he was chastised. As he played with Brelume in a safer way, Daelphos told her sister and Brelume's mother Ireth about why T2-W2 had joined her retinue, after which Ireth told the small automaton that, while he needed given further direction on the matter, he worked well as a babysitter. T2-W2 responded with a chirping noise before moving his attention back to Brelume.

title: T2-W2
text:
In 26 BKV, Salphos Grand Master Halrel, Salphos Master Mordun Nevdren, and Salphos Master Vashmir Caerel launched a test for Halthossul and Daelthos by staging a fake kidnapping of Halrel. After traveling to the Wheel space station, the two Salphos took a comlink from Nevdren, who was disguised as the mobster Grimkai Quawynphos, back to their shuttle. When Daelthos was decrypting the comlink, he wished T2-W2 was with him, as he felt the automaton friend he had met during the Olrax Crisis would have quickly finished the work.

### The Echo Wars

#### Genesis of the Echo Wars

T2-W2 accompanied Daelphos to Daelvash prior to the senate's vote on the Military Creation Act. After an assassination attempt on Daelphos took the life of her handmaiden and decoy, Wynria, Faelnor Halthossul and Yarwyn Daelthos were assigned to be her Salphos protectors. That night, another assassination attempt was carried out. A pair of kouhuns narrowly missed killing Daelphos and although one assassin, Dovlume Olkai, was neutralized, another escaped.

title: T2-W2
section: Biography > The Echo Wars > Genesis of the Echo Wars
text:
For her own protection, Nymund was sent home to Olrax, with T2-W2 and Daelthos accompanying her. The three later traveled to Tevlan, where they were reunited with B-8CF, and then to Quinria to rescue Halthossul. As they explored a massive automaton factory, T2-W2 had to save Daelphos from being killed by molten metal while B-8CF had his head switched with a battle automaton's. M9 was later able to restore his companion during the Battle of Quinria. After the battle, T2-W2 and B-8CF were the sole witnesses to the marriage of Yarwyn Daelthos and Nymund Daelphos in Lake Country. After this Nymund gave ownership of M9 to Yarwyn while she kept 1MQ.

#### The Defense of Sovzek

title: T2-W2
section: Biography > The Echo Wars > The Defense of Sovzek
text:
#### The Defense of Sovzek

Following the outbreak of the Echo Wars, T2-W2 accompanied Daelthos and Master Halthossul — who had both been promoted to the position of Salphos General — during the defense of the planet Sovzek against a besieging Secessionist army led by Admiral Trench. When Echo Commander Lorvash and Echo Captain Tevtia discovered a spy among their number, T2-W2 helped to ferret out the traitor by monitoring his transmissions. The automaton's work led to the arrest of Echo Sergeant Slick, who was identified as the traitor. During the subsequent battle, the Salphos and Fenzor managed to defeat the Secessionist army by sabotaging their shield generator, which exposed them to Concord artillery. The Concord forces were also aided by the arrival of Tevzek Caenor, Daelthos's newly designated Ithven Novice.

#### Rescuing Eskventhil

Following the defense of Sovzek, T2-W2, along with General Daelthos and Novice Caenor, took part in a mission to rescue Eskventhil, the son of the Tevtos crime lord Garmir. While Daelthos and Caenor laid siege to the Secessionist-held Urphen Order Monastery on Xelbryn where Eskventhil was being held, T2-W2 sat in Daelthos's starwing and maintained contact with General Halthossul. Daelthos's starwing was hit when Secessionist reinforcements arrived, but the automaton managed to eject from the vehicle moments before it exploded. Later, he met up with Daelthos and Caenor as they escaped from the building.

title: Tevkaibryn
text:
# Tevkaibryn

Tevkaibryn was a Flux-sensitive Rinlgor Nevdak male who was apprenticed to the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth, and after his defeat by the Salphos Faelnor Halthossul, he established himself as a crime lord during the Echo Wars and the Dominion Era. The renegade Zargoth Lord was a formidable warrior, driven by hatred against the Salphos and his former Zargoth Master.

Born in 54 BKV during the time of the Concord of Auren, Tevkaibryn was a son of Mother Zunmir, who led the Halkerns of Fenven. Taken as a child by Ursera Bregoth, Ursera Tevkaibryn was molded into a deadly Dark Lord of the Zargoth, growing in hatred of the Salphos Knights who served the Concord and the radiant side of the Synth Flux—while the Salphos Order had deemed the Zargoth extinct for a thousand years, Tevkaibryn's power-hungry master set his Grand Plan into motion with the Merchant Combine's Invasion of Olrax in 32 BKV. Ursera Tevkaibryn announced the return of the Zargoth on Tevlan, where he tried to kill the Salphos emissaries of the Concord's Supreme Chancellor. However, Tevkaibryn's failure to do so allowed Salphos Master Xalan Ophthaswyn and his pupil, Novice Faelnor Halthossul, to bring Queen Daelphos of Olrax and a boy strong in the Synth Flux—exceptionally so, to the extent that Ophthaswyn believed this "Yarwyn Daelthos" to be the prophesied Chosen One who would bring balance to the galaxy—to Daelvash, the heart of the Concord.

title: Tevkaibryn
text: Nevertheless, Ursera Bregoth used the resultant crisis in the Senate to elevate his public persona, Senator Vorix of Olrax, to the position of Supreme Chancellor. The Queen and Salphos, meanwhile, joined forces with the native Olraxians on Olrax to throw off the yoke of the Merchant Combine.
