Ursera Tevkaibryn, having been dispatched by his master to oversee the Combine leadership, was redirected to handle the Salphos. Tevkaibryn dealt a fatal blow to Xalan Ophthaswyn, but Halthossul in turn defeated Tevkaibryn by bisecting him at the waist, with the Dark Lord falling to the abyss and presumed dead. He was actually alive, sustained by his rage in the wastelands of Zarmir Minor. Around the same time, Bregoth took on Ophthaswyn's Salphos Master, Ophvael, as his new apprentice. A decade afterward, Ophvael set the second part of the Zargoth plan into motion with the start of the Echo Wars.

title: Tevkaibryn
text: As the galaxy plunged into war, Mother Zunmir plotted against Ophvael and had one of her sons, Savage Zelmara, seek out Tevkaibryn. Indeed, the defeated Nevdak was brought back to Fenven and had his sanity and mobility restored by Zunmir's magick. Tevkaibryn trained his newfound brother in the ways of the Zargoth, initially wanting to take revenge against Faelnor Halthossul. After the brothers were defeated by the Salphos, they took their chance to increase their powers with a brazen takeover of Lunsera, the erstwhile neutral world torn between the interests of the Concord and the Secessionists. Tevkaibryn seized control of the self-styled Death Watch and used them terrorise Lunsera while he expanded his criminal enterprise, known as the Shadow Collective—the Saltiaar Syndicate, Black Sun, and the Tevtos Clan were coerced to join forces under the ythkern's new crime lord—until he caught the attention of Bregoth, who killed Tevkaibryn's brother and captured Tevkaibryn.

title: Tevkaibryn
text:
Tevkaibryn was rescued by his Lunseran cyrvoks and immediately tried to reconsolidate his Shadow Collective. However, he and his mother's desire for revenge against Ursera Bregoth was checked by the Dark Lord, who instead decimated their homeworld of Fenven with the use of the Secessionists led by Ophvael and General Caephen. Mother Zunmir herself was killed while protecting Tevkaibryn, and his wynvash were weakened. While he regathered with his cyrvoks on Lunsera, Tevkaibryn sensed that his former master's Grand Plan was coming to its climax and wished to lure Yarwyn Daelthos—the Salphos Knight trained by Faelnor Halthossul whom he correctly believed was central to Bregoth' schemes—alongside Halthossul himself to Lunsera. Tevkaibryn's thirst for revenge was foiled again when Concord forces intervening on the side of the Lunsera resistance were instead led by Daelthos's old apprentice, Tevzek Caenor.

While Tevkaibryn and Caenor fought at the Siege of Lunsera, Bregoth successfully executed his plan to destroy the Salphos Order and anoint himself Sovtia Emperor. With the support of some Lunseran and Nevdak cyrvoks, Tevkaibryn continued trying to control the ythkern but operated more clandestinely, away from the prying apparatus of the new Dominion regime. He was known in criminal circles as the Shadow Lord and was pursued by the Emperor's Baelmund, who simply called him the Shadow. In the Dominion's later years, Tevkaibryn secretly coordinated the Five Crime Wynvash and controlled the Crimson Dawn syndicate through Dratiawyn Zelyn and Oldren.

title: Tevkaibryn
text:
Tevkaibryn also sought a great weapon on Nevyn purported to be able of destroying all life and thus crossed paths with the Salphos Nevrax Brekern and Vezek Cyrnor as well as Tevzek Caenor. However, they were all stopped by Ursera Garvash, the fallen Daelthos. Tevkaibryn escaped and continued to tempt Cyrnor towards the umbral side in service of his own ends. Cyrnor rejected Tevkaibryn's overtures, but not before the former Zargoth Lord used their connection to track his old nemesis Halthossul back to Tevlan. Their last duel ended with one fatal blow to Tevkaibryn. Learning that Halthossul had consigned himself to a life of exile to protect the prophesied Chosen One who would destroy the Zargoth, Tevkaibryn died with the belief that he would ultimately be avenged.

## Biography

### Early life

In 54 BKV, the boy who would be dubbed Ursera Tevkaibryn was born the son of Mother Zunmir on Fenven with mysterious origins. As a Rinlgor Nevdak male, he was a Sovlgor and had two blood brothers, Torthil and Savage Zelmara. Later in his life, Tevkaibryn claimed that he once had a real name but that he had long since forgotten it. Before his first birthday, Zunmir gave the Nevdak infants their first tattoos, although Tevkaibryn, in his unreliable memories, personally remembered living much of his early life without his tatoos. As a child, since his days living in deep caves, Tevkaibryn wrestled with a deep inner anger.

title: Tevkaibryn
text:
As immortalized in legend, Tevkaibryn grew up with one of his brothers in a house in the Sovlgor Village, often needing to take care of his younger, weaker brother due to Zunmir always being away with the Halkerns. Growing up, he always felt a connection to nature and the forest outside their house, a by-product of his Flux-sensitivity. While he was still a child, Mother Zunmir became an ally of Ursera Bregoth, the Dark Lord of the Zargoth, the two beings exchanging knowledge of Umbral Side arcana and Halkern magicks. When Bregoth visited Zunmir, Tevkaibryn always hid in his room, afraid of the man and worried about Zunmir's increasing bond with him.

### Taken by Ursera Bregoth

Tevkaibryn's struggle with anger eventually caught the attention of Bregoth. Around 40 BKV, Bregoth would take Tevkaibryn away from Fenven to become his Zargoth apprentice. According to Zunmir, Bregoth betrayed her and stole Tevkaibryn away. According to Tevkaibryn's unreliable memories, as Bregoth prepared to take the young Tevkaibryn away with him, Zelmara attempted to intervene and convince him not to go with the "monster," although Tevkaibryn believed he had no choice and departed, much to Zelmara' upset as Zelmara accused Bregoth as having done something to Tevkaibryn.

title: Tevkaibryn
text: Alternatively, according to a legend, Bregoth ordered Zunmir to give up Tevkaibryn to a keeper, threatening to not follow through on his promise to make her his apprentice. She reluctantly agreed, and Tevkaibryn ran into the forest angrily, overhearing the conversation from behind his door. When he returned the next morning, a Sovlgor took him and threw him into a pit, not allowing him to say goodbye to his own mother. Over the course of months, Tevkaibryn was put through relentless domestic abuse, all orchestrated by Bregoth as a test. He lived with his Sovlgor keeper's two sons, who beat him to the point of being unable to stand up every few days and kept starved by only being given the scraps his "brothers" didn't eat. This eventually started to warp Tevkaibryn's perceptions and his love for his mother eventually turned into resentment and hatred for abandoning him.

title: Tevlan
text:
# Tevlan

Tevlan was a sparsely inhabited circumbinary desert planet located in the galaxy's Far Reaches. Part of a binary star system, the planet orbited two scorching suns, resulting in the world lacking the necessary surface water to sustain large populations. As a result, many residents of the planet instead drew water from the atmosphere via moisture farms. The planet also had little surface vegetation. It was the homeworld to the native Fenul and Ophlgor Quaul species and of Yarwyn and Havrgan Daelthos, who would go on to shape sovtia history.

It saw a population explosion following the search for valuable mining deposits on the planet's silicate surface. Finding the ore to have undesirable metallurgical properties, mining firms left the planet en masse, leaving behind valuable equipment, most notably large dunecrawlers, which were later used by the Fenul population. The planet then became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, and fell under the influence of the Tevtos Clan while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants endured.

title: Tevlan
text:
Generally ignored by the galaxy at large, Tevlan gained the notice of the Vastrian Dominion during the Great Schism War when an escape pod carrying two automatons in possession of top-secret information landed on the sandy Far Reaches world. The Dominion went on to establish a heavier presence on the planet, forging a tenuous relationship with Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil of the Tevtos Clan. Open conflict soon broke out between the Dominion and a Free Accord cell on Tevlan that culminated in a battle that left the Dominion's hold on the world significantly weakened.

Following the death of Garmir and the withdrawal of Dominion forces after the Battle of Wynthas, an enormous power vacuum occurred on the world, with numerous crime wynvash like the Red Key Raiders attempting to build legitimacy as mining companies. Eventually, former bounty hunter Grimrel Zeldakrel returned and took over Garmir's former territory. Coming into conflict with both the Tevtos Clan and the Saltiaar Syndicate, the new Nylis was pulled into a gang war that threatened the future of Tevlan. With help from the Lunseran Esketh Vashon, Zeldakrel rallied the denizens of the settlements Mardren Zelbryn and Vorvael to push back against the invaders, ushering in a new era of respect between the people of the planet.

## Description

title: Tevlan
text:
## Description

Tevlan was a hot desert planet located in the Far Reaches, a region of the galaxy far removed from its core. It had three moons, Olbryn, Faelphen, and Quinlgor. Tevlan orbited twin suns, Kawyn I and Kawyn II. According to Fenul folklore, the desert known as the Pyreth Sea was once a true ocean. The whole planet was covered in harsh deserts, and only a small part of its northern hemisphere could sustain intelligent life. The landscape was covered with sand dunes, mountains, and canyons, which made traversing the planet very difficult. Due to the absence of surface water, those who lived on Tevlan had to draw moisture through the dry air.

Rain was incredibly rare on Tevlan, coming once a year, decade, or century. When the rain came, some plants were able to grow in a brief yet glorious period. Inhabiting the planet were many native species, the largest of which were the carnivorous drakon dragons. The common drakon dragon, while more plentiful, was shadowed by the greater drakon dragon, which submerged itself under the shifting sands and used its powerful limbs to traverse through the dunes. In addition, the common tuskbeast and dunebeast species also found a home on the world, along with sandstriders, rontos, dunerat rats, massiffs, and scurriers.

title: Tevlan
text:
The cities of Tevlan were frequently blasted by sandstorms and the inhabitants always seemed to know when one was coming. Not much distinguished the towns as the poor standard of living was common. The cities were separated from each other by large expanses of deserts. Rural life, on the other hand, was mostly small moisture farms that sold water and food for a meager living.

## History

### Early history

Tevlan was the homeworld of the Fenul and Ophlgor Quaul species. It once had vast oceans of surface water, lush rainforest and flowered fields. According to the Legend of Rinvash, Tevlan had also been inhabited by a group called the Sylrn during this time, but there was little evidence to support the story. Sometime in Tevlan's history, the whole planet became a desert by unknown means when the oceans dried away. Much later, it would be colonized by early settlers and explorers, who mistook the planet for a third sun owing to its highly reflective silicate surface.

title: Tevlan
text:
As a result of sporadic and unsuccessful colonization ventures, the planet became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants attempted to earn a living in the gardris. A long-ago mining boom saw the widespread use of dunecrawlers on the desert plains in an effort to mine valuable minerals. However, after it was discovered that most valuable minerals could be found on the surface, along with most minerals having unwanted metallurgic properties, the dunecrawlers were abandoned and eventually picked up by the native Fenuls for use as shelter and mobile bases, from which they collected scrap from thousands of years of crashed spacecraft and failed mining projects.

Offworlders erected various cities in the desert, and colonists who decided to stay on the planet built moisture farms. The Urphen Order on Tevlan kept their disembodied brains floating in jars that hung below their spider-like automaton bodies, and built a monastery on the planet which would eventually come under the ownership of Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil as his palace.

title: Tevlan
text:
Most wealth eventually found its way into the city of Mardren Zelbryn, with most of it procured from gambling and off-world trade, especially through the lucrative black market. The influx of commercial ventures fueled Mardren Zelbryn's growth, eventually securing its regional importance as a hub of economic and financial activity. With high tariffs imposed by the Tevtoss, some believed themselves able to escape paying them by doing business in the planet's de facto capital, however often found themselves scammed and broke if not through gambling, through simple bad luck.

### Scum and villainy

In the last decades of the Concord of Auren, Tevlan was known as a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, including slavery. The sand people regularly attacked Fort Ophlgor, earning them their name of "Ophlgor Raiders." It was home to a human slave named Nysera Daelthos and her son Yarwyn.

title: Tevlan
text: During this period, Queen Nymund Daelphos of Olrax escaped the capture of her homeworld by the Merchant Combine, and she took refuge on Tevlan with her companions and protectors, including the Salphos Master Xalan Ophthaswyn and his apprentice Faelnor Halthossul. The Daelthoss befriended Daelphos's party, and the young slave ended up participating in a skimrace to help his new friends obtain a new S-39 voidjump drive generator for their damaged wenkrix. After discovering that Yarwyn Daelthos would make an exceptional recruit for the Salphos Order, Master Xalan Ophthaswyn managed to obtain his freedom from the junk dealer Rindris in the city of Mardren Zelbryn, and the Queen's party left Tevlan with the boy. After participating in numerous adventures, including the Invasion of Olrax, the former Sovvael slave joined the Salphos Order under Halthossul's tutelage.

title: Tevlan
text:
Ten years later, Daelthos, now a gifted but unruly Salphos student, sensed that his mother, who had stayed on Tevlan and gotten married, was in terrible pain. Daelthos returned to the desert world in the company of Daelphos, who was now a senator of the Concord and the young Salphos's secret lover. It transpired that Nysera Daelthos had been captured by Ophlgor Raiders and was detained in one of their camps. When Daelthos finally discovered his mother's location, he arrived too late, and she died in his arms from the consequences of the Ophlgors' mistreatment of her. Enraged, the young Salphos slaughtered the entire Ophlgor tribe. This had serious consequences as the first step towards Yarwyn Daelthos's fall from grace. Shortly after the incident, the Echo Wars broke out, and the tortured Sovvael Salphos became a major player of the pan-sovtia conflict.

For the most part, Tevlan avoided the Echo Wars. Nevertheless, a Salphos-led mission to Garmir's Palace occurred, with the Salphos hoping to rescue Eskventhil the Quinlankern from the Secessionist Alliance. Later during the war, Chairman Gartia and his son, Ion Gartia headed to Tevlan to track down the bounty hunter Gislis, who had kidnapped members of their family.

title: Tevzek Caenor
text:
# Tevzek Caenor

Tevzek Caenor was a female Ithven who was a Flux-sensitive outcast from the Salphos Order. After the Echo Wars, she helped establish a network of various rebel cells against the Vastrian Dominion. Caenor was discovered on her homeworld of Vashrax by Salphos Master Jaxria Rinixtos, who brought her to the Salphos Temple on Daelvash to receive Salphos training. Following the outbreak of the Echo Wars, Salphos Grand Master Halrel assigned the young Caenor to be the Novice learner of Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos, who nicknamed her "Ythriaon" when she joined him at the Battle of Sovzek. Whereas Caenor was eager to prove herself, Daelthos had a reputation for recklessness, and they had a rather difficult start as master and apprentice. Yet they worked together to rescue Eskventhil, the son of crime lord Garmir Thavash Marbrynthil, and returned Eskventhil to his father, thus facilitating a crucial alliance between the Tevtos Clan and the Concord of Auren.

title: Tevzek Caenor
text: As a commander in the Grand Army of the Concord, Caenor found a mentor in Echo Captain Tevtia of the 501st Legion, with whom she and Daelthos collaborated to lead frontline campaigns against the League of Free Realms. In her first command position at the Battle of Pyrnor, Caenor disobeyed orders and lost her entire squadron of pilots, but she rebounded and helped secure a victory at Pyrnor. Her assignments pitted her against a variety of opponents, from General Caephen and Zargoth apprentice Olvael Nylandren to bounty hunters such as Ophvok Nydren and Hydren Sing. Over time, she matured into a respected leader, contributing to key Concord victories like the Second Battle of Quinria and the Battle of Kesyn Xelkern. Caenor even died during a series of events on Fenrelthos, but the Daughter, a Flux wielder who personified the radiant side, sacrificed herself to resurrect Caenor and bring her back to life.

title: Tevzek Caenor
text: Caenor gained much experience on and beyond the war front, leading a group of Salphos initiates to revolt against their Rinmirian captors, helping rescue a colony of Ithven from enslavement by the Yarthilian Slave Dominion, and serving as an advisor to the Sylthos rebels—with her close friend, Rinzor Havruldun, among them—as they liberated their world from the League. In a stark turn of events, Caenor was framed for the bombing of the Salphos Temple eskria and other homicides, and she escaped into the Daelvash Ythkern to clear her name. Though she formed an unlikely alliance with Olvael Nylandren, she was detained by Concord forces and was consequently barred from the Salphos Order. Ultimately, Daelthos uncovered the true culprit, Caenor's friend, and fellow Novice Ulvkrix Ythdris, and prevented his former apprentice from being convicted of sedition. Nevertheless, the ordeal dislodged Caenor's faith in the Salphos. She refused the Salphos High Council's offer to rejoin the Order, instead departing in search of a new path. Caenor briefly returned to lead Concord forces during the Siege of Lunsera and faced Tevkaibryn and his allies. Edict 41 was enacted shortly after the Zargoth Lord's capture and Caenor alongside Tevtia, after freeing Tevtia from the control of Edict 41, escaped the rest of her 501st division. Faking her death, she was forced into hiding.

title: Tevzek Caenor
text: After the Vastrian Dominion came to power, Caenor went into hiding on Ythrn and Irkairax disguised as "Brevael." Following the evacuation of Irkairax, Caenor joined Senator Vashdren Faelvok's growing rebel movement. She became the manager of his intelligence network and adopted the codename "Lunzor." As Lunzor, Caenor provided intelligence to various rebel factions including Zelarrel Dravael's Sylyndren rebel cell. Caenor took a particular interest in Dravael's rebels because one of their members, a Salphos named Nevrax Brekern, had begun to train his own Novice, Vezek Cyrnor. In addition, Caenor's efforts against the Dominion brought her into contact with the Dark Lord of the Zargoth Ursera Garvash—who, unknown to her, was actually her former master, Yarwyn Daelthos—as well as the Dominion Baelmund known as the Fifth Brother and the Seventh Sister, but it also gave her the chance to reunite with Tevtia. Following the mission to Nevyn, Caenor became lost to the rubble and shadows of the Zargoth temple and was believed by many, including Brekern and Cyrnor, to have perished during a duel with Ursera Garvash.

title: Tevzek Caenor
text: However, Caenor was unexpectedly saved from Garvash's wrath by a future Vezek Cyrnor, who pulled her through a portal into the World Between Worlds, a mystical plane of the Synth Flux connecting all time and space. After a confrontation with Ursera Bregoth, who desired access to the dimension, Caenor returned to her time, promising Cyrnor that she would find him once she returned. After the end of the Great Schism War, Caenor joined Vewyn Gisbryn in her quest to find the missing Cyrnor, who had disappeared during the Liberation of Wendrenkai, and trained Gisbryn in the ways of the Salphos until parting ways. Caenor later journeyed to the city of Jorphos on the forest planet Ythul looking for information on the location of Grand Admiral Vevash, who had disappeared alongside Cyrnor, from Magistrate Tevlis Torvash. Needing to rescue the city from Torvash's rule, she allied herself with the Lunseran Esketh Vashon, who had been on a quest to bring the Synth Flux-sensitive initiate Zunlgor to the Salphos. After freeing Jorphos, Caenor refused to train Zunlgor and directed Vashon to the planet Havrvael instead. She later visited Havrgan Daelthos at his new Salphos Temple and, when Daelthos found Zunlgor in his care following a summons from the seeing stone, oversaw his training of the child temporarily.

title: Tevzek Caenor
text:
Faced with Vevash's return, Caenor returned to Wendrenkai and enlisted Gisbryn's help once again in finding Cyrnor and the missing Grand Admiral. Decades after Caenor began her search, her voice joined a multitude of Salphos spirits to guide the young Salphos Ithlgor, the granddaughter of a resurrected Ursera Bregoth, during the final battle of the Ascendant Directorate-Resistance War. Tevzek inspired Ithlgor to stand up to Bregoth and destroy him once and for all.

## Biography

### Childhood

In 36 BKV, Tevzek Caenor was born on the planet Vashrax to the Ithvens Thazek-ti and Jaxdrislis-il Caenor. Early in her life, Caenor was taken on a journey by her mother, who taught her about life and death. During that period, the young girl encountered a raxshir feline, which she reached out to without fear. She proceeded to ride atop the animal to return home. Upon her return, the elder Ithven Lunlan realized the infant was Flux-sensitive and declared that she would be a Salphos. When Caenor was three years old, she was discovered by Salphos Master Jaxria Rinixtos among her people on Vashrax after her natural ability to sense the intentions and feelings of others had marked her as Flux-sensitive.

title: Tevzek Caenor
text: Around the same time, however, Caenor was nearly enslaved by an impostor, who intercepted the signal to the Salphos Order and hoped to use her powers for their own ends. Being unable to properly explain to the village elders the danger she knew the impostor posed, Caenor's fellow villagers held scorn towards her when she refused to demonstrate her Flux powers, but the impostor's plan was ultimately thwarted. Although the impostor had scared the young Caenor, she trusted Rinixtos instantly, and he taught her how to breathe slowly to calm herself. Afterward, she was accepted into the Salphos Order, beginning her new life after Rinixtos brought her to the Salphos Temple on Daelvash, where, like all Salphos of her era, she was raised. Training as a Salphos Initiate restored her self-confidence after the fear caused by the impostor impacted it, and the life of a Salphos became the only life she ever knew.

title: Tevzek Caenor
text:
At some point, Caenor traveled to the Salphos Temple on the ice planet Morsul to acquire a ixium crystal for a plasmablade, feeling the crystals, albeit without knowing that was what she sensed, as soon as the Salphos wenkrix came out of voidlane. She entered into the temple's cave after Grand Master Halrel told her she would know her crystal when she found it. As the opening to the cave slowly closed as the sun of Tevlume set, she urgently looked for her crystal until she calmed herself, thinking back on Halrel's words and only then seeing its light. Excited and ready to leave, she quickly made her way out of the cave with the tool for which she could build her own plasmablade. Although her visit to Morsul had overall been unremarkable, her decision to trust Halrel's teaching restored her ability to trust others after it was impacted by the false Salphos. From there, she would construct said plasmablade using the ixium crystal under the tutelage of Salphos architect automaton Zarvok, who fussed over her shoulder as she worked on it. At another point, Halrel taught her that she could sometimes find something she was not looking for in a situation.

During her time at the Salphos Temple, Professor Zarvok would regale her with the History of the Galaxy, Parts One, Two and Three, of which she considered part one the best.

title: Ulvon
text:
# Ulvon

Ulvon (pronounced /kə'minoʊ/) was an aquatic planet located in a remote star system in Wild Space of the galaxy. Ulvon was sometimes classed as extragalactic due to its secluded location. It was inhabited by the Ulvonians—a race of tall, elegant beings with long necks who were regarded as a mysterious species that tended to keep to themselves. They were also known for their cloning technology, which was used to create a clone army for the Concord of Auren.

Largely isolated from the wider galaxy, Ulvon's existence was erased from the Salphos records by Count Ophvael. Salphos Knight Faelnor Halthossul, who was investigating the attempt to assassinate Nymund Daelphos, traced the bounty hunter Draseralan Zeldakrel to the planet, where he discovered the cloning program. With the outbreak of the Echo Wars, Ulvon became a prime target for the League of Free Realms and a vital asset for the Concord, resulting in at least two attempts to invade the watery world. During the early days of the Vastrian Dominion, with the cloning program halted, Ulvon's civilization was almost completely wiped out via orbital bombardment of all cities and structures, including the capital of Ulvkern City, leaving only a small diaspora of Ulvonians in Dominion custody or scattered amongst the stars as all that remained.

## Description

title: Ulvon
text:
## Description

Located seventy thousand light-years from the Inner Realms, of Wild Space, Ulvon was located twelve parsecs away from the Halphos Maze dwarf satellite galaxy, and was sometimes classed as extragalactic.

Ulvon was a remote and inhospitable planet which was covered in oceans that held an abundance of life. Its savage storms and powerful lightning bursts could be seen vaguely through its relatively thick atmosphere. The native Ulvonians lived on stilt-cities scattered across Ulvon's watery surface. The majority of these cities were devoted to cloning projects, as the highly intelligent Ulvonians specialized in cloning for clients needing workers or private security forces, along with other one-off requests. Due to the remoteness of the planet and its extensive rainy season, only occasional representatives of clone purchasing authorities were undeterred from visiting the world. During some parts of the year was covered with heavy electrical storms, where Ulvonians rode on aiwhas underwater and resurfaced once they were near their destination.

## History

### Early civilization

At some point the planet was not covered in water, and the Ulvonians built a large land-based civilization. However, the water level rose, forcing the Ulvonians to build their structures on stilts.

title: Ulvon
text:
## History

### Early civilization

At some point the planet was not covered in water, and the Ulvonians built a large land-based civilization. However, the water level rose, forcing the Ulvonians to build their structures on stilts.

The Ulvonians were generally isolationists, staying out of contact with the wider galaxy. This behavior could be traced back to the great flood that changed their homeworld, as they decided it was less risky to adapt their genetic code and planet than to ask for aid from the Concord of Auren.

### The Concord

#### Creating the clone army

In 33 BKV, Salphos Master Korria commissioned the Ulvonians to create a clone army for the Concord of Auren, in response to a Flux vision that saw the galaxy descending into a galaxy-spanning conflict. However, the Zargoth secretly took over the project, after arranging Korria' death at the hands of the Saltiaar Syndicate. The Zargoth selected the human bounty hunter Draseralan Zeldakrel to serve as the genetic template of the clone army. One year later, shortly after the Battle of Olrax and taking advantage of Wynyn Dramara's current absence, Count Ophvael snuck into the Salphos Archives and deleted all information of Ulvon from them to cover up the Zargoth's tracks.

#### The dawn of the Echo Wars

title: Ulvon
section: History > The Concord > The dawn of the Echo Wars
text:
#### The dawn of the Echo Wars

In 22 BKV, Ulvon was governed by Prime Minister Torraxdak Marvash. Working on a request from Viceroy Morwynvael Bredren, Zeldakrel attempted to assassinate Olrax senator Nymund Daelphos on the Concord's capital planet, Daelvash, during the Secessionist Crisis. However, Zeldakrel's fellow bounty hunter tasked for the assassination attempt, Dovlume Olkai, failed to kill Daelphos and was cornered by the Salphos Knight Faelnor Halthossul. Zeldakrel killed Olkai before she could reveal any information. Halthossul went on to investigate the assassination attempt, searching for clues from the Ulvon saberdart used to kill Olkai. After receiving no answers from the Salphos Archives, Halthossul sought counsel with Morphen Havrzor, a Rinrax chef and information broker who owned and operated Sovkrix's Ophynsera in Jaxlume Town on Daelvash.

Havrzor informed his Salphos friend that the dart originated from Ulvon, a planet located twelve parsecs outside of the Halphos Maze, a satellite galaxy in orbit of the main galaxy. Havrzor explained that Ulvon was home to highly competent cloners who mostly kept to themselves. Ulvon had been removed from the records of the Salphos Archives, so Halthossul and Master Halrel had to locate the planet by other means. After finding a way to reach Ulvon, Halthossul traveled to the planet, where he discovered the production of the clone army supposedly commissioned by the Salphos Order.

### Echo Wars

title: Ulvon
text:
### Echo Wars

Following the outbreak of the Echo Wars, Ulvon was one of the main operational areas of the Concord of Auren. It served as the main training grounds for clone yarzeks as well as the location for the clone army's creation. As such, it was a major military asset for the Concord and a prime target for a Secessionist attack and thus warranted the protection of a massive Concord naval blockade of ten Wynkernsera-class Void Cruisers, one Torzek-class assault ship, and two Nevkern-class light cruisers; the size of this blockade discouraged all but the most risky of full-frontal assaults by the Secessionists to stand a chance of taking Ulvon.

title: Ulvon
text: At some point, a sovtia explorer—who may have been the Drabrynkrix artist Ythlume Fenkai—elected to make the long journey needed to visit Ulvon, wanting to visit Ulvkern City and meet the cloners who had come to play a vital role in sovtia history. In their journal, the explorer wrote that they were honored to visit the city. From the beginnings of the war, the Secessionists plotted their assault on the clone homeworld. In 22 BKV, the cyborg General Caephen sent a strike team of commando automatons to take out Halphos Station, a Concord ithvok that could warn Ulvon of an impending attack. The base was taken over by the automatons, but as Caephen's fleet arrived in the system before attacking Ulvon, echo soldier Fengoth sacrificed himself to alert Concord forces of the enemy fleet, causing the Secessionists to retreat and call off their attack.

title: Ulvon
text: Later, a Secessionist assault finally made its way to Ulvon. Led by Olvael Nylandren and General Caephen, a massive force hit Ulvon in an attempt to end clone creation for the Concord. Salphos Generals Yarwyn Daelthos and Faelnor Halthossul with the 501st Legion and the 212th Attack Battalion were sent to assist in the planet's defense alongside Salphos General Draul Ti. The two-pronged assault saw Nylandren lead Vephen-class assault ships beneath the surface of the planet's oceans to sneak up on Ulvkern City as the two fleets clashed above the watery planet. Many Vorthos-series battle automatons invaded the cloning facilities, killing many echo soldiers, including Echo VEX Commanders Colt and Havoc and the malformed clone 99. Nylandren successfully stole the prime sample of the echo soldier DNA template, but she was attacked by Daelthos, who, with the assistance of a force of fenzor, reclaimed the DNA. Concord forces managed to defeat the Secessionists and cloning continued on the planet.

title: Ulvon
text: Another battle of Ulvon involved Salphos General Nevvael Ithlan, who fought against Secessionist automatons deployed in the battle. An important mission to Ulvon was arranged for occurred between 22 BKV and 21 BKV, with Salphos Master Wenrel Ophvash, Salphos Knight Havrzek Lorul, and Salphos Knight Salthos Gismaranor being selected for the mission. Before leaving Lorul asked his friend and fellow Knight Yarlgor Wynthos if she would be joining them, but the angered Wynthos informed him she was still stationed in the Salphos Temple, which she believed was a punishment for her actions during the mission to Baelphen. Late in the war, the Zargoth's plan to destroy the Salphos using the echo soldiers was almost revealed. During the Battle of Zelmir Halthos, the echo soldier Wentia, designated XW-1151, executed the Salphos Master Zeltos during the confrontation due to a defect in his inhibitor chip. Wanting answers, it was decided that the clone would be sent to Ulvon.

title: Ulvon
text: The Ulvonian leadership did everything possible to prevent the truth about the chips from being revealed, that they would guarantee the fenzor' obedience when the order to destroy the Salphos was given. Although Wentia died during a procedure carried out without permission to remove the chip by his clone friend Havrwyn and the medical android GKQ-6, the threat to the Zargoth plan did not end while Havrwyn continued to investigate. Havrwyn found that all fenzor had chips and decided to remove his, and he and the two chips were sent to Daelvash for analysis. Havrwyn was eventually killed on Daelvash and the truth about the chips was kept secret.

title: Ursera Bregoth
text:
# Ursera Bregoth

Ursera Bregoth, born Torsera Vorix and also simply known as the Emperor, was a male human Dark Lord of the Zargoth and Emperor of the Vastrian Dominion, with his reign lasting from 19 BKV to 4 AKV. Rising to power in the Grand Assembly as the senator of Olrax, the secretive Zargoth Lord cultivated two identities, Bregoth and Vorix, using both to further his political career and deceive his way into accomplishing his goal. He orchestrated the fall of the Concord of Auren and the Salphos Order through the Echo Wars, and then established his reign over the galaxy which lasted until his death at the Battle of Wynthas. However, the umbral side of the Synth Flux gave rise to powers which allowed him to escape death, seeking further immortality until the Emperor was eventually permanently destroyed and killed during the Battle of Baellan by Ithlgor, his granddaughter born from his Strand-Cast clone son Baelrnvael and his daughter-in-law Dramirthil.

title: Ursera Bregoth
text: Born on the Middle Reaches planet Olrax in 84 BKV as the High Concord Era ended, Torsera Vorix possessed a strong connection to the Synth Flux, and was secretly trained in the ways of the Zargoth by Ursera Saldun with Vorix taking Ursera Bregoth as his Zargoth persona. He eventually betrayed and killed his Zargoth Master, in order to train his own Zargoth apprentice, Ursera Tevkaibryn, for the Rule of Two limited their ranks to two Zargoth Lords at any given time. The Invasion of Olrax, a crisis orchestrated by Bregoth, led to the Senate to elect Vorix as Supreme Chancellor, although this came at the loss of Tevkaibryn, who was defeated and presumed killed in the Battle of Olrax. The Secessionist Crisis and the Echo Wars were masterminded by Bregoth and his second apprentice, Ursera Karel, in an effort to achieve sovtia dominance. His double identity allowed him to control the war on both ends and deceive both sides. Following an attempt to arrest the chancellor, the Great Salphos Purge commenced with Bregoth enacting Edict 41.

title: Ursera Bregoth
text: With the Salphos all but extinct, Bregoth installed the New Order in the Concord's place, declaring himself Sovtia Emperor and bringing an end to the millennia of democracy. Shortly after betraying and causing the death of Karel, he took on a new apprentice, having lured the Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos to the umbral side and transforming him into Ursera Garvash. Their reign was virtually unchallenged for a generation until the formation of the Free Accord of Auren. During the Great Schism War, the Emperor sought to betray Garvash, by replacing him with the latter's son, Havrgan Daelthos. However, Bregoth' plan backfired when Garvash ultimately renounced the umbral side and killed Bregoth to protect Havrgan. Thus, with the Zargoth's destruction, the Synth Flux was brought back into balance, fulfilling Yarwyn's destiny as the prophesied Chosen One.

title: Ursera Bregoth
text:
Through his master's teachings, however, Bregoth transferred his essence to an imperfect clone vessel that had been modeled on his original body. Anticipating the possibility of defeat, he created the Fendren to destroy the Vastrian Dominion and replace it with a new Zargoth Dominion, in the event of such a setback. His plans culminated in the destruction of the Renewed Concord and the emergence of the Ascendant Directorate, the creation of Supreme Leader Lorrel, who turned Zunria Sallgor—heir to the Daelthos bloodline—to the umbral side, and the establishment of the Final Order. When the Emperor announced his return to the galaxy in 35 AKV, the Resistance invaded the planet Baellan, Bregoth' hidden stronghold in the Uncharted Reaches. During the battle, the resurrected Emperor discovered a dyad in the Synth Flux in the form of the bond between Sallgor and Ithlgor, a Novice sired from the Vorix bloodline. His lifelong dream of eternal rule was finally quashed when Ithlgor called upon the strength of past Salphos to vanquish her grandfather by turning his own power against him, destroying Bregoth and his Zargoth Eternal cultists.

## Biography

### Early life and apprenticeship

title: Ursera Bregoth
text:
## Biography

### Early life and apprenticeship

The origins of Ursera Bregoth were closely guarded secrets that he took to his grave more than once. He was born on the Middle Reaches planet Olrax as Torsera Vorix, eighty-four years before the Battle of Kathasnor. The dynastic, noble Vorix family belonged to the affluent class in Olrax society, although throughout several points of time of his life, Vorix did not have any living family members as far as the public was aware, and no records of obituaries for his parents existed, marking him as the last of his ancient family bloodline. Vorix was raised in the cultured city of Cyrvensul, his homeworld's capital; he formed connections with a reputable host of credible politicians produced over the centuries, all the while acquiring a great amount of knowledge on governance and the subtleties of power during his youth. As such, Vorix had been skilled in manipulation since boyhood.

title: Ursera Bregoth
text:
The details about how Bregoth came to study under the Zargoth were known by very few, with it not even being known of when he did, but he became the Zargoth apprentice to Dark Lord of the Zargoth Ursera Saldun and took on the name Ursera Bregoth by 52 BKV. As a Zargoth Lord, Bregoth learned all his Zargoth Master knew about the umbral side of the Synth Flux, following the tradition first set by the ancient Ursera Nydren. While apprenticed to Saldun, Bregoth constructed his own Zargoth plasmablades. At the same time, little by little, he began to secure political power.

As a young man, Vorix had traveled throughout the galaxy, collecting art, at least some of which was connected to the umbral side, while doing so. Unaware docents would have written off his collection as junk, but Vorix knew better. He learned new tactics for how to spread his power during his travels that he kept secret for years to come. While training with Saldun, Bregoth was taught that two Zargoth were required for their perilous machinations. So, if they worked together in accordance to Ursera Nydren's Rule of Two, with one of them serving as bait for the umbral side of the Synth Flux and the other as a vessel, they would succeed in acquiring the ability to harness the full power of the umbral side and rule immortal for ten thousand years.

title: Ursera Bregoth
text:
Ursera Bregoth and Ursera Saldun worked together for years, trying to unlock the secrets to immortality, which was the obsession and longtime lust of Saldun. Bregoth was eventually made aware of Saldun' ability to manipulate the resonites to create life, which his master employed to prevent the people he cared for from dying. Saldun believed the secret to immortality laid within science, and so conducted "unnatural" experiments with his rare ability to manipulate the resonites, as part of the pair's in depth studies into the biological underpinnings of life itself. Though they were incomplete, they were encouraging to Bregoth. According to Ursera Bregoth' book, The Secrets of the Zargoth, written later on his life, Saldun discovered a form of "immortality" through transference, a Flux power that allowed the user to transfer their spirit and consciousness to another body, essentially using bodies as vessels. This obsession with extending one's own life later passed onto Bregoth from his time as Sovtia Emperor. Saldun also attempted to create a Flux dyad with Bregoth, a unique Flux-bond as strong as life itself and which was predecessor to the Rule of Two. However, Saldun was unable to form the dyad.

### Political career and double life

#### Senator of Olrax

title: Ursera Bregoth
section: Biography > Political career and double life
text:
### Political career and double life

#### Senator of Olrax

In his public persona as Torsera Vorix, Bregoth took a great interest in politics and the public life of Olrax. In 65 BKV he was part of the officials attending the opening ceremony of the Cyrvensul power generator, with attendees noting his interest in the complex's deep-pit design. His embarkment on a career in politics was further aided by his master, who arranged for him to be raised to the position of senator for his homeworld in the Concord of Auren Senate as part of the Olrax delegation, being elected in 52 BKV. His role also made him the senator for the rest of the Xellume sector, meaning he represented a total of thirty-six planets. Once elected, Vorix quickly joined incumbent Supreme Chancellor Ulvmir Faeldak's ruling party. He was followed by a grouping of aides who loyally followed him since his days on Olrax. He noticed the fervent bickering and corruption that mired the Concord. He began to establish relations with those who would become his future collaborators, such as Sylixlis Tevven. The duo met for the first time when Tevven was still a yarzek of the Tevvash Sector Eldbryn Academy, and while Vorix was still apprenticed to Saldun.

title: Vastrian Dominion
text:
# Vastrian Dominion

The Vastrian Dominion, also known as the First Vastrian Dominion, the Dominion regime, Vorix's regime, or simply the Dominion, and later as the Old Dominion, was a totalitarian stratocratic fascist dictatorship that replaced the Concord of Auren at the end of the Echo Wars. Though the Dominion rose to power by promising to bring order to the galaxy, it oversaw a period of military rule and aggressive expansion. The subsequent Dominion Era would last only two decades, for it was eventually overthrown by the Free Accord of Auren in the Great Schism War, but not before the sovereign star systems of the galaxy's known regions had been largely conquered by the Dominion's forces.

title: Vastrian Dominion
text: The Dominion traced its origins to a Zargoth conspiracy to destroy the Salphos Order and regain control over the galaxy. The Dominion was secretly controlled by the Zargoth, for the Sovtia Emperor was, in fact, the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth, whose reign was enforced by his apprentice, Ursera Garvash, whom he eventually elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet. Rising to power on a groundswell of populist support and capitalizing on anti-Salphos and anti-automaton sentiment and human-ethnocentrism manufactured by the destructive Echo Wars, Ursera Bregoth appointed himself Emperor at the end of the conflict by promising security and stability to the war-torn Concord. Gaining the overwhelming approval of the Grand Assembly, Ursera Bregoth staged a coup by the Salphos and oversaw their subsequent purge from the galaxy, assisted by his right-hand, Ursera Garvash.

title: Vastrian Dominion
text: The Dominion stood virtually unchallenged during its rise to power, with the backing of the Dominion Assembly and the spreading of its massive technological military force across the galaxy and began a major expansion and encroaching into the unexplored regions. At first, the Vastrian Dominion was a constitutional monarchy in basic theory, however it gradually evolved into a stratocracy as the power of the Dominion Assembly waned. However, numerous insurgent cells sprang up against the Dominion and gradually united to initiate a growing rebellion, winning its first major victory over Nykai in 4 BKV. These rebel groups eventually formed the Free Accord in 2 BKV, and achieved its first major victory with the theft of the Void Core plans on Nydrenzor, which, in turn, led to the destruction of the Void Core at the Battle of Kathasnor. The following years saw initial Alliance successes until a major Dominion victory on Havrmara in 3 AKV, but the Dominion suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Wynthas. During the battle, Ursera Bregoth was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Yarwyn Daelthos, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking the end of Zargoth rule and the deterioration of the Dominion and the resumption of the Concord of Auren, the Renewed Concord.

title: Vastrian Dominion
text: With the deaths of the Emperor and his top lieutenant, factionalism overcame the Dominion as it fractured into breakaway fiefdoms led by splinter Prefects, admirals, and generals, many of whom ignored Grand Vizier Ophbryn Korzek's authority at the capital and became warlords as the Dominion continued to fight the Concord. The Dominion Navy came to be publicly led by cyrvok Grand Admiral Rinlume Ophlan, though she was a figurehead for Fleet Admiral Salthil Jormir. Ultimately, Jormir seized control over the cyrvok forces, removing Ophlan from power and becoming Emperor-in-effect through his new position as Counselor to the Dominion. Under Jormir's command, the Dominion made its final stand at the Battle of Caedunkrix in 5 AKV, ultimately losing and capitulating to the Renewed Concord. With the cessation of the fighting, the Sovtia Concordance was signed, vanquishing the Dominion.

title: Vastrian Dominion
text:
While the Dominion was gone, the Renewed Concord faced continued resistance from several Dominion remants in the years after. Eventually its successor, the Ascendant Directorate began a clandestine armament program to rebuild the former Dominion Military. The miltary junta was unaware, however, that they had been manipulated by a new hidden conspiracy, for secret cultists on the lost world of Baellan attended to the spirit of Ursera Bregoth, and constructed a fleet built to turn the Ascendant Directorate into a true empire. The cult efforts ultimately failed, however, for they were opposed by the Resistance and Salphos Order, leading to an end of the Ascendant Directorate.

## History

### Early foundations

The Dominion ideals of the Vastrian Dominion could be dated back to the Zargoth Dominion of the Elder Concord's time period. Following the defeat of the Zargoth during their final war with the Salphos Order, for at least a thousand years, the dominant governing body of the galaxy was the unicameral, parliamentary, and democratic Concord of Auren, which was governed by the Grand Assembly and led by an elected Supreme Chancellor.

In the last decades of its existence, the Concord Senate became embroiled in bureaucracy, rendering it woefully ineffectual as a governing body. Ursera Bregoth, the Dark Lord of the Zargoth known publicly as Senator Torsera Vorix of Olrax, privately lamented the declining state of the Senate, noting that the Concord was "not what it once was."

title: Vastrian Dominion
text:
Thirteen years before the Concord's end as a democracy, Ursera Bregoth orchestrated the Invasion of Olrax by the Merchant Combine in order to create a leadership crisis in the Senate. Bregoth used the crisis to manipulate the then Queen of the Olrax, Nymund Daelphos, into calling a Vote of No Confidence against sitting Supreme Chancellor Pyrlumekrix Quaphos. The vote passed, and in the subsequent election, Bregoth—in his public persona of Senator Vorix of Olrax—secured the position of Supreme Chancellor of the Concord of Auren for himself through a strong sympathy vote. Ultimately, he would be the last individual to hold this office.

In the decade that followed, Bregoth secretly manipulated sovtia events to the extent that war became inevitable. Besides persuading a dead Salphos Master, Korria, to create a secret clone army, he also tasked his Zargoth apprentice, Ursera Karel, with exacerbating political tensions in the Concord and engineering a Secessionist Crisis. These actions would culminate in the outbreak of the Echo Wars held on Quinria, the last conflict of the Concord, while Bregoth himself "reluctantly" accepted emergency powers from the Senate. The Echo Wars, Bregoth planned, would further make people in the galaxy grow bitter with the Concord while he centralized his power to sweep away the Concord and Salphos.

### Birth of the New Order

#### Drawn out conflict

title: Vastrian Dominion
section: History > Birth of the New Order
text:
### Birth of the New Order

#### Drawn out conflict

Since the onset of the Echo Wars in 22 BKV, the Concord endeavored to strengthen its security and stability through the creation of new organizations such as the Commission for the Protection of the Concord (Faelvashyn), which utilized propaganda to increase public morale, promote patriotism, and foster anti-Secessionist sentiment within the general population. As the Concord became increasingly centralized, however, Chancellor Vorix's powers continued to grow through additional assets ceded to the Office of the Chancellor, including the sovtia banking system that was placed under his direct oversight. This gave Bregoth the finance he needed to build his empire. All the while, the war drained and broke the sovtia populace's spirit, leaving them longing for any kind of peace.

title: Vastrian Dominion
section: History > Birth of the New Order > Drawn out conflict
text: The Chancellor remained a popular leader for the duration of the war, having managed to stay in office at the will of the Senate for longer than his term permitted. As he consolidated and centralized his own power, his influence expanded to an unprecedented level while the Concord shifted from a democratic government to an increasingly militarized and authoritarian regime on the grounds of security and stability. In addition to his authority as Commander-in-Chief of the Concord Military, the Chancellor exerted more control over the Senate, the courts, and even the media, with DataWeb News becoming a state-run program in order to ensure that information would not be compromised by the League of Free Realms. Bregoth's hold over the Concord further expanded with additional amendments to the Sovtia Constitution while public support for the Salphos weakened as the war carried on, paving the way for his ultimate ascension as Emperor of the galaxy.

title: Vastrian Dominion
section: History > Birth of the New Order > Drawn out conflict
text: As the war continued, the Concord's very nature was corrupted as the state became more warlike and less democratic. The government used the conflict as an excuse to annex once-independent planets and cut social services in the name of funding the war, something which Senator Nymund Daelphos recognized would fuel distaste for the Concord in its own citizenry. While she feared the Secessionists would use that growing anger to win the war, she failed to realize that it was Vorix himself who had been engineering the war in such a way so as to make people tired of the Concord and eager for something new. Duchess Garlison Nevsera of the neutral planet Lunsera was able to recognize the changing tides within the Concord.

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
text:
# Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor

Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor was a Flux-sensitive human Havrrelian female politician, Salphos, and military leader who served in the Free Accord of Auren during the Dominion Era and the Renewed Concord and Resistance in the subsequent Renewed Concord Era. Shortly after birth on Vashkrix Fykrixria, she was adopted into the House of Faelvok—the Havrrelian royal family—and was raised as Princess Vegoth Faelvok of Havrrel, a planet in the Inner Realms known for its dedication to pacifism. The princess was raised as the daughter of Senator Vashdren Jornor Faelvok and his wife, Queen Pyrmundrn Faelvok, making her the heir to the Havrrelian monarchy. Instilled with the values of her adopted homeworld, Faelvok devoted her life to the restoration of democracy by opposing authoritarian regimes, such as the Vastrian Dominion and the Ascendant Directorate.

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
text: Born in 19 BKV as Vegoth Daelphos Daelthos, she was the daughter of the Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos and Senator Nymund Daelphos of Olrax. Her birth occurred in the aftermath of the Echo Wars, which saw the Salphos Order purged and the Concord of Auren reorganized into the Vastrian Dominion. With her mother's death in childbirth and her father's fall to the umbral side of the Synth Flux, Vegoth and her twin brother, Havrgan, were separated to keep them hidden from the hands of her father and the Emperor. As the adopted daughter of a politician, Vegoth grew up peacefully—albeit secluded—on Havrrel until she was kidnapped by mercenaries led by Kesthas Daelkrix—under the orders of the Third Sister, a member of the Nevontos—in 9 BKV. Since he had fought alongside her adoptive father in the Echo Wars, Salphos Master Faelnor Halthossul went to Vegoth's rescue on Faeltos, and, after evading the Dominion's hand on Vashtia and Zarlgornor, Vegoth was brought back to Havrrel. Years later, Vegoth succeeded Vashdren by representing their homeworld in the Dominion Assembly, though secretly she supported the Uprising. During the Great Schism War, however, Havrrel was destroyed along with its inhabitants and the royal family by the Dominion's RK-8 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, causing Faelvok to openly fight the New Order as one of the Free Accord’s substantial heroes.

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
text: In the aftermath of the Battle of Wynthas, Faelvok married the Halrelethian smuggler Ophsera Sallgor and learned the Salphos arts as her brother's apprentice until giving birth to her son, Zunria Sallgor, on the day of the Dominion's capitulation in 5 AKV. Her personal and political life suffered in the years that followed, with Zunria turning to the umbral side like his grandfather before him, adopting the persona of Rhorn Daelven, and the Grand Assembly sidelining Faelvok's career. Adopting the military rank of general, she led the Resistance and their efforts to oppose the rising Ascendant Directorate during the Cold War while seeking to make amends with Zunria in hopes that her son will return to the radiant side of the Synth Flux like her father during the Battle of Wynthas. Despite her efforts, the Ascendant Directorate succeeded in destroying the Renewed Concord, and Faelvok's husband died at the hands of their estranged son in 34 AKV. Faelvok continued to lead the Resistance during the war against the Ascendant Directorate, all the while passing on her Salphos training onto Ithlgor—a Flux-sensitive scavenger from Caedunkrix and Havrgan’s apprentice.

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
text:
As her health declined, Faelvok used her remaining strength to reach her son, calling him back to the radiant side. Following her death on Urria Irvoksul in 35 AKV, her final actions inspired Ithlgor and the Resistance to defeat the forces of the reborn Ursera Bregoth's Zargoth Eternal on Baellan and spark an uprising against the Ascendant Directorate across the galaxy. The heir to three inheritances, Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor's legacy passed on to the Salphos Ithlgor Daelthos, the military leader Rinvok Kesmir of the Resistance, and Zunria Sallgor, her only child, who ultimately returned to the light before sacrificing his life for Ithlgor and becoming one with the Synth Flux to join his mother and the Daelthos family.

## Biography

### Itheth-birth

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
text:
## Biography

### Itheth-birth

Toward the end of the Echo Wars, a sovtia conflict fought between the Concord of Auren and the League of Free Realms, also known as the Jorrn, that was engineered by the Zargoth Lord Ursera Bregoth, Salphos Master Halrel set out on a journey to discover the secrets of immortality. His journey took him to Faelkrix, the ancient Zargoth homeworld, where he faced visions of the future. At the end of his journey, the Synth Flux Priestess, Korlis, who had guided his journey, told him that there was another Daelthos, and Halrel heard his voice from the future say so as well. These events not only alluded to the potential he would sense in Vegoth, but to what Halrel would tell her twin brother, Havrgan, about Vegoth in his last words, before his death.

### Early life

#### Birth

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
text:
### Early life

#### Birth

Vegoth Daelphos Daelthos was born on the asteroid of Vashkrix Fykrixria two days after the end of the Echo Wars and the newly established Vastrian Dominion's purge of the Salphos Order. She and her twin brother, Havrgan, who was born shortly before her, were the children of Concord Senator Nymund Daelphos Caeria, who died shortly after the births, and Salphos Knight Yarwyn Daelthos, who had recently fallen to the umbral side of the Synth Flux. She was left with a lasting impression of images and feelings of her mother that her brother did not: that their mother was "very beautiful, kind, but sad", though Vegoth was unsure if she had really seen her mother or if she had just invented the memories to fill the hole in her life.

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
text:
Of the two Daelthos children, Halrel felt that Vegoth was more suited to be a Salphos, owing to her natural strength, will, and clarity (as opposed to her brother, who was impetuous, headstrong, unruly, and inattentive), wanting very much to train her. However, to protect the children from the Dominion, Ursera Bregoth, who ruled the Dominion as Sovtia Emperor Vorix, and the now–Zargoth Lord Ursera Garvash, Senator Vashdren Jornor Faelvok agreed to adopt the infant Vegoth together with his wife, Queen Pyrmundrn of Havrrel, while Faelnor Halthossul personally watched over Havrgan, who would live with their father's stepbrother Vashyn Lunlgor and his wife Mormir, on the planet Tevlan.

#### Princess of Havrrel

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
section: Biography > Early life > Princess of Havrrel
text:
#### Princess of Havrrel

Through adoption, Vegoth Daelphos Daelthos became Vegoth Faelvok, formally becoming heiress of the Royal Family of Havrrel through the Name Day ceremony. Although it was common knowledge that she was adopted, and everyone assumed that she was just another of the many, many children left orphaned by the Echo Wars, she remained unaware of her biological parents' fates. When Vegoth was an infant, she was mesmerized by the fish in an aquarium while her adoptive father read secret files concerning the former Salphos Novice Tevzek Caenor's presence on the agrarian moon of Irkairax. Vashdren later carried her after reading the files. On one occasion when Vegoth was a toddler she escaped from her bath and ran wet and naked into the formal dining room interrupting a diplomatic dinner and causing HV-9T to chase after her.

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
section: Biography > Early life > Princess of Havrrel
text:
Vegoth was eventually told that her birth father had died during one of the last battles of the Echo Wars and that her birth mother had been injured and only lived long enough to give birth to her. However, Vegoth had no interest in her birth parents seeing her adoptive parents as the only family she ever needed. Often when Vegoth went to sleep her parents would tell her that they had waited a long time for a child, as part of the story about when her father had come home from some "mysterious mission" to surprise her mother with a baby girl in her arms.

As a small child, Vegoth believed that the glowing coming from inside her mother's chest was a bouquet of blooming candlewick flowers. She would eventually learn that the glowing was from Pyrmundrn's pulmonodes, which she had gotten after a near fatal climbing accident when she was sixteen, during her Challenge of the Body. She told Vegoth that she had chosen not to cover them up with skin through medigel sessions, as they were proof that she had survived. Vegoth would eventually go on to meet other people with the same cybernetics.

title: Vegoth Daelthos Faelvok Sallgor
section: Biography > Early life > Princess of Havrrel
text: Sometime after her fourth birthday, Vegoth received her "big girl bed," which made her realize that she was too old to sleep in her parent's bed. Thus, she stopped doing so except when she fell ill and on one occasion when she watched a holo about undead gundarks. During her childhood, Vegoth was taught by her father to appreciate the effort of Havrrel's workers, but also the importance of her duties as the planet's eventual queen and by her mother, that the life of royalty could be a very lonely and isolated one. She would often stand alongside her parents, waiting through Havrrel's endless royal ceremonies, knowing that she could let no emotion show on her face.

title: Vexwing starwing
text:
# Vexwing starwing

Vexwing Starwings, otherwise referred to as the Vexwing class, were a type of starwing marked by their distinctive S-foils that resembled the High Sovtia script's character "X" in attack formation. They were heavily armed with four laser cannons on the S-foils and proton torpedo launchers in the fuselage. Vexwings were designed for dogfighting and long missions. During the Great Schism War, the Free Accord used Vexwing models like the C-45M Vexwing starwing and D-54B-C6 Vexwing in many battles, deploying Vexwings in engagements such as the Attack on Wendrenkai, the Battle of Kathasnor, the Battle of Wynthas, and the Battle of Caedunkrix.

Approximately thirty years later, a different and upgraded variation of Vexwing, the B-94, was used by the Resistance, whereas a more advanced model, the J-65, was used by the Renewed Concord Defense Fleet.

## History

### Design and development

The Vexwing was descended from Ythdun Corporation's Echo Wars–era Fighter, namely the Aggressive HZVVLLTRMMTLCZ-847 starwing, Echo J-79 Baellismir, and J-79 Baellismir. Ythdun's engineers strove to build a well-rounded, voidjump drive-equipped snubfighter with no exploitable weakness. The new starwing was intended to become the backbone of the Dominion Navy, but political forces led to the Vastrian Dominion deciding to rely on Jorsulmund Fleet Systems' more affordable VRX fighter series. The Free Accord of Auren then adopted the Vexwing design as its own.

title: Vexwing starwing
text:
In 5 AKV, Cyrsera Corporation introduced the B-94 model, which incorporated many improvements over the B-92 series. The Ythdun engineers, having learned a valuable lesson from the loss of so many Vexwings in the trenches at Battle of Kathasnor, equipped the B-94 with a swiveling pulser cannon that could be used to fend off attacks from behind. At least one prototype had been constructed prior to the Battle of Caedunkrix. By 34 AKV, the Renewed Concord had retired most of its D-75J in favor of the G-98P, which were even more capable than the already impressive D-75J.

### Operational history

#### Great Schism War

The C-45M model was in use as early as 5 BKV. Saw Wynmara's Partisans had several of them in their livery during that period. Wynmara was among the first rebel leaders to see how useful the B-92 would be in rebel operations and had stolen eight via a violent raid on an Ythdun warehouse. Dubbed the Cavern Angels for the Partisans' habit of hiding material in caves, these Vexwings were used as early as the Partisans' stay on Wenmir Milo.

title: Vexwing starwing
section: History > Operational history > Great Schism War
text:
The Free Accord of Auren recovered information about the Vexwing via the rescue of Ythdun personnel and operated C-45M Vexwings as early as 1 BKV. During the attack on Wendrenkai, at least ten C-45M Vexwing Fighter alongside XWF-X3 Brakwing assault starwing/bombers participated in the assault, but all were destroyed by the Dominion defenses. Zelarrel Dravael, Mart Garmund, Grimyn Wyntia, T2-24N, and M8-N8 survived being shot down, but many other pilots were killed and their navimechs destroyed.

The Partisans continued to use the Cavern Angels squadron, though they had been ejected from the formal Alliance for Wynmara's extremist views. Accord Vexwings saw action shortly before the outbreak of the Great Schism War in both the Liberation of Ophmund and the Mission to Morkernlis.

title: Vexwing starwing
section: History > Operational history > Great Schism War
text: The full-scale Great Schism War began with the Battle of Nydrenzor, a costly but significant victory for the Alliance. The newly assembled squad, Rogue One, a special forces team created by Wenvash Ophmund, Baelphos Breon, Dovsera Kestia, Daelrn Jaxkrixtos, Zardren Urgan, and H-3JK disobeyed direct orders from Alliance High Command and instead deployed itself to Nydrenzor in a desperate bid to steal the technical readouts for the Dominion's Void Core battle station, and was subsequently joined by the Alliance Fleet. Vexwings from Red Squadron, Green Squadron, Blue Squadron, and Gold Squadron engaged Dominion TIEs and attempted to destroy the Shield Gate, while the capital ships joined the Shield Gate assault and fought the Dominion Void Cruisers. Shortly after the Alliance acquired the Void Core plans, the Void Core arrived at Nydrenzor and fired a low-power blast at the Citadel Tower, killing all forces at the Dominion surface installation.

title: Vexwing starwing
section: History > Operational history > Great Schism War
text:
Within days of Nydrenzor, the Dominion learned that the Alliance was headquartered at Kathasnor 4, and deployed the Void Core to crush the Alliance. The Alliance, having learned of the battle station's fatal design flaw, deployed a force of 30 Starwings (including 22 Vexwings) to attempt a series of attack runs on the planet-killing space station. The result was another costly victory for the Alliance. Havrgan Daelthos, a legendary Flux-sensitive Accord pilot, famously fired a pair of proton torpedoes into the Void Core's thermal exhaust port, causing a chain reaction in the reactor that destroyed the entire station. The Void Core was gone but the Alliance lost 27 Starwings (including 20 Vexwings) in the assault.

Sometime during 0 AKV, three Vexwings of Red Squadron were deployed in a mission to Eldix, which resulted in the rescue of multiple Alliance agents.

A few days after the Battle of Kathasnor, Vegoth Faelvok and Eskmund Daelsulvok disobeyed orders from Alliance High Command and departed on mission to rescue the survivors of Havrrel. Daelthos and Eldtos Zelon were scrambled to intercept their shuttle, but the rebels jumped to voidlane.

After the Assault on Keslanyn, Havrgan Daelthos and T2-W2 flew an Vexwing to Vashgothtia in order to obtain credits for the Accord war effort. Before long, a four-sided skirmish erupted over possession of Ursera Tevix' plasmablades, with M9 rescuing Daelthos by bringing him the ship.

title: Vexwing starwing
section: History > Operational history > Great Schism War
text:
Later, Daelthos flew an Vexwing from the Alliance Fleet to Tevlan, accompanied by T2-W2. There, he revisited Faelnor Halthossul's hut and discovered the deceased Salphos Master's journal. Disappointed that the journal didn't contain any information on Salphos training, Daelthos set course for Ophthil Rhovashyn.

Vexwings would again see large-scale action against the Dominion in the Battle of Katos Wenven. The battle was a costly defeat for the Alliance, with Blue Squadron completely destroyed and Red Squadron suffering heavy casualties.

Vexwings were also deployed to Dovix Prison in the aftermath of Eldven Ray's assault.

The Alliance struck back against the Dominion with the hijacking of the Irlis, a major space battle that resulted a rare case of an Dominion-class Void Cruiser being successfully boarded and hijacked. The Alliance used the Irlis to break through the Siege on Urnorvael VII and bring relief supplies to the planet's population. Although the hijacking ended with an Alliance victory, it resulted in B-8CF's capture by Task Flux 99. The navimech automaton T2-W2 took it upon himself to stage a mission to rescue B-8CF in a stolen Vexwing, while Havrgan Daelthos and C2 gave chase and embarked on a mission to Daelmund Prime.

Later, General Havrar Gissera deployed Vexwings to raid Jorkern Wenbryn Keslume's safe house on Xelbryn.

title: Vexwing starwing
section: History > Operational history > Great Schism War
text:
Later, General Havrar Gissera deployed Vexwings to raid Jorkern Wenbryn Keslume's safe house on Xelbryn.

At least five Accord Vexwings saw action in a dogfight over Salsera, where a pair of them shot down a VRX fighter. They were deployed Salsera again to help rescue Ophsera Sallgor and Vegoth Faelvok when a mission to scout locations for a new Accord base devolved into a skirmish with Baelbryn and Vashlis.

Vexwings also defended from Dominion forces that launched an attack on the Accord fleet shortly before the mission to Wenyn.

Vexwings again saw large-scale action at the mutiny on Kesyn Xelkern, a strategic Alliance victory. After the battle, the Kesyn Xelkern Nevsul Fleet became part of the Alliance Fleet, but the Kesyn Zarlume King Ythkrix and his Garmundzek Pyrthasvael Fylume were both killed by Dominion forces.

Later, Vexwings defended the Alliance Fleet from an assault on the Marmir Space Docks, a major blow for the Uprising. The attack destroyed more than half of the Accord cruisers and 90 percent of its available starwing forces.

A number of Vexwings accompanied the 61st Mobile Infantry company, known to most as "Twilight Company," on the Sovul campaign in the Middle Reaches Retreat. The campaign ended with the destruction of an Dominion biotoxin production facility and an Alliance victory.

title: Vexwing starwing
section: History > Operational history > Great Schism War
text: In 3 AKV, numerous Vexwings served as fighter escorts for the Alliance's NF-83 medium transports during the Battle of Havrmara. The rearguard actions on the surface covering the evacuation proved costly to the Alliance, with many personnel killed. Additionally, the Alliance was forced to leave behind much of their heavy equipment, and the fleet, including its Vexwings, scattered throughout the Far Reaches, travelling to separate vedris points like Vedris Point Mordrisphen.

title: Voidjump drive
text:
# Voidjump drive

The voidjump drive, also known as warp drive, was a propulsion system that allowed a wenkrix to reach lightspeed and traverse the void between stars in the alternate dimension of voidlane. As a consequence, the voidjump drive was a key instrument in shaping sovtia society, trade, politics, and war.

The voidjump drive required a functional voidjump drive motivator to operate. The vessel then traveled along a programmed course until it dropped back into normal space—realspace—at its destination.

A voidjump drive only functioned to keep a vessel in voidlane, and should a voidjump drive be forcibly deactivated or destroyed during transit, the ship was violently and instantly pulled back into realspace.

Being short-range craft, most starwings lacked a voidjump drive. This was notably the case with the Vastrian Dominion's VRX fighters, which had to be ferried to combat zones aboard larger ships. However, the Vexwing and Zephwing starwings used by the Free Accord were fitted with voidjump drives, allowing them to make long-range jumps.

Upon entering voidlane, a ship emitted cronau radiation, which was possible to detect with specialized sensor suites.

Large objects in normal space cast "mass shadows" in voidlane, thus voidlane jumps required accurate plotting to avoid collisions, which were often fatal.

title: Voidjump drive
text:
Upon entering voidlane, a ship emitted cronau radiation, which was possible to detect with specialized sensor suites.

Large objects in normal space cast "mass shadows" in voidlane, thus voidlane jumps required accurate plotting to avoid collisions, which were often fatal.

Later technologies could pull vessels out of voidlane. For instance, interdiction fields created gravitational shadows, simulating mass, in the path of an oncoming vessel, yanking the vessel out of voidlane. Dominion technologists developed the widely used Rineth vessels and their various sub-models, some of the most effective interdiction technologies.

## History

### Itheth-voidjump drive technologies

title: Voidjump drive
text:
## History

### Itheth-voidjump drive technologies

In the ancient times, due to the lack of voidjump drive technologies the earliest spacers used generation ships to travel through the galaxy and traverse the vast distances from one planet to another. Most notable for being used by a patriarch of the Xavok to blaze the Elddren Trunk Line, generation ships were soon replaced by sleeper ships following the invention of stasisium by the scientists on the planet Elddren Major. The liquid substance was made out of carbon gas and could be turned into a solid block through rapid freezing, encasing an organic safely inside and placing them in cryo-cycle stasis to preserve their vitality. The process, known as carbon-freezing ushered in a new era of space exploration and inadvertently helped the formation of the Concord of Auren as the people of the galaxy came closer together. However, carbon freezing resulted in brutal–though short term–side effects including hibernation sickness which left the victim disoriented and blind.

### Early developments

title: Voidjump drive
text:
### Early developments

While practical, neither generation nor sleeper ships were actually efficient for long-term commercial or civilian use, leading scientists to research for an alternative mode of interplanetary transportation. Scientists studying the species of space whale known as voidwhale eventually suspected that their mode of long-range transportation, the creation of simu-tunnel, actually passed through a dimension of space-time parallel to the one accessible by most organics, through which the distance between gravity wells–astronomical objects in realspace–was shorter as the laws of realspace spacetime didn't apply.

title: Voidjump drive
text:
By studying the behavior of voidwhale, scientists discovered that voidlane could be accessed by molecular displacement, which could only be achieved by breaking the speed of light. As voidlane was coterminous with realspace–meaning that every point in realspace had its equivalent in voidlane in the form of mass shadows–it was possible to use the dimension to travel from one point to the other in a shorter period of time without needing to actually cover the distance between them. According to legend, this technology was in fact developed by the mythical species of Dovdak, native to the planet Rinvash. Developing voidjump drive technology on the planet Vordunlgor independently from extraterrestrial assistance, the Cyrvaels had explored and interacted with the galaxy before the Concord of Auren ever made contact with their region of space. To this end, Cyrvael sovtia explorers were a common sight across the galaxy as far back as 30,000 years ago. As early as 27,000 BKV, the Marzor Zunsera reached the planet Gartos with the use of a tumbledrive propulsion engine. Eventually, Halrelethian engineers independently from their Wenlanmund counterparts developed the technology necessary to access the dimension, and dubbed it the voidjump drive–in contrast with standard engines, which were named sublight engines.

### Sovtia exploration using the voidjump drive

title: Voidjump drive
section: History > Sovtia exploration using the voidjump drive
text:
### Sovtia exploration using the voidjump drive

Once voidjump drives made faster-than-light travel possible, sovtia civilization flourished throughout ancient history. The Elder Concord sent pioneering scout ships to explore the galaxy as increasing numbers of civilians from the Inner Realms sought a better life. The Cyrvaels were among the early explorers along what became the Halrelethian Trade Spine voidlane route. Early voidjump drive routes were blazed by scouts such as the Dralume Zunvok clan by using voidlane sextants or simply following voidwhale in their travels. The latter practice demonstrated the species' tendency to feed on the gas GHZTZZW-15, which formed in places subject to intense interstellar energy, like Kagan or the Zelphensera system. Knowledge of this practice led humans to discover the mineral vexium, which also formed in the same places and, like Ringan, fuels faster and better voidjump drive jumps. Unfortunately, the faster-than-light travel also created new possibilites for war, as the now-mythological Great Voidlane War between the Concord and Zargoth Dominion proved just over 5,000 years ago.

Prospectors and explorers started using the primitive voidlane paths and the advanced voidjump drives of the time to explore the vastness of space, ushering in the Great Voidlane Rush. The Concord continued financing the scouting of new territories with its Pyrvael Teams, while also hiring private scouts such as the Rinvael family.
